children.title: Integer Variable Identities
children.top_down_role: Solver-facing identities, indices, references, plus variable metadata.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Variable Identities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical identities for integer variables and their sign-reversed views.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\) index stored integer variables. A signed identity space is \(\widetilde I=I	imes\{-1,1\}\), with interpretation \(\operatorname{val}(i,s)=s x_i\). Define negation by \(
u(i,s)=(i,-s)\) and canonical identity by \(\operatorname{base}(i,s)=i\). Then \(
u(
u(q))=q\) and \(\operatorname{val}(
u(q))=-\operatorname{val}(q)\) for every \(q\in\widetilde I\). Thus a variable and its negated view share one stored domain while retaining distinct signed identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer variable and its negated view share one underlying variable identity; negation is an involution and reverses the represented value.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\) is integer-valued for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nu^2=\operatorname{id}_{\widetilde I}\) and \(\operatorname{val}(\nu(q))=-\operatorname{val}(q)\).
review_flags: CP-SAT implementation-specific identity encoding requires an authoritative architecture source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is internally coherent and fits the leaf, but the claimed shared-domain and signed-identity architecture is CP-SAT-specific and has no cited source.

children.title: Integer Bound Representation
children.top_down_role: Lower-bound, upper-bound, plus endpoint representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Bound Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed interval bounds attached to a signed integer-variable identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer variable \(x\), a bound representation is a pair \((\ell,u)\in\mathbb Z^2\) with \(\ell\le u\), denoting \(D_{\ell,u}=\{z\in\mathbb Z:\ell\le z\le u\}\). The lower-bound predicate is \(x\ge\ell\), the upper-bound predicate is \(x\le u\), and consistency requires \(\ell\le u\). Under the negated view \(y=-x\), the represented interval transforms exactly as \([\ell,u]\cap\mathbb Z\mapsto[-u,-\ell]\cap\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer bounds are an inclusive integral interval. Negating the variable swaps and negates its endpoints, while an interval is inconsistent when its lower endpoint exceeds its upper endpoint.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in[\ell,u]\cap\mathbb Z\iff -x\in[-u,-\ell]\cap\mathbb Z\).

notation.meaning: Inclusive lower and upper integer bounds.
Integer interval represented by the bounds.

review_flags: Standard interval semantics are clear, but the CP-SAT storage convention needs a solver-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interval and negation formulas are correct, but no evidence establishes that this is CP-SAT's bound representation or storage convention.

children.title: Holed Integer Domains
children.top_down_role: Noncontiguous domains, excluded values, plus interval-list storage.

knowledge_statements.title: Holed Integer Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite unions of disjoint integer intervals representing nonconvex domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A holed integer domain is a finite union \(D=\bigcup_{k=1}^{m}([\ell_k,u_k]\cap\mathbb Z)\), where \(m\ge1\), \(\ell_k\le u_k\), and \(u_k+1<\ell_{k+1}\) for \(1\le k<m\). The strict-gap condition makes the intervals ordered, disjoint, and nonadjacent, hence gives a canonical interval-union representation. A value \(v\) is feasible exactly when \(\ell_k\le v\le u_k\) for some \(k\); integers between successive intervals are holes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A holed domain is a canonical ordered union of separated integer intervals; membership holds in an interval, while omitted integers between intervals are forbidden.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_k,u_k\in\mathbb Z\) for \(1\le k\le m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\in D\iff\exists k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:\ell_k\le v\le u_k\).
review_flags: Canonical union semantics are standard, but CP-SAT domain normalization needs a solver-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The canonical finite union is mathematically precise and appropriate as a representation, but CP-SAT's domain normalization and interval encoding require solver-specific evidence.

children.title: Boolean Literal Representation
children.top_down_role: Literal polarity, identifiers, constants, plus negated references.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Literal Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signed representation of Boolean variables and their complements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\) index Boolean variables \(b_i\in\{0,1\}\). A literal is a pair \(p=(i,s)\in B\times\{0,1\}\), interpreted by \(\operatorname{lit}(i,1)=b_i\) and \(\operatorname{lit}(i,0)=1-b_i\). Its complement is \(\bar p=(i,1-s)\). Consequently \(\operatorname{lit}(p)\in\{0,1\}\), \(\operatorname{lit}(\bar p)=1-\operatorname{lit}(p)\), and complementation is involutive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Boolean literal pairs a variable identity with a polarity. Complementing the polarity complements its truth value and applying complement twice recovers the original literal.
assumptions_latex: \(b_i\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(i\in B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lit}(\bar p)=1-\operatorname{lit}(p)\) and \(\bar{\bar p}=p\).
review_flags: Abstract literal semantics are standard; the concrete CP-SAT literal encoding needs an authoritative solver source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract literal semantics are correct and the content kind fits, but the record lacks evidence connecting this pair-and-polarity representation to CP-SAT.

children.title: Integer View Representation
children.top_down_role: Integer projections used for Boolean-valued quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer View Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-one integer view associated with a Boolean literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a Boolean literal \(p\), its integer view is an integer variable \(v_p\) constrained by \(v_p\in\{0,1\}\) and \(v_p=\operatorname{lit}(p)\). The complementary literal may share the same base view through the affine identity \(v_{\bar p}=1-v_p\). Hence a linear expression containing a literal can replace its truth value by \(v_p\), and a complemented truth value by \(1-v_p\), without changing any feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer view represents a literal by a zero-one integer variable; the complementary literal is represented by one minus that view.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a Boolean literal with truth value \(\operatorname{lit}(p)\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_p=\operatorname{lit}(p)\) and \(v_{\bar p}=1-v_p\).

notation.meaning: Zero-one integer view of literal p.

review_flags: Existence, allocation, and reuse of integer views are CP-SAT implementation details requiring a solver-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-one view equations are coherent, but existence, allocation, sharing, and affine reuse of CP-SAT integer views are unsupported implementation claims.

children.title: Literal–View Channeling
children.top_down_role: Consistency boundary between Boolean literals plus corresponding integer views.

knowledge_statements.title: Literal–View Channeling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bidirectional consistency between a literal and its zero-one integer view.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) be a Boolean literal and let \(v_p\in\{0,1\}\) be its integer view. Exact literal–view channeling is the equivalence \(p\iff(v_p=1)\), together with \(\bar p\iff(v_p=0)\). Equivalently, every admissible assignment satisfies \(v_p=\operatorname{lit}(p)\). Both implications are required: assigning the literal fixes the view, and fixing the view to either endpoint fixes the corresponding literal. One-way implication alone is not exact channeling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact channeling equates a literal's truth value with its zero-one integer view in both directions; either object therefore determines the other.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) and \(\bar p\) are complementary literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\iff(v_p=1)\), \(\bar p\iff(v_p=0)\), and \(v_p=\operatorname{lit}(p)\).
review_flags: The mathematical equivalence is clear, but CP-SAT's posted channeling constraints require an authoritative architecture source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bidirectional channeling condition is mathematically exact and fits the leaf, but no source supports how CP-SAT establishes or maintains these equivalences.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Linear Expression Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse affine expressions over integer variables with integral coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An integer linear expression over variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) is represented by a constant \(c\in\mathbb Z\) and finitely many pairs \((i,a_i)\) with \(a_i\in\mathbb Z\), denoting \(E(x)=c+\sum_i a_i x_i\). A canonical sparse representation removes zero coefficients, combines repeated variable identities by coefficient addition, and orders the remaining identities. Its value is integral for every integral assignment, and a linear constraint is represented by requiring \(E(x)\in D\) for an integer domain \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer linear expression is a sparse integer coefficient map plus a constant; duplicates combine, zero coefficients disappear, and constraints restrict the resulting integer value to a domain.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\in\mathbb Z\) for every represented variable.
\(a_i,c\in\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E(x)=c+\sum_i a_i x_i\in\mathbb Z\), with a constraint expressed as \(E(x)\in D\).

notation.meaning: Allowed integer values of the expression.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.1 Linear integer program p. 29

review_flags: CP-SAT-specific sparse normalization remains to be checked against solver documentation.

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.1 Linear integer program p. 29

children.title: Integer Scaling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scale-factor choices for integral model conversion.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Scaling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-denominator scaling of rational linear models into integer form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite rational linear model, choose an integer scale \(S>0\). Scaling is exact when every coefficient, constant, and finite bound \(q\) satisfies \(Sq\in\mathbb Z\). Multiplying each constraint by its chosen positive scale preserves its equality or inequality sense and its rational feasible set. A global scale may be any common multiple of all reduced denominators; constraint-wise scales may instead be chosen separately. If any scaled datum is rounded rather than integral, the regime is approximate rather than exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rational linear data admit exact integer scaling when chosen positive scales clear every relevant denominator; any required rounding makes the conversion approximate.
assumptions_latex: The model contains finitely many rational coefficients, constants, and finite bounds.
Every applied scale is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Sq\in\mathbb Z\) for every scaled datum \(q\) is necessary and sufficient for denominator-clearing without rounding.

source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming
source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. Theory of lattices and linear diophantine equations p. 45

review_flags: Locator provisionally supports integer and Diophantine normalization; exact scaling discussion requires confirmation.

source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming
source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 4. Theory of lattices and linear diophantine equations p. 45

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The denominator-clearing condition is plausible, but the cited general chapter on lattices and Diophantine equations does not inspectably establish the stated global and constraint-wise scaling regimes or their CP-SAT context.

children.title: Exact Integer Encodings
children.top_down_role: Cases preserving source-model values without approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Integer Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving integer encoding of bounded rational linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a rational constraint be \(\sum_{i=1}^{n}q_i x_i\mathrel{\bowtie}r\), where \(q_i,r\in\mathbb Q\), \(x_i\in\mathbb Z\), and \(\bowtie\in\{\le,=,\ge\}\). If \(S>0\) is divisible by every reduced denominator of \(q_1,\ldots,q_n,r\), define \(a_i=S q_i\in\mathbb Z\) and \(b=S r\in\mathbb Z\). Then \(\sum_i q_i x_i\mathrel{\bowtie}r\) and \(\sum_i a_i x_i\mathrel{\bowtie}b\) have exactly the same integer solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clearing all denominators with a positive common multiple converts a rational linear constraint to an integer one without changing its integer solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(q_i,r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(x_i\in\mathbb Z\).
\(S\) is a positive common multiple of all reduced denominators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i q_i x_i\mathrel{\bowtie}r\iff\sum_i(Sq_i)x_i\mathrel{\bowtie}Sr\).

notation.meaning: One of the relations less-than-or-equal, equality, or greater-than-or-equal.

children.title: Precision-Loss Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where integral conversion cannot preserve intended precision.

knowledge_statements.title: Precision-Loss Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rounding threshold separating exact scaling from altered feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\in\mathbb Q\) be model data, let \(S>0\), and encode it as \(\widehat q=\operatorname{round}(Sq)/S\). Exactness is guaranteed only when \(Sq\in\mathbb Z\), equivalently \(\widehat q=q\). If \(Sq\notin\mathbb Z\), feasibility can change: for the equality \(q x=q\) with \(x\in\mathbb Z\), independently rounding the coefficient and right-hand side under different accumulated errors may destroy or introduce solutions. Thus a nonzero rounding residual \(\delta=Sq-\operatorname{round}(Sq)\) marks loss of exact-encoding guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactness ends when scaled data require rounding. Any nonzero rounding residual removes the general guarantee that the encoded model has the same feasible solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(q\in\mathbb Q\) and \(S\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
Encoding uses a specified deterministic rounding rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta\ne0\) implies that preservation of the original feasible set is not guaranteed in general.
review_flags: A precise CP-SAT rounding policy and a solver-specific counterexample require authoritative documentation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The general loss-of-guarantee claim is plausible, but the discussion of independently accumulated rounding errors is not derived from the stated single deterministic rounding rule, and no source supplies a precise CP-SAT policy or counterexample.

children.title: Safe Coefficient Range
children.top_down_role: Supported coefficient magnitudes across encoded constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Coefficient Range
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient machine-integer bounds for coefficients and evaluated linear expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume signed \(w\)-bit arithmetic with representable interval \([L,U]=[-2^{w-1},2^{w-1}-1]\). For \(E(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i x_i\) and finite domains \(x_i\in[\ell_i,u_i]\cap\mathbb Z\), define \(M_i=\max\{|\ell_i|,|u_i|\}\). A sufficient safe-range condition is \(a_i,c,\ell_i,u_i\in[L,U]\) and \(|c|+\sum_i|a_i|M_i\le U\). Then every exact value of \(E\), and every partial sum accumulated in nondecreasing included terms, lies in \([L,U]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficients and domains are safely representable when their worst-case absolute-value sum fits within the signed accumulator range.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic uses signed \(w\)-bit integers.
Every variable has finite integer bounds \(\ell_i\le u_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|c|+\sum_i|a_i|M_i\le U\) ensures \(E(x)\in[L,U]\) for every domain-feasible \(x\).

notation.meaning: Maximum absolute magnitude of variable i.

review_flags: The sufficient arithmetic bound is generic; CP-SAT's actual integer width, headroom, and validation rules need a solver-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The absolute-value inequality is a valid generic sufficient certificate, but the leaf is within CP-SAT architecture and the actual integer width, reserved headroom, validation rules, and accumulation behavior are uncited.

children.title: Accumulator Overflow Boundary
children.top_down_role: Arithmetic limits for aggregated integer quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Accumulator Overflow Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case magnitude at which fixed-width linear accumulation becomes unsafe.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For signed \(w\)-bit accumulation with range \([L,U]=[-2^{w-1},2^{w-1}-1]\), let \(E(x)=c+\sum_i a_i x_i\). Overflow occurs whenever an executed partial sum leaves \([L,U]\), even if the final mathematical value would return to that interval. Moreover, if \(|c|+\sum_i|a_i|M_i>U\), where \(M_i=\max\{|\ell_i|,|u_i|\}\), the absolute-value safety certificate fails; some sign-compatible bounded assignments may exceed the accumulator range. Exceeding this bound signals risk, not overflow for every instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overflow occurs when any intermediate sum leaves the machine range. Exceeding the worst-case magnitude bound removes safety but does not prove every evaluation overflows.
assumptions_latex: Accumulation uses signed \(w\)-bit arithmetic without an exact wider intermediate.
\(x_i\in[\ell_i,u_i]\cap\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An executed partial sum outside \([L,U]\) is an overflow; \(|c|+\sum_i|a_i|M_i>U\) removes the generic no-overflow guarantee.

notation.meaning: Maximum absolute domain value of variable i.

review_flags: CP-SAT accumulator width, summation strategy, and overflow checks require an authoritative implementation source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic distinction between actual intermediate overflow and failure of a sufficient bound is sound, but CP-SAT's accumulator width, evaluation order, wider intermediates, and overflow checks require authoritative implementation evidence.

children.title: Range–Overflow Interaction
children.top_down_role: Combined impact of coefficient magnitude, domain width, plus aggregation.

assumptions_latex: \(a_i,c,L_i,U_i,m,M\in\mathbb Z\) with \(L_i\le U_i\) and \(m<M\).
Terms may be accumulated in any order, starting from \(c\), using fixed-width signed arithmetic with representable range \([m,M]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c+\sum_i\min(0,q_i^-)\ge m\) and \(c+\sum_i\max(0,q_i^+)\le M\) are sufficient for every partial accumulation, in any term order, to remain in \([m,M]\).

notation.meaning: minimum and maximum contribution of term i

review_flags: Authoritative CP-SAT implementation evidence is required for the actual accumulator-width and validation policy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe evaluation boundary for bounded integer linear expressions in fixed-width signed arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\), where \(a_i,c\in\mathbb Z\), \(x_i\in[L_i,U_i]\cap\mathbb Z\), and fixed-width signed arithmetic represents \([m,M]\). Define \(q_i^- = \min(a_iL_i,a_iU_i)\) and \(q_i^+=\max(a_iL_i,a_iU_i)\). The aggregate conditions \(c+\sum_i q_i^-\ge m\) and \(c+\sum_i q_i^+\le M\) ensure that every complete expression value is representable, but they do not ensure that every partial sum is representable under an arbitrary accumulation order. A sufficient order-independent condition is \[c+\sum_{i=1}^n\min(0,q_i^-)\ge m\quad\text{and}\quad c+\sum_{i=1}^n\max(0,q_i^+)\le M.\] If the relevant complete-value or partial-sum bound fails, unchecked fixed-width evaluation may overflow and invalidate comparisons involving \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete expression bounds guarantee representable final values, while arbitrary-order accumulation requires stronger bounds covering every possible partial sum.
