children.title: Reified Constraint Semantics
children.top_down_role: Constraint truth represented through designated literals.

knowledge_statements.title: Reified Constraint Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full reification of a constraint by a Boolean literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C(x)\) be a constraint over assignments \(x\in D\), and let \(b\in\{0,1\}\). Full reification of \(C\) by \(b\) is the equivalence \[b=1\;\Longleftrightarrow\;C(x).\] Equivalently, the feasible assignments satisfy both implications \(b=1\Rightarrow C(x)\) and \(C(x)\Rightarrow b=1\), or, when the complement is representable, \(b=0\Rightarrow\neg C(x)\). Thus the value of \(b\) records the truth value of \(C(x)\), rather than merely enabling its enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fully reified literal equals the truth value of its constraint, so both the forward and reverse implications must hold.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is the assignment domain and \(C:D\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b=1\Longleftrightarrow C(x)\).
review_flags: Standard-field definition; authoritative CP-SAT interface source is still required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly describes full reification and fits the leaf, but it has no citation or inspectable locator. A CP-SAT interface or implementation source is required.

children.title: Enforcement Literal Scope
children.top_down_role: Activation coverage for literal-controlled constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Enforcement Literal Scope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjunctive activation semantics for literals attached to one constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C(x)\) be a constraint and let \(L=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k)\) be the enforcement literals attached to that constraint. Their scope is local to \(C\), and the guarded semantics is \[\left(\bigwedge_{j=1}^k \ell_j\right)\Longrightarrow C(x).\] If every \(\ell_j\) is true, \(C\) must hold. If at least one is false, this guarded constraint imposes no restriction through \(C\) alone. For \(k=0\), the empty conjunction is true, so \(C\) is unconditionally enforced. The guard does not by itself impose the converse implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All enforcement literals form one conjunctive guard local to the attached constraint; a false guard disables that constraint without asserting its negation.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\ell_j\) is a Boolean literal.
\(C(x)\) has defined semantics on the model domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\bigwedge_j\ell_j)\Rightarrow C(x)\), with an empty guard interpreted as true.
review_flags: Exact supported constraint families and enforcement behavior require CP-SAT API documentation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conjunctive, constraint-local guard semantics and empty-guard convention are precise, and definition is the correct knowledge kind. No source supports the CP-SAT-specific interface semantics or supported constraint scope.

children.title: Half-Reification Boundary
children.top_down_role: Distinctions between one-way enforcement plus full logical equivalence.

assumptions_latex: \(C(x)\) is a Boolean-valued predicate on an assignment domain \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b=1\Rightarrow C(x)\) alone does not in general entail \(b=1\Longleftrightarrow C(x)\).
review_flags: Standard logical boundary; CP-SAT-specific documentation remains required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary between enforcement and full truth-value channeling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an assignment \(x\in D\), a Boolean literal \(b\), and a predicate \(C:D\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\), the guarded relation \[b=1\Longrightarrow C(x)\] is half-reification. It excludes assignments with \(b=1\) and \(C(x)\) false, but it imposes no condition through this relation when \(b=0\). Consequently, half-reification does not in general establish \(b=1\Longleftrightarrow C(x)\). Full reification requires an additional reverse direction, such as \(C(x)\Rightarrow b=1\), or an equivalent complementary guard \(b=0\Rightarrow\neg C(x)\) when \(\neg C\) is modeled exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An enforcement implication acts only when its literal is true; without an exact reverse direction, the literal does not in general encode the constraint's truth value.
knowledge_statements.title: Half-Reification Boundary
Boolean–Integer Channeling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence between a Boolean literal and an integer-domain proposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in D\subseteq\mathbb Z\), let \(P(x)\) be a predicate, and let \(b\in\{0,1\}\). Exact Boolean–integer channeling imposes \[b=1\Longleftrightarrow P(x).\] For the equality predicate \(P(x)\equiv(x=v)\), this is represented by the two guarded constraints \(b=1\Rightarrow x=v\) and \(b=0\Rightarrow x\ne v\). For a threshold predicate \(P(x)\equiv(x\le t)\), the complementary direction over integers is \(b=0\Rightarrow x\ge t+1\). Both directions are required when \(b\) must expose the predicate's exact truth value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Channeling links a Boolean variable to an integer predicate in both directions, using the exact integer complement for the false branch.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb Z\) and \(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b=1\Longleftrightarrow P(x)\), with both guarded directions represented exactly.
review_flags: Standard-field definition; solver-specific supported channeling forms require a source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record precisely defines exact Boolean–integer channeling and gives correct equality and integer-threshold complements. It lacks an authoritative source for the CP-SAT-local interpretation and supported forms.

children.title: Clausal Interface
children.top_down_role: Clause-oriented Boolean model input.

knowledge_statements.title: Clausal Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjunctive Boolean constraint interface used by the SAT layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given Boolean literals \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k\), a clause is the constraint \[\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\ell_k=\mathrm{true}.\] Under the encoding \(v(\ell)\in\{0,1\}\), where \(v(p)=p\) and \(v(\neg p)=1-p\), the same condition is \(\sum_{i=1}^k v(\ell_i)\ge1\). A unit clause forces its sole literal true; the empty clause is infeasible. A conjunction of clauses is satisfied precisely when every constituent clause contains at least one true literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The clausal interface accepts disjunctions of Boolean literals; each clause requires at least one true literal, and all posted clauses must hold.
assumptions_latex: Every \(\ell_i\) is a positive or negated Boolean variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigvee_i\ell_i\) is equivalent to \(\sum_i v(\ell_i)\ge1\).

notation.meaning: zero-one truth value of a literal

review_flags: Standard SAT definition; an authoritative CP-SAT interface locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clause semantics, unit-clause case, empty-clause case, and zero-one representation are mathematically consistent, and definition fits the interface leaf. No citation or locator is supplied.

children.title: Cardinality Interface
children.top_down_role: Literal-count constraint input.

knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted counting constraints over Boolean literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean literals \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n\) with truth values \(v(\ell_i)\in\{0,1\}\), a cardinality constraint restricts their unweighted count: \[L\le\sum_{i=1}^n v(\ell_i)\le U,\] where \(0\le L\le U\le n\). The special cases \(U=1\), \(L=1\), and \(L=U=1\) are respectively at-most-one, at-least-one, and exactly-one constraints. Repeated occurrences, if admitted by an interface, count as separate terms unless normalized before compilation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cardinality constraint bounds the number of true literals; at-most-one, at-least-one, and exactly-one are its standard special cases.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n\) are Boolean literals.
\(L,U\in\mathbb Z\) and \(0\le L\le U\le n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le\sum_i v(\ell_i)\le U\).

notation.meaning: zero-one truth value of literal i

review_flags: Standard-field definition; normalization and native-interface details require a CP-SAT source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unweighted cardinality definition and named special cases are correct. The statement about repeated occurrences is explicitly interface-dependent and cannot be reviewed without a CP-SAT API or implementation source.

children.title: Pseudo-Boolean Interface
children.top_down_role: Weighted Boolean constraint input.

assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb Z\) and every \(\ell_i\) is a Boolean literal.
Each finite bound and every normalized coefficient lies in the model interface's accepted integer range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le\sum_i a_i v(\ell_i)\le U\) defines the accepted assignments; cardinality constraints arise when \(a_i=1\) for every term.

notation.meaning: zero-one truth value of literal i

review_flags: An authoritative CP-SAT source is required for accepted coefficients, bounds, and normalization behavior.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted linear inequalities over Boolean literal truth values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n\) be Boolean literals, let \(a_i\in\mathbb Z\), and let \(L,U\in\mathbb Z\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}\). A pseudo-Boolean constraint has the form \[L\le\sum_{i=1}^n a_i v(\ell_i)\le U,\] where \(v(\ell_i)\in\{0,1\}\) is the truth value of \(\ell_i\). Negated literals may be normalized using \(v(\neg p)=1-p\), with the resulting constant transferred to the bounds. Cardinality constraints are the special case \(a_i=1\) for every term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pseudo-Boolean interface expresses bounded weighted sums of literal truth values and includes unweighted cardinality constraints when every weight is one.
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Boolean Interface

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite constraint system.
Each \(a_i\) is a Boolean literal recognized as an assumption.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Infeasibility under \(A\) may be certified by \(A'\subseteq A\) such that \(F\land\bigwedge_{a\in A'}a\) is infeasible.
review_flags: Core guarantees and solver-call persistence semantics require authoritative CP-SAT documentation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporary activation of model conditions for satisfiability queries and conflict extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a base constraint system and let \(A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}\) be a set of designated assumption literals. Solving under assumptions asks whether \[F\land\bigwedge_{i=1}^k a_i\] is satisfiable without permanently adding the unit constraints \(a_i=1\) to \(F\). If it is infeasible, an assumption core is a subset \(A'\subseteq A\) such that \[F\land\bigwedge_{a\in A'}a\] is infeasible. Minimality is an additional property and is not implied merely by returning a core.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assumption literals temporarily activate conditions for one solve; infeasibility may yield a conflicting subset, which need not be minimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Assumption-Literal Modeling

children.title: Linear Constraint Compilation
children.top_down_role: Translation of integer linear constraints into solver-facing structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Constraint Compilation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equisatisfiable normalization of bounded integer linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an integer linear constraint \(L\le c+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le U\) with finite-domain \(x_i\). First combine repeated variables and remove zero coefficients. Transfer \(c\) to obtain \(L-c\le\sum_i a_i x_i\le U-c\); intersect these bounds with the activity interval computed from the variable domains. Divide all coefficients and finite bounds by a common positive divisor only when the corresponding integer rounding preserves equivalence. Emit the normalized linear constraint, optionally guarded by its enforcement literals, and report infeasibility if the tightened lower bound exceeds the tightened upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compilation combines terms, shifts constants, tightens bounds from domains, applies equivalence-preserving integer normalization, and emits a guarded or unconditional linear constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,c,L,U\in\mathbb Z\) and every \(x_i\) has a finite integer domain.
All intermediate products, bounds, and sums are representable exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The emitted normalized constraint has exactly the same feasible assignments on the original variables as the input constraint.
review_flags: Exact CP-SAT presolve and compilation sequence requires an implementation source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate kind, but the claimed compilation sequence, activity tightening, divisor normalization, guarded emission, and exact equivalence are solver-specific and unsupported. The available inventory does not provide an inspectable CP-SAT implementation locator.

children.title: Pseudo-Boolean Constraint Compilation
children.top_down_role: Translation of weighted Boolean constraints into solver-facing structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Boolean Constraint Compilation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization and Boolean encoding of weighted literal constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(L\le\sum_{i=1}^n a_i v(\ell_i)\le U\). Replace every negated literal using \(v(\neg p)=1-v(p)\), transfer generated constants to \(L,U\), combine coefficients of identical Boolean variables, and eliminate zero coefficients. Normalize negative coefficients by complementing the associated literal and shifting the bounds. Tighten the bounds using the attainable activity range. Then retain the normalized pseudo-Boolean propagator or encode it by clauses and auxiliary Boolean variables. The emitted representation must be equisatisfiable after existentially quantifying any auxiliaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compilation normalizes negations and coefficients, tightens activity bounds, then retains a weighted constraint or emits an equisatisfiable Boolean encoding.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,L,U\in\mathbb Z\) and every \(\ell_i\) is a Boolean literal.
All normalized coefficients and intermediate sums are exactly representable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each original Boolean assignment, the input holds exactly when some auxiliary assignment satisfies the emitted representation.

notation.meaning: zero-one truth value of literal i

review_flags: Choice of native propagator versus encoding and exact normalization rules require a CP-SAT implementation source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the compilation leaf, but the choice between a native propagator and a clausal auxiliary encoding, as well as the exact normalization sequence, requires CP-SAT implementation evidence. No source or locator is cited.

children.title: Shared Encoding Boundary
children.top_down_role: Representation choices shared across linear plus pseudo-Boolean inputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Encoding Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between common zero-one linear semantics and integer-specific compilation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pseudo-Boolean constraint \(L\le\sum_i a_i b_i\le U\), with \(b_i\in\{0,1\}\), is also an integer linear constraint and may share normalization, bound tightening, and guarded-enforcement machinery with general linear constraints. This equivalence ends at representations that rely on Boolean complementation, clauses, or literal-level propagation: \(1-b_i\) is a Boolean complement only because \(b_i\) is binary. Replacing \(b_i\) by a general integer variable \(x_i\) makes such transformations invalid unless an explicit channeling relation supplies the required Boolean literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean weighted sums share linear arithmetic machinery, but literal complementation and clausal propagation do not extend to unrestricted integer variables without channeling.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,L,U\in\mathbb Z\).
Each shared variable \(b_i\) has domain exactly \(\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Arithmetic normalization is shared, while literal-specific encodings are valid only on binary variables or explicitly channeled predicates.
review_flags: The architectural sharing boundary is solver-specific and requires CP-SAT implementation evidence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical distinction between binary complementation and unrestricted integer variables is sound, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. The assertion that CP-SAT shares the listed compilation machinery is architectural and cannot be established without implementation evidence.

children.title: Table Constraint Compilation
children.top_down_role: Allowed-tuple plus forbidden-tuple model translation.

assumptions_latex: \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\) are finite integer domains.
\(T\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) is the set of allowed tuples.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in T\) holds exactly when one tuple selector is true and its coordinates are channeled to the variables.

notation.meaning: Boolean selector for allowed tuple t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the extensional-selector encoding is a standard finite-domain compilation, but the intended CP-SAT implementation variant is not sourced
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct Boolean-selector compilation of a positive extensional table.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given variables \(x_i\in D_i\), introduce one Boolean variable \(b_t\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\in T\). Post \(\sum_{t\in T}b_t=1\) and, for every \(t\in T\), \(i\in\{1,
\ldots,n\}\), the implication \(b_t=1\Rightarrow x_i=t_i\). If \(T=\varnothing\), return infeasible. After propagation or search, output the original variables and discard the auxiliary selectors. The resulting formulation projects onto exactly \(T\): an assignment to \((x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) extends to the auxiliaries if and only if it is an allowed tuple.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Create one Boolean selector per allowed tuple, require exactly one selector, and channel every selected coordinate to its variable; the projected feasible assignments are exactly the table rows.
knowledge_statements.title: Table Constraint Compilation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selector construction is mathematically coherent and algorithm is the correct knowledge kind, but no citation establishes that this is the intended CP-SAT table-compilation architecture.

children.title: Automaton Constraint Compilation
children.top_down_role: State-transition model translation.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\) and every symbol domain \(D_i\) are finite.
\(q_0\in Q\), \(F\subseteq Q\), and \(\Delta_i\subseteq Q\times D_i\times Q\) specify a layered automaton.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compiled constraints are feasible exactly for words \((x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) labeling an accepting path from \(q_0\) to \(F\).

notation.meaning: allowed labeled transitions at layer i
Boolean selector for a layered transition

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: layered network-flow compilation is standard for regular constraints, but the intended CP-SAT encoding is not sourced
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layered accepting-path compilation for a finite automaton constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each transition \((p,v,q)\in\Delta_i\), introduce \(a_{i,p,v,q}\in\{0,1\}\). Impose unit flow leaving \(q_0\) at layer \(0\), flow conservation at every intermediate pair \((i,q)\), and one unit of total flow entering states in \(F\) at layer \(n\). Channel selected labels by requiring \(a_{i,p,v,q}=1\Rightarrow x_i=v\), together with \(\sum_{(p,v,q)\in\Delta_i}a_{i,p,v,q}=1\) for each layer \(i\). Remove unreachable transitions before posting. Output the original variables; their feasible words are precisely those accepted by the automaton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a layered transition network, send one unit of flow from the initial state to an accepting state, and channel each selected arc label to the corresponding variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Automaton Constraint Compilation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The layered-flow construction has the correct algorithmic role and describes an accepting-path encoding, but its correspondence to the intended CP-SAT compilation requires an authoritative source.

children.title: Tuple-to-State Compilation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural overlap between extensional tuples plus state-based encodings.

knowledge_statements.title: Tuple-to-State Compilation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete exponential separation between explicit tuples and state-based compilation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(n\ge 1\), let \(L_n=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\equiv0\pmod 2\}\). Any positive extensional table representing \(L_n\) contains exactly \(2^{n-1}\) tuples, because every accepted assignment must occur as a row. In contrast, a deterministic layered automaton represents \(L_n\) with two states recording the current parity and transitions that toggle on symbol \(1\). Thus tuple enumeration can be exponentially larger than state compilation. Such compression is available when prefixes having identical feasible suffix languages can share a state; without such equivalence, state compilation need not reduce the representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every positive length n, even parity needs 2^(n-1) explicit rows but only two automaton states; state compression works by sharing prefixes having the same feasible suffixes.
assumptions_latex: \(n\) is a positive integer.
Words have fixed length \(n\) over the alphabet \(\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Explicit tuple compilation requires \(2^{n-1}\) rows for \(L_n\), whereas an equivalent deterministic automaton uses two states.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the positive-length parity family exhibits the table-versus-state separation

children.title: All-Different Constraint Interface
children.top_down_role: Model representation for pairwise-distinct value requirements.

assumptions_latex: \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) are integer variables with finite domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface accepts exactly assignments satisfying \(x_i\ne x_j\) for all distinct \(i,j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain, pairwise-distinct semantics of the global all-different interface.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Constraint programming (CP) p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The all-different constraint on \((x_1,
\ldots,x_n)\) denotes the relation \[\operatorname{AllDifferent}(x_1,
\ldots,x_n)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigwedge_{1\le i<j\le n}x_i\ne x_j.\] Hence every value occurs at most once among the variables. The interface specifies this feasible relation independently of whether the solver enforces it through pairwise disequalities, matching-based propagation, cardinality reasoning, or a SAT encoding. If some variables are optional, their presence semantics require a separate interface contract and are not implicit in this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All-different requires every pair of present finite-domain variables to take unequal values, regardless of the internal propagation or encoding method.
knowledge_statements.title: All-Different Constraint Interface

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Constraint programming (CP) p. 17

children.title: Inverse Constraint Interface
children.top_down_role: Model representation for mutually inverse index mappings.

assumptions_latex:
\(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}\) and \(y_0,\ldots,y_{n-1}\) have domains contained in \(\{0,
\ldots,n-1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface enforces that \(x\) and \(y\) are mutually inverse permutations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-based inverse-permutation semantics for two equal-length variable arrays.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Constraint programming (CP) p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The inverse constraint on arrays \(x=(x_0,
\ldots,x_{n-1})\) and \(y=(y_0,
\ldots,y_{n-1})\) is the relation \[\operatorname{Inverse}(x,y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigwedge_{i=0}^{n-1}\bigwedge_{j=0}^{n-1}(x_i=j\Longleftrightarrow y_j=i).\] Together with the stated domains, this relation forces each array to be a permutation of \(\{0,
\ldots,n-1\}\), and each array is the inverse permutation of the other. The indexing base is part of the interface and must be translated explicitly when a model uses one-based indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two equal-length arrays satisfy inverse when assigning value j to x at i is equivalent to assigning value i to y at j.
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse Constraint Interface

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Constraint programming (CP) p. 17

children.title: Element Constraint Interface
children.top_down_role: Model representation for index-selected values.

assumptions_latex:
\(A=(A_0,
\ldots,A_{m-1})\) is an array of integer constants or integer variables.

The index variable satisfies \(i\in\{0,
\ldots,m-1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface accepts exactly assignments satisfying \(z=A_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-based element-selection relation with an in-range index.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Constraint programming (CP) p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The element constraint denotes \[\operatorname{Element}(i,A,z)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigvee_{k=0}^{m-1}(i=k\wedge z=A_k).\] Because \(i\) is in range, exactly one disjunct determines the selected entry. If the entries of \(A\) are variables, the equality is between variables; if they are constants, it fixes \(z\) to the indexed constant. An offset indexing convention is represented by replacing \(A_k\) with \(A_{k-o}\) and requiring \(i\in\{o,
\ldots,o+m-1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Element links an in-range index to an array entry: the target equals the unique constant or variable selected by that index.
knowledge_statements.title: Element Constraint Interface

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Constraint programming (CP) p. 17

children.title: Circuit Constraint Interface
children.top_down_role: Graph-cycle model representation.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite vertex set and \(E\subseteq V\times V\) includes every permitted arc and any required self-loop.
Each arc \((i,j)\in E\) has a Boolean literal \(a_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selected non-self arcs form one directed cycle through all non-self-looped vertices.

notation.meaning: Boolean literal selecting arc from i to j
vertices not excluded by selected self-loops

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the stated relation matches the common optional-node directed-circuit interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed circuit semantics with self-loops representing excluded vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A circuit assignment satisfies \(\sum_{j:(i,j)\in E}a_{ij}=1\) and \(\sum_{j:(j,i)\in E}a_{ji}=1\) for every \(i\in V\). Define \(V'=\{i\in V:a_{ii}=0\}\), treating an absent self-loop as fixed to \(0\). When \(V'\ne\varnothing\), the selected non-self arcs \(\{(i,j)
\in E:i\ne j,
a_{ij}=1\}\) must constitute one directed cycle whose vertex set is exactly \(V'\). Thus a selected self-loop excludes its vertex, while disconnected subtours on active vertices are forbidden.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every vertex chooses one incoming and outgoing arc; self-loops exclude optional vertices, and all remaining selected arcs must form one directed cycle.
knowledge_statements.title: Circuit Constraint Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is an appropriate knowledge kind, but exact CP-SAT circuit behavior for self-loops, absent self-loops, and the case with no active vertices cannot be established from the supplied evidence.

children.title: Route Constraint Interface
children.top_down_role: Route-oriented graph model representation.

assumptions_latex:
\(V=\{0,
\ldots,n\}\) has distinguished depot \(0\).
Permitted arcs \(E\subseteq V\times V\) carry Boolean literals \(a_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selected non-self arcs decompose into depot-rooted routes, with every active nondepot vertex occurring on exactly one route.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the definition captures the common multiple-circuit or routes relation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple directed routes sharing one distinguished depot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every nondepot vertex \(i\), require exactly one selected incoming arc and one selected outgoing arc, counting \(a_{ii}\) when present. Require balanced depot degree, \(\sum_{j:(0,j)\in E,
j
e0}a_{0j}=\sum_{i:(i,0)\in E,
i
e0}a_{i0}\). Let \(V'=\{i
e0:a_{ii}=0\}\). The selected non-self arcs must decompose into directed cycles, every one containing depot \(0\), and together cover exactly \(V'\). Consequently, no selected subtour may avoid the depot, while a selected self-loop omits its nondepot vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Routes are directed cycles sharing a depot; each active customer has one predecessor and successor, excluded customers use self-loops, and depot-free subtours are forbidden.
knowledge_statements.title: Route Constraint Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed multiple-route relation is plausible, but depot degree, admissibility of self-loops, optional-node behavior, and empty-route behavior are solver-specific and unsupported.

children.title: Discrete-Arithmetic Constraint Interface
children.top_down_role: Integer multiplication, division, modulo, minimum, plus maximum inputs.

assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb Z^k\) is the declared operand domain.
\(f:D\rightharpoonup\mathbb Z^r\) is the precisely specified integer operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
The interface accepts exactly the graph \(\{(x,z):x\in\operatorname{dom}(f),
z=f(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract graph-relation interface; each arithmetic operator requires separately fixed semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A discrete-arithmetic constraint for an operator \(f\) denotes its graph relation \[R_f(x,z)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname{dom}(f)\wedge z=f(x).\] Typical instances include products, absolute values, minima, maxima, integer quotients, and remainders, but each instance is a distinct relation. For a partial operator, assignments outside \(\operatorname{dom}(f)\), such as a zero divisor, are infeasible. The interface must fix operand order, signed overflow policy, and, for division or remainder, the rounding convention; these choices cannot be inferred from the generic arithmetic-interface name.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete-arithmetic primitive enforces the exact graph of a specified integer operator; partial-domain, overflow, division, and remainder conventions belong to that operator's contract.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Arithmetic Constraint Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graph-of-an-operator abstraction fits the generic interface leaf, but it cannot determine the actual supported operators or their overflow, division, remainder, and partial-domain conventions without solver documentation.

children.title: Packing Constraint Interface
children.top_down_role: Placement plus capacity-oriented packing inputs.

assumptions_latex: Each rectangle \(i\) has intervals \(X_i=[x_i,x_i+w_i)\) and \(Y_i=[y_i,y_i+h_i)\), with \(w_i,h_i\ge0\).
Optional rectangle \(i\) has presence literal \(p_i\); mandatory rectangles use \(p_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every pair of present rectangles has disjoint interiors.

notation.meaning: horizontal and vertical half-open intervals of rectangle i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-dimensional orthogonal no-overlap packing with optional rectangles.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Packing, Covering, Partitioning p. 51

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The packing relation requires, for every pair \(i<j\), \[p_i=p_j=1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_i+w_i\le x_j\vee x_j+w_j\le x_i\vee y_i+h_i\le y_j\vee y_j+h_j\le y_i.\] Thus two present axis-aligned rectangles must be separated on at least one coordinate axis. Equality is permitted, so boundaries may touch. A containing-bin requirement is separate: for a bin \([0,W)\times[0,H)\), it adds \(0\le x_i\), \(x_i+w_i\le W\), \(0\le y_i\), and \(y_i+h_i\le H\) for each present rectangle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Present axis-aligned rectangles must be separated horizontally or vertically; touching boundaries is allowed, while containment in a bin is a separate condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Packing Constraint Interface

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Packing, Covering, Partitioning p. 51

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited set-packing section does not establish the solver's geometric no-overlap interface. Moreover, with zero width or height allowed, the displayed axis-separation relation is not equivalent in general to merely having disjoint interiors, so authoritative interface semantics are required.

children.title: Reservoir Constraint Interface
children.top_down_role: Time-indexed level-change inputs.

assumptions_latex:
Events \(i=1,
\ldots,n\) have integer times \(t_i\), signed level changes \(d_i\), and presence literals \(p_i\).

The initial level is \(L_0\), with prescribed bounds \(L_{\min}\le L_{
max}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reservoir level remains in \([L_{\min},L_{\max}]\) after every event time.

notation.meaning: reservoir level after all events through time t
signed level change at event i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bounded prefix sums define the standard reservoir relation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded level process generated by optional signed events.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reservoir sums signed changes from all present events up to each time and requires the resulting level to stay between fixed lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Reservoir Constraint Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded prefix-sum relation is standard, but the intended CP-SAT interface may impose specific initial-level, event-time, optional-event, and simultaneous-event conventions that are not sourced.

children.title: Resource Constraint Interface
children.top_down_role: General resource-consumption model inputs.

assumptions_latex: Task \(i\) has a half-open interval \([s_i,e_i)\), demand \(d_i\ge0\), and presence literal \(p_i\).
The renewable-resource capacity is \(C\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every time, the total demand of present active tasks does not exceed \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Renewable cumulative-resource capacity for mandatory or optional interval tasks.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.1 Resource allocation in production planning p. 4

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The cumulative resource constraint is the relation \[\operatorname{Cumulative}((s_i,e_i,d_i,p_i)_{i=1}^n,C)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \forall t,
\sum_{i:s_i\le t<e_i}p_i d_i\le C.\] The half-open convention means a task ending at \(t\) releases its capacity before a task starting at \(t\) consumes capacity. Mandatory tasks use \(p_i=1\); an optional task with \(p_i=0\) contributes no demand. This interface models a renewable resource and does not impose a reservoir-style balance across time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every time point, sum the demands of present tasks whose half-open intervals contain that time; the sum must not exceed the renewable-resource capacity.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource Constraint Interface

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.1 Resource allocation in production planning p. 4

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula correctly defines a cumulative renewable-resource constraint, but the cited general resource-allocation section does not support these exact interval, presence, and half-open-time semantics or establish that the generic leaf denotes this particular CP-SAT interface.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Scheduling recipes; interval, no-overlap, cumulative, and two-dimensional non-overlap models

children.title: Mandatory Interval Representation
children.top_down_role: Always-present interval objects plus their stored attributes.

knowledge_statements.title: Mandatory Interval Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time, always-present interval used by CP-SAT scheduling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mandatory interval is a tuple \(I=(s,d,e)\) of bounded integer variables or constants satisfying \(d\ge 0\) and \[e=s+d.\] Its occupied time set is the half-open set \([s,e)=\{t\in\mathbb Z:s\le t<e\}\). The interval is present in every feasible assignment, so every scheduling constraint containing \(I\) treats its occupied time and any associated demand as active. Fixed-size intervals are the special case in which \(d\) is an integer constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mandatory interval is always active, has nonnegative duration, satisfies end equals start plus duration, and occupies the half-open time range from start to end.
assumptions_latex: \(s,d,e\) have bounded integer domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\) is always present and satisfies \(e=s+d\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Standard discrete scheduling interval semantics.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the mandatory-interval leaf and is internally coherent, but no inspectable source supports the CP-SAT-specific claims about bounded integer components, half-open occupancy, duration admissibility, and unconditional participation in scheduling constraints.

children.title: Optional Interval Representation
children.top_down_role: Presence-controlled interval objects plus their stored attributes.

knowledge_statements.title: Optional Interval Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time interval whose scheduling participation is controlled by a Boolean presence literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An optional interval is a tuple \(I=(s,d,e,p)\), where \(s,d,e\) are bounded integer variables or constants, \(d\ge0\), and \(p\in\{0,1\}\) is its presence indicator. Its defining relation is enforced conditionally: \[p=1\;\Longrightarrow\;e=s+d.\] When \(p=1\), the interval occupies \([s,e)\) and participates in every scheduling constraint containing it. When \(p=0\), those scheduling constraints ignore the interval; constraints separately imposed on \(s,d,e\) remain effective unless they are also reified by \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optional interval is active only when its presence Boolean is true; absence removes its scheduling contribution but does not automatically disable separate variable constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(s,d,e\) have bounded integer domains and \(d\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=1\) activates \(I\) and enforces \(e=s+d\); \(p=0\) removes \(I\) from scheduling constraints.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Standard optional-interval and reification semantics.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local scope are appropriate, but authoritative solver documentation is required for the conditional interval equation, absence behavior in scheduling constraints, and the claim that separately imposed constraints on temporal variables remain active.

children.title: Interval Presence Linkage
children.top_down_role: Connection between optional interval existence plus presence literals.

knowledge_statements.title: Interval Presence Linkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linkage between an optional interval's presence literal, defining equality, and global scheduling participation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an optional interval \(I=(s,d,e,p)\), the same literal \(p\) gates both its interval identity and its contribution to scheduling constraints. Formally, \[p=1\Longrightarrow e=s+d,\qquad p=0\Longrightarrow I\text{ contributes no occupied time or resource demand}.\] If another decision literal \(a\) is intended to select the interval, the model must impose \(a=p\), or the appropriate one-way implication when selection and presence are not equivalent. Absence alone does not assign canonical values to \(s,d,e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One presence literal must consistently gate interval validity and scheduling participation; linking it to selection decisions prevents logically active but absent, or selected but inactive, tasks.
assumptions_latex: \(I=(s,d,e,p)\) is an optional interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The presence literal consistently controls the defining equality and every scheduling contribution of \(I\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Standard linkage requirement for optional scheduling objects.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property matches the linkage leaf, but no source verifies that the same presence literal gates all stated CP-SAT effects. The modeling recommendation concerning an external selection literal also requires a precise source or a clearly delimited modeling assumption.

children.title: Temporal Quantity Representation
children.top_down_role: Start, size, end, plus time-domain model fields.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Quantity Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-integer representation of starts, durations, ends, and scheduling horizons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a discrete CP-SAT scheduling model, every temporal quantity is represented by a bounded integer variable or integer constant. For task \(i\), let \(s_i\), \(d_i\), and \(e_i\) denote start, duration, and end, with \(d_i\ge0\). A mandatory task satisfies \(e_i=s_i+d_i\); an optional task with presence indicator \(p_i\) satisfies \(p_i=1\Longrightarrow e_i=s_i+d_i\). Bounds such as \(0\le s_i\le H\) and \(0\le e_i\le H\) place the task within an integer horizon \(H\). Rational physical times require scaling to integer units before encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CP-SAT scheduling uses bounded integer time quantities; interval equations connect start, duration, and end, conditionally for optional tasks.
assumptions_latex: Time has been discretized into integer units.
All encoded bounds and scaled coefficients fit the solver's supported integer range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each task has a bounded-integer temporal representation coupled by its interval equation.

notation.meaning: start, duration, and end of task i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Standard bounded-integer CP scheduling representation.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the terminal container and introduces its notation, but the universal claim that every temporal quantity has the stated form, the interval equations, scaling requirement, and supported integer-range condition need solver-version-specific evidence.

children.title: Precedence Relation Representation
children.top_down_role: Ordering relations between scheduling entities.

knowledge_statements.title: Precedence Relation Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reified representation of a directed finish-to-start precedence relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tasks \(i\) and \(j\), finish-to-start precedence is the inequality \[e_i\le s_j.\] An unconditional precedence constraint enforces this inequality in every feasible assignment. A conditional precedence controlled by a Boolean literal \(b_{ij}\) is represented by \[b_{ij}=1\Longrightarrow e_i\le s_j.\] If \(b_{ij}\) is intended to denote the truth value of the precedence rather than merely enable it, the reverse implication must also be encoded, with the integer negation \(b_{ij}=0\Longrightarrow e_i\ge s_j+1\). Optional tasks additionally require presence-consistent gating.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A precedence is encoded by end-before-start; a Boolean implication enables it, while exact truth-value representation also requires the reverse integer inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(s_j\) and \(e_i\) are integer temporal quantities.
\(b_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) when precedence is conditional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The encoded relation enforces \(e_i\le s_j\) whenever its enabling condition holds.

notation.meaning: task i finishes before task j starts

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Standard reified finish-to-start precedence encoding.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finish-to-start and integer-complement formulas are mathematically coherent and the representation kind fits the leaf. An inspectable source is still required for the CP-SAT reification semantics and for the additional presence-consistent gating requirement.

children.title: Temporal–Precedence Coupling
children.top_down_role: Links between interval timing plus ordering constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal–Precedence Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency conditions coupling precedence literals to temporal variables and optional-task presence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b_{ij}\) select the precedence of task \(i\) before task \(j\), and let \(p_i,p_j\) be their presence indicators. A presence-consistent temporal coupling is \[b_{ij}\le p_i,\qquad b_{ij}\le p_j,\qquad b_{ij}=1\Longrightarrow e_i\le s_j.\] If two present tasks must be ordered in exactly one direction, introduce \(b_{ij},b_{ji}\) and impose \[b_{ij}+b_{ji}=p_i p_j,\] replacing the product by its standard Boolean linearization. For mandatory tasks the right-hand side is \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selected precedence requires both tasks to be present and enforces the corresponding end-before-start inequality; mutually ordered present tasks select exactly one direction.
assumptions_latex: Each task's temporal quantities satisfy its interval representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selected precedence arcs are temporally valid and cannot connect absent tasks.

notation.meaning: indicator that task i precedes task j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Standard presence-gated disjunctive precedence coupling.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the coupling leaf, but the proposed formulation is a particular modeling construction rather than a source-backed intrinsic solver representation. Its presence implications, exactly-one-direction equation, and supported linearization must be documented precisely.

children.title: Unary Resource Representation
children.top_down_role: Single-capacity resource model structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Unary Resource Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity-one resource represented by pairwise non-overlap of active intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_i=(s_i,d_i,e_i,p_i)\) be intervals assigned to one unary resource, taking \(p_i=1\) for mandatory intervals. The resource is represented by a non-overlap constraint requiring, for every distinct pair \(i,j\), \[p_i=p_j=1\Longrightarrow \bigl(e_i\le s_j\bigr)\lor\bigl(e_j\le s_i\bigr).\] Equivalently, at every integer time \(t\), at most one present interval occupies \(t\): \[\sum_i p_i\mathbf 1\{s_i\le t<e_i\}\le1.\] Zero-duration intervals occupy no time under the half-open convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unary resource allows at most one present task at a time, represented by a non-overlap constraint over its intervals.
assumptions_latex: Each \(I_i\) has a valid interval representation.
All intervals in the constraint use the same time scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No two present positive-duration intervals overlap on the unary resource.

notation.meaning: presence indicator, equal to one for mandatory intervals

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role and unary-capacity interpretation are appropriate. Solver documentation is required to support optional-interval filtering, equivalence with the pointwise formula, and especially the treatment of zero-duration intervals.

children.title: Cumulative Resource Representation
children.top_down_role: Multi-capacity resource model structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Resource Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Renewable resource represented by time-indexed demand not exceeding capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let interval \(I_i=(s_i,d_i,e_i,p_i)\) consume an integer demand \(q_i\ge0\) from a renewable resource of integer capacity \(C\ge0\), with \(p_i=1\) for mandatory intervals. The cumulative-resource representation is the family of inequalities \[\sum_{i:s_i\le t<e_i}p_iq_i\le C\qquad\text{for every integer time }t.\] A cumulative global constraint represents these inequalities without explicitly enumerating every time point. Only present intervals contribute demand, and each contribution applies throughout the interval's half-open occupied time set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cumulative resource limits the total demand of all present intervals active at each time to the resource capacity.
assumptions_latex: Intervals and resource quantities use integer domains.
\(q_i\ge0\) and \(C\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every integer time, active demand is at most \(C\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Standard cumulative scheduling constraint semantics.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise capacity condition matches the cumulative-resource leaf, but no source establishes the exact CP-SAT cumulative semantics, accepted demand and capacity expression types, optional-interval behavior, or the claim that the global constraint represents the displayed family without time enumeration.

children.title: Demand–Capacity Linkage
children.top_down_role: Connections among interval demands, resource capacities, plus presence.

knowledge_statements.title: Demand–Capacity Linkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise feasibility condition linking interval presence, resource demand, and capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For intervals \(I_i\) sharing a cumulative resource, demand and capacity are correctly linked when each demand \(q_i\) is aligned with \(I_i\), absence suppresses that demand, and \[\sum_i p_iq_i\mathbf 1\{s_i\le t<e_i\}\le C\qquad\text{for all integer }t.\] Thus every present task individually satisfies \(q_i\le C\), while simultaneous present tasks must satisfy the aggregate inequality. If \(q_i\) or \(C\) is variable, its bounded integer value in the assignment is used. Constraints on demand variables outside the cumulative constraint remain active when an interval is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presence gates each task's resource contribution, and the sum of active demands must never exceed capacity; separate demand-variable constraints remain active during absence.
assumptions_latex: Each demand entry and interval entry refer to the same task.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Presence-weighted active demand is bounded pointwise by resource capacity.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The linkage condition is locally relevant, but source support is required for variable demands, variable capacity, and absence behavior. Moreover, the assertion that every present task individually satisfies q_i <= C requires the task to occupy at least one represented time point; it need not follow for a zero-duration interval under the stated half-open convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Dimensional Non-Overlap Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Axis-interval representation of non-overlapping, axis-aligned rectangles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent rectangle \(i\) by an x-axis interval \(X_i=[x_i,x_i+w_i)\) and a y-axis interval \(Y_i=[y_i,y_i+h_i)\), with \(w_i,h_i\ge0\). Optional rectangles use one shared presence indicator \(p_i\) for both axis intervals. Two present rectangles \(i\ne j\) do not overlap precisely when \[x_i+w_i\le x_j\;\lor\;x_j+w_j\le x_i\;\lor\;y_i+h_i\le y_j\;\lor\;y_j+h_j\le y_i.\] A two-dimensional non-overlap constraint enforces this disjunction for every present pair. Container bounds are separate constraints on the axis coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each rectangle is represented by linked x- and y-intervals; every present pair must be separated along at least one axis.
assumptions_latex: Coordinates, widths, and heights are bounded integers.
Rectangles are axis-aligned and use half-open axis intervals.
Both axis intervals of an optional rectangle share its presence indicator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every pair of present rectangles has disjoint interiors along at least one coordinate axis.

notation.meaning: x- and y-axis intervals of rectangle i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Standard axis-separation representation for rectangle non-overlap.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the topic and the axis-separation disjunction is standard for positive-size rectangles. Solver-version-specific evidence is needed for shared optional presence and for zero-width or zero-height rectangles, whose treatment can differ from the stated pairwise disjunction.

children.title: Unsupported Model Constructs
children.top_down_role: Model features outside the accepted solver interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Model Constructs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compilation boundary for mathematically meaningful constructs outside the accepted CP-SAT model language.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be the set of submitted model objects and let \(\mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal M\) be the domain accepted by the solver's validator and encoder. A construct is unsupported when it is syntactically identifiable but has no defined encoding in the applicable solver version, so the containing model lies in \(\mathcal M\setminus\mathcal E\). Validation must then reject the model before search rather than silently discard the construct or substitute a different feasible set. Unsupportedness is distinct from infeasibility: a supported model may encode an empty feasible set and still be structurally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unsupported construct has no defined solver encoding and causes pre-search rejection; this differs from a valid model whose constraints are infeasible.
assumptions_latex: The accepted model language and encoder are fixed for a particular solver version.
Validation precedes search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A model containing an unsupported construct is rejected as outside \(\mathcal E\), not classified as infeasible.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate and the unsupportedness-versus-infeasibility distinction is useful, but the accepted language and the claim of mandatory pre-search rejection are solver-version-specific and unsupported by any cited validator or encoder documentation.

children.title: Malformed Model Structures
children.top_down_role: Invalid references, inconsistent fields, plus structurally defective input.

knowledge_statements.title: Malformed Model Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural validity boundary for model objects that violate representation invariants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A model structure is malformed when it fails a required representation invariant before mathematical feasibility is considered. Such failures include an out-of-range variable or literal reference, an invalid domain encoding, mismatched parallel arrays, an interval referring to missing components, or an arithmetic encoding outside the permitted integer range. If \(V(M)\) denotes the conjunction of all structural validation predicates, malformedness is \[\neg V(M).\] A malformed model has no well-defined encoded feasible set and must be rejected before presolve or search. By contrast, \(V(M)\) may hold even when the encoded feasible set is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A malformed model violates structural invariants such as valid references, domains, arities, or integer ranges and is rejected independently of feasibility.
assumptions_latex: A fixed schema and structural validator define \(V\).
Validation predicates are evaluated before optimization search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\neg V(M)\) causes structural rejection and is not an infeasibility certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the listed malformed structures, integer-range rules, and assertion that all such models are rejected before presolve or search require authoritative schema, validator, and solver-version references with specific locators.

children.title: Validation Rejection Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary between accepted, repairable, plus rejected model input.

knowledge_statements.title: Validation Rejection Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract boundary between accepted and rejected finite-domain CP-SAT model representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a serialized finite-domain model and let \(V(M)\) be the conjunction of the solver's structural validity predicates: every referenced variable exists, every domain is finite and nonempty, every constraint has an admitted arity and type, and every stored integer expression is representable without overflow. The validation rejection boundary is \[\mathcal R=\{M: \neg V(M)\}.\] Validation must reject every \(M\in\mathcal R\) before presolve or encoding. Conversely, validation acceptance asserts only \(V(M)\); it does not assert feasibility, boundedness, or satisfiability of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model crosses the rejection boundary when any required structural validity predicate fails; acceptance certifies well-formedness, not feasibility or satisfiability.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) uses finite-domain variables and finite serialized data.
The implementation publishes fixed admissibility and integer-range rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is rejected at validation}\iff M\in\mathcal R\).
review_flags: implementation-specific validation predicates require an authoritative CP-SAT specification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the asserted validation predicates and rejection stage are implementation-specific and require an authoritative CP-SAT specification with a precise locator.

children.title: Encoding Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion in generated variables, literals, constraints, plus clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Encoding Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size growth of a direct Boolean encoding of finite-domain variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For variables \(x_i\in D_i\) with \(q_i=|D_i|\), introduce literals \(b_{i,v}\leftrightarrow(x_i=v)\) for every \(v\in D_i\). The direct encoding introduces exactly \(B=\sum_i q_i\) Boolean literals. An at-least-one clause plus pairwise at-most-one clauses uses \(n+\sum_i\binom{q_i}{2}\) clauses, hence quadratic growth in the largest domain. Replacing pairwise at-most-one constraints by a linear-size auxiliary cardinality encoding yields \(O(B)\) clauses and auxiliary literals. These counts exclude clauses generated from the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct value encoding uses one literal per domain value; pairwise exactly-one constraints grow quadratically, while auxiliary cardinality encodings can remain linear.
assumptions_latex: Every \(D_i\) is finite.
Encoding size counts Boolean literals and clauses before solver simplification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=\sum_i q_i\), with pairwise clause count \(n+\sum_i\binom{q_i}{2}\).

source_refs.locator: 1.3.1 Problems, Instances, Encoding Size p. 17

review_flags: exact Boolean clause counts need source confirmation

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3.1 Problems, Instances, Encoding Size p. 17

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind and counts are mathematically plausible, but the cited general encoding-size section does not establish the direct Boolean encoding, exact clause count, or linear auxiliary cardinality claim.

children.title: Weak Channeling
children.top_down_role: Loose communication between linked representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Channeling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical weakness caused by encoding only one direction of an intended equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\{0,1,2\}\) and let \(b\) be intended to represent \(x=1\). Full channeling is \(b\leftrightarrow(x=1)\). The one-way constraint \(b\Rightarrow(x=1)\) is weak channeling: it admits \((x,b)=(1,0)\), which violates the intended equivalence. Dually, \((x=1)\Rightarrow b\) admits \((0,1)\) and \((2,1)\). Thus either single implication strictly enlarges the encoded solution set, and deductions available through the omitted implication cannot propagate between \(x\) and \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One implication does not encode an intended equivalence: it admits assignments excluded by full channeling and loses propagation in the omitted direction.
assumptions_latex: \(b\in\{0,1\}\) is interpreted as a Boolean proposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(b\leftrightarrow(x=1))\subsetneq\operatorname{Sol}(b\Rightarrow(x=1))\) and similarly for the reverse implication alone.

notation.meaning: Boolean indicator intended for the equality \(x=1\)

review_flags: standard logical counterexample but no supplied locator supports channeling completeness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon and counterexamples are precise, but no cited source supports the channeling terminology or propagation claim.

children.title: Growth–Strength Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Interaction between encoding size plus propagation strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Growth–Strength Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of equivalent encodings by size and propagation strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) encode the same constraint over original variables \(X\), so their solution projections onto \(X\) coincide. Write \(E_1\succeq_p E_2\) when, after every common domain restriction on \(X\), propagation in \(E_1\) removes every original-variable value removed by propagation in \(E_2\). Encoding size and propagation strength are distinct criteria: adding sound channeling constraints preserves the projected solution set and cannot weaken propagation, but increases or preserves representation size. Consequently, selecting an encoding requires comparing both its generated size and its propagation dominance, rather than either measure alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent encodings may differ in size and propagation; adding sound channeling can strengthen deductions while increasing the generated representation.
assumptions_latex: Both encodings are sound and complete after projection onto the original variables.
The same propagation procedure and initial domains are used for comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_1\succeq_p E_2\) does not imply that \(E_1\) has smaller encoding size.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Comparing the Strength of Different Formulations p. 70

review_flags: locator concerns formulation strength generally rather than CP-SAT propagation specifically

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 Comparing the Strength of Different Formulations p. 70

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits, but formulation strength is not the same as CP-SAT propagation dominance. The claim that adding sound channeling preserves projection also requires the stronger condition that the added constraints are projection-redundant.

children.title: Inexact Scaling Failures
children.top_down_role: Loss of intended numeric meaning during integral scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Scaling Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of feasible-set equivalence when rational data cannot be scaled exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) over an integer domain \(D\). For scale \(S>0\), an exact integerization requires \(Sa_i\in\mathbb Z\) and \(S\beta\in\mathbb Z\), producing \((Sa)^{\mathsf T}x\leq S\beta\). If any scaled datum is nonintegral and is replaced by an integer approximation, equivalence is no longer automatic. Scaling fails semantically precisely when there exists \(x\in D\) satisfying exactly one of the original and approximated inequalities. Large exact scales also fail operationally when a scaled coefficient or attainable activity exceeds the solver's supported integer range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling fails when approximation changes feasibility, or when an exact common scale makes coefficients or activities exceed the solver’s integer range.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) is finite.
The target representation accepts only bounded-range integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x\in D\) with differing inequality truth values is a certificate of semantic scaling failure.
review_flags: no supplied source specifies CP-SAT scaling and overflow boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantic distinction is coherent and the failure-boundary kind fits, but CP-SAT integerization and supported activity-range behavior need an authoritative implementation-specific source.

children.title: Rounding Failures
children.top_down_role: Feasibility or objective distortion caused by rounding choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete feasibility error caused by rounding scaled coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\{0,1,2,3\}\) and consider \(0.4x\leq1\), whose feasible values are \(\{0,1,2\}\). With scale \(S=1\) and nearest-integer rounding applied independently to the coefficient and right-hand side, the encoded constraint becomes \(0x\leq1\). Its feasible set is \(\{0,1,2,3\}\), so \(x=3\) is a false feasible assignment. Hence coefficientwise rounding without a certified error margin need not preserve the feasible set, even for one bounded nonnegative integer variable and one linear inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding 0.4 to zero turns a restrictive integer inequality into a tautology and admits the invalid assignment x = 3.
assumptions_latex: Nearest-integer rounding resolves \(0.4\) to \(0\).
review_flags: self-contained counterexample lacks an external source locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is correct and its content kind fits exactly, but the record supplies no external source locator as required by the evidence contract.

children.title: Scaling–Rounding Interaction
children.top_down_role: Compound error regimes arising across scaling plus rounding.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling–Rounding Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A margin condition guaranteeing truth-value preservation after scaled rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\), define \(\widehat a_i=S^{-1}\operatorname{round}(Sa_i)\) and \(\widehat\beta=S^{-1}\operatorname{round}(S\beta)\). Nearest rounding gives \(|\widehat a_i-a_i|\leq(2S)^{-1}\) and \(|\widehat\beta-\beta|\leq(2S)^{-1}\). Therefore, for any fixed \(x\), \[| (\widehat a^{\mathsf T}x-\widehat\beta)-(a^{\mathsf T}x-\beta)|\leq \frac{\|x\|_1+1}{2S}.\] If \(|a^{\mathsf T}x-\beta|>(\|x\|_1+1)/(2S)\), the original and rounded inequalities have the same truth value at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A larger scale reduces rounding error; an assignment’s feasibility is preserved whenever its slack or violation exceeds the derived error bound.
assumptions_latex: Rounding is to a nearest integer.
All arithmetic used to form the scaled integers remains within range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|a^{\mathsf T}x-\beta|>(\|x\|_1+1)/(2S)\) guarantees preservation at \(x\).
review_flags: elementary derived bound lacks a supplied authoritative locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated nearest-rounding error bound and strict margin condition are mathematically consistent, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Expression Normalization
children.top_down_role: Canonical forms for linear expressions plus constraint-side expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical normalization of finite affine integer expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite affine expression \(e=c+\sum_{j=1}^m a_jx_{i_j}\) with integer coefficients. Initialize a coefficient map \(A_i=0\); for each term, update \(A_{i_j}\leftarrow A_{i_j}+a_j\). Remove every entry with \(A_i=0\), order remaining variables by a fixed global identifier order, and output \[N(e)=c+\sum_{i:A_i\neq0}A_ix_i.\] The procedure terminates after one aggregation and sorting pass, preserves the value of \(e\) under every assignment, and is idempotent: \(N(N(e))=N(e)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalization aggregates duplicate variables, deletes zero coefficients, and sorts terms canonically while preserving every expression value.
assumptions_latex: Coefficient additions are exact and remain within the supported integer range.
Variables have stable global identifiers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N(e)(x)=e(x)\) for every assignment \(x\), and \(N(N(e))=N(e)\).

source_refs.locator: 3.5.5 Special purpose generators using a high level language p. 41

review_flags: exact canonicalization algorithm may not be stated at the supplied locator

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5.5 Special purpose generators using a high level language p. 41

children.title: Objective Normalization
children.top_down_role: Canonical objective representation, offsets, scaling, plus direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical minimization form for an affine integer objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an affine integer objective \(c+\sum_i a_ix_i\) and sense \(s\in\{\min,\max\}\). First apply expression normalization. Set \(\sigma=1\) for minimization and \(\sigma=-1\) for maximization, and solve \[\min_x\; \sigma\sum_i a_ix_i.\] Store the offset \(c\), sign \(\sigma\), and, optionally, the positive greatest common divisor \(g\) of the nonzero coefficients. Division by \(g\) preserves the optimizer set. A normalized solver value \(z\) reconstructs the original objective value as \(c+\sigma gz\) when gcd division is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert maximization to minimization, isolate the constant offset, and optionally divide integer coefficients by their gcd while retaining a value-reconstruction map.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is unchanged by objective normalization.
All objective coefficients and the offset are exact integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized and original objectives have the same optimizer set, with value reconstruction \(c+\sigma gz\).

source_refs.locator: 3.5.8.4 OBJECTIVE p. 43
10.6 The Interplay of Normalization and the Objective Function p. 136

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5.8.4 OBJECTIVE p. 43

children.title: Cross-Context Canonicalization
children.top_down_role: Shared normalization conventions across constraints plus objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Context Canonicalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistent canonical forms across constraints, objectives, and reified expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\) normalize affine expressions by exact coefficient aggregation and fixed term ordering. Cross-context canonicalization applies the same \(N\) whenever an expression occurs in a constraint, objective, enforcement condition, or auxiliary definition. It must satisfy semantic preservation \(N(e)(x)=e(x)\), idempotence \(N(N(e))=N(e)\), and context independence: identical expressions receive identical canonical representations regardless of their enclosing model construct. Consequently, structural equality of normalized expressions is a sound test for their algebraic equality under the supported affine rewrite rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same idempotent normalization must be used in every model context so algebraically identical affine expressions obtain identical representations.
assumptions_latex: All contexts use the same variable identifiers and exact coefficient arithmetic.
Equality is considered modulo aggregation, zero deletion, and term ordering only.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_1\equiv e_2\) under the supported rewrites implies \(N(e_1)=N(e_2)\) in every context.
review_flags: implementation-level cross-context invariant lacks an authoritative supplied locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits, but uniform canonicalization across constraints, objectives, enforcement conditions, and auxiliary definitions is an implementation-level invariant without a supplied source.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Level Constraint Expansion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics-preserving compilation by introducing auxiliary variables and primitive constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a high-level constraint \(H(X)\). Choose fresh auxiliary variables \(Y\), finite domains for \(Y\), and primitive constraints \(P_1(X,Y),\ldots,P_k(X,Y)\) satisfying \[H(X)\iff \exists Y\;\bigwedge_{j=1}^k P_j(X,Y).\] Add \(Y\) and all \(P_j\) to the compiled model, replace \(H\), and record the projection map that discards \(Y\). Expansion is correct when every solution of \(H\) extends to a compiled solution and every compiled solution projects to a solution of \(H\). Stop when every remaining constraint belongs to the solver's primitive vocabulary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace each high-level constraint by primitive constraints and fresh auxiliaries whose existential projection is exactly the original constraint.
assumptions_latex: Auxiliary variables are fresh and have finite declared domains.
Each expansion template establishes the displayed existential equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(H)=\operatorname{proj}_X\operatorname{Sol}(P_1\land\cdots\land P_k)\).

notation.meaning: original variables of the high-level constraint

source_refs.locator: 3.5.5 Special purpose generators using a high level language p. 41

review_flags: locator may support generation generally rather than existential expansion correctness

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5.5 Special purpose generators using a high level language p. 41
