knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Encoding Expansion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-size Tseitin expansion of a Boolean formula into clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a Boolean formula \(F\) represented as a syntax DAG. Process nodes bottom-up and assign a fresh literal \(p_G\) to each nonliteral subformula \(G\). For \(G=A\land B\), add \((
eg p_G\lor p_A)\), \((
eg p_G\lor p_B)\), and \((p_G\lor
eg p_A\lor
eg p_B)\); use the dual three clauses for \(G=A\lor B\), and two clauses for negation equivalence. Finally add the unit clause \((p_F)\). The resulting CNF is satisfiable exactly when \(F\) is satisfiable, and its variables and clauses are linear in the DAG size of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tseitin expansion introduces one literal per Boolean subformula and local equivalence clauses, producing an equisatisfiable CNF of linear size.
assumptions_latex: Shared subformulas are represented once in the syntax DAG.
Fresh literals do not occur in the original formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is satisfiable}\iff T(F)\text{ is satisfiable}\), with \(|T(F)|=O(|F|)\).
review_flags: no supplied source locator specifically supports Tseitin encoding and its linear-size bound

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, and the Tseitin clauses and linear-size claim are standard and internally consistent, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Fixed-Variable Reductions
children.top_down_role: Elimination opportunities created by singleton domains.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is defined over finitely many integer variables with explicitly represented finite domains.
Presolve transformations must preserve feasibility and support reconstruction of an original solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced model obtained by replacing every occurrence of the fixed variable and deleting its domain declaration is equisatisfiable with the original model; reconstruction sets \(x:=c\).

notation.meaning: The singleton value remaining in the domain of x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singleton-domain elimination with explicit postsolve reconstruction.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The Gaussian elimination method p. 31
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be an integer variable whose current domain is the singleton \(D_x=\{c\}\). For every constraint \(C(x,y)\), replace it by \(C(c,y)\), simplify the resulting expression, and report infeasibility if any simplified constraint is false. Delete constraints that simplify to true and remove \(x\) from the active model. Record the reconstruction rule \(x:=c\). The projection of the original feasible set onto the remaining variables equals the feasible set of the reduced model, and every reduced feasible assignment extends uniquely by \(x=c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace a singleton-domain variable by its fixed value, simplify affected constraints, and record the value for reconstruction; this preserves feasibility exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Variable Reductions

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 The Gaussian elimination method p. 31
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and projection claim are mathematically sound and fit the leaf, but the cited Gaussian-elimination section does not specifically support singleton-domain elimination or CP-SAT postsolve reconstruction. A presolve or solver-specific source is required.

children.title: Substitution Reductions
children.top_down_role: Variable replacement opportunities exposed by model relations.

assumptions_latex: The defining equality is valid for every feasible assignment.
Substitution preserves the declared domains and integrality of all remaining expressions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating \(x\) by its defining expression preserves the projection of the feasible set, and \(x\) is recovered uniquely from the stored equality.

notation.meaning: An integer-valued defining expression on feasible assignments.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination using a globally valid defining equality.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The Gaussian elimination method p. 31
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the model contains an equality \(x=g(y)\) that defines \(x\) uniquely in terms of the remaining variables \(y\). Replace every other occurrence of \(x\) by \(g(y)\), simplify the affected constraints and objective, and remove both \(x\) and its defining equality. Any domain restriction \(x\in D_x\) becomes the constraint \(g(y)\in D_x\). Store \(x:=g(y)\) for postsolve. The reduced feasible set is exactly the projection of the original feasible set onto \(y\), and each reduced solution reconstructs one original solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a defining equality to eliminate a variable, transfer its domain restriction, and store the equality for exact solution reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.title: Substitution Reductions

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 The Gaussian elimination method p. 31
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

children.title: Affine Reductions
children.top_down_role: Reduction opportunities based on affine variable relations.

assumptions_latex: The affine relation holds for every feasible assignment.
All transformed expressions remain representable without arithmetic overflow.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(x\) through the affine relation and retaining the induced divisibility and domain conditions yields an equisatisfiable reduced integer model.

notation.meaning: Integer coefficients with nonzero coefficient of x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer affine elimination, including divisibility and induced-domain conditions.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The Gaussian elimination method p. 31
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let integer variables \(x,y\) satisfy \(a x+b y=c\) with \(a\ne0\). Eliminating \(x\) replaces it by \((c-b y)/a\), but the reduced model must also enforce \(a\mid(c-b y)\) and \((c-b y)/a\in D_x\). Substitute this affine expression into every affected constraint and objective term, simplify, and store \(x=(c-b y)/a\) for reconstruction. If the induced congruence or domain condition is impossible, declare infeasibility. Otherwise the reduced feasible assignments in the retained variables are precisely the projections of original feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate an integer variable through an affine equality while preserving the induced congruence, domain restriction, and reconstruction formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Reductions

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 The Gaussian elimination method p. 31
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The integer-affine reduction is mathematically plausible and correctly retains divisibility and domain conditions, but the cited Gaussian-elimination locator does not clearly support the integer congruence treatment or solver representability requirements. A specific integer-presolve source is needed.

children.title: Redundancy Elimination
children.top_down_role: Removal of constraints or literals already implied elsewhere.

assumptions_latex: The candidate constraint and the retained model are interpreted over the same variable domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deleting \(C\) is valid exactly when every assignment satisfying \(M\) also satisfies \(C\); hence the feasible set remains unchanged.

notation.meaning: The conjunction of retained constraints and domain restrictions.
The feasible assignments of a formula.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic criterion for deleting an implied constraint during presolve.

source_refs.locator: 7.6 Affine form of Farkas' lemma p. 93
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a retained model \(M\) and a candidate constraint \(C\), the constraint is redundant relative to \(M\) when \(M\models C\), equivalently when \(M\land\neg C\) is infeasible. In feasible-set notation this is \(\operatorname{Sol}(M)=\operatorname{Sol}(M\land C)\). A sound presolver may delete \(C\) after establishing this implication by an appropriate certificate, such as subsumption, bound reasoning, or a valid linear implication. The deletion changes neither feasibility nor the values attainable by any objective defined on the retained variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint may be deleted when the remaining model implies it, equivalently when adding its negation makes the model infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy Elimination

source_witnesses.locator: 7.6 Affine form of Farkas' lemma p. 93
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

children.title: Dominance Reductions
children.top_down_role: Model simplifications supported by dominance relations.

assumptions_latex: Both alternatives use the same variable domains and objective convention.
The replacement relation is established for all assignments admitted by the retained model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A dominated alternative can be removed because every solution using it has a no-worse feasible counterpart using the dominating alternative.

notation.meaning: Replacement of assignment s using q by one using p.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution-replacement criterion for optimization-preserving dominance elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization model, alternative \(q\) is dominated by alternative \(p\) if there exists a replacement map \(T\) such that, for every feasible assignment \(s\) selecting \(q\), the assignment \(T(s)\) is feasible, selects \(p\), preserves all required external variable values, and satisfies \(f(T(s))\le f(s)\). Under this condition, forbidding \(q\) preserves feasibility whenever \(q\) is used only through the replaceable choice and preserves the optimal objective value. For a satisfaction model, the objective inequality is omitted and feasibility preservation alone is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Remove an alternative when every solution using it can be replaced by a feasible solution using another alternative with no worse objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Reductions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The replacement-map criterion is coherent, but no cited source establishes this particular optimization-preserving dominance rule or the required meaning of an interchangeable alternative in CP-SAT presolve.

children.title: Constraint Merging
children.top_down_role: Consolidation of compatible or overlapping constraint structures.

assumptions_latex: The replacement constraint is interpreted over the same domains as the original constraints.
The equivalence is valid in the context of all retained constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) by \(C\) preserves the feasible set exactly when their conjunction is contextually equivalent to \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact contextual-equivalence criterion for combining constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) denote the constraints retained outside \(C_1\) and \(C_2\). A merge replacing \(C_1\land C_2\) by a single constraint \(C\) is sound when \(M\models\bigl(C\leftrightarrow(C_1\land C_2)\bigr)\). Equivalently, \(\operatorname{Sol}(M\land C)=\operatorname{Sol}(M\land C_1\land C_2)\). The presolver may then delete \(C_1,C_2\), insert \(C\), and retain any metadata needed for reconstruction. If only one implication is known, the operation is merely a relaxation or strengthening and is not an exact presolve merge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two constraints may be merged when their conjunction is equivalent, within the retained model, to the replacement constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Merging

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Contextual equivalence is a sound abstract condition for exact replacement, and the content kind fits. No source, however, supports this as a CP-SAT constraint-merging reduction or identifies the constraint families for which it is implementable.

assumptions_latex: Auxiliary variables introduced by decomposition are existentially quantified.
The linking constraints enforce consistency between every duplicated or auxiliary quantity and the original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A decomposition is presolve-valid when projecting the extended feasible set onto the original variables recovers exactly the original constraint relation.

notation.meaning: Original variables of the decomposed constraint.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-formulation criterion for exact constraint decomposition in presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint \(C(x)\) admits an exact presolve decomposition into \(D_1(x,z),\ldots,D_k(x,z)\) when, for every assignment \(x\) in the original domains, \[C(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists z\;\bigwedge_{i=1}^{k}D_i(x,z).\] The presolver replaces \(C\) by the decomposed constraints and declares domains for \(z\). Consequently, projecting the feasible set of the extended model onto \(x\) yields exactly the original feasible set. Any postsolve procedure may discard \(z\), while a reduced solution must provide or permit construction of a witnessing value of \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace a constraint by linked simpler constraints whose auxiliary-variable projection equals the original relation exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Decomposition in Presolve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The existential-projection criterion is mathematically precise and representation is a suitable content kind, but no cited source supports its use as a CP-SAT presolve decomposition or the witness-construction requirement.

assumptions_latex: Propagation is performed at decision level zero under all permanent constraints.
Each domain update is justified by a sound propagator or infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing every domain by its root-propagated subset preserves all feasible assignments, and an empty tightened domain certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision-level-zero propagation to a sound domain fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize propagation with the permanent model and domains \(D=(D_1,\ldots,D_n)\), with no search decisions. Repeatedly apply sound propagators to obtain \(P(D)\subseteq D\) until a fixpoint \(D^*=P(D^*)\) is reached or some \(D_i^*=\varnothing\). Soundness requires that every feasible assignment \(s\) satisfies \(s_i\in D_i^*\) for every \(i\). Replace the root domains by \(D^*\); if a domain is empty, report the model infeasible. Variables whose domains become singletons may subsequently undergo fixed-variable reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run sound propagation without search decisions until domains stabilize; retain the tightened domains or report infeasibility if one becomes empty.
knowledge_statements.title: Root-Level Domain Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm states a reasonable sound-fixpoint abstraction, but no source supports the CP-SAT root-level propagation semantics, termination assumptions, propagator scheduling, or interpretation of the operator P.

children.title: Literal Probing
children.top_down_role: Temporary literal assignments used for root-level inference.

assumptions_latex: Propagation under temporary assumptions is sound.
All consequences are recorded relative to the permanent root state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A probe of \(\ell\) either proves \(\ell\) impossible or discovers literals and domain bounds logically implied by \(\ell\).

notation.meaning: The Boolean or encoded integer literal being probed.
The propagated closure under the probe.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporary root assumption followed by propagation and rollback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a root formula \(F\) and a candidate literal \(\ell\), temporarily assume \(\ell\), propagate to closure, and record every derived literal and domain bound. If propagation derives contradiction, record \(F\models\neg\ell\). Otherwise, for each derived consequence \(q\), record the valid implication \(F\models(\ell\rightarrow q)\). Roll back the temporary state before probing another literal; only certified consequences are committed at the root. The probe outputs either a conflict under \(\ell\) or a set of conditional implications and bound tightenings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporarily assume a literal, propagate, record contradiction or conditional consequences, then restore the root state.
knowledge_statements.title: Literal Probing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The probing procedure and logical consequences are internally consistent, but no source supports the CP-SAT probe lifecycle, rollback semantics, integer-literal encoding, or certification requirements.

children.title: Failed-Literal Detection
children.top_down_role: Contradictory probe outcomes yielding fixed literal values.

assumptions_latex: The contradiction is derived by sound propagation from the permanent model and the probed literal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A contradiction under \(\ell\) certifies \(F\models\neg\ell\), so fixing \(\ell\) false preserves the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical certificate obtained from an inconsistent probe branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A failed-literal certificate for \(\ell\) is a sound propagation derivation \(F\land\ell\vdash\bot\), where \(F\) is the permanent root formula. Soundness of the propagation rules gives \(F\land\ell\models\bot\), hence \(F\models\neg\ell\). The presolver may therefore fix \(\ell\) to false and propagate that fixing at the root. If both \(F\land\ell\) and \(F\land\neg\ell\) yield contradiction, then \(F\) itself is infeasible. The certificate is locally checkable by replaying its propagation reasons.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If sound propagation reaches contradiction while a literal is assumed, the opposite literal is mandatory; failure of both polarities proves infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Failed-Literal Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failed-literal inference is logically correct, but no source supports the claimed locally replayable certificate representation. Because the terminal title emphasizes detection, a solver source is also needed to determine whether algorithm rather than certificate is the proper knowledge kind.

children.title: Probe Outcome Reuse
children.top_down_role: Retention of bounds, implications, plus equivalences exposed by probes.

assumptions_latex: Cached consequences retain their original root assumptions and valid propagation reasons.
Reuse occurs only in a root state that entails those assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cached consequence may be reused exactly when the current permanent formula entails the cache context; otherwise it must be revalidated.

notation.meaning: The context under which a probe was performed.
A cached consequence of probing literal l.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for caching and replaying probe consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose probing under context \(F_0\) established \(F_0\models(\ell\rightarrow q)\) or \(F_0\models\neg\ell\). The result may be applied without re-probing in a current context \(F_1\) when \(F_1\models F_0\), because strengthening the context preserves both entailments. Each cached outcome must therefore carry a context identifier or reasons sufficient to verify this condition. If model transformations invalidate a reason, weaken the permanent formula, or change literal meaning, the cached outcome must be discarded or revalidated before use.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse a probe result only when the current model entails the context that justified it and all recorded reasons remain valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Probe Outcome Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strengthening-context entailment rule is logically sound for formulas with stable semantics, but no source establishes the cache context, reason invalidation, or literal-identity policy used by CP-SAT presolve.

children.title: Implication Discovery
children.top_down_role: Directed literal consequences exposed during preprocessing.

assumptions_latex: Propagation under the assumed literal is sound.
The discovered consequence is expressed using literals whose meanings remain stable after probing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every consequence \(q\) reached under probe \(\ell\) yields the valid implication \(F\models(\ell\rightarrow q)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction of binary implications from successful propagation probes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each candidate literal \(\ell\), propagate \(F\land\ell\). If a literal \(q\) is derived without contradiction, add the implication \(\ellightarrow q\), equivalently the clause \(
eg\ell\lor q\), provided its propagation reasons are sound under \(F\). If probing \(
eg\ell\) derives \(
eg q\), the two probe outcomes additionally establish \(F\models(\ell\leftrightarrow q)\). Newly stored implications may be closed transitively or used by later propagation, but only logically entailed edges may be committed. The output is a sound extension of the root implication graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probe a literal and convert each propagated literal into a valid binary implication; complementary probe outcomes can reveal equivalence.
knowledge_statements.title: Implication Discovery

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conversion of sound probe consequences into implications is correct, including the stated complementary-probe equivalence inference. A source is still required for CP-SAT implication discovery, storage, and graph-update semantics.

children.title: Equivalence Discovery
children.top_down_role: Interchangeable literals or variables exposed during preprocessing.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence Discovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discovery of equivalent Boolean literals from a finite implication graph during presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be a finite set of Boolean literals, closed under complementation, and let \(G=(L,E)\) contain an arc \((a,b)\) for every established implication \(a\Rightarrow b\). Compute the strongly connected components of \(G\). Declare \(a\equiv b\) exactly when \(a\) and \(b\) belong to the same component. If a component contains both \(a\) and \(\neg a\), return infeasibility. Otherwise choose one representative per complementary pair of components and replace every literal by its representative or its complement. The output is the resulting substitution map together with the reduced implication graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strongly connected literals are equivalent; a component containing a literal and its negation certifies infeasibility. Otherwise each equivalence class is replaced by a representative.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) contains only sound implications of the current Boolean model.
\(L\) is finite and closed under complementation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\equiv b\iff a\leadsto b\text{ and }b\leadsto a\) in \(G\).

notation.meaning: a directed path from literal a to literal b

review_flags: Exact CP-SAT implementation source and locator are missing.
Algorithm stated from standard implication-graph semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the CP-SAT procedure. Pairing SCCs with complementary SCCs additionally requires the implication graph to be closed under contraposition, which is not stated.

children.title: Implication–Equivalence Closure
children.top_down_role: Combined closure structure over discovered logical relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Implication–Equivalence Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint transitive implication closure and equivalence contraction for finite Boolean presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a finite sound implication graph \(G=(L,E)\), compute its reachability relation \(R\), where \((a,b)\in R\) exactly when \(b\) is reachable from \(a\). Form the equivalence relation \(a\sim b\) when both \((a,b)\in R\) and \((b,a)\in R\), and contract its classes. On the quotient vertices, retain the induced strict implications and transitively close them. If \((a,
eg a)\in R\), fix \(a=0\); if both \((a,
eg a)\in R\) and \((
eg a,a)\in R\), return infeasibility. Stop when neither contractions nor new fixings occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reachability adds implied arcs, mutual reachability contracts equivalent literals, and implication to a complement fixes a literal; complementary equivalence proves infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Every initial arc is a logically valid implication.
Literal complementation is defined on all vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quotient closure preserves all assignments satisfying the original implications and exposes every consequence represented by reachability.

notation.meaning: reachability relation of the implication graph

review_flags: Exact solver closure policy requires an architecture source.
Algorithm stated from standard implication-graph semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, and the fixing rules follow implication semantics, but no source establishes that CP-SAT computes this full reachability closure or uses this stopping policy. The assignment-preservation claim also needs a precise correspondence between quotient and original assignments.

children.title: Automorphism Detection
children.top_down_role: Model symmetries represented through structure-preserving permutations.

knowledge_statements.title: Automorphism Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detection of variable-value symmetries through automorphisms of a colored model graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Encode a finite constraint model as a colored graph \(H=(V,E,c)\): variable, value, constraint, coefficient, and enforcement roles receive colors sufficient to distinguish noninterchangeable data. Compute generators of \(\operatorname{Aut}(H,c)=\{\pi\in\operatorname{Sym}(V):c(\pi v)=c(v),\ \{u,v\}\in E\iff\{\pi u,\pi v\}\in E\}\). Retain only generators whose restriction induces a valid permutation of model variables and their domains. Verify each retained permutation by checking that it maps every constraint and the objective to an identical constraint or objective term. Output the verified generators; the identity alone means that no nontrivial symmetry was detected by this encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a role-colored model graph, compute its color-preserving automorphisms, and retain only permutations that preserve domains, constraints, and the objective.
assumptions_latex: The model and its graph encoding are finite.
Colors and incidence data distinguish every semantically noninterchangeable role.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every output generator induces a model automorphism and therefore maps feasible solutions to feasible solutions of equal objective value.

notation.meaning: colored graph encoding the constraint model

review_flags: No supplied source supports the CP-SAT graph encoding or verification procedure.
Encoding details may vary by solver implementation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Automorphism Detection, but the graph encoding, coloring scheme, generator filtering, and verification pass are solver-specific and unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Orbit Structure
children.top_down_role: Variable or literal classes induced by detected symmetries.

knowledge_statements.title: Orbit Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbit partition induced by a detected permutation group on model entities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a permutation group \(\Gamma\) act on a finite set \(X\) of variables, literals, or variable-value pairs. The orbit of \(x\in X\) is \(\operatorname{Orb}_{\Gamma}(x)=\{\gamma(x):\gamma\in\Gamma\}\), and its stabilizer is \(\operatorname{Stab}_{\Gamma}(x)=\{\gamma\in\Gamma:\gamma(x)=x\}\). The family \(X/\Gamma=\{\operatorname{Orb}_{\Gamma}(x):x\in X\}\) is the orbit structure. Its members are pairwise disjoint and cover \(X\). If \(X\) is finite, then \(|\operatorname{Orb}_{\Gamma}(x)|=[\Gamma:\operatorname{Stab}_{\Gamma}(x)]\). Entities in one orbit are interchangeable under detected model symmetries, although their values need not coincide in any particular solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetry orbit contains all entities reachable from one entity under the detected permutation group; these orbits partition the acted-on set.
assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma\) is a group acting on the finite set \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=\bigsqcup_{O\in X/\Gamma}O\) and \(|\operatorname{Orb}_{\Gamma}(x)|=[\Gamma:\operatorname{Stab}_{\Gamma}(x)]\).

notation.meaning: orbit of x under the group action

review_flags: Standard group-action definition, but no relevant source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically standard and correctly distinguishes orbit interchangeability from equal values, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Orbitope Representation
children.top_down_role: Matrix-structured symmetry classes plus associated restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Orbitope Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic representative for binary matrices with interchangeable columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integers \(p,q\geq1\), let \(X\in\{0,1\}^{p\times q}\), and suppose every permutation of its columns preserves feasibility and objective value. A full orbitope representative is obtained by requiring the column vectors to be lexicographically nonincreasing: \[X_{\cdot,1}\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}X_{\cdot,2}\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}X_{\cdot,q}.\] Equivalently, the representative set is the intersection of the original binary-matrix set with one lexicographic fundamental domain of the column-permutation action. Every column-permutation orbit contains at least one such matrix; if all columns are distinct, it contains exactly one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For interchangeable binary-matrix columns, lexicographically sorting the columns selects an orbit representative without removing all representatives of any symmetry class.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a binary \(p\)-by-\(q\) matrix.
The full column-permutation group preserves feasibility and objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every orbit \(\{X\sigma:\sigma\in S_q\}\) meets the lexicographically ordered representative set.

notation.meaning: column j of the binary matrix

review_flags: The record uses the full binary column-permutation orbitope; solver-specific variants may be narrower.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits, and lexicographic column ordering selects a representative under the full column-permutation action. A source is required to support the use of “full orbitope” and to distinguish this representative set from the associated orbitope polytope and solver-specific variants.

children.title: Variable Mapping
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between original variables plus presolved variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composable correspondence from presolved variables to original-variable expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in D\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) be the original variables and \(y\in D'\subseteq\mathbb Z^m\) the presolved variables. A variable postsolve mapping is a function \(P:D'\to D\), stored as a composition \(P=P_1\circ\cdots\circ P_k\) of reconstruction maps associated with presolve transformations, such that every feasible presolved assignment \(y\) yields a feasible original assignment \(x=P(y)\). Eliminated variables are recovered from stored constants, affine relations, Boolean equivalences, or transformation-specific witnesses. For optimization, the mapping must additionally preserve the objective value up to the separately recorded objective transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable mapping composes inverse presolve transformations so every feasible reduced assignment reconstructs a feasible assignment of all original variables.
assumptions_latex: Every presolve transformation records a reconstruction map on its feasible output assignments.
The reconstruction maps are applied in reverse transformation order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\in F'\Longrightarrow P(y)\in F\), where \(F'\) and \(F\) are the presolved and original feasible sets.
review_flags: No supplied source specifies CP-SAT postsolve mapping invariants.
Permitted reconstruction-map forms are implementation dependent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits, but no source establishes CP-SAT's reconstruction-map invariant or the listed forms used to recover eliminated variables.

children.title: Constraint Mapping
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between original constraints plus transformed structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trace relation connecting original constraints with their presolved images and certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=(C_1,\ldots,C_r)\) be the original constraints and \(C'=(C'_1,\ldots,C'_s)\) the presolved constraints. A constraint mapping is a relation \(M_C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}\times\{1,\ldots,s\}\), augmented by transformation records for deleted constraints, such that satisfaction of \(C'\), followed by variable reconstruction, implies satisfaction of every \(C_i\). A surviving or rewritten constraint is linked to each original constraint it represents; a deleted constraint is marked redundant, absorbed, fixed, or infeasible with the corresponding presolve witness. The relation need not be one-to-one because transformations may merge, split, or derive constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint mapping records which reduced constraints represent each original constraint and why deleted constraints remain satisfied or establish infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Each constraint transformation is logically sound.
Deleted constraints carry an appropriate redundancy, fixing, absorption, or infeasibility witness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\models C'\Longrightarrow P(y)\models C\) for the associated variable reconstruction map \(P\).
review_flags: No supplied source defines a CP-SAT constraint-trace representation.
Some solvers preserve transformation logs rather than an explicit relation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits, but the explicit original-to-presolved constraint relation and the proposed witness categories are implementation-specific and unsupported. Some presolve systems guarantee reconstruction without maintaining this relation.

children.title: Objective Mapping
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between original objective terms plus presolved objective terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine correspondence between original and presolved objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original minimization objective be \(f(x)\) and the presolved objective be \(g(y)\). An objective mapping consists of a reconstruction map \(P\), a nonzero scale \(\alpha>0\), and an offset \(\beta\) satisfying \[f(P(y))=\alpha g(y)+\beta\] for every feasible presolved assignment \(y\). Consequently, minimizers of \(g\) reconstruct to minimizers of \(f\), and a presolved bound \(g(y)\geq L\) maps to the original bound \(f(x)\geq\alpha L+\beta\). For maximization, the same representation is used after adopting a consistent objective-sense convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The original objective equals a positive affine transformation of the reduced objective after reconstruction, preserving minimizers and translating bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) maps every feasible presolved assignment to a feasible original assignment.
\(\alpha>0\) and the displayed equality holds on the presolved feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{y}g(y)\) reconstructs into \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}f(x)\), with values related by \(f=\alpha g+\beta\).
review_flags: The supplied objective-modeling locator does not establish CP-SAT postsolve semantics.
Solver conventions for scaling, integrality, and objective sense require confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits, but the stated assumptions do not imply that a minimizer of the reduced problem reconstructs to a global minimizer of the original problem; an optimality-equivalence or suitable coverage condition is needed. The bound translation is likewise justified only for reconstructed solutions unless a stronger correspondence is established. Solver scaling conventions also lack a source.

children.title: Solution Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original-model assignments from presolved solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse replay of presolve records to recover an original feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a feasible presolved assignment \(y^{(k)}\) and transformation records \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\), where presolve applied \(T_i\) from stage \(i-1\) to stage \(i\). For \(i=k,k-1,\ldots,1\), apply the stored reconstruction operator \(P_i\) to obtain \(y^{(i-1)}=P_i(y^{(i)})\), recovering eliminated variables and undoing substitutions, aggregations, and canonicalizations. At each stage require \(y^{(i-1)}\) to satisfy the stage-\(i-1\) domains and constraints. Output \(x=y^{(0)}\); if any operator has no valid extension, report a postsolve inconsistency rather than an original-model solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replay reconstruction operators in reverse presolve order, extending the reduced solution until all original variables and constraints are restored.
assumptions_latex: The presolved assignment satisfies the terminal presolved model.
Each stored operator reconstructs a feasible predecessor from every feasible successor in its domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs \(x\in F\) with the objective value prescribed by the objective mapping, or reports a reconstruction inconsistency.

notation.meaning: reconstruction operator for the i-th transformation

review_flags: No supplied source documents CP-SAT reverse-replay postsolve.
Stage-validation behavior is an abstract correctness specification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Solution Reconstruction, but no source supports reverse replay as the CP-SAT postsolve mechanism or stage-by-stage validation as actual solver behavior.

children.title: Hint Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Translation of partial assignments across presolve mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Hint Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward transport of a partial original assignment into the presolved model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a partial original hint \(h^{(0)}:I_0\to\mathbb Z\) and presolve transformations \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\). For \(i=1,\ldots,k\), transport every assigned value whose image is determined by \(T_i\), producing a partial hint \(h^{(i)}\) on stage-\(i\) variables. Remove assignments to eliminated variables after using them to infer surviving values; merge duplicate images only when their values agree. If mapped assignments conflict with each other or with a reduced domain, flag inconsistency. Output the consistent terminal partial hint \(h^{(k)}\); variables not determined by the original hint remain unassigned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transport a partial original hint through presolve, retaining determined surviving values and flagging conflicts without inventing values for undetermined variables.
assumptions_latex: The original hint assigns only values in the declared original domains.
Each transformation supplies a sound forward rule for hinted values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every assignment retained in \(h^{(k)}\) is implied by \(h^{(0)}\) and the recorded transformations.

notation.meaning: partial hint at presolve stage i
set of originally hinted variable indices

review_flags: No supplied source establishes the solver's hint-remapping policy.
Whether inconsistent hint entries are dropped, repaired, or rejected is implementation specific.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but hint transport, inference, conflict detection, and the treatment of eliminated assignments are solver policies requiring an implementation source. The current statement cannot determine whether conflicts are rejected, repaired, or discarded.

children.title: Hint Consistency Boundary
children.top_down_role: Compatibility limits for hints affected by eliminated or transformed entities.

knowledge_statements.title: Hint Consistency Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between soundly transportable hints and conflicting partial assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) be a partial original assignment and let presolve establish a relation \(x_i=\phi_i(y)\) for each hinted eliminated variable whose value can be transported. The hint is transport-consistent exactly when there exists a presolved assignment \(y\) within the reduced variable domains such that \(\phi_i(y)=h(x_i)\) for every transported hint entry. If no such \(y\) exists, preserving all hint entries is impossible: for example, hints \(h(x_1)=0\) and \(h(x_2)=1\) conflict after presolve proves \(x_1=x_2\). This inconsistency concerns the hint and does not by itself certify infeasibility of the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hint crosses the consistency boundary when its mapped entries have no common reduced-domain extension; this invalidates the hint, not necessarily the model.
assumptions_latex: Presolve relations used for transport are logical consequences of the model.
A hint is advisory and is not itself a model constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists y\ \forall x_i\in\operatorname{dom}(h):\phi_i(y)=h(x_i)\) implies that all hint entries cannot be preserved simultaneously.

notation.meaning: partial assignment supplied as a solution hint
recorded expression reconstructing hinted variable i

review_flags: The logical boundary is standard, but CP-SAT's handling of inconsistent hints needs an implementation source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits and correctly notes that an inconsistent advisory hint does not prove model infeasibility. However, the existential test alternates between reduced-domain consistency and model-feasible consistency, and it quantifies over hint entries for which a transport expression may not exist. A source is needed to fix the intended CP-SAT boundary.

children.title: Assumption Mapping
children.top_down_role: Translation of original assumption literals into presolved references.

knowledge_statements.title: Assumption Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Traceable transport of user assumptions through presolve transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_r\}\) be designated original assumption literals and let \(A'\) be their presolved representatives. An assumption mapping assigns to each \(a_i\) either a representative literal \(\mu(a_i)\in A'\), a fixed truth value, or a transformation record expressing \(a_i\) through presolved literals. It must satisfy, for every feasible presolved assignment \(y\), that evaluating the recorded image under \(y\) equals the value of \(a_i\) under reconstruction. Multiple original assumptions may share one representative. The reverse incidence relation is retained so any reduced assumption or core literal can be traced to all contributing original assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each original assumption is mapped to a reduced representative, fixed value, or recorded expression, with reverse links retained for core traceability.
assumptions_latex: Assumption literals and all substitutions affecting them are explicitly recorded.
The variable reconstruction map is sound on feasible presolved assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(a_i\in A\) and feasible \(y\), \(a_i(P(y))=\mu(a_i)(y)\), with fixed images interpreted as constants.
review_flags: No supplied source documents CP-SAT assumption preservation through presolve.
Core expansion from shared representatives requires a separate traceability specification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits, but no source establishes that CP-SAT preserves assumptions through the stated representative-expression mapping or maintains the proposed reverse incidence relation. The claim that reduced core literals can be expanded to all contributing original assumptions requires a separate, precise core-validity specification.

children.title: Unsatisfiable Core Mapping
children.top_down_role: Translation of presolved conflict cores into original assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsatisfiable Core Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maps a reduced-model assumption core back to original assumptions while preserving unsatisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be the original constraint system with assumption literals \(A\), and let presolve produce \(F'\), assumptions \(A'\), and a trace map \(\tau:A'\to 2^A\). For every reduced unsatisfiable core \(C'\subseteq A'\) satisfying \(F'\land\bigwedge_{a'\in C'}a'\) unsatisfiable, define \(C=\bigcup_{a'\in C'}\tau(a')\). A sound core mapping satisfies
\[
F\land\bigwedge_{a\in C}a\quad\text{is unsatisfiable}.
\]
The mapped set need not be minimal, even when \(C'\) is inclusion-minimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced unsatisfiable core maps to original assumptions whose simultaneous activation remains unsatisfiable; the mapped core need not be minimal.
assumptions_latex: \(F'\) is satisfiability-equivalent to \(F\) under the recorded presolve trace.
Each \(\tau(a')\) contains only original assumption literals sufficient to justify \(a'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F'\land\bigwedge_{a'\in C'}a'\) unsatisfiable implies \(F\land\bigwedge_{a\in\cup_{a'\in C'}\tau(a')}a\) unsatisfiable.

notation.meaning: Trace map from reduced assumptions to supporting original assumptions.

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses CP-SAT assumption-core reconstruction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but soundness depends on the precise presolve trace invariant and direction of justification. No cited source or locator establishes that invariant for CP-SAT assumption-core reconstruction.

children.title: Core Traceability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on preserving assumption identity through model transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Core Traceability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies when presolve traces cannot support a sound or precise original-model core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C'\subseteq A'\) be an unsatisfiable core of a presolved system and let \(\tau:A'\rightharpoonup 2^A\) be its recorded assumption trace. Traceability is guaranteed only if \(\tau\) is defined for every member of \(C'\) and every presolve inference used by those members has a sound dependency record. If either condition fails, no core obtained solely by taking unions of recorded antecedents is guaranteed to certify unsatisfiability of the original system. Even with complete sound traces, inclusion-minimality and minimum cardinality generally do not transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Missing or unsound presolve dependencies prevent guaranteed core reconstruction; complete traces preserve soundness but generally not minimality.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(A'\) are the original and presolved assumption sets.
Core reconstruction may use only the recorded trace \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An undefined or unsound dependency on \(C'\) destroys the general guarantee that the reconstructed original assumptions form an unsatisfiable core.

notation.meaning: Unsatisfiable core in the presolved model.
Partial trace from reduced assumptions to original assumptions.

review_flags: No relevant architecture source was supplied.
Boundary depends on the solver's recorded transformation semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but the claimed reconstruction guarantee and loss of minimality depend on architecture-specific transformation records. No supporting citation or inspectable locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Expansion Blowup
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes exponential growth when presolve materializes combinations of locally compact constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge 1\), consider \(n\) independent binary disjunctions \((p_i\lor q_i)\). A presolve procedure that explicitly distributes their conjunction into complete alternatives produces one alternative for every vector in \(\{p_i,q_i\}_{i=1}^n\), hence \(2^n\) alternatives. Thus a representation of size \(O(n)\) can be expanded to size \(\Omega(2^n)\). Any presolve rule that materializes an unrestricted Cartesian product of alternatives has no polynomial output-size bound in the original encoding length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Materializing all combinations of independent disjunctions can turn a linear-size input into an exponentially large presolved representation.
assumptions_latex: The presolver explicitly enumerates the Cartesian product of independent alternatives.
Equivalent alternatives are not merged by additional structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The presolved representation may contain \(2^n\) alternatives despite an \(O(n)\)-size input.

notation.meaning: The two alternatives in disjunction number \(i\).

review_flags: Concrete combinatorial claim is standard, but no supplied source covers CP presolve expansion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exponential Cartesian-product calculation is mathematically plausible and the failure-boundary kind fits, but no source connects this materialization mechanism to presolve or supports the stated general output-size boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction-Mapping Inconsistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the correctness failure caused by disagreement between presolve reductions and reconstruction maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) and \(S'\) denote the solution sets of an original and reduced model, and let \(\rho:S'\to S\) be the postsolve reconstruction map. A reduction-mapping inconsistency occurs if either some \(y\in S'\) has \(\rho(y)\notin S\), or some \(x\in S\) has no \(y\in S'\) with \(\rho(y)=x\) when complete solution preservation is required. The first case permits an invalid reconstructed solution; the second loses an original solution and may invalidate completeness or optimality claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reconstruction map is inconsistent when it produces an infeasible original solution or, where completeness is required, fails to represent an original solution.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(S'\) are defined under the same feasibility and objective conventions.
Postsolve reports original solutions exclusively through \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either inconsistency prevents the reduction and reconstruction pair from establishing the required correspondence between \(S'\) and \(S\).
review_flags: No supplied locator supports presolve-postsolve correspondence.
Whether surjectivity is required depends on the solver's preservation contract.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary formulation distinguishes reconstruction soundness from conditional completeness appropriately, but the required correspondence depends on the solver's feasibility and optimality preservation contract, for which no source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve–Propagation Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes how eliminating structure can reduce model size while weakening propagation after domains are mapped between the original and presolved variable spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a model on variables \(V\), let \(P(M)\) be a satisfiability-equivalent presolved model on variables \(V'\), and let \(\operatorname{cl}_Q(N,D)\) denote the domain state obtained by running a fixed propagation regime \(Q\) to a fixpoint on model \(N\) from domain state \(D\). Let \(\nu\) map an original domain state to the corresponding initial domain state on \(V'\), and let \(\mu\) map a presolved domain state back to domains on \(V\). Satisfiability equivalence alone does not imply propagation equivalence: for some original domain state \(D\), it is possible that
\[
\operatorname{cl}_Q(M,D)_x\subseteq\bigl[\mu(\operatorname{cl}_Q(P(M),\nu(D)))\bigr]_x\quad\text{for every }x\in V,
\]
with strict inclusion for at least one \(x\). The larger mapped domain means weaker pruning. Consequently, a reduction that removes variables or constraints may increase search by eliminating structure used by specialized propagators, whereas retaining redundant structure may strengthen pruning at additional memory and propagation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even when presolve preserves satisfiability, propagation on the presolved model can leave strictly larger domains after they are mapped back to the original variables. A smaller model may therefore prune less and require more search.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) and \(P(M)\) are satisfiability-equivalent under the stated model transformation.
The maps \(\nu\) and \(\mu\) provide a sound, componentwise-comparable correspondence between original and presolved domain states.
The same fixed propagation regime \(Q\) is used in both closure computations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Satisfiability preservation does not imply preservation of propagation strength or search effort.

notation.meaning: Variable sets of the original and presolved models.
Domain state at the propagation fixpoint for model N from initial domain state D.
Forward and backward maps between original and presolved domain states.

review_flags: No supplied source covers propagation-equivalence tradeoffs in CP-SAT presolve.
The exact domain-state maps and attainable strength relation are solver-dependent.

children.title: Explanation-Producing Propagation
children.top_down_role: Covers the LCG bridge from finite-domain propagation to Boolean reasons and learned nogoods.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Lazy Clause Generation: Combining the Power of SAT and CP
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Domain encodings, propagator explanations, and learned nogoods

knowledge_statements.title: Booleanization of Domain Events
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents finite-domain facts by Boolean literals used in clauses and explanations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer variable \(x\) with finite domain \(D_x\subset\mathbb Z\), associate Boolean literals with selected domain events, such as \(b_{x\le k}\leftrightarrow(x\le k)\), \(b_{x=k}\leftrightarrow(x=k)\), and \(b_{x\ne k}\leftrightarrow(x\ne k)\). The encoding must include channeling constraints making each Boolean truth value equivalent to its integer-domain event. Under a partial domain \(D'_x\subseteq D_x\), an event literal is true when every value in \(D'_x\) satisfies the event, false when none does, and otherwise unassigned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Booleanization assigns literals to integer-domain events and channels their truth values to the current domain, enabling clause-based reasoning.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) has a finite integer domain.
Every created event literal has sound bidirectional channeling constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each represented domain event can participate as a Boolean literal in propagation reasons and learned clauses.

notation.meaning: Initial finite domain of integer variable \(x\).

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses lazy-clause-generation Booleanization.
The set of materialized event literals is implementation-dependent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and finite-domain truth semantics fit the leaf, but the materialized events and channeling behavior are architecture-dependent. No lazy-clause-generation or CP-SAT source with a locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagator Reason Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the sound explanation a propagator must expose for each inference or conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a propagator derives literal \(\ell\) under the current trail. Its reason interface must return assigned literals \(R=\{r_1,\ldots,r_m\}\) such that the propagator's constraint entails
\[
(r_1\land\cdots\land r_m)\Rightarrow \ell.
\]
Equivalently, \(\neg r_1\lor\cdots\lor\neg r_m\lor\ell\) is valid. For a detected conflict it must return assigned literals \(R\) whose conjunction is inconsistent with the constraint, so \(\neg r_1\lor\cdots\lor\neg r_m\) is valid. Every member of \(R\) must be identifiable on the trail at the explanation time required by the solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each propagated literal or conflict must have a trail-based antecedent set forming a valid implicative clause.
assumptions_latex: All reason literals have defined Boolean or Booleanized semantics.
The propagator's constraint is part of the active model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned reason yields a logically valid clause suitable for conflict analysis.
review_flags: Standard explanation condition, but no relevant CP-SAT or lazy-clause-generation source was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly describes the intended logical role of propagation and conflict reasons, but no cited source establishes the required trail and explanation-time interface for the target architecture.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Integer–Boolean Nogoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines nogoods combining native Boolean literals with Booleanized integer-domain events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L_B\) be Boolean literals and \(L_I\) be literals denoting integer-domain events. A mixed integer–Boolean nogood is a finite set \(N\subseteq L_B\cup L_I\) such that the model entails
\[
\neg\bigwedge_{\ell\in N}\ell,
\]
or, equivalently, entails the clause \(\bigvee_{\ell\in N}\neg\ell\). It is unit under a partial assignment when every member except one is true and the remaining member is unassigned; unit propagation then forces the remaining member false through its Boolean or integer channel.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed nogood forbids a simultaneous combination of Boolean facts and integer-domain events and propagates through their channeling literals.
assumptions_latex: Every integer event in \(L_I\) has a sound Booleanized interpretation.
Nogood validity is evaluated against the active model constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No feasible model assignment can make every literal in \(N\) true simultaneously.
review_flags: No supplied source supports mixed nogoods in lazy clause generation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits and the nogood/clause equivalence is internally consistent, but no source with a specific locator supports mixed Boolean and integer-event nogoods in the relevant lazy-clause-generation setting.

children.title: Eager Explanations
children.top_down_role: Reasons materialized at propagation time.

knowledge_statements.title: Eager Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructs and stores each propagation reason at the moment the inference is produced.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a propagator state, current trail \(T\), and a newly inferred literal \(\ell\). Immediately compute antecedents \(R\subseteq T\) satisfying \(R\Rightarrow\ell\), validate that every antecedent is currently assigned, and store the clause \(\bigvee_{r\in R}\neg r\lor\ell\) with \(\ell\)'s trail entry. If the propagator reports conflict, immediately compute and store \(\bigvee_{r\in R}\neg r\). Conflict analysis retrieves the stored clause without invoking the propagator again; propagation stops at the solver's fixpoint or first conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eager explanation computes and stores a valid reason whenever propagation occurs, making it immediately available to conflict analysis.
assumptions_latex: The propagator can compute a sound reason at inference time.
Trail assignments referenced by the reason remain identifiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every recorded inference or conflict has an explanation materialized before subsequent search changes the state.
review_flags: Timing-regime terminology requires an architecture-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is suitable for the terminal timing-regime container, and the procedure is coherent. A source is required to establish that this materialization policy is the intended meaning of eager explanations in the target architecture.

children.title: Lazy Explanations
children.top_down_role: Reasons materialized when conflict analysis requests them.

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stores reconstruction data at propagation and materializes a reason only when conflict analysis requests it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a propagator state, current trail \(T\), and an inferred literal \(\ell\). At propagation time, store with \(\ell\) a handle \(h\) containing enough immutable state to reconstruct its inference context, but do not materialize its antecedent clause. When conflict analysis requests the reason, invoke \(\operatorname{explain}(h,T)\) to produce \(R\) such that every \(r\in R\) precedes \(\ell\) on the relevant trail and \(R\Rightarrow\ell\) is valid. Return \(\bigvee_{r\in R}\neg r\lor\ell\); unrequested reasons are never constructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lazy explanation records reconstruction data during propagation and creates the actual reason only if conflict analysis requests it.
assumptions_latex: The stored handle preserves all state needed for sound reconstruction.
Explanation reconstruction respects the historical trail context of \(\ell\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every requested reason is valid for its recorded inference, while reasons never requested incur no materialization cost.
review_flags: Lazy explanation semantics vary across solver architectures.
No relevant source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf and states the historical-trail requirement, but lazy explanation reconstruction and handle semantics vary by solver architecture. No supporting locator is supplied.

children.title: Deferred Explanations
children.top_down_role: Reason construction postponed through retained propagation context.

knowledge_statements.title: Deferred Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Queues explanation construction until a designated synchronization or analysis phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a sequence of propagations \((\ell_j,s_j)\), where \(s_j\) is sufficient snapshot data for inference \(\ell_j\). During propagation, enqueue \((\ell_j,s_j)\) without constructing antecedent clauses. At a designated explanation phase, process each required queue entry and compute \(R_j\) satisfying \(R_j\Rightarrow\ell_j\) in snapshot \(s_j\); store or return \(\bigvee_{r\in R_j}\neg r\lor\ell_j\). Before discarding or mutating any snapshot, materialize all explanations that can still be requested. Output the requested valid reasons, or a conflict clause when the queued item represents failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deferred explanation batches reason construction for a later phase while retaining snapshots sufficient to reproduce each inference soundly.
assumptions_latex: Each snapshot records the historical state needed to explain its inference.
The solver materializes required reasons before their snapshots become unavailable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Required explanations remain valid despite being constructed after the associated propagation events.

notation.meaning: Snapshot supporting later explanation of event \(j\).

review_flags: The distinction between deferred and lazy explanations is architecture-dependent.
No relevant source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is internally coherent, but whether deferred explanations form a distinct timing regime from lazy explanations is architecture-dependent and unsupported by any cited source.

children.title: Bound Literals
children.top_down_role: Literal representation for lower-bound plus upper-bound events.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Literals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines Boolean literals representing lower or upper bounds on an integer variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be an integer variable and \(k\in\mathbb Z\). An upper-bound literal is \([x\le k]\), with negation \([x\ge k+1]\); a lower-bound literal is \([x\ge k]\), with negation \([x\le k-1]\). Under current domain \(D_x\), \([x\le k]\) is true if \(\max D_x\le k\), false if \(\min D_x\ge k+1\), and otherwise unassigned. The lower-bound case is symmetric. Channeling must make Boolean assignment of either literal impose the corresponding domain restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound literal is a Boolean view of an integer upper or lower bound, with its negation represented by the complementary integral bound.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is integer-valued with nonempty current domain \(D_x\).
Bound literals are connected to \(x\) by sound channeling constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bound propagation on \(x\) and Boolean propagation on its bound literals have consistent truth semantics.

notation.meaning: Boolean literal representing an upper bound on \(x\).
Boolean literal representing a lower bound on \(x\).

review_flags: Standard integer-literal semantics, but no relevant CP-SAT source was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, and the complementary integral bounds and three-valued domain semantics are precise. No authoritative CP-SAT or lazy-clause-generation source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Equality Literals
children.top_down_role: Literal representation for equality to a designated integer value.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality Literals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality propositions represented on a CP-SAT Boolean trail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x,y\) be integer variables and \(c\in\mathbb Z\). An equality literal is a Boolean proposition \(e\) whose intended interpretation is \[e\Longleftrightarrow x=y+c.\] Its negation represents \(x\ne y+c\). A correct channeling interface enqueues \(e\) whenever the current integer domains entail the equality, enqueues \(\neg e\) whenever they exclude it, and, conversely, restricts the domains to satisfy the asserted proposition when either polarity is assigned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality literal is a Boolean proposition equivalent to an integer equality; propagation communicates its truth, falsity, and asserted polarity between Boolean and integer domains.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) and \(y\) have finite integer domains.
The Boolean and integer propagation states are consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e\Longleftrightarrow x=y+c\)

notation.meaning: current domain of integer variable x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and bidirectional channeling requirements are architecture-specific, and no cited source establishes that CP-SAT uses “equality literal” for the general predicate x=y+c rather than a narrower encoder construct.

children.title: Value Literals
children.top_down_role: Literal representation for value membership or exclusion events.

knowledge_statements.title: Value Literals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean encoding of membership at one integer value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an integer variable \(x\) with finite domain \(D(x)\subseteq\mathbb Z\) and \(v\in\mathbb Z\), a value literal is a Boolean proposition \(b_{x,v}\) interpreted by \[b_{x,v}\Longleftrightarrow x=v.\] Thus \(
