eg b_{x,v}\); and either asserted polarity must impose the corresponding domain restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A value literal is true exactly when an integer variable takes a specified value, with both polarities channeled to domain propagation.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) has a finite integer domain.
\(v\in\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_{x,v}\Longleftrightarrow x=v\)

notation.meaning: Boolean literal encoding x equal to v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical channel b_{x,v} iff x=v is coherent, but its classification as a distinct CP-SAT value-literal type and the stated mandatory channeling behavior require an authoritative architecture source.

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Literal Creation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: On-demand construction and reuse of Boolean encodings for integer predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an integer predicate \(P\), the current integer domains, and a map \(M\) from canonical predicates to Boolean variables. Canonicalize \(P\). If \(M(P)\) exists, return its literal. Otherwise create a fresh Boolean variable \(b\), set \(M(P)=b\), install channeling propagators enforcing \(b\Longleftrightarrow P\), and immediately propagate the current domains through those propagators. Stop with conflict if channeling is inconsistent; otherwise return \(b\). Consequently, repeated requests for the same canonical predicate return the same Boolean literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Create an integer predicate's Boolean encoding only when requested, cache it canonically, install bidirectional channeling, and immediately reconcile it with the current domains.
assumptions_latex: Canonicalization identifies semantically identical supported predicates.
Fresh Boolean variables are unassigned before channeling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(P)=b\ \land\ (b\Longleftrightarrow P)\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is appropriate for the leaf, but canonical reuse, fresh-variable creation, bidirectional channel installation, and immediate propagation are implementation-level claims unsupported by a source.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean–Integer Trail Synchronization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency invariant linking Boolean assignments and integer-domain updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T_B\) be a Boolean trail and \(T_I\) an integer-domain trail. For every registered channel \(b\Longleftrightarrow P\), synchronization maintains \[T_B\models b\Rightarrow T_I\models P,\qquad T_B\models
eg b\Rightarrow T_I\models
eg P,\] and enqueues the corresponding Boolean polarity whenever \(T_I\) entails \(P\) or \(
eg P\). Each cross-trail enqueue carries an explanation using assignments preceding it. Backtracking both trails to decision level \(d\) removes every update made above \(d\), preserving the invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronized trails propagate every registered predicate in both directions, attach prior-state explanations, and backtrack consistently by decision level.
assumptions_latex: Every exchanged predicate has a registered bidirectional channel.
Both trails use compatible decision levels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_B\text{ and }T_I\text{ agree on every registered predicate after propagation and backtracking}\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the synchronization leaf, but the explanation ordering, bidirectional entailment, and common decision-level backtracking invariant require an inspectable CP-SAT architecture source.

children.title: Boolean Clause Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation over clausal Boolean structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Clause Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit propagation with clause explanations on a Boolean trail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each clause \(C=\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\ell_m\), inspect it under the current partial Boolean assignment. If some \(\ell_i\) is true, take no action. If exactly one literal \(\ell_k\) is unassigned and every other literal is false, enqueue \(\ell_k\) with reason \(C\setminus\{\ell_k\}\). If every literal is false, return \(C\) as a conflict. Reprocess affected clauses after each enqueue and stop when no clause is unit or a conflict is found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clause propagation enqueues the sole unassigned literal of a unit clause, reports an all-false clause as conflict, and repeats to a fixpoint.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\ell_i\) is a Boolean literal.
The current trail contains no variable in both polarities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{output is a conflict or a unit-propagation fixpoint}\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a standard unit-propagation algorithm and the content kind fits, but no source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Pseudo-Boolean Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation over weighted Boolean inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Boolean Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slack-based propagation for a normalized pseudo-Boolean inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\sum_{i=1}^m a_i\ell_i\ge K\), where \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\). Under a partial assignment, compute \(U=\sum_{i:\ell_i\ne0}a_i\), the maximum attainable left side. If \(U<K\), report conflict. For every unassigned \(\ell_j\), if \(U-a_j<K\), enqueue \(\ell_j=1\), because setting it to zero would violate the inequality. Repeat after each enqueue until no further literal is forced or a conflict occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pseudo-Boolean propagation uses remaining attainable weight to detect conflict and forces any literal whose removal would make the required threshold unreachable.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\ge0\) for every \(i\).
The inequality has been normalized to Boolean literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U<K\text{ yields conflict, while }U-a_j<K\text{ yields }\ell_j=1\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The slack-based propagation rule is mathematically coherent for nonnegative coefficients, but the record has no inspectable citation supporting the algorithm.

children.title: Shared Trail Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of Boolean plus pseudo-Boolean consequences on the shared trail.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Trail Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cooperative Boolean and pseudo-Boolean propagation over one assignment trail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain one Boolean trail \(T\), a clause-propagator queue, and a pseudo-Boolean-propagator queue. Whenever a literal is appended to \(T\), notify every subscribed propagator. Repeatedly run an eligible propagator, append each justified consequence to \(T\), and notify subscribers of the new suffix. Stop and return the recorded reason if a propagator reports conflict; otherwise stop when both queues are empty. On backtracking, truncate \(T\) and restore each propagator to the same decision level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clause and pseudo-Boolean propagators consume and extend one trail, exchange notifications until both queues are empty, and backtrack to a common decision level.
assumptions_latex: Every enqueue has a reason over earlier trail assignments.
Each propagator supports restoration by decision level.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\text{ is conflicting or jointly propagation-closed}\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the coordination leaf, but its shared queues, subscription protocol, reason discipline, and synchronized restoration are architecture claims without cited evidence.

children.title: Integer-Domain Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation over finite integer domains plus bound events.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Domain Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone filtering of finite integer domains with explanations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given integer variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) with finite domains \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\) and constraints \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\), repeatedly select a constraint whose watched domain event occurred and replace each affected domain \(D_i\) by a sound subset \(D_i'\subseteq D_i\) that retains every value of \(D_i\) extendable to a tuple satisfying that constraint within the current domains. Record an explanation for every removed value or tightened bound. If some \(D_i'=\varnothing\), return conflict; otherwise stop when no propagator changes a domain and output the resulting domain fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer-domain propagators soundly remove values or tighten bounds, explain each change, detect empty domains, and iterate to a fixpoint.
assumptions_latex: \(D_i\subseteq\mathbb Z\) is finite for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
Each filtering operator is sound and contracting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_i'\subseteq D_i\text{ for every affected }i\), with conflict if a propagated domain is empty

notation.meaning: current domain of the i-th integer variable
constraint equipped with a domain-filtering propagator

children.title: Linear-Constraint Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation over integer linear constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Constraint Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound propagation for one integer linear inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le b\) with integer bounds \(L_i\le x_i\le U_i\), define \(m_i=a_iL_i\) when \(a_i\ge0\) and \(m_i=a_iU_i\) otherwise, and let \(M=\sum_i m_i\). If \(M>b\), report conflict. Otherwise, for each \(a_k>0\), impose \(x_k\le\left\lfloor L_k+(b-M)/a_k\right\rfloor\); for each \(a_k<0\), impose \(x_k\ge\left\lceil U_k+(b-M)/a_k\right\rceil\). Iterate after bound changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear propagation computes the minimum possible activity, detects overload, and derives coefficient-sensitive upper or lower bounds for each variable.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,b,L_i,U_i\in\mathbb Z\).
\(L_i\le U_i\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M>b\text{ yields conflict; otherwise the displayed bounds are valid}\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimum-activity conflict test and coefficient-sensitive bound updates are coherent, and algorithm is the correct content kind, but no matching propagation source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Cross-Family Fixpoint Coordination
children.top_down_role: Exchange of consequences between domain plus linear propagators.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Family Fixpoint Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven closure across integer-domain and linear propagator families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P_D\) and \(\mathcal P_L\) be sound, contracting integer-domain and linear propagators over a common finite domain state \(D\). Initialize a queue with all applicable propagators. Apply a queued propagator, enqueue every propagator watching a changed domain event, and record its explanations. Return conflict if any domain becomes empty or any propagator detects infeasibility. Otherwise stop when the queue is empty; then \(p(D)=D\) for every enabled \(p\in\mathcal P_D\cup\mathcal P_L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Domain and linear propagators notify one another through shared events until every enabled operator leaves the finite domain state unchanged or conflict occurs.
assumptions_latex: All domains are finite.
Every propagator is sound and contracting.
Every relevant domain change schedules all affected propagators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(D)=D\quad\text{for all enabled }p\in\mathcal P_D\cup\mathcal P_L\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-state event-driven closure algorithm fits the leaf, but the scheduling completeness condition and claimed simultaneous fixpoint require a source describing the event and rescheduling semantics.

children.title: Precedence Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation over temporal ordering relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Precedence Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound propagation for a scheduling precedence relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For activities \(i\) and \(j\) with integer start times \(s_i,s_j\), duration \(p_i\ge0\), and enforced precedence \(s_i+p_i\le s_j\), update \[L_j\leftarrow\max(L_j,L_i+p_i),\qquad U_i\leftarrow\min(U_i,U_j-p_i).\] If either updated lower bound exceeds its upper bound, report conflict. For a reified precedence \(b\Rightarrow s_i+p_i\le s_j\), perform these updates when \(b\) is true and infer \(\neg b\) when \(L_i+p_i>U_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An enforced precedence pushes the successor's lower bound forward and the predecessor's upper bound backward; impossible reified precedence forces its Boolean guard false.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i,s_j\in\mathbb Z\) have current bounds.
\(p_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_j\ge L_i+p_i\ \land\ U_i\le U_j-p_i\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The precedence bound updates and reified infeasibility test are mathematically coherent, but no scheduling-propagation source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Global-Constraint Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation over specialized combinatorial constraint structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Global-Constraint Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explanation-producing filtering interface for a scheduling global constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a scheduling global constraint \(G\), current finite domains \(D\), and optional presence literals, invoke a sound filtering operator \(F_G\). If \(F_G(D)=\bot\), return an explanation whose conjunction with \(G\) is inconsistent. Otherwise replace \(D\) by \(F_G(D)\subseteq D\), attaching to every bound change, value removal, or presence assignment an antecedent sufficient to imply it under \(G\). Reschedule \(F_G\) after watched scheduling events and stop when \(F_G(D)=D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduling global propagator soundly filters shared domains, explains every consequence or conflict, and reruns on watched events until locally stable.
assumptions_latex: The current domains and presence assignments are finite.
\(F_G\) is sound and contracting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_G(D)=\bot\text{ or }F_G(D)\subseteq D\), with every consequence explained

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic interface fits the leaf, but explanation generation, presence-literal handling, watched-event scheduling, and local stabilization are unsupported architecture-specific claims.

children.title: Shared Scheduling Event Flow
children.top_down_role: Exchange of temporal events across precedence plus global propagators.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Scheduling Event Flow
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven interface shared by scheduling propagators over interval bounds and presence literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be scheduling propagators sharing a reversible state \(D\), and let \(W(e)\subseteq P\) contain the propagators watching event \(e\). Initialize a queue \(Q\) with propagators affected by the initial domain changes. Repeatedly remove some \(p\in Q\), run \(p(D)\), and require either a conflict reason or a finite set \(E_p\) of newly produced bound, precedence, or presence events. For every \(e\in E_p\), enqueue each unscheduled member of \(W(e)\). Stop on conflict or when \(Q=\varnothing\); in the latter case output the resulting common scheduling state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scheduling propagators consume shared bound, precedence, and presence events, emit explained changes, and awaken event watchers until conflict or queue exhaustion.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is finite.
Every accepted propagation strictly tightens the finite-domain state or fixes a literal.
Each propagated change or conflict has an explanation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either an explained conflict or a state with no pending watched scheduling event.

notation.meaning: Shared reversible domain and literal state.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the event-flow leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no inspectable source supports this CP-SAT scheduling interface or its event taxonomy.

children.title: Propagator Priority Policies
children.top_down_role: Priority classes, queue ordering, and workload-sensitive scheduling choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagator Priority Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Priority-queue policy for reaching a propagation fixpoint without changing propagator semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition a finite propagator set \(P\) into priority classes \(P_0,\ldots,P_k\), where smaller indices run first. Maintain one FIFO queue per class and at most one pending copy of each propagator. Whenever an event awakens \(p\in P_i\), append \(p\) to queue \(i\) if it is not already pending. Select from the least-index nonempty queue, except that a fairness rule must eventually select every continuously pending propagator. After running \(p\), enqueue all propagators awakened by its domain changes. Stop only when every priority queue is empty or a conflict is produced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagators run from priority-indexed queues, with duplicate suppression and fairness ensuring that every persistently enabled propagator eventually executes.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and the set of priority classes are finite.
Propagators are sound and inflationary with respect to domain information.
The selection rule is fair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Queue priority changes execution order but not the requirement that termination without conflict occurs only after all pending propagators have run.

notation.meaning: Priority class i, with lower index having higher priority.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but the priority, duplicate-suppression, and fairness policy is uncited and implementation-specific.

children.title: Propagation Fixpoint Detection
children.top_down_role: Termination conditions for propagation rounds across active propagators.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Fixpoint Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational and semantic criterion for detecting a propagation fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be a domain state, let \(P\) be the registered propagators, and let each \(p\in P\) implement a sound contracting operator \(F_p\). Executing \(p\) replaces \(D\) by \(F_p(D)\). Whenever this execution strictly changes \(D\), the event mechanism must schedule every propagator whose output may thereby change, including \(p\) itself when \(F_p\) is not idempotent. If all scheduled executions have completed and every event queue is empty, then \[F_p(D)=D\quad\text{for every }p\in P.\] Conversely, if these equalities already hold, draining any pending propagators produces no change and leaves the queues empty. A reported inconsistency terminates propagation with conflict rather than a fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With complete dependency scheduling, empty queues after all scheduled work completes certify that every propagator leaves the domains unchanged. At a semantic fixpoint, draining stale pending work makes no changes and empties the queues; inconsistency yields conflict instead.
assumptions_latex: Event subscriptions cover every dependency of every propagator.
Queue updates caused by an execution are completed atomically with that execution.
Each \(F_p\) is sound and contracting, and every non-idempotent propagator is rescheduled when its own change may enable further contraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Queue exhaustion after completed processing certifies \(F_p(D)=D\) for every \(p\in P\); a semantic fixpoint yields queue exhaustion after pending work is drained.

notation.meaning: Domain operator implemented by propagator p.

children.title: Starvation Avoidance
children.top_down_role: Fairness boundaries for low-priority propagators under sustained activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Starvation Avoidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-fairness requirement for a prioritized propagation scheduler.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an infinite scheduler trace \((Q_t,p_t)_{t\geq 0}\), starvation is avoided if every propagator \(p\) that remains pending from some time \(t_0\) onward is selected at some finite time \(t\geq t_0\). A sufficient implementation condition is bounded overtaking: there exists \(B<\infty\) such that, while \(p\) remains pending, at most \(B\) other selections occur before \(p\) is selected. Under finite-domain monotone propagation, weak fairness prevents a lower-priority propagator from being postponed forever by repeated higher-priority awakenings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starvation avoidance requires every continuously pending propagator to run eventually; bounded overtaking is a sufficient scheduling rule.
assumptions_latex: The propagator set is finite.
Pending status persists until execution or cancellation.
Scheduler traces record every selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every continuously pending propagator is selected after finitely many scheduler steps.

notation.meaning: Pending propagators at scheduler step t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly expresses weak fairness and bounded overtaking as a sufficient policy, but no inspectable scheduler-fairness source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Antecedent Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical antecedent literals used to explain integer-bound propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), and let integer variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) have current bounds \(L_i\leq x_i\leq U_i\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). A bound-antecedent family is a finite set \(R\) of currently true literals, each of the form \(x_i\geq \ell\), \(x_i\leq u\), or a Boolean enforcement literal. For a model constraint \(C\), it explains a propagated bound literal \(q\) when \[C\land\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\;\Longrightarrow\;q.\] It explains a conflict when the same antecedent conjunction with \(C\) implies false. A valid family may mix lower-bound, upper-bound, and enforcement literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound-antecedent family is a finite set of currently true bound or enforcement literals whose conjunction with the responsible constraint implies a propagated bound or a conflict.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
Each \(x_i\) is integer-valued and has current integral bounds \(L_i\) and \(U_i\).
Every member of \(R\) is true in the current solver state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) is a valid propagation reason when \(C\land\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\Rightarrow q\), and a valid conflict reason when that conjunction implies false.

children.title: Linear Constraint Reasons
children.top_down_role: Reason structures derived from active linear rows and bound literals.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Constraint Reasons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-literal certificate for propagation from one linear inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R\), and \(x\in\mathbb Z^n\), and consider the valid row \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\). Fix \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(a_j>0\), and let \(u\in\mathbb Z\). Choose currently true antecedent bounds that imply \(m_i\leq a_i x_i\) for every \(i\neq j\). If \[a_j(u+1)+\sum_{i\neq j}m_i>b,\] then the antecedents together with the row exclude every integer value \(x_j\geq u+1\) and therefore certify \(x_j\leq u\). Sign-reversed activity bounds analogously certify lower-bound propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an integer target bound u, antecedent activity bounds certify a linear propagation when their minimum row activity makes every integer value at least u+1 violate the row.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R\), \(x\in\mathbb Z^n\), and \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) is valid.
\(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(a_j>0\), and \(u\in\mathbb Z\).
Each selected antecedent soundly implies \(m_i\leq a_i x_i\) for its corresponding \(i\neq j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected antecedents and the row imply \(x_j\leq u\).

notation.meaning: Antecedent-implied lower bound on term activity.
Integer upper bound propagated for x_j.

children.title: Integer-Rounding Reasons
children.top_down_role: Reason structures associated with integral rounding of propagated bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Rounding Reasons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for integral rounding of a rational bound implied by antecedents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_j\in\mathbb Z\), \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), and \(c\in\mathbb Z\). Suppose a constraint \(C\), together with currently true antecedents \(R\), implies \(d x_j\leq c\). Then \[x_j\leq\left\lfloor\frac{c}{d}\right\rfloor.\] Thus \(C\), \(R\), the derived inequality, and the integrality declaration for \(x_j\) form a verifiable rounding reason. Dually, if \(C\) and \(R\) imply \(d x_j\geq c\), these data certify \(x_j\geq\lceil c/d\rceil\). The rounding step is distinguished from the antecedents establishing the unrounded inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint and its true antecedents first imply an unrounded inequality; together with the target variable's integrality, that inequality certifies the floor- or ceiling-rounded bound.
assumptions_latex: \(x_j\in\mathbb Z\).
\(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) and \(c\in\mathbb Z\).
Every literal in \(R\) is currently true, and \(C\land\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\) implies the stated unrounded inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\), \(R\), the derived inequality, and integrality certify \(x_j\leq\lfloor c/d\rfloor\), or dually \(x_j\geq\lceil c/d\rceil\).

notation.meaning: Constraint responsible for the unrounded implication.
Positive integer coefficient of the propagated variable.
Integral right-hand side of the derived inequality.

children.title: Rounding Support from Linear Rows
children.top_down_role: The interface between linear-row evidence and rounded integer conclusions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Support from Linear Rows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: How a linear-row reason supplies the inequality required for integer rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the row \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\), fix \(j\) with \(a_j>0\), and let antecedents \(R\) imply \(m_i\leq a_i x_i\) for all \(i
eq j\). Then \[R\land(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b)\;\Longrightarrow\;a_jx_j\leq b-\sum_{i
eq j}m_i.\] If \(x_j\in\mathbb Z\) and \(a_j\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), this supports the rounded propagation \[x_j\leq\left\lfloor rac{b-\sum_{i
eq j}m_i}{a_j}ightfloor.\] Therefore the same activity-bound antecedents support both the linear implication and its integer-rounding consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds on all other row terms isolate one integer variable, after which floor division yields its propagated upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) is valid.
The antecedents imply every selected activity bound \(m_i\leq a_i x_i\).
\(x_j\in\mathbb Z\) and \(a_j\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The row and antecedents imply the displayed floor-rounded upper bound on \(x_j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly isolates the target term and applies integrality-based floor rounding, and its role fits the leaf. No inspectable source supports its use as a CP-SAT explanation interface.

children.title: Optional Constraint Reasons
children.top_down_role: Reasons whose applicability depends on constraint presence.

knowledge_statements.title: Optional Constraint Reasons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reason form for propagation by a constraint guarded by a presence literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an optional constraint have semantics \(e\Rightarrow C\), where \(e\) is its presence literal. If currently true bound antecedents \(R\) satisfy \[C\land\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\;\Longrightarrow\;q,\] then propagation of \(q\) while \(e\) is true is certified by \(R\cup\{e\}\), because \[(e\Rightarrow C)\land e\land\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\;\Longrightarrow\;q.\] If \(C\land\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\) is inconsistent, the optional constraint may instead propagate \(\neg e\), with \(R\) as its reason.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consequence propagated from an optional constraint includes its true presence literal in the reason; antecedents making the active constraint infeasible can instead justify absence.
assumptions_latex: The optional constraint is modeled by \(e\Rightarrow C\).
Every antecedent in \(R\) is currently true.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\cup\{e\}\) certifies \(q\), while inconsistency of \(C\land\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\) certifies \(\neg e\).

notation.meaning: Constraint active when e is true.
Bound antecedents used by the active constraint.

children.title: Reified Constraint Reasons
children.top_down_role: Reasons linking Boolean control literals to constraint consequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Reified Constraint Reasons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explanation rules for both directions of a fully reified constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(e\leftrightarrow C\) be a fully reified constraint, and let every literal in \(R\) be currently true. If \[C\land igwedge_{r\in R}r\;\Longrightarrow\;q,\] then \(R\cup\{e\}\) certifies propagation of \(q\). If \[
eg C\land igwedge_{r\in R}r\;\Longrightarrow\;q,\] then \(R\cup\{
eg e\}\) certifies propagation of \(q\). Moreover, if \( igwedge_{r\in R}r\Rightarrow C\), then \(R\) certifies \(e\); if \( igwedge_{r\in R}r\Rightarrow

eg e\). A branch literal may be omitted only when the remaining antecedents already determine that branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full reification explains consequences from either selected branch by including its branch literal, and antecedents that determine the constraint's truth or falsity explain the corresponding value of the reification literal.
assumptions_latex: The model contains the equivalence \(e\leftrightarrow C\).
Every literal in \(R\) is currently true.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated implications provide checkable reasons for a branch consequence \(q\), for \(e\), or for \(\neg e\).

notation.meaning: Reification literal selecting C when true and its complementary branch when false.
Consequence derived within a selected branch.

children.title: Enforcement-Literal Scope
children.top_down_role: Scope restrictions governing enforcement literals within explanations.

knowledge_statements.title: Enforcement-Literal Scope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion determining when enforcement literals must occur in an explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a constraint guarded by the finite set \(E=\{e_1,\ldots,e_m\}\) have semantics \((\bigwedge_{e\in E}e)\Rightarrow C\). Suppose currently true non-enforcement antecedents \(R\) satisfy \[C\land\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\;\Longrightarrow\;q.\] For \(E'\subseteq E\), the reason \(R\cup E'\) soundly activates this inference when every omitted guard literal is entailed by the included antecedents: \[\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\land\bigwedge_{e\in E'}e\;\Longrightarrow\;\bigwedge_{e\in E\setminus E'}e.\] Under these conditions, the guarded constraint and \(R\cup E'\) imply \(q\). Guard literals that are not entailed must be included; entailed or otherwise redundant guard literals may be omitted, but a nonminimal reason may still retain them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reason using a guarded constraint must establish every guard literal, either explicitly or through other antecedents. Entailed guard literals may be omitted, while unrelated true literals are not required.
assumptions_latex: The guarded constraint has semantics \((\bigwedge_{e\in E}e)\Rightarrow C\).
Every literal explicitly included in the reason is currently true.
\(C\land\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\Rightarrow q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\cup E'\) soundly supports the guarded inference when it explicitly includes or entails every member of \(E\).

notation.meaning: Full finite set of enforcement literals guarding C.
Guard literals explicitly included in the reason.
Consequence obtained from the activated constraint.

children.title: Reason Minimization
children.top_down_role: Reduction of redundant antecedents in propagation explanations.

knowledge_statements.title: Reason Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion-based minimization of a valid propagation or conflict reason.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite valid reason \(R\), a consequence \(q\), and a sound implication oracle for the responsible constraint \(C\), initialize \(S\leftarrow R\). Visit each \(r\in S\) in a fixed order; delete \(r\) whenever the oracle confirms \[C\land\bigwedge_{s\in S\setminus\{r\}}s\;\Longrightarrow\;q.\] For conflict minimization, replace \(q\) by false. Return \(S\) after a full pass with no further accepted deletion. The output remains a valid reason and is deletion-minimal relative to the oracle and visitation procedure, but need not have minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly delete an antecedent when the remaining literals still imply the propagation or conflict; the result is deletion-minimal, not necessarily smallest.
assumptions_latex: The initial reason \(R\) is finite and valid.
The implication oracle is sound.
Every deletion test uses the current set \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \(S\subseteq R\) is valid and no single remaining antecedent can be deleted using the oracle.

notation.meaning: Propagated consequence, or false for conflict.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, and the statement correctly distinguishes deletion minimality relative to the oracle from minimum cardinality. No authoritative reason-minimization source is supplied.

children.title: Reason Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Replacement or refinement of antecedents to improve explanatory force.

knowledge_statements.title: Reason Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion-based strengthening by clause subsumption while preserving propagation validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be an encoded constraint system, let \(p\) be a propagated literal, and let \(R\) be a finite set of antecedent literals such that \(F\models (\bigwedge_{r\in R}r)\rightarrow p\). Select \(R'\subseteq R\) and accept it only if \(F\models (\bigwedge_{r\in R'}r)\rightarrow p\). Output \(C(R')=\bigvee_{r\in R'}\neg r\vee p\). Then \(F\models C(R')\), and \(C(R')\models C(R)\), where \(C(R)=\bigvee_{r\in R}\neg r\vee p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete antecedents only after checking that the retained antecedents still imply the propagation. The resulting valid explanation clause subsumes the original clause.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is finite
\(F\models (\bigwedge_{r\in R}r)\rightarrow p\)
\(R'\subseteq R\)
The validity test for \(R'\) is sound
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\models C(R')\) and \(C(R')\models C(R)\)

notation.meaning: explanation clause induced by antecedent set R

children.title: Reason Strength–Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Structural tradeoffs among reason size, strength, and production cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Reason Strength–Cost Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes the competing effects of reason refinement on clause strength and solver cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid reason \(R\) of propagation \(p\), let \(C(R)=\bigvee_{r\in R}\neg r\vee p\), let \(s(R)\) measure explanation strength, and let \(c(R)\) include construction, validation, storage, and later propagation costs. Refinement from \(R\) to \(R'\) is worthwhile under weights \(\alpha,\beta>0\) only when \(\alpha(s(R')-s(R))>\beta(c(R')-c(R))\), subject to \(F\models(\bigwedge R')\rightarrow p\). Thus logical improvement alone does not determine the preferred reason: its incremental search benefit must exceed its incremental computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stronger valid explanation is preferable only when its expected search benefit exceeds the added cost of constructing, checking, storing, and using it.
assumptions_latex: Both \(R\) and \(R'\) are valid reasons for \(p\)
\(s\) and \(c\) use a fixed comparison convention
\(\alpha,\beta>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R'\) is preferred only if \(\alpha\Delta s>\beta\Delta c\)

notation.meaning: aggregate computational cost of a reason

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted inequality is a proposed solver-dependent utility model, not a generally established mathematical principle. A CP-SAT-specific source must define or justify the strength and cost measures and the claimed decision rule.

children.title: Antecedent Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity requirements for literals used as explanation antecedents.

knowledge_statements.title: Antecedent Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for antecedents used by an explanation-producing propagator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At trail state \(T\), a finite antecedent set \(R\) is admissible for explaining propagated literal \(p\) exactly when every \(r\in R\) is true in \(T\), each \(r\) denotes a valid encoded fact, and \(F\models(\bigwedge_{r\in R}r)\rightarrow p\). Under these conditions the clause \(\bigvee_{r\in R}\neg r\vee p\) is entailed by \(F\) and is unit or satisfied at the state where the propagation is recorded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every antecedent must be true on the relevant trail, correctly encoded, and jointly sufficient under the model to imply the propagated literal.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is the trail state at which \(p\) is explained
\(F\) is the active encoded constraint system
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\models\bigl(\bigvee_{r\in R}\neg r\vee p\bigr)\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical entailment condition is standard and the content kind fits, but the exact admissibility and trail-state requirements are architecture-specific and have no cited source.

children.title: Reification Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity requirements for explanations controlled by reification literals.

knowledge_statements.title: Reification Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Permitted use of full and one-way reifications in explanations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Boolean literal \(b\) encode an integer predicate \(P(x)\). If the encoding enforces full reification \(F\models b\leftrightarrow P(x)\), either direction may be used in an explanation. If it enforces only \(F\models b\rightarrow P(x)\), then \(b\) may justify \(P(x)\), but \(P(x)\) may not justify \(b\) without an additional constraint establishing the reverse implication. Symmetrically, an encoding of \(P(x)\rightarrow b\) licenses only that direction. Every reified antecedent must use a direction entailed by the active encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reified literal may support an explanation only in a direction actually enforced by its full or half-reified encoding.
assumptions_latex: \(b\) is Boolean and \(P(x)\) is an integer predicate
All cited encoding constraints belong to \(F\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b\) and \(P(x)\) are interchangeable only if \(F\models b\leftrightarrow P(x)\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The directional distinction between full and half reification is mathematically appropriate, but no inspectable source establishes these semantics for the active CP-SAT encoding.

children.title: Cross-Layer Validity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Correctness at the interface between integer propagation and Boolean control.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Layer Validity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient bridge conditions for translating an integer deduction into a Boolean explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a combined Boolean-integer encoding. Suppose the integer layer derives \((\bigwedge_{i=1}^{m}Q_i(x))\rightarrow P(x)\), while the Boolean layer uses antecedents \(q_1,\ldots,q_m\) and conclusion \(p\). If \(F\models q_i\rightarrow Q_i(x)\) for every \(i\), \(F\models (\bigwedge_{i=1}^{m}Q_i(x))\rightarrow P(x)\), and \(F\models P(x)\rightarrow p\), then \(F\models (\bigwedge_{i=1}^{m}q_i)\rightarrow p\). If any bridge implication is unavailable, this compositional argument does not certify the Boolean reason, which must instead be justified directly from \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer deduction certifies a Boolean reason when every antecedent and the conclusion are translated in the required entailed direction. A missing bridge removes that certificate and requires a separate validity check.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\)
\(F\) is the active combined Boolean-integer encoding
\(Q_i(x)\) and \(P(x)\) are integer-layer predicates
\(q_i\) and \(p\) are Boolean literals
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated bridge implications imply \(F\models (\bigwedge_{i=1}^{m}q_i)\rightarrow p\)

children.title: Rounding Correctness
children.top_down_role: Correctness boundaries for integral rounding within bound explanations.

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Correctness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact floor rounding for an upper bound derived from a linear inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let integer variables satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le b\), and fix \(k\) with \(a_k>0\). For each \(i\ne k\), let \(m_i=\min\{a_i\ell_i,a_i u_i\}\), where \(\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\). Define the exact residual \(r=b-\sum_{i\ne k}m_i\). Every feasible integer assignment then satisfies \(a_kx_k\le r\), hence \(x_k\le\lfloor r/a_k\rfloor\). The floor must be mathematical floor, including when \(r<0\); truncation toward zero is not equivalent for negative nonintegral quotients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive coefficient, subtract exact minimum contributions and apply mathematical floor; truncation toward zero is wrong for negative nonintegral residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i,a_i,b,\ell_i,u_i\in\mathbb Z\)
\(\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\) for every \(i\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\le\left\lfloor\dfrac{b-\sum_{i\ne k}m_i}{a_k}\right\rfloor\)

notation.meaning: minimum contribution of term i over current bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound formula and warning about negative-quotient truncation are mathematically correct, and the property kind fits the leaf, but no source with a specific locator is cited.

children.title: Overflow Safety
children.top_down_role: Representational limits arising from finite-width arithmetic.

knowledge_statements.title: Overflow Safety
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic precondition for sound fixed-width integer propagation and explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=[L,U]\cap\mathbb Z\) be the representable machine-integer range. A bound computation is overflow-safe when every evaluated product, partial sum, residual, sign change, and rounding adjustment either lies in \(I\) or is performed with checked or wider exact arithmetic whose final representable result is verified before conversion to \(I\). If an operation leaves \(I\), the propagator must use an exact fallback, return a conservative bound, or decline the propagation; wrapped or saturated arithmetic may not be used as though it were exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every arithmetic intermediate must be representable or computed exactly with checks; otherwise the propagator must fall back, weaken the bound, or decline propagation.
assumptions_latex: Machine integers represent exactly \(I=[L,U]\cap\mathbb Z\)
The mathematical deduction is defined over \(\mathbb Z\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z\notin I\) for any intermediate \(z\) requires a sound fallback rather than unchecked conversion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is a sound arithmetic-safety requirement, but the prescribed fallback behavior and treatment of saturation are implementation-specific and unsupported by a cited CP-SAT source.

children.title: Overflow-Sensitive Rounding Cases
children.top_down_role: Cases where rounding behavior depends on arithmetic range protection.

knowledge_statements.title: Overflow-Sensitive Rounding Cases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual overflow can invalidate an otherwise correct bound formula under unchecked two's-complement arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let signed \(w\)-bit two's-complement integers have range \(I=[-2^{w-1},2^{w-1}-1]\cap\mathbb Z\), where \(w\ge2\), and write \(U=2^{w-1}-1\) and \(L=-2^{w-1}\). Consider integer variables satisfying \(x+y\le U\) with current bound \(y\ge-1\). Exact activity reasoning forms the residual \(r=U-(-1)=U+1\), giving the redundant mathematical bound \(x\le U+1\). The residual is not in \(I\). If its subtraction is evaluated by unchecked two's-complement wraparound, \(U+1\) becomes \(L\), producing the false bound \(x\le L\). Thus residual formation must be checked or performed in wider exact arithmetic before division or rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representable operands can produce an unrepresentable residual. In unchecked two's-complement arithmetic, that residual can wrap to the minimum integer and turn a redundant bound into a false restrictive bound.
assumptions_latex: \(w\in\mathbb N\) and \(w\ge2\)
Machine arithmetic uses signed \(w\)-bit two's-complement representation
The example assumes unchecked wraparound for the faulty computation
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-(-1)=U+1\notin I\), while unchecked wraparound maps \(U+1\) to \(L\)

notation.meaning: maximum and minimum representable signed integers

knowledge_statements.title: Correctness Preservation Under Reason Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion-based minimization of an already valid propagation reason.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a constraint encoding, \(p\) a propagated literal, and \(R\) a finite reason with \(F\models(\bigwedge R)\rightarrow p\). If a minimization procedure outputs \(R'\subseteq R\) and establishes \(F\models(\bigwedge R')\rightarrow p\), then \(R'\) is a correct reason for \(p\). Moreover, its explanation clause \(C(R')=\bigvee_{r\in R'}\neg r\vee p\) is entailed by \(F\) and subsumes \(C(R)\). Merely deleting literals without re-establishing the implication does not preserve correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reason minimization is correct when the retained antecedents still imply the propagation; its clause then remains entailed and subsumes the original explanation.
assumptions_latex: \(F\models(\bigwedge R)\rightarrow p\)
\(R'\subseteq R\)
\(F\models(\bigwedge R')\rightarrow p\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\models C(R')\) and \(C(R')\models C(R)\)

notation.meaning: explanation clause induced by reason R

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is precise and correct for deletion-based minimization, and its content kind matches the topic. It nevertheless has no citation or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Missing, Incomplete, or Stale Reasons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure modes of explanation records relative to the relevant trail prefix and active encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the active encoding, let \(p\) be a propagated literal, and let \(T_p\) be the trail prefix relative to which \(p\) was propagated. A required reason record is missing when no reason is available. A recorded finite antecedent set \(R\) is incomplete when \(F\not\models(\bigwedge_{r\in R}r)\rightarrow p\), and it is stale when some \(r\in R\) is not true in \(T_p\) or no longer denotes the encoded fact used to establish the implication. A missing, incomplete, or stale reason may not be used for conflict analysis or learning until a valid reason is reconstructed. The empty set \(R=\varnothing\) is valid when \(F\models p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A required reason is unusable when absent, insufficient to imply the propagation, or invalid for the relevant trail prefix or encoding. An empty reason is nevertheless valid for a root-level consequence.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the active encoding
\(T_p\) is the trail prefix relevant to propagation \(p\)
Any recorded reason \(R\) is finite
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A recorded \(R\), including \(R=\varnothing\), is valid when every \(r\in R\) is true in \(T_p\) and \(F\models(\bigwedge_{r\in R}r)\rightarrow p\)

notation.meaning: trail prefix relevant to propagation p

children.title: Oversized Reasons
children.top_down_role: Explanation structures whose literal volume creates excessive processing cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Oversized Reasons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid explanations containing antecedents that can be deleted while preserving validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be an encoding, let \(p\) be a propagated literal, and let \(R\) be a finite valid reason for \(p\). Relative to a comparison class \(\mathcal R_p\), call \(R\) oversized when there exists \(R'\in\mathcal R_p\) such that \(R'\subsetneq R\) and \(F\models(\bigwedge_{r\in R'}r)\rightarrow p\). For \(C(S)=\bigvee_{r\in S}\neg r\vee p\), this implies \(C(R')\models C(R)\). The clause \(C(R)\) contains the avoidable literals associated with \(R\setminus R'\), which may increase representation and processing cost, although \(R\) remains logically valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reason is oversized when a proper subset still implies the propagation. Its clause is then dominated by the subset clause and contains avoidable literals, though it remains sound.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) and \(R'\) are finite antecedent sets
\(R'\subsetneq R\)
\(R'\in\mathcal R_p\)
\(F\models(\bigwedge_{r\in R'}r)\rightarrow p\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(R')\models C(R)\), and \(R\setminus R'\) consists of avoidable antecedents relative to \(\mathcal R_p\)

notation.meaning: comparison class of admissible reasons for p
explanation clause induced by antecedent set S

children.title: Weak Reasons
children.top_down_role: Explanation structures with limited pruning or learning value.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Reasons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative weakness of valid explanation clauses under logical implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) be valid reasons for the same propagated literal \(p\), with explanation clauses \(C(R_j)=\bigvee_{r\in R_j}\neg r\vee p\). Reason \(R_1\) is weak relative to \(R_2\) when \(C(R_2)\models C(R_1)\) but \(C(R_1)\not\models C(R_2)\). In the deletion-only case, \(R_2\subsetneq R_1\) suffices. A weak reason is sound, but it excludes fewer assignments and may yield less effective propagation or conflict learning than the dominating alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reason is relatively weak when another valid reason produces a strictly stronger clause; it remains sound but can support less effective learning.
assumptions_latex: \(F\models C(R_1)\) and \(F\models C(R_2)\)
Both reasons explain the same literal \(p\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(R_2)\models C(R_1)\) and \(C(R_1)\not\models C(R_2)\)

notation.meaning: alternative valid reasons for the same propagation
explanation clause induced by reason j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implication-based definition of relative weakness is mathematically sound and the failure-boundary kind fits. The assertion about practical propagation or learning effectiveness is solver-dependent and lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Reason Size–Strength Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Regimes where compactness and explanatory strength compete.

knowledge_statements.title: Reason Size–Strength Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause strength versus construction and processing cost for propagation reasons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be the currently true literals, let \(p\) be a propagated literal, and let \(R\subseteq A\) satisfy \(R\Rightarrow p\). Its clausal reason is \(C_R=\bigvee_{\ell\in R}\neg\ell\vee p\). If \(R_1\subseteq R_2\), then \(C_{R_1}\Rightarrow C_{R_2}\), so deleting redundant antecedents strengthens the reason. However, if \(c_{\mathrm{find}}(R)\) is the cost of deriving or minimizing \(R\) and \(c_{\mathrm{use}}(R)\) is its later processing cost, reason selection minimizes neither size nor strength alone, but a policy-dependent objective such as \(c_{\mathrm{find}}(R)+c_{\mathrm{use}}(R)+\lambda |R|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smaller valid reasons yield stronger clauses and may reduce later processing, but finding them may cost more than the resulting search benefit.
assumptions_latex: \(R\Rightarrow p\) is valid for every selected reason \(R\).
All literals in \(R\) are true at the propagation point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_1\subseteq R_2\Rightarrow C_{R_1}\Rightarrow C_{R_2}\), while total explanation cost may favor \(R_2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation-Cost Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational condition identifying explanations as the dominant propagation expense.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For propagation events \(k=1,\ldots,m\), decompose measured processing time as \(T=\sum_k(s_k+r_k+q_k)\), where \(s_k\) is detection or scanning time, \(r_k\) is reason construction and minimization time, and \(q_k\) is enqueueing and bookkeeping time. Weak explanation-cost dominance holds on the measured workload when \(\sum_k r_k\geq \sum_k(s_k+q_k)\). Equivalently, for \(\rho=\sum_k r_k/T\), weak dominance is \(\rho\geq 1/2\), and strict dominance is \(\rho>1/2\). This predicate concerns observed computational cost, not the logical strength or correctness of the produced reasons.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explanation cost weakly dominates when reason generation and minimization consume at least as much time as detection, enqueueing, and bookkeeping combined; dominance is strict when they consume more.
assumptions_latex: The timing categories are exhaustive and do not overlap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak dominance is \(\sum_k r_k\geq\sum_k(s_k+q_k)\), equivalently \(\rho\geq 1/2\); strict dominance is \(\rho>1/2\).

notation.meaning: scan, explanation, and bookkeeping costs of event k
fraction of time spent producing explanations
