children.title: Optional-Interval Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation behavior for intervals controlled by presence literals.

knowledge_statements.title: Optional-Interval Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain propagation for an interval guarded by a Boolean presence literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given integer domains for start \(s\), end \(e\), fixed duration \(p\geq0\), and presence literal \(b\), impose \(b\Rightarrow e=s+p\). If \(b=1\), iterate the bound updates \(\underline e\leftarrow\max(\underline e,\underline s+p)\), \(\overline e\leftarrow\min(\overline e,\overline s+p)\), \(\underline s\leftarrow\max(\underline s,\underline e-p)\), and \(\overline s\leftarrow\min(\overline s,\overline e-p)\). If no pair in the current domains satisfies \(e=s+p\), propagate \(b=0\), or report conflict when \(b=1\). When \(b\) is undecided, bounds justified only by activity remain conditional on \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optional interval obeys its start-end equation when present; impossibility forces absence, while activity-dependent deductions remain guarded.
assumptions_latex: \(s,e\in\mathbb Z\) have finite current bounds.
\(b\in\{0,1\}\) and \(p\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting domains preserve every assignment satisfying \(b\Rightarrow e=s+p\).

notation.meaning: current lower and upper bounds of x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches optional-interval propagation and is internally coherent, but no inspectable source supports the guarded equation, bound updates, or absence deduction.

children.title: Precedence Propagation
children.top_down_role: Bound propagation arising from temporal precedence relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Precedence Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound propagation for a possibly guarded scheduling precedence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For intervals \(i\) and \(j\), lag \(d\in\mathbb Z\), and activation literal \(q\), enforce \(q\Rightarrow s_j\geq e_i+d\). When \(q=1\), update \(\underline s_j\leftarrow\max(\underline s_j,\underline e_i+d)\) and \(\overline e_i\leftarrow\min(\overline e_i,\overline s_j-d)\), repeating with other interval constraints until stable. If \(\underline e_i+d>\overline s_j\), propagate \(q=0\); if \(q=1\), report conflict. Every propagated bound or falsification is emitted with the active precedence and the bounds establishing it as its reason.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active precedence raises the successor start and lowers the predecessor end; incompatible bounds falsify its guard or cause conflict.
assumptions_latex: \(s_j,e_i,d\in\mathbb Z\).
Current bounds enclose all still-feasible values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updates are valid consequences of \(q\Rightarrow s_j\geq e_i+d\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The guarded bound-propagation algorithm fits the leaf, but no cited source supports either the propagation rules or the implementation-specific claim that every deduction is emitted with a reason.

children.title: Presence-Sensitive Precedence Links
children.top_down_role: Precedence relations whose activity depends on interval presence.

knowledge_statements.title: Presence-Sensitive Precedence Links
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean representation of precedence activated by joint interval presence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b_i,b_j\in\{0,1\}\) denote interval presence and introduce \(a_{ij}=b_i\wedge b_j\) using \(a_{ij}\leq b_i\), \(a_{ij}\leq b_j\), and \(a_{ij}\geq b_i+b_j-1\). A presence-sensitive precedence from \(i\) to \(j\) with lag \(d\) is represented by \(a_{ij}\Rightarrow s_j\geq e_i+d\). Thus the temporal inequality is mandatory exactly when both intervals are present. If current bounds imply \(e_i+d>s_j\) for all remaining values, the valid Boolean consequence is \(\neg b_i\vee\neg b_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint presence activates the precedence; if that precedence is impossible, at least one participating interval must be absent.
assumptions_latex: The precedence is intended to apply whenever both intervals are present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_{ij}=b_i\wedge b_j\) and \(a_{ij}\Rightarrow s_j\geq e_i+d\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and joint-presence encoding fit the leaf, but the record has no source for the guarded precedence model or its Boolean consequence.

knowledge_statements.title: No-Overlap Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise disjunctive propagation for optional fixed-duration intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each pair of intervals \(i,j\) with presence literals \(b_i,b_j\), no-overlap requires \((b_i\wedge b_j)\Rightarrow(e_i\leq s_j\vee e_j\leq s_i)\). If both are present and current bounds make \(e_j\leq s_i\) impossible, enforce \(e_i\leq s_j\) and propagate its bounds; symmetrically enforce the reverse order when the first order is impossible. If both orders are impossible, report conflict when both are present, or propagate the presence nogood \(\neg b_i\vee\neg b_j\). Repeat over affected pairs until no bound or literal changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No-overlap propagation fixes the only feasible ordering of two present intervals, or rejects their simultaneous presence when neither ordering works.
assumptions_latex: Each interval satisfies \(e_k=s_k+p_k\) when present.
Durations satisfy \(p_k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All retained assignments satisfy pairwise non-overlap for simultaneously present intervals.

notation.meaning: start, end, and duration of interval k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pairwise algorithm is mathematically plausible, but the broad leaf title can also encompass stronger global no-overlap propagation. A source is needed to establish that this deliberately pairwise scope is appropriate here.

children.title: Cumulative Resource Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation based on aggregate use of capacity-constrained resources.

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Resource Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core feasibility and overload deductions for a discrete cumulative resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integer time, each present activity \(i\) occupying \([s_i,e_i)\) consumes demand \(r_i\geq0\) from capacity \(C\). Feasibility requires \(\sum_{i:b_i=1,\ s_i\leq t<e_i}r_i\leq C\) for every integer \(t\). Consequently, any set of activities forced to cover a time \(t\) whose demands sum above \(C\) certifies conflict. If a compulsory load \(H_{-i}(t)\) from other activities satisfies \(H_{-i}(t)+r_i>C\), every start of \(i\) that would make it cover \(t\) is infeasible and may be removed or excluded by bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative propagation detects compulsory overloads and removes activity placements that would make resource usage exceed capacity.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i,e_i,t\in\mathbb Z\).
\(r_i,C\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\).
Present activities occupy half-open intervals \([s_i,e_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No retained placement may produce load greater than \(C\) at any time.

notation.meaning: compulsory load at t excluding activity i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasibility and overload-filtering property fits cumulative resource propagation, but no source supports the compulsory-load deductions or their stated scope.

children.title: Timetabling Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation based on compulsory task occupancy over time.

knowledge_statements.title: Timetabling Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compulsory-part filtering for a discrete cumulative constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For activity \(i\) with earliest start \(\underline s_i\), latest start \(\overline s_i\), and duration \(p_i\), define its compulsory part as \([\overline s_i,\underline s_i+p_i)\) when this interval is nonempty. Build the profile \(H(t)=\sum_i r_i\mathbf 1\{\overline s_i\leq t<\underline s_i+p_i\}\). If \(H(t)>C\), report conflict. Otherwise, for each activity \(i\), form the profile excluding its own compulsory contribution and delete every candidate start \(u\) for which some \(t\in[u,u+p_i)\) satisfies \(H_{-i}(t)+r_i>C\). Rebuild the profile after domain changes and iterate to stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Timetabling builds a compulsory-load profile, detects overload, and removes starts whose execution would exceed remaining capacity.
assumptions_latex: Activities have fixed integer durations and demands.
Start domains are finite subsets of \(\mathbb Z\).
The resource has constant capacity \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every retained start \(u\) satisfies \(H_{-i}(t)+r_i\leq C\) throughout \([u,u+p_i)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compulsory-part profile algorithm matches timetabling propagation, but its profile construction, domain deletion rule, and fixed-point claim lack an inspectable citation.

children.title: Timetable-Driven Cumulative Filtering
children.top_down_role: Filtering regimes that use timetable occupancy within cumulative reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Timetable-Driven Cumulative Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-filtering operator induced by a compulsory timetable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_i\subset\mathbb Z\) be the current start domain of activity \(i\), with duration \(p_i\), demand \(r_i\), and presence fixed true. Given the compulsory profile \(H_{-i}\) of all other activities, timetable-driven filtering replaces \(D_i\) by \[D_i'=\{u\in D_i: H_{-i}(t)+r_i\leq C\text{ for every integer }t\in[u,u+p_i)\}.\] For an optional activity with undecided presence, each excluded start is conditional on presence; if \(D_i'=\varnothing\), its presence literal is falsified, or a conflict is reported when presence is already true.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The timetable filter retains exactly those starts compatible with the compulsory load of other activities, with deductions guarded for optional activities.
assumptions_latex: \(H_{-i}\) contains only load compulsory under current domains.
\(p_i,r_i,C\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_i\leftarrow D_i'\) is a sound cumulative-domain reduction.

notation.meaning: current start domain of activity i

children.title: Unary Resource Energy Reasoning
children.top_down_role: Energy reasoning specialized to unit-capacity scheduling resources.

knowledge_statements.title: Unary Resource Energy Reasoning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval-energy overload certificate for a unit-capacity unary resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonpreemptive activity \(i\) of duration \(p_i\), earliest start \(\operatorname{est}_i\), and latest completion \(\operatorname{lct}_i\), its mandatory processing inside a window \([a,b)\) is \[w_i(a,b)=\max\{0,p_i-\max(0,a-\operatorname{est}_i)-\max(0,\operatorname{lct}_i-b)\}.\] On a unary resource, the window supplies only \(b-a\) units of processing capacity. Hence \(\sum_i w_i(a,b)>b-a\) is a verifiable infeasibility certificate. Equality exhausts the window and can justify excluding additional processing from it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unary schedule is infeasible when activities must execute more processing inside a window than the window can contain.
assumptions_latex: All considered activities are present and nonpreemptive.
\(a<b\) and durations are nonnegative.
At most one activity may execute at any time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i w_i(a,b)>b-a\Rightarrow\) the current scheduling domains are infeasible.

notation.meaning: minimum processing of activity i forced into the window

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The overload certificate fits the leaf, but the proposed window-processing formula and the equality-based exclusion claim require authoritative verification. The equality claim also needs precise hypotheses describing the additional execution being excluded.

children.title: Cumulative Resource Energy Reasoning
children.top_down_role: Energy reasoning for resources with aggregate capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Resource Energy Reasoning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Window-energy overload certificate for a constant-capacity cumulative resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For activity \(i\) with demand \(r_i\) and mandatory processing \(w_i(a,b)\) inside \([a,b)\), define mandatory resource energy \(E_i(a,b)=r_iw_i(a,b)\). A cumulative resource of constant capacity \(C\) supplies at most \(C(b-a)\) energy in that window. Therefore \[\sum_i E_i(a,b)>C(b-a)\] certifies infeasibility of the current domains. When equality holds, the window has no residual energy; any optional or movable execution requiring positive additional energy inside it must be excluded, shifted, or made absent with an appropriate guarded reason.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative energetic reasoning compares mandatory demand-time inside a window with the window's capacity-time supply.
assumptions_latex: Activities are nonpreemptive with demands \(r_i\geq0\).
The resource capacity \(C\) is constant on \([a,b)\).
\(w_i(a,b)\) is a valid lower bound on processing forced into the window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i r_iw_i(a,b)>C(b-a)\Rightarrow\) infeasibility.

notation.meaning: mandatory resource energy of activity i in the window

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and overload inequality fit cumulative energetic reasoning, but no source establishes the mandatory-energy bound. The equality-based shifting or absence consequences require more precise hypotheses and guarded-reason semantics.

children.title: Capacity-Sensitive Energy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Applicability changes caused by resource-capacity structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity-Sensitive Energy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction and strengthening regimes determined by demands relative to capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For capacity \(C>0\) and demands \(0<r_i\leq C\), energetic feasibility in every window requires \(\sum_i r_iw_i(a,b)\leq C(b-a)\). When \(C=1\) and every \(r_i=1\), this is the unary energy test. Whenever \(r_i+r_j>C\), activities \(i\) and \(j\) cannot overlap and therefore induce a unary pairwise disjunction. More generally, any subset \(S\) with \(\sum_{i\in S}r_i>C\) cannot have all its members executing simultaneously. Thus increasing normalized demands \(r_i/C\) creates stronger disjunctive structure in addition to aggregate energy overload tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Demand-to-capacity ratios determine whether cumulative energy reasoning also yields unary or higher-order non-simultaneity constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(C>0\) is constant.
Each present activity consumes demand \(r_i\) throughout execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_i+r_j>C\Rightarrow\) activities \(i\) and \(j\) cannot overlap; \(C=r_i=1\Rightarrow\) the unary regime.

notation.meaning: processing forced into the selected window

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property matches capacity-sensitive energy regimes and its pairwise non-overlap implication is coherent, but the aggregate energy premise and qualitative strengthening claim have no cited support.

knowledge_statements.title: Energy-Based Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict and bound explanations for cumulative energetic propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=[a,b)\) and let \(S\) be activities whose current bound literals imply mandatory energies \(e_i(I)\). If \(\sum_{i\in S}e_i(I)>C(b-a)\), those literals certify infeasibility: their conjunction implies violation of the cumulative-capacity inequality. For bound propagation, a proposed bound literal \(\ell\) is refuted when the current literals together with \(\ell\) imply \(\sum_{i\in S}e_i(I)>C(b-a)\); the learned explanation is the clause containing the negations of the antecedent literals and \(\neg\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An overload interval and the bound literals forcing its energy form a checkable conflict or bound-propagation explanation.
assumptions_latex: \(C>0\) is constant on \(I\).
Each \(e_i(I)\) is a valid lower bound on activity \(i\)'s energy executed in \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in S}e_i(I)>C(b-a)\) certifies that the explaining literals cannot hold simultaneously.

notation.meaning: mandatory energy of activity i in I

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf, but no source supports the exact energetic antecedents or learned-clause convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Energy-Reasoning Applicability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of classical fixed-duration, fixed-demand energetic reasoning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inequality \(\sum_i q_i p_i\le C(b-a)\) is sound only when every counted activity is forced wholly into \([a,b)\), with fixed duration \(p_i\) and fixed demand \(q_i\). Replacing a variable duration by its upper bound is unsound: with \(C=1\), one activity having \(p\in[0,2]\), demand \(1\), and window \([0,1)\) is feasible at \(p=1\), although the substitution \(p=2\) reports energy \(2>C\cdot1\). Sound extensions must use lower bounds on unavoidable energy and condition optional activities on presence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Energetic tests require unavoidable energy; maximum duration, maximum demand, or unconditional optional energy can create false conflicts.
assumptions_latex: Activities are nonpreemptive unless the energy formula explicitly models preemption.
Variable quantities are replaced only by valid lower bounds on unavoidable interval energy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Using nonmandatory energy in an overload inequality can invalidate the inferred conflict.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but the variable-duration counterexample requires a precise scheduling model and source. The plain statement also mentions maximum demand, which the formal example does not separately establish.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Edge-Finding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edge-finding for one nonpreemptive unary resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonempty activity set \(\Omega\), compute \(\operatorname{ect}(\Omega)\), the earliest completion time of any feasible nonoverlapping schedule of \(\Omega\), and \(L(\Omega)=\max_{i\in\Omega}d_i\). For every \(j\notin\Omega\), test whether \(\operatorname{ect}(\Omega\cup\{j\})>L(\Omega)\). If so, \(j\) cannot precede every activity of \(\Omega\); apply the corresponding edge-finding release-time update justified by the critical subset. Apply the time-reversed test to update deadlines. Iterate until no bound changes or an overload is detected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edge-finding tests activity sets to infer forced ordering, tighten start or completion bounds, and detect unary-resource overloads.
assumptions_latex: Each activity \(i\) has release time \(r_i\), deadline \(d_i\), and fixed duration \(p_i>0\).
Activities are nonpreemptive and pairwise nonoverlapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every emitted bound update removes only schedules violating a certified unary-resource ordering test.

notation.meaning: earliest attainable completion of the set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the exact edge-finding test, critical-subset update, and deadline convention require an authoritative scheduling reference.

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Edge-Finding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Energy-based edge-finding for a constant-capacity cumulative resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate activity set \(\Omega\) and boundary \(L\), compute a valid lower bound \(E(\Omega,L)\) on energy that members of \(\Omega\) must consume before \(L\). For each activity \(j\notin\Omega\), hypothetically place the energy forced by \(j\) before \(L\). If the resulting energy exceeds \(C(L-a)\) on some interval \([a,L)\), reject that ordering and raise the relevant start bound of \(j\); use the symmetric reversed-time test for completion bounds. Iterate valid updates until closure or overload.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative edge-finding rejects hypothetical orderings whose mandatory resource energy exceeds interval capacity and propagates the resulting bounds.
assumptions_latex: Activities are nonpreemptive with fixed positive durations and demands.
The resource has constant capacity \(C>0\).
Every computed energy is a lower bound under the tested ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An ordering is removed only if its unavoidable energy exceeds \(C(L-a)\) on a tested interval.

notation.meaning: lower bound on energy before L

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the energy function and resulting start-bound update are not defined precisely enough to identify and validate a cumulative edge-finding variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Timetable Edge-Finding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid propagation combining compulsory-part timetabling with edge-finding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct the compulsory profile \(h(t)=\sum_i q_i\mathbf 1_{[\overline s_i,\underline e_i)}(t)\), where \(\overline s_i\) is the latest start and \(\underline e_i\) the earliest completion. Reject if \(h(t)>C\). Otherwise, for each candidate ordering and interval \(I\), reserve profile energy \(\int_I h(t)\,dt\) and test the additional unavoidable energy against residual capacity \(C|I|-\int_I h(t)\,dt\). Any overload refutes the ordering and yields a start or completion bound update. Rebuild affected profile segments and iterate to a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Timetable edge-finding reserves compulsory profile capacity before applying ordering-based energy tests to the residual resource.
assumptions_latex: Activities are nonpreemptive with fixed duration and demand.
The cumulative resource has constant capacity \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every detected excess over residual interval capacity certifies a conflict or a valid ordering-bound update.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the additional unavoidable energy must explicitly exclude energy already represented in the compulsory profile. A timetable-edge-finding source is needed to validate the accounting and updates.

children.title: Edge-Finding Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanation structures attached to edge-finding deductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Edge-Finding Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-learning certificates for edge-finding conflicts and bound updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be bound and presence literals fixing the windows used by an edge-finding test. A valid conflict explanation is any subset \(B'\subseteq B\) whose conjunction implies that the tested activities cannot fit within the relevant resource interval. For an inferred bound literal \(u\), a propagation explanation additionally satisfies \(\bigwedge B'\Rightarrow u\). The clauses \(\bigvee_{b\in B'}\neg b\) for conflict and \(\bigvee_{b\in B'}\neg b\vee u\) for propagation are independently checkable certificates; irrelevant literals may be removed while preserving the implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An edge-finding explanation is a subset of bound and presence literals sufficient to imply the conflict or propagated bound.
assumptions_latex: The underlying edge-finding overload or ordering implication is sound.
Each literal in \(B'\) has a defined Boolean encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conflict or propagation clause is valid whenever its antecedent literals entail the edge-finding inference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits and the propositional clause forms are coherent, but the claimed edge-finding explanation interface and literal semantics lack a source.

children.title: Explanation Coverage Gaps
children.top_down_role: Edge-finding deductions lacking adequate explanatory support.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation Coverage Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits imposed by an explanation language or incomplete propagator instrumentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an edge-finding propagator derives \(u\) from internal facts \(H\), but the explanation interface exposes only literals \(B\). If there exist assignments \(x\) and \(y\) agreeing on every literal in \(B\), while \(H\Rightarrow u\) holds at \(x\) and \(u\) is false in a feasible completion of \(y\), then no clause using only \(B\) can explain that particular inference soundly. The propagator must expose additional literals, derive a weaker explainable bound, or omit the inference from clause learning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If exposed literals cannot distinguish states where an inference is valid from states where it fails, no sound explanation clause exists.
assumptions_latex: Explanations are restricted to clauses over the exposed literal set \(B\).
Learned clauses must be valid for every feasible completion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Agreement on \(B\) with differing validity of \(u\) proves an explanation-coverage gap.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but the meanings of internal facts holding at a state and of assignments agreeing on exposed literals require a formal explanation-interface model and source.

children.title: Edge-Finding Weakness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scheduling regimes where edge-finding explanations or deductions lose practical force.

knowledge_statements.title: Edge-Finding Weakness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A cumulative packing conflict invisible to aggregate horizon energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider capacity \(C=3\) on the common horizon \([0,3)\) and two nonpreemptive activities, each with duration \(2\), demand \(2\), release time \(0\), and deadline \(3\). Their total energy is \(8\le9=C\cdot3\), so the aggregate horizon-energy relaxation accepts the instance. Nevertheless, the activities cannot overlap because their combined demand is \(4>C\), and sequential execution requires time \(4>3\). Thus aggregate energetic or weak cumulative edge-finding tests can miss conflicts requiring pairwise demand incompatibility or stronger packing reasoning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two high-demand activities can pass total-energy capacity yet be infeasible because they cannot overlap and do not fit sequentially.
assumptions_latex: Activities are nonpreemptive.
Both activities must execute within \([0,3)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(8\le9\) does not imply cumulative schedulability for this instance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is internally correct and its content kind fits the weakness-regime leaf, but the record supplies neither a cited source nor an explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: No-Overlap Linearizations
children.top_down_role: Linear relaxation structures representing pairwise or global non-overlap.

knowledge_statements.title: No-Overlap Linearizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise big-M representation of a mandatory no-overlap disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For activities \(i\) and \(j\) with start variables \(s_i,s_j\), durations \(p_i,p_j>0\), and ordering variable \(y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\), the no-overlap disjunction \(s_i+p_i\le s_j\) or \(s_j+p_j\le s_i\) is represented by \[s_i+p_i\le s_j+M_{ij}(1-y_{ij}),\qquad s_j+p_j\le s_i+M_{ji}y_{ij}.\] Here \(M_{ij}\) and \(M_{ji}\) are valid upper bounds on the corresponding precedence violations. With finite start bounds, choosing the smallest valid constants strengthens the continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary ordering variable activates one of two precedence inequalities, giving a mixed-integer representation of pairwise non-overlap.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i\) and \(s_j\) have finite bounds sufficient to derive valid big-M constants.
Both activities are present and nonpreemptive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For binary \(y_{ij}\), the two inequalities are equivalent to the pairwise no-overlap disjunction.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
source_refs.locator: 2.2.2 Disjunctive constraints p. 10

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.2 Disjunctive constraints p. 10

children.title: Precedence Linearizations
children.top_down_role: Linear relaxation structures representing temporal order.

knowledge_statements.title: Precedence Linearizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear enforcement of mandatory or conditional scheduling precedence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mandatory precedence \(i\prec j\) is the linear inequality \(s_i+p_i\le s_j\). If it is enforced only when a Boolean literal \(z=1\), a bounded big-M representation is \(s_i+p_i\le s_j+M(1-z)\), where \(M\ge \overline s_i+p_i-\underline s_j\). Equivalently, a solver may store the inequality with enforcement literal \(z\). For optional activities with presence literals \(x_i,x_j\), joint enforcement uses a literal equivalent to \(z\wedge x_i\wedge x_j\), preventing absent activities from imposing precedence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Precedence is a linear completion-before-start inequality, optionally activated by ordering and presence literals.
assumptions_latex: \(\underline s_k\le s_k\le\overline s_k\) are finite bounds on each relevant start variable \(s_k\).
The duration \(p_i\) is fixed and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the enforcement literal is true, every feasible solution satisfies \(s_i+p_i\le s_j\).

children.title: Coupled Ordering Linearizations
children.top_down_role: Relaxation structures linking non-overlap choices to precedence relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Ordering Linearizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint ordering formulation with exclusivity and transitivity constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For mandatory pairwise nonoverlapping activities, let \(y_{ij}=1\) mean that \(i\) precedes \(j\). Couple the precedence inequalities to the ordering variables and impose \(y_{ij}+y_{ji}=1\) for each distinct pair. For distinct \(i,j,k\), the transitivity inequality \(y_{ij}+y_{jk}-1\le y_{ik}\) excludes directed ordering cycles. Together with valid precedence linearizations, these constraints represent a consistent total order on every set of simultaneously present activities; for optional activities, the pair and transitivity constraints must be conditioned on the relevant presence literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise ordering binaries become globally consistent when linked to precedence, exclusivity, transitivity, and activity presence.
assumptions_latex: Ordering variables are binary.
Every considered mandatory pair must be nonoverlapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled binary variables encode an acyclic total ordering of the simultaneously present activities.

notation.meaning: one when activity i precedes activity j

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative-Energy Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval-energy necessary inequalities for nonpreemptive cumulative scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each interval \(I=[a,b)\), define the unavoidable processing time of activity \(i\) inside \(I\) by \(w_i(I)=\max\{0,p_i-\max(0,a-r_i)-\max(0,d_i-b)\}\). Every feasible cumulative schedule satisfies \[\sum_i q_i w_i(I)\le C(b-a).\] Imposing these inequalities for selected intervals gives a cumulative-energy relaxation. The inequalities are necessary but generally not sufficient because they aggregate resource consumption and may omit incompatibilities caused by nonpreemption or large simultaneous demands.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each interval must have enough capacity for the processing energy that activity windows force into it.
assumptions_latex: Activity \(i\) is nonpreemptive with release time \(r_i\), deadline \(d_i\), duration \(p_i\), and demand \(q_i\ge0\).
The resource has constant capacity \(C>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible schedule obeys \(\sum_i q_iw_i([a,b))\le C(b-a)\) for all \(a<b\).

notation.meaning: unavoidable processing time of activity i in I

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role and interval-energy inequality fit the leaf, but the exact unavoidable-processing formula and its scheduling assumptions require a specific energetic-reasoning source.

children.title: Completion-Time Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxations organized around task completion variables and temporal aggregates.

knowledge_statements.title: Completion-Time Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection of a discrete-time packing relaxation onto job completion variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let jobs be indexed by \(J\), let \(T_i\) be the admissible integer start times of job \(i\), and let \(p_i>0\) be its processing time. Given a packing-relaxation polyhedron \(P_{\mathrm{pack}}\) in variables \(x_{it}\), define \[C_i=\sum_{t\in T_i}(t+p_i)x_{it}\qquad(i\in J).\] The associated completion-time relaxation is the projection \[P_C=\left\{C\in\mathbb R^{J}:\exists x\in P_{\mathrm{pack}}\text{ such that }C_i=\sum_{t\in T_i}(t+p_i)x_{it}\ \forall i\in J\right\}.\] Every feasible nonpreemptive schedule induces a point of \(P_C\); hence minimizing any linear completion objective over \(P_C\) gives a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Completion variables are obtained by projecting a fractional time-indexed packing model. Every feasible schedule remains represented, so optimizing over the projection yields a valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) and every \(T_i\) are finite.
\(P_{\mathrm{pack}}\) contains every integral start-time encoding of a feasible schedule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{C(S):S\text{ is a feasible schedule}\}\subseteq P_C\).

notation.meaning: fraction of job i assigned start time t

review_flags: No supplied source directly supports this scheduling-specific projection formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the Completion-Time Relaxations leaf and the projection claim is plausible, but no cited source supports this scheduling-specific formulation. The phrase "any linear completion objective" also needs a precise objective domain and feasible-schedule optimization problem before the lower-bound claim can be source-checked.

children.title: Packing Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxations based on capacity usage and packing structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Packing Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-indexed linear relaxation for nonpreemptive jobs sharing a renewable resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each job \(i\in J\), let \(p_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), demand \(q_i>0\), and admissible integer start set \(T_i\) be given; let the resource capacity be \(Q>0\). The time-indexed packing relaxation is \[P_{\mathrm{pack}}=\left\{x:\sum_{t\in T_i}x_{it}=1\ \forall i,\quad \sum_{i\in J}q_i\sum_{\substack{t\in T_i:\\t\le \tau<t+p_i}}x_{it}\le Q\ \forall \tau,\quad 0\le x_{it}\le1\right\}.\] Requiring \(x_{it}\in\{0,1\}\) selects one start per job and enforces capacity at every time; relaxing integrality produces a linear outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional start-time assignment chooses one start distribution per job while respecting resource capacity at every time point.
assumptions_latex: Time is discretized over a finite integer horizon.
Each job uses constant demand \(q_i\) throughout its processing interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\mathrm{integer}}\subseteq P_{\mathrm{pack}}\).

notation.meaning: admissible start times of job i

review_flags: No supplied source directly supports the stated time-indexed scheduling relaxation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is appropriate for the Packing Relaxations leaf, but no scheduling source is cited. The capacity constraints quantify over an undefined time index tau; a source-backed replacement should explicitly specify the finite horizon or set of capacity-checking times.

children.title: Completion-Based Packing Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bound-producing links between completion structure and packing capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Completion-Based Packing Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset completion inequality for jobs packed on one unit-capacity machine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be nonpreemptive jobs processed without overlap on one unit-capacity machine, with processing times \(p_i>0\), nonnegative start times, and completion times \(C_i\). For every subset \(S\subseteq J\), the completion vector satisfies the packing inequality \[\sum_{i\in S}p_iC_i\ge \frac12\left(\left(\sum_{i\in S}p_i\right)^2+\sum_{i\in S}p_i^2\right).\] Consequently, violation of this inequality by a candidate completion vector certifies that the vector cannot arise from a feasible nonoverlapping schedule. The full family over all subsets is a valid strengthening of a completion-time relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every job subset must have sufficiently large processing-time-weighted completions. A violated subset inequality certifies that the candidate completion vector is not schedulable.
assumptions_latex: All jobs in \(S\) require the same unit-capacity machine.
Processing is nonpreemptive and start times are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \sum_{i\in S}p_iC_i\ge\frac12\left((\sum_{i\in S}p_i)^2+\sum_{i\in S}p_i^2\right)\) for every \(S\subseteq J\).
review_flags: The supplied locator hints do not identify a source for this scheduling inequality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subset inequality is mathematically plausible for nonpreemptive single-machine schedules with nonnegative start times, and its use as an infeasibility certificate fits the leaf. However, the specialized inequality and the claimed strengthening are unsupported by any cited scheduling source.

children.top_down_role: Covers the Boolean search kernel and its coordination with integer and scheduling propagators.
