children.title: Lifted Cuts
children.top_down_role: Strengthened cuts obtained by extending a base inequality to additional variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-variable lifting of a valid inequality from a binary face, with a nonempty restored branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), let \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(b\in\mathbb R\) satisfy \(a_j=0\). Suppose \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is valid for \(X_0=\{x\in X:x_j=0\}\), and suppose \(X_1=\{x\in X:x_j=1\}\) is nonempty. Compute \(M_j=\max\{a^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X_1\}\) and set \(\gamma_j=b-M_j\). The lifted inequality \[a^{\mathsf T}x+\gamma_jx_j\le b\] is valid for \(X\). Applying the same construction successively can restore additional binary variables fixed on the original face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty restored branch, the exact coefficient of a restored binary variable is the original right-hand side minus the largest unlifted left-hand side on the branch where that variable equals one.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) and \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
\(a\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R\), and \(a_j=0\).
\(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is valid for \(X_0\).
\(X_1\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x+(b-M_j)x_j\le b\) is valid for \(X\).

notation.meaning: face where the lifted variable is fixed to zero
restored branch where the lifted variable equals one
maximum unlifted left-hand side on the restored branch

children.title: Cut-Lifting Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Validity and strength limits for lifting disjunctive or base cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Lifting Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, uniqueness, and order boundaries for exact one-variable lifting of a binary coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and suppose \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(x\in X\). Let \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(b\in\mathbb R\), with \(a_j=0\), and suppose \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is valid on \(X_0=\{x\in X:x_j=0\}\). For the restored branch \(X_1=\{x\in X:x_j=1\}\), if \(X_1\ne\varnothing\), define \(\theta_j=\sup\{a^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X_1\}\). A finite exact coefficient \(\gamma_j=b-\theta_j\) exists only when \(\theta_j<+\infty\). If \(\theta_j=+\infty\), no finite \(\gamma_j\) makes \(a^{\mathsf T}x+\gamma_jx_j\le b\) valid for \(X\). If \(X_1=\varnothing\), every finite coefficient is valid on the absent branch, so no unique strongest finite coefficient is determined. In sequential lifting, the resulting coefficients may depend on the order in which variables are restored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a binary lifted coordinate, an unbounded nonempty restored branch prevents any finite lifted coefficient, an empty restored branch prevents a unique strongest finite coefficient, and sequential coefficients may depend on restoration order.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(x\in X\).
\(a\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R\), and \(a_j=0\).
\(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is valid on \(X_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite exact coefficient exists when \(X_1\ne\varnothing\) and \(\theta_j=+\infty\); no unique strongest finite coefficient is determined when \(X_1=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: branch where the lifted coordinate equals zero
restored branch where the lifted coordinate equals one
supremum of the unlifted left-hand side on the restored branch

children.title: Cut Validity
children.top_down_role: Soundness criteria for relaxation cuts admitted by the solver.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global validity of a linear inequality for a feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set and let \(c^{\mathsf T}x\le d\) be a linear inequality. The inequality is valid for \(F\) if and only if \[c^{\mathsf T}x\le d\qquad\text{for every }x\in F.\] Equivalently, \(F\subseteq\{x:c^{\mathsf T}x\le d\}\). It is a separating cut for a relaxation point \(\bar x\) only if it is valid and \(c^{\mathsf T}\bar x>d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is valid when every feasible point satisfies it; it separates a relaxation point when that point violates the valid inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
\(c\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(d\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validity is equivalent to \(F\subseteq\{x:c^{\mathsf T}x\le d\}\).

children.title: Cut Applicability Scope
children.top_down_role: Model states, assumptions, and local contexts in which a cut remains applicable.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Applicability Scope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global, subtree-local, and node-local domains of cut enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a search tree with node set \(T\), associate each node \(v\) with a domain \(F_v\) satisfying the decisions on its root-to-node path. The applicability scope of a cut \(c^{\mathsf T}x\le d\) is a set \(S\subseteq T\) such that the cut is valid for every \(F_v\) with \(v\in S\). A global cut has \(S=T\); a cut derived under node \(u\)'s assumptions may use the descendant scope \(S=\operatorname{desc}(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut’s scope is the collection of search nodes whose path-conditioned feasible sets all satisfy it; global cuts cover the entire tree.
assumptions_latex: Each search node \(v\) has a path-conditioned feasible set \(F_v\).
The cut is valid for every \(F_v\) in its declared scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut may be enforced only at nodes \(v\in S\) unless validity is established on a larger scope.

notation.meaning: feasible set conditioned by node v

children.title: Scope-Sensitive Cut Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity dependencies arising from local, conditional, or incremental scope.

knowledge_statements.title: Scope-Sensitive Cut Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity inheritance and invalid reuse across search-tree scopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_v\) denote the feasible set at search node \(v\), and suppose descendants strengthen ancestor decisions, so \(F_w\subseteq F_v\) whenever \(w\) descends from \(v\). If \(c^{\mathsf T}x\le d\) is valid for \(F_v\), then it is valid for every descendant set \(F_w\). The converse need not hold: a cut derived using assumptions introduced at \(v\) may be invalid at an ancestor or outside \(v\)'s subtree and therefore must not be enforced there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validity propagates from a node to its descendants, but a locally valid cut cannot generally be moved to ancestors or unrelated branches.
assumptions_latex: \(F_w\subseteq F_v\) whenever \(w\) descends from \(v\).
\(c^{\mathsf T}x\le d\) is valid for \(F_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^{\mathsf T}x\le d\) is valid for every descendant \(F_w\), but not necessarily outside that subtree.

notation.meaning: feasible set at search node v
feasible set at a descendant node w

children.title: Cut Selection
children.top_down_role: Admission and prioritization of candidate cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted selection from cuts violated at the current relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation point \(\bar x\), candidate inequalities \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\), and budget \(k\), compute violations \(v_i=a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b_i\). Discard candidates with \(v_i\le\varepsilon\) or invalid applicability scope. Assign each remaining cut a score, for example \(s_i=v_i/\lVert a_i\rVert_2\), optionally suppressing near-parallel or duplicate cuts. Select at most \(k\) highest-scoring admissible cuts, add them to the relaxation, and reoptimize.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter invalid or insignificant candidates, rank the remaining cuts by normalized violation, retain a budgeted diverse subset, and reoptimize.
assumptions_latex: Every candidate has been validated on the current node's scope.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\) and \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
Each retained cut has \(\lVert a_i\rVert_2>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output contains at most \(k\) scope-valid cuts with violation exceeding \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: selection score of candidate cut i

children.title: Cut Efficacy
children.top_down_role: Measures of expected relaxation improvement from candidate cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Efficacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean distance-based efficacy at a relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonzero inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) and relaxation point \(\bar x\), define its violation by \(v(\bar x)=a^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b\). Its Euclidean efficacy is \[\operatorname{eff}(a,b;\bar x)=\frac{\max\{0,v(\bar x)\}}{\lVert a\rVert_2}.\] This quantity is invariant under positive rescaling of the inequality and equals the Euclidean distance from \(\bar x\) to the boundary hyperplane when the cut is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut efficacy is positive violation divided by the coefficient norm, making it scale-invariant and equal to distance from a violated cut hyperplane.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\), \(b\in\mathbb R\), and \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{eff}(a,b;\bar x)=\max\{0,a^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b\}/\lVert a\rVert_2\).

notation.meaning: signed cut violation at the relaxation point

children.title: Cut Aging
children.top_down_role: Retention and removal behavior for cuts over repeated relaxation solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Aging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic age counter for governing cuts in a repeatedly solved linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each retained valid cut \(j\), initialize its age by \(a_j=0\). After relaxation solve \(t\), compute a prescribed activity indicator \(u_j^t\in\{0,1\}\), where \(u_j^t=1\) means that the cut is active or otherwise useful. Update \[a_j\leftarrow\begin{cases}0,&u_j^t=1,\\a_j+1,&u_j^t=0.\end{cases}\] Given an age limit \(A\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\), remove cut \(j\) from the active relaxation when \(a_j>A\), unless it belongs to a protected class. Removal affects only the relaxation representation and does not revoke the cut's validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reset a useful cut's age to zero, increment it otherwise, and remove an unprotected cut once its age exceeds a fixed limit.
assumptions_latex: Each retained inequality is valid for the integer-feasible set.
The activity indicator and protected classes are fixed by the solver policy.
\(A\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every unprotected cut unused for more than \(A\) consecutive relaxation solves is removed from the active relaxation.

notation.meaning: activity or usefulness indicator at solve t

children.title: Efficacy-Sensitive Retention
children.top_down_role: Cut-lifecycle policies combining measured utility with age.

knowledge_statements.title: Efficacy-Sensitive Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retention policy combining recent cut efficacy with age and a finite cut budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At relaxation solution \(x^t\), assign each cut \(a_j^Tx\le b_j\) normalized violation \(e_j^t=\max\{0,a_j^Tx^t-b_j\}/\lVert a_j\rVert_2\). Update a score by \(s_j^t=\lambda s_j^{t-1}+(1-\lambda)e_j^t\), where \(0\le\lambda<1\). Protect cuts required by correctness; among all other cuts, retain at most \(B\) cuts having the largest scores, subject to deleting any cut whose age exceeds \(A\). Ties are resolved by a fixed rule. The output is the resulting active cut pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain high-scoring cuts under a pool budget, while protecting mandatory cuts and deleting sufficiently old unprotected cuts.
assumptions_latex: All scored inequalities are valid for the integer-feasible set.
\(B,A\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(0\le\lambda<1\).
Cut norms are nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unprotected retained pool has cardinality at most \(B\) and favors cuts with greater recent normalized violation.

notation.meaning: normalized violation of cut j at solve t

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Strength–Cost Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A budgeted selection principle for valid cuts used in a linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\supseteq F\) be a relaxation of the feasible set and let each candidate valid cut \(i\) have predicted bound improvement \(g_i\ge0\) and processing cost \(c_i>0\). For a cut budget \(C>0\), select a subset \(S\) by the optimization surrogate \[\max_{S}\ G(S)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{i\in S}c_i\le C,\] where \(G(S)\) estimates the bound improvement obtained from intersecting \(R\) with the selected halfspaces. Thus cut strength is evaluated jointly with separation, insertion, and repeated relaxation-solve cost; validity alone does not imply retention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose valid cuts by predicted bound gain under a computational budget, because stronger relaxations can cost more to separate and solve.
assumptions_latex: Every candidate cut contains \(F\).
Costs are positive and the budget is finite.
\(G(S)\) is a specified prediction or measured surrogate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A governance policy may reject a valid strong cut when its marginal predicted gain is insufficient relative to its computational cost.

notation.meaning: predicted bound gain from selected cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Implied Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A bound on one variable that is valid only under an explicit Boolean condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^m\times\mathbb Z^n\), let \(\ell:\{0,1\}^m\to\{0,1\}\) be a Boolean literal, and let \(x_k\) be an integer variable. A conditional implied lower bound is a value \(L\in\mathbb Z\) satisfying \[\forall (z,x)\in F:\quad \ell(z)=1\Longrightarrow x_k\ge L.\] Equivalently, the implication may be encoded as \(x_k\ge L-M(1-\ell(z))\) whenever a finite valid value of \(M\) makes the inequality nonrestrictive for feasible points with \(\ell(z)=0\). A conditional upper bound \(U\in\mathbb Z\) is defined analogously by \(\ell(z)=1\Longrightarrow x_k\le U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional implied bound restricts an integer variable whenever a designated Boolean literal is true; a valid big-M encoding must remain nonrestrictive when that literal is false.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^m\times\mathbb Z^n\).
Any big-M encoding uses a finite value valid for every point of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever \((z,x)\in F\) and \(\ell(z)=1\), the corresponding lower or upper bound holds for \(x_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: LP-Derived Bound Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-bound strengthening obtained from a valid linear relaxation at a search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with integer objective \(c^Tx\), let \(F_N\) be the feasible set at search node \(N\), and let \(P_N\supseteq F_N\) be a linear relaxation. If \(z_{LP}(N)=\inf\{c^Tx:x\in P_N\}\) is finite, then every \(x\in F_N\) satisfies \(c^Tx\ge z_{LP}(N)\). Hence the node's integral objective lower bound may be strengthened to \(L_N'=\max\{L_N,\lceil z_{LP}(N)\rceil\}\). The node is infeasible whenever \(P_N=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node LP supplies a valid minimization lower bound; round it upward for an integral objective and combine it with the existing bound.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(F_N\subseteq P_N\).
\(c^Tx\) is integral on \(F_N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N'=\max\{L_N,\lceil z_{LP}(N)\rceil\}\) is a valid lower bound for every feasible completion at node \(N\).

children.title: Propagation-Derived Objective Bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Derived Objective Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective bounds inferred by sound domain propagation at a search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_N\) be the feasible completions at node \(N\), and suppose sound propagation produces domains \(x_i\in D_i^N\) containing every coordinate of every point in \(F_N\). For the separable linear minimization objective \(f(x)=\sum_i c_ix_i\), define \[L_{\mathrm{prop}}(N)=\sum_{c_i\ge0}c_i\min D_i^N+\sum_{c_i<0}c_i\max D_i^N.\] Then \(f(x)\ge L_{\mathrm{prop}}(N)\) for all \(x\in F_N\). Additional sound propagators may replace this separable bound by any larger value that they certify for all feasible completions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound propagated variable domains yield a valid objective lower bound by minimizing each linear objective term over its current domain.
assumptions_latex: Propagation never removes a feasible completion.
Every \(D_i^N\) is nonempty and has finite extrema.
The objective is \(f(x)=\sum_i c_ix_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{prop}}(N)\) is a valid lower bound on the objective over \(F_N\).

notation.meaning: propagated domain of variable i at node N

children.title: Search-Derived Objective Bounds
children.top_down_role: Objective bounds produced from explored search states and incumbent information.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Derived Objective Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global primal and dual bounds accumulated from incumbent solutions and exhaustive search reasoning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization of \(f\) over a feasible set \(F\), with optimum \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). Every feasible incumbent \(\bar x\in F\) gives an upper bound \(U=f(\bar x)\). Let \(\mathcal O\) be a nonempty finite set of open search regions whose union contains every feasible point not already resolved, and suppose each region \(F_N\), \(N\in\mathcal O\), has a certified lower bound \(L_N\le\inf_{x\in F_N}f(x)\). Then \[L=\min_{N\in\mathcal O}L_N\] is a global lower bound on every unresolved feasible point. A region with \(L_N\ge U\) may be pruned. If no open region remains, exhaustive resolution with an incumbent certifies that the best incumbent is optimal; exhaustive resolution without any incumbent certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent supplies an upper bound, and the minimum certified bound over a nonempty frontier supplies a lower bound for every unresolved feasible point; exhausting the frontier certifies optimality or infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
While \(\mathcal O\ne\varnothing\), the open regions cover every unresolved feasible point.
Each \(L_N\) is valid for its region \(F_N\).
Every removed region is resolved by infeasibility, exhaustive processing, or valid pruning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: While \(\mathcal O\ne\varnothing\), \(L\) bounds every unresolved feasible point from below; exhaustive resolution proves optimality when an incumbent exists and infeasibility otherwise.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound for open region N
minimum lower bound over the nonempty open frontier

children.title: Cross-Channel Bound Sharing
children.top_down_role: Exchange of objective-bound improvements between propagation and search.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Channel Bound Sharing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone exchange of certified global objective bounds among concurrent solver channels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization of \(f\) over a global feasible set \(F\) with optimum \(f^*\), maintain shared bounds \((L,U)\) initialized so that \(L\le f^*\le U\). When a channel submits a globally certified lower bound \(\widehat L\le f^*\), atomically update \(L\leftarrow\max\{L,\widehat L\}\). When a channel submits the value \(\widehat U=f(\widehat x)\) of a feasible point \(\widehat x\in F\), atomically update \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,\widehat U\}\). Each channel may import these global bounds for its subproblem. A bound certified only for a local scope is not merged into the global pair and may be imported separately only when its declared scope contains the receiving subproblem. For exact objective comparison, stop with an optimality certificate when \(L\ge U\); otherwise return the best shared bounds at termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Channels share global certified lower bounds by maximum and global feasible incumbent values by minimum; locally scoped bounds remain separate and may be used only on contained subproblems.
assumptions_latex: Every lower bound merged into \(L\) is valid for the global feasible set \(F\).
Every upper-bound submission is \(f(\widehat x)\) for some \(\widehat x\in F\).
Atomic updates and validity-scope metadata are observed consistently.
Optimality termination uses the solver's exact objective comparison convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The global shared bounds remain valid and monotone: \(L\) never decreases, \(U\) never increases, and \(L\le f^*\le U\).

notation.meaning: bound contributions submitted by a solver channel

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Objective-Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation rule for compatible objective bounds produced by multiple solver mechanisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with optimum \(f^*\), initialize shared valid bounds \(L_0\le f^*\le U_0\). Upon receiving certified lower bounds \(L_1,\ldots,L_p\) and feasible-solution values \(U_1,\ldots,U_q\), update \[L\leftarrow\max\{L_0,L_1,\ldots,L_p\},\qquad U\leftarrow\min\{U_0,U_1,\ldots,U_q\}.\] Publish a tightening only if it improves the stored bound and preserves its validity scope. For an integral objective, a real lower bound may first be replaced by its ceiling. Output the tightened interval \([L,U]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate compatible lower bounds by maximum and feasible upper bounds by minimum, publishing only valid improvements with appropriate scope.
assumptions_latex: Each \(L_i\) is a valid lower bound for the same declared scope.
Each \(U_j\) is attained by a feasible solution in that scope.
Objective scaling and integrality conventions are consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated interval is no weaker than the initial interval and remains valid: \(L_0\le L\le f^*\le U\le U_0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Relaxation Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure regime where a relaxation contains points with substantially better objective values than every integer-feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, let \(F\subseteq P\) be a nonempty integer-feasible set and a relaxation, and suppose \(z_F=\inf_{x\in F}c^Tx\) and \(z_P=\inf_{x\in P}c^Tx\) are finite. The relaxation is weak for this objective when the additive gap \(g=z_F-z_P\ge0\) is large relative to the relevant objective scale. For \(F_k=\{x\in\{0,1\}^k:\sum_{i=1}^k x_i\ge1\}\), let \(P_k=[0,1]^k\), which omits the covering constraint. With objective \(\sum_{i=1}^k x_i\), one has \(z_F=1\) and \(z_P=0\). Thus this relaxation supplies no positive objective lower bound, even though every feasible integer solution has value at least one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation is weak for an objective when it admits objective-favorable points excluded by the original feasible set and consequently produces a large or uninformative relaxation gap.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(F\) is nonempty and \(F\subseteq P\).
Both displayed optimal values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A large gap \(g=z_F-z_P\) weakens relaxation-based pruning, and the displayed family has \(g=1\) for every integer \(k\ge1\).

children.title: Relaxation Scaling Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Coefficient-range and normalization problems affecting relaxation behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Scaling Pathologies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of numerical reliability caused by equivalent formulations with badly scaled rows or columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a linear relaxation \(Ax\le b\). Replacing row \(i\) by \(\alpha_i a_i^Tx\le\alpha_i b_i\), with \(\alpha_i>0\), preserves the exact feasible set but changes floating-point magnitudes. If \(\max_i\lVert \alpha_i a_i\rVert/\min_{i:\,a_i\ne0}\lVert \alpha_i a_i\rVert\) is very large, fixed absolute feasibility and pivot tolerances become scale dependent: a residual accepted in one row may correspond to a materially different unscaled violation in another. Consequently, mathematically equivalent scalings can yield different numerical feasibility decisions, unstable bases, or unreliable relaxation bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive row scaling preserves exact feasibility but can make floating-point tolerances inconsistent, causing unstable solves and unreliable bound decisions.
assumptions_latex: Relaxation computations use finite-precision arithmetic.
Feasibility or pivot tests use nonzero numerical tolerances.
All row multipliers satisfy \(\alpha_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact equivalence under positive scaling does not imply numerically equivalent relaxation behavior when coefficient magnitudes span an extreme range.

children.title: Numerical Degradation
children.top_down_role: Loss of reliability or usefulness caused by finite-precision effects.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision failure boundary for trusting relaxation feasibility and objective bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a relaxation solver return \(\widehat x\) and claimed lower bound \(\widehat z\) for a minimization problem. Define the primal residual \(r_p=\lVert(A\widehat x-b)_+\rVert_\infty\). If \(r_p\) exceeds the scale-adjusted feasibility tolerance, or if a dual certificate for \(\widehat z\) has residual exceeding its scale-adjusted tolerance, then neither feasibility of \(\widehat x\) nor validity of \(\widehat z\) is certified at the required numerical standard. Such a bound must not be used for irreversible pruning without exact verification, safe outward rounding, or a validated error allowance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large primal or dual residuals invalidate reliance on a floating-point relaxation result for irreversible pruning unless the result is safely verified.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation is solved in finite precision.
Pruning requires a certified minimization lower bound.
Scale-adjusted primal and dual tolerances are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of the residual tests places \(\widehat x\) or \(\widehat z\) outside the trusted numerical regime for correctness-critical deductions.

children.title: Scale-Sensitive Numerical Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Sensitive Numerical Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when equivalent rescaling can change floating-point relaxation behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the relaxation be \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\). For a row index \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), replace \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) by \(s_i a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le s_i b_i\), where \(s_i>0\). In exact arithmetic this preserves \(P\). A scale-sensitive numerical regime occurs when, under fixed feasibility and optimality tolerances, this transformation changes at least one computed outcome: acceptance of a row, detected feasibility, selected cut, relaxation bound, or solver termination status. Thus mathematical equivalence under positive row scaling does not imply computational invariance in finite precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive row scaling preserves the exact relaxation but may change computed feasibility, cuts, bounds, or termination when fixed tolerances and finite precision are used.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
All scaling factors satisfy \(s_i>0\).
Relaxations are processed in finite precision with fixed numerical tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is unchanged exactly, while the computed relaxation process need not be invariant under the scaling.

notation.meaning: positive scaling factor for relaxation row i
row i of the matrix A

children.title: Cut-Pool Growth
children.top_down_role: Covers excessive cut accumulation, retention pressure, and pool-management burden.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Pool Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines unproductive cut-pool expansion relative to bound improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At relaxation round \(t\), let \(C_t\) be the retained cut pool and let \(L_t\) be a valid lower bound for a minimization problem. Suppose \(C_t\subseteq C_{t+1}\), and define \(g_t=|C_{t+1}\setminus C_t|\) and \(\Delta_t=L_{t+1}-L_t\ge 0\). For a finite index set \(T\), a prescribed growth threshold \(G>0\), and a bound-improvement tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), cut-pool growth is overhead-dominant when \(\sum_{t\in T}g_t\ge G\) while \(\sum_{t\in T}\Delta_t\le\varepsilon\). In this regime, retained cuts expand relaxation-processing work without material bound production under the prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut-pool growth is overhead-dominant when cumulative retained-cut growth exceeds a prescribed threshold while cumulative bound improvement remains within its tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem and each \(L_t\) is a valid lower bound.
Cuts are retained monotonically during the rounds being assessed.
\(T\) is finite, \(G>0\), and \(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{t\in T}g_t\ge G\) together with \(\sum_{t\in T}\Delta_t\le\varepsilon\) identifies unproductive cut-pool growth under the prescribed thresholds.

notation.meaning: retained cut pool after round t
valid relaxation lower bound after round t
new-cut count and bound improvement at round t

children.title: LP Processing Overhead
children.top_down_role: Covers relaxation-processing costs that outweigh useful bound production.

knowledge_statements.title: LP Processing Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies relaxation-processing cost that dominates runtime without material search progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a search interval \(I\), let \(T_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)\) be the time spent constructing, solving, and maintaining linear relaxations, and let \(T_{\mathrm{tot}}(I)>0\) be total solver time. Define \(\rho_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)=T_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)/T_{\mathrm{tot}}(I)\in[0,1]\). For a prescribed threshold \(\tau\in(0,1)\), LP processing is overhead-dominant on \(I\) when \(\rho_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)\ge\tau\) while neither the certified bound nor the incumbent improves beyond its prescribed significance tolerance on \(I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LP processing is overhead-dominant when it consumes at least a prescribed share of runtime without material bound or incumbent improvement.
assumptions_latex: Timing categories are disjoint and cover the measured interval \(I\).
Bound and incumbent improvements have fixed significance tolerances.
\(T_{\mathrm{tot}}(I)>0\) and \(\tau\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)\ge\tau\) together with negligible certified progress classifies \(I\) as LP-overhead-dominant.

notation.meaning: linear-relaxation processing time on interval I
total solver time on interval I
fraction of total time spent on LP processing

children.title: Dominance Crossover Regimes
children.top_down_role: Identifies regimes where cut maintenance or LP work becomes the principal runtime cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Crossover Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locates the point where relaxation cost overtakes its search savings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compare two otherwise identical search configurations on a common workload: configuration \(R\) uses relaxation processing and configuration \(B\) omits it. For each progress index \(k\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(T_R(k)\) and \(T_B(k)\) be their expected cumulative times to complete progress units \(1,\ldots,k\), including all propagation, relaxation, and node-processing costs. A dominance crossover occurs at \(k^*\in\mathbb{N}\) when \(T_R(k)<T_B(k)\) for every \(k<k^*\), but \(T_R(k)\ge T_B(k)\) for every \(k\ge k^*\) in the assessed range. Beyond \(k^*\), relaxation processing no longer reduces expected cumulative time relative to the baseline.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A crossover occurs when relaxation processing changes from reducing expected cumulative search time to matching or exceeding the baseline time.
assumptions_latex: Both configurations solve the same model under the same correctness and stopping requirements.
Expected times use a common workload distribution and progress definition.
The assessed range exhibits the stated single-crossover ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every assessed \(k\ge k^*\), configuration \(R\) is not faster in expectation than configuration \(B\).

notation.meaning: configurations with and without relaxation processing
expected cumulative times through progress unit k

children.title: Bound-Production Collapse
children.top_down_role: Covers poor bound progress resulting from excessive relaxation overhead.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Production Collapse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes sustained relaxation effort yielding effectively no bound progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization search, let \(L_t\) be the best certified lower bound after relaxation event \(t\), and let \(w_t>0\) measure the event's computational work. Over windows \(W_k\), define the production rate \(r_k=(L_{\max W_k}-L_{\min W_k})/(\sum_{t\in W_k}w_t).\) Bound-production collapse occurs when \(\sum_{t\in W_k}w_t\) remains positive and substantial but \(r_k\to0\), with the incumbent and correctness requirements fixed. Relaxation work then ceases to produce material certified progress per unit work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound production collapses when substantial relaxation work yields a bound-improvement rate converging to zero.
assumptions_latex: Each \(L_t\) is a valid lower bound for the same minimization problem.
The windows use a consistent positive work measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_k\to0\) identifies asymptotically vanishing certified bound gain per unit relaxation work.

notation.meaning: best certified lower bound after event t
relaxation work charged to event t

review_flags: Authoritative source needed for this operational collapse criterion.

children.title: Single-Solution Mode
children.top_down_role: Covers search configured to return one qualifying solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Solution Mode
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility search terminating at the first complete solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite-domain constraint model \(M\). Initialize the search frontier with the root state. Repeatedly select a frontier state, propagate its constraints, discard it if inconsistent, and otherwise branch if some variable remains unfixed. If propagation produces a complete assignment \(x\) satisfying every constraint of \(M\), return \(x\) immediately and stop. If the frontier becomes empty first, return \(\mathrm{INFEASIBLE}\). The mode makes no claim that another feasible assignment is absent after returning \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search stops at the first feasible complete assignment; exhaustion before finding one certifies infeasibility, but one returned solution does not establish uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: Every variable of \(M\) has a finite domain.
Branching is exhaustive and propagation never removes a feasible completion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either one feasible assignment \(x\) or \(\mathrm{INFEASIBLE}\) after exhaustive search.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: This is the standard exhaustive finite-domain search stopping convention.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: All-Solution Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Covers exhaustive traversal of qualifying solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: All-Solution Enumeration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive enumeration of distinct feasible assignments for a finite-domain model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite-domain constraint model \(M\) with variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\). Initialize an empty output set \(S\) and the root search state. Repeatedly propagate and branch exhaustively. Whenever a complete feasible assignment \(x\) is reached, emit it once, insert it into \(S\), and continue search with that assignment excluded. Stop only when the remaining search space is proved empty, and return \(S\). Consequently, \(S=\{x:x\text{ satisfies }M\}\), with no duplicate assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solver emits each feasible assignment once and continues until exhaustive search proves that no unreported solution remains.
assumptions_latex: All variable domains are finite.
Branching covers every feasible completion and propagation is sound.
Previously emitted assignments are excluded without excluding distinct assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) equals the complete finite set of feasible assignments of \(M\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Exhaustive search with solution exclusion is the standard finite-model enumeration scheme.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exhaustive finite-domain enumeration algorithm is coherent and appropriately classified, but no inspectable source supports its use as the CP-SAT architecture statement.

children.title: Mode Selection Boundary
children.top_down_role: Distinguishes use cases, completion expectations, and reporting behavior across the two modes.

knowledge_statements.title: Mode Selection Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates first-solution termination from complete feasible-set enumeration within the solution-enumeration mode pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(M)=\{x:x\text{ satisfies }M\}\) for a finite-domain model \(M\), and let \(Q\) denote the requested output. Single-solution mode is sufficient when \(Q\) permits either one arbitrary element of \(F(M)\) or an infeasibility result when \(F(M)=\varnothing\). All-solution enumeration is required within this mode pair when correctness demands that every member of \(F(M)\) be emitted, that \(Q=F(M)\), or that \(|F(M)|\) be obtained by counting the emitted assignments. The selection boundary is the output specification, not the observed number of solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use first-solution mode for one feasible witness; within this mode pair, use enumeration when the output must contain every solution or count solutions by enumerating them.
assumptions_latex: The model \(M\) has finite variable domains.
The requested output semantics are fixed before search.
Only the stated single-solution and all-solution modes are being compared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The required mode is determined by whether \(Q\) needs one witness or exhaustive emitted coverage of \(F(M)\).

notation.meaning: set of feasible assignments of model M

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: The distinction follows from witness versus exhaustive-output semantics.

children.title: Boolean Literal Branching
children.top_down_role: Covers branch choices expressed through Boolean literals.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Literal Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary search branching on an unassigned Boolean literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a propagated search state containing an unassigned Boolean variable \(b\in\{0,1\}\). Select a literal \(\ell\in\{b,
eg b\}\) by the branching policy and create two child states: one with \(\ell\) asserted and one with \(
eg\ell\) asserted. Propagate each child and discard any child that becomes inconsistent. Because \(\ell\lor
eg\ell\) is exhaustive and the children are disjoint, every completion of the parent belongs to exactly one child. Stop locally when both children are processed or pruned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on a Boolean literal by exploring its true and false cases; the two children are disjoint and exhaust the parent state.
assumptions_latex: The selected Boolean variable is not fixed in the parent state.
Propagation is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two child states form a disjoint exhaustive partition of the parent's feasible completions.

children.title: Integer-Domain Branching
children.top_down_role: Covers branch choices that partition or restrict integer domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Domain Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partitions a finite integer domain into disjoint exhaustive child domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a propagated state with an integer variable \(x\) having finite current domain \(D\subset\mathbb{Z}\) and \(|D|>1\). Choose an integer \(k\ge 2\) and nonempty sets \(D_1,\ldots,D_k\) such that \(D_i\cap D_j=\varnothing\) for \(i\ne j\) and \(D=\bigcup_{j=1}^kD_j\). Create child \(j\) by imposing \(x\in D_j\), propagate it, and discard it if inconsistent. Process all surviving children. The partition may use a value split, an interval split, or another finite-domain partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer branching partitions a non-singleton finite domain into disjoint nonempty pieces and explores every surviving child after propagation.
assumptions_latex: The current domain \(D\) is finite and has at least two values.
Propagation is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The children form a disjoint exhaustive partition of all parent completions according to the value of \(x\).

children.title: Mixed Branching Coordination

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Branching Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinates Boolean and integer decisions through a shared propagated state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a propagated state \(s\) containing Boolean literals and finite-domain integer variables. Compute eligible Boolean decisions \(B(s)\) and integer-domain partitions \(I(s)\). A coordination policy selects one decision \(d\in B(s)\cup I(s)\), creates its disjoint exhaustive children, and propagates every child through both Boolean and integer constraint channels before another decision is selected. Any cross-channel implication is recorded in the child state. Search stops when a complete feasible assignment is found under the requested mode or every child is proved inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared policy selects either a Boolean or integer split, then propagates every consequence across both representations before the next decision.
assumptions_latex: Boolean and integer views represent compatible restrictions of the same search state.
Each selected branching decision is exhaustive and propagation is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coordinated branching preserves exhaustive coverage while sharing implications between Boolean and integer channels.

children.title: Fixed Branching

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a predetermined variable order and predetermined domain-reduction rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite-domain model, an ordered variable list \((x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), and a fixed domain-partition rule \(R\). At each propagated nonterminal state, choose the first variable in the list whose current domain is not a singleton. Apply \(R\) to partition that domain into nonempty disjoint subsets whose union is the current domain; create, propagate, and process the corresponding children in the prescribed order. Return according to the selected solution mode, or report infeasibility after exhaustive frontier depletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed branching always selects the earliest unfixed variable in a predetermined order and applies a predetermined exhaustive domain split.
assumptions_latex: Every variable has a finite domain.
The fixed rule \(R\) produces an exhaustive disjoint partition whenever applied.
Propagation is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting search follows the fixed decision order and remains exhaustive when all children are processed.

children.title: Pseudo-Cost Branching
children.top_down_role: Covers branching guided by observed objective or bound impact.

knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Cost Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-variable scoring for a minimization branch-and-bound or CP-SAT search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with lower bound \(z\), let \(J\) be the unfixed integer variables and let \(d_j^-,d_j^+>0\) denote the changes imposed by the two candidate branches for \(j\in J\). Maintain nonnegative pseudo-cost estimates \(p_j^-\) and \(p_j^+\), initialized by positive defaults. Compute \(q_j^-=p_j^-d_j^-\), \(q_j^+=p_j^+d_j^+\), and \(s_j=(1-\mu)\min\{q_j^-,q_j^+\}+\mu\max\{q_j^-,q_j^+\}\), where \(0\leq\mu\leq1\). Branch on an index in \(\arg\max_{j\in J}s_j\). After obtaining a finite child bound \(z'\), update the corresponding pseudo-cost estimate with the observation \((z'-z)/d_j^\pm\), typically by an empirical average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate each candidate variable's bound degradation in both branch directions, select the best combined score, and update estimates from observed child bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and nonempty.
\(d_j^-,d_j^+>0\) for every \(j\in J\).
Child lower bounds are comparable with the parent lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(j^*\in\arg\max_{j\in J}s_j\) is the selected branching variable.

notation.meaning: Estimated lower-bound degradation per unit branch displacement.
Displacement imposed by the down or up branch.
Weight balancing the weaker and stronger predicted branches.

children.title: Objective-Guided Branching
children.top_down_role: Covers branching priorities derived from objective structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Guided Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value and child ordering induced by a linear minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(c^\mathsf{T}x\) over finite integer domains. For an unfixed variable \(x_j\) with \(c_j\neq0\), an objective-guided branch orders exhaustive child domains so that the child containing values minimizing \(c_jx_j\) is explored first. Thus smaller values are preferred when \(c_j>0\), and larger values are preferred when \(c_j<0\). The child domains must remain disjoint and cover the parent domain; objective guidance changes search order, not the feasible set. Variables may be ranked by a deterministic score such as \(|c_j|\) times their remaining domain width, with constraint-propagation scores used to break ties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prefer variable values that locally improve the objective, while retaining an exhaustive partition so search correctness is unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) has finite integer domains.
The objective is \(c^\mathsf{T}x\) and is minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcup_r D_{j,r}=D_j\) and \(D_{j,r}\cap D_{j,s}=\varnothing\) for \(r\neq s\), with an objective-preferred child visited first.

children.title: Branching-Policy Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Distinguishes model conditions favoring each policy family.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Policy Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static, portfolio, and adaptive selection among complete branching policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite collection of branching policies, each producing a complete child partition whenever invoked. A static regime selects one \(P\in\mathcal P\) before search and uses it at every eligible node. A portfolio regime runs several policies on separate search workers or restarts and shares valid incumbents and bounds. An adaptive regime selects \(P_t\in\arg\max_{P\in\mathcal P}I_t(P)\) at decision time \(t\), where \(I_t\) is computed only from search history available by time \(t\). Search stops upon a proof, a requested solution condition, or a resource limit. Policy selection preserves completeness whenever the resulting node schedule is fair and every chosen split is exhaustive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose branching statically, across parallel or restarted portfolios, or adaptively from observed performance while preserving exhaustive splits and fair node processing.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is finite.
Every policy produces an exhaustive child partition.
Any completeness claim uses a fair node schedule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fair policy selection preserves exhaustive search independently of the regime used.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Driven Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization by repeated feasibility search below the current incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization problem \(\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\), assume objective values lie on a lattice of spacing \(\delta>0\) and begin with a feasible incumbent \(\bar x\) of value \(U=f(\bar x)\). Repeatedly solve the feasibility problem \(x\in F\) and \(f(x)\leq U-\delta\). If a feasible \(x'\) is found, set \(\bar x\leftarrow x'\) and \(U\leftarrow f(x')\); otherwise stop and return \(\bar x\). Each successful iteration strictly improves the incumbent. Infeasibility of the final threshold problem certifies that no feasible objective value is smaller than \(U\), so the returned incumbent is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly seek a feasible solution strictly better than the incumbent; infeasibility of the next improvement threshold proves optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the feasible set.
\(f(F)\) lies on a lattice with spacing \(\delta>0\).
An initial feasible incumbent is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists x\in F:f(x)\leq U-\delta\) implies \(f(\bar x)=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Minimum positive spacing between attainable objective values.

knowledge_statements.title: Core-Based Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unsatisfiable-core lower-bound refinement for weighted Boolean penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be Boolean constraints and minimize \(\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\ell_i\), where \(w_i>0\) and penalty literal \(\ell_i=1\) incurs cost. Initialize \(L=0\). Query feasibility while assuming selected positive-residual penalty literals are zero. If the assumptions are satisfiable, obtain a primal solution and update the upper bound. If they are infeasible, extract a core \(C\) satisfying \(F\models\sum_{i\in C}\ell_i\geq1\), set \(\alpha=\min_{i\in C}w_i\), increase \(L\leftarrow L+\alpha\), subtract \(\alpha\) from the residual weights in \(C\), and retain the core constraint. Continue until a feasible solution has value \(L\), or another valid stopping rule proves equality of lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use unsatisfiable assumption cores to identify unavoidable weighted penalties, raise the lower bound, and stop when it meets a feasible solution's value.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite Boolean constraint system.
\(w_i>0\) for every penalty literal.
Extracted cores are logically valid consequences of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination with primal value \(U=L\), the returned solution is optimal.

notation.meaning: Minimum residual weight extracted from a core.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Bound Tree Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-bound tree search for finite discrete minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a queue \(Q\) of search nodes, a feasible incumbent value \(U\), and a valid lower bound \(L(N)\leq\min\{f(x):x\in F_N\}\) for every node \(N\). Repeatedly remove a node of minimum \(L(N)\). Prune it if \(L(N)\geq U\); otherwise propagate, update \(U\) from any feasible solution found, and either close the node or partition \(F_N\) into exhaustive child regions inserted into \(Q\). The global lower bound is \(L_Q=\min_{N\in Q}L(N)\), with \(L_Q=U\) when \(Q\) is empty. Stop with an optimal incumbent when \(Q\) is empty or \(L_Q\geq U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explore the open node with the smallest valid lower bound, pruning nodes that cannot beat the incumbent and stopping when no improving node remains.
assumptions_latex: The discrete search tree is finite.
Every child collection exhaustively partitions its parent region.
Every node bound is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=\varnothing\) or \(L_Q\geq U\) implies that the incumbent is globally optimal.

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound for node N.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Limited Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-relative optimality-gap stopping condition for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\in\mathbb R\) be the objective value of a feasible incumbent and let \(L\in\mathbb R\) be a valid global lower bound for a minimization problem, so \(L\leq f^*\leq U\). For tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\geq0\), gap-limited optimization may terminate when \[U-L\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|U|\}.\] The incumbent then has objective error at most the right-hand side. With both tolerances zero, this condition reduces to equality of primal and dual bounds and therefore certifies exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when the difference between a feasible value and a valid lower bound is within the requested absolute-relative tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(L\leq f^*\leq U\).
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq U-f^*\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|U|\}\).

children.title: Solution Hint Semantics
children.top_down_role: Covers user-supplied candidate assignments presented to the solver.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Hint Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A hint is a partial preferred assignment, not an added constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-domain constraint model with variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), a solution hint is a partial map \(h:D\to\bigcup_{i=1}^n\operatorname{dom}(x_i)\), where \(D\subseteq\{1,ldots,n\}\) and \(h(i)\in\operatorname{dom}(x_i)\) for each \(i\in D\). It supplies preferred values to initialization or search but does not replace any variable domain or add equalities to the model. A hinted assignment is a solution only if it extends to some \(x\) satisfying every original constraint. Consequently, a correct solver may ignore, modify, or fail to complete a validly encoded hint without changing the model's feasible set or optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solution hint is a domain-valid partial preferred assignment. It guides search but neither constrains the model nor guarantees a feasible completion.
assumptions_latex: Every model variable has a finite domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\mathrm{hinted}}=F\) when the hint is used only as search guidance.
review_flags: implementation treatment of invalid hints requires confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits, but CP-SAT hint semantics and treatment of invalid or ignored hints require an authoritative interface source. The index set also contains the malformed text `1,ldots,n` instead of a properly delimited `\ldots` expression.

children.title: Partial Hint Completion
children.top_down_role: Covers solver treatment of incomplete candidate assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Hint Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict completion test for a domain-valid partial solution hint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible-set description \(F\), variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), and a domain-valid partial hint \(h:D\to\bigcup_i\operatorname{dom}(x_i)\), initialize the completion subproblem \[F(h)=\{x\in F:x_i=h(i)\text{ for every }i\in D\}.\] Propagate the fixed hinted values and search only over variables not fixed by propagation. If a point \(x\in F(h)\) is found, return it as a completed feasible solution. If \(F(h)=\varnothing\) is proved, report that the hint has no strict completion; this does not imply that \(F\) itself is empty. Under a finite exhaustive search, the procedure terminates with one of these two outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporarily fix all hinted values and search the remaining variables; return a completion or prove only that this exact hint cannot be completed.
assumptions_latex: All hinted values belong to their declared domains.
The completion search is finite and exhaustive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either \(x\in F(h)\) or a certificate that \(F(h)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Feasible solutions agreeing with every hinted value.

review_flags: strict fixing differs from heuristic hint use

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is mathematically coherent as a strict completion test, but no source establishes that this strict-fixing procedure is the intended CP-SAT partial-hint completion behavior rather than a separate validation mode.

children.title: Warm-Start Transfer
children.top_down_role: Covers reuse of prior solution information across related solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of compatible incumbent values between related finite-domain models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a source solution \(x^S\) be given and let \(\phi\) map selected source variables to target variables with the same intended semantics. Initialize an empty target hint. For each mapped source variable \(i\), transfer \(x_i^S\) to \(x_{\phi(i)}^T\) only if the target variable exists, the value is exactly representable, and \(x_i^S\in\operatorname{dom}(x_{\phi(i)}^T)\). Discard unmapped or incompatible entries, resolve duplicate target mappings only when their values agree, and submit the remaining partial assignment as a hint. The target solver must validate all target constraints; transferred feasibility is guaranteed only when the completed target assignment satisfies the target model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map compatible values from a source solution into a target-model hint, discarding invalid entries and rechecking all target constraints.
assumptions_latex: Mapped variables have matching semantics.
The source assignment supplies exact finite-domain values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transferred map is domain-valid, but target feasibility still requires membership in \(F_T\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits, but model-identity, representability, duplicate-mapping, and compatibility requirements are solver-interface claims without cited support.

children.title: Hint Rejection Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Covers infeasible, inconsistent, or operationally unhelpful starting information.

knowledge_statements.title: Hint Rejection Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes malformed hints from valid hints lacking a feasible completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partial hint \(h\) is interface-invalid if it refers to a nonexistent variable, assigns a value outside the variable's declared domain, is not exactly representable in the model's value type, or assigns conflicting values to the same variable. Such entries may be rejected before search. A domain-valid hint can nevertheless be globally inconsistent: \[F(h)=\{x\in F:x_i=h(i)\text{ for all }i\in D\}=\varnothing.\] This failure rules out only strict completion of \(h\), not feasibility of \(F\). If hints are advisory, neither inconsistency nor rejection may justify declaring the original model infeasible; the solver must search independently or return an explicit hint-validation status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject malformed assignments at the interface; a well-formed but inconsistent hint proves only that the hinted values cannot all be retained.
assumptions_latex: Hints are advisory rather than model constraints.
\(F\) denotes the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(h)=\varnothing\) does not imply \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Solutions agreeing with every hinted value.

review_flags: missing CP-SAT validation and rejection specification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate and the set-theoretic distinction is correct, but the listed interface rejection conditions and required advisory-hint behavior are implementation-dependent and unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Feasibility-Jump Search
children.top_down_role: Covers primal repair driven by movements toward constraint satisfaction.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Jump Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized finite-domain local search minimizing aggregate constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite-domain variables, initialize an assignment \(x\), not necessarily feasible, and define \(V(x)=\sum_{k=1}^m w_kv_k(x)\), where \(w_k>0\) and \(v_k(x)\geq0\) vanishes exactly when constraint \(k\) is satisfied. At each iteration, sample candidate variable-value moves and apply a move minimizing the resulting \(V\), with randomized tie breaking. If no sampled move improves \(V\), perturb one or more values, enlarge the sampled neighborhood, or restart. Stop and return \(x\) when \(V(x)=0\); at a resource limit, return the best assignment found together with its violation value. Failure to reach zero is not an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomly explore variable-value jumps that reduce weighted constraint violation, perturbing or restarting at local minima and accepting feasibility only at zero violation.
assumptions_latex: Every variable domain is finite.
\(v_k(x)=0\) exactly when constraint \(k\) is satisfied.
\(w_k>0\) for every constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\) satisfies all modeled constraints.
review_flags: exact CP-SAT move and weighting rules require confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm container fits, but the statement describes a broad randomized violation-minimizing local search. A source is needed to verify that its move selection, weighting, perturbation, and restart rules accurately represent the specific CP-SAT feasibility-jump method.

children.title: Randomized Primal Search
children.top_down_role: Covers stochastic diversification in candidate construction or repair.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Primal Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic randomized local search for a finite-domain feasibility model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finite domains \(D_i\), constraints \(C\), a violation score \(V(x)\ge 0\), and iteration limit \(T\), initialize \(x^0\) by independently sampling each \(x_i^0\in D_i\). For \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), stop and return \(x^t\) when \(V(x^t)=0\). Otherwise sample a variable \(i_t\) with positive probability, sample a candidate value from \(D_{i_t}\), and accept a candidate \(y\) according to a rule assigning positive probability to every improving move. If no feasible point is found, return the least-violating visited point and status \(\mathrm{UNKNOWN}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomly initialize and modify finite-domain assignments, retaining improving moves until feasibility is reached or the iteration limit expires.
assumptions_latex: \(D_i\) is finite and nonempty for every variable.
\(V(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\) satisfies every constraint in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a feasible assignment when it visits one; otherwise it returns an incumbent with no feasibility guarantee.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic random local-search scheme does not capture feasibility-jump search in the exact parent container. Moreover, the plain statement says improving moves are retained, whereas the formal rule only requires positive acceptance probability for them.

children.title: Randomized Jump Diversification
children.top_down_role: Covers randomized choices used to diversify feasibility-jump trajectories.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Jump Diversification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diversification step for escaping a locally stagnant feasibility-jump trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\prod_i D_i\), let \(V\) be a violation score, and let \(J(x)\) be a nonempty set of admissible jumps. After \(L\) consecutive iterations without decreasing the best observed violation, sample \(j\in J(x)\) from a distribution \(p_x\) satisfying \(p_x(j)>0\) for every \(j\in J(x)\), and set \(x\leftarrow j(x)\), even when \(V(j(x))\ge V(x)\). Resume ordinary improving search afterward. The randomized jump is a diversification operation and does not itself certify feasibility or improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After sustained nonimprovement, randomly take an admissible jump, possibly worsening violation, and then resume ordinary primal search.
assumptions_latex: Every current state has a finite, nonempty admissible jump set \(J(x)\).
The stagnation threshold \(L\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admissible jump has positive selection probability at a diversification event.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diversification trigger, full-support jump distribution, worsening-move policy, and restart behavior are implementation-specific and are not supported by the cited generic local-search section. A direct feasibility-jump or CP-SAT architecture source is required.

children.title: Primal Search Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Covers repeated moves or sampling patterns that fail to produce useful candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Search Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational stagnation predicate based on incumbent and violation progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal-search trajectory \((x^t)_{t\ge0}\), define the best violation \(b_t=\min_{0\le s\le t}V(x^s)\). Given a window length \(L\ge1\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), search is stagnant at iteration \(t\ge L\) precisely when \(b_{t-L}-b_t\le\varepsilon\) and no feasible incumbent has been found by iteration \(t\). With integer-valued \(V\) and \(\varepsilon=0\), this is equivalent to observing no strict improvement in the best violation during the last \(L\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search is stagnant when the best violation has not improved beyond a tolerance over a fixed window and no feasible incumbent exists.
assumptions_latex: \(V(x)\ge0\) and \(V(x)=0\) exactly for feasible assignments.
\(L\ge1\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Stagnant}(t;L,\varepsilon)\iff b_{t-L}-b_t\le\varepsilon\ \land\ b_t>0\).

notation.meaning: Best violation observed through iteration t.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predicate is mathematically coherent, and condition is the correct content kind, but the window-and-tolerance definition is a solver-dependent operational choice not established by the cited generic local-search source.

children.title: Feasibility-Pump Search
children.top_down_role: Covers primal candidate generation through alternating discrete and relaxed guidance.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Pump Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical alternating projection scheme for mixed-integer linear feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) with integer index set \(I\), choose \(x^0\in P\). At iteration \(t\), form an integer target \(z^t\) by rounding \(x_i^t\) for \(i\in I\), leaving continuous coordinates unrestricted. If some \(x\in P\) satisfies \(x_I=z_I^t\), return such an \(x\). Otherwise compute \(x^{t+1}\in\arg\min\{\sum_{i\in I}|x_i-z_i^t|:x\in P\}\). Detect repeated targets and perturb selected components of \(z^t\); stop at feasibility or a prescribed limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate rounding an LP-relaxation point and projecting back to the relaxation, perturbing cycles until an integer-feasible point or limit is reached.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is nonempty and each projection subproblem attains its minimum.
Integer variables have specified rounding and perturbation rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned point \(x\) belongs to \(P\) and satisfies \(x_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|}\); termination without such a point proves nothing about infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Rounded integer target at iteration t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The canonical MILP feasibility-pump description is plausible and algorithm is the appropriate content kind, but no source is supplied and its relationship to the CP-SAT-specific parent container is unresolved.

children.title: Relaxation-Guided Search
children.top_down_role: Covers primal search informed by relaxation solutions or relaxation-derived signals.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Guided Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal branching guided by a current continuous-relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\supseteq F\) be a tractable relaxation of a finite-domain feasible set \(F\), and let \(\bar x\in P\) solve the current relaxation. For each unfixed discrete variable \(x_i\in D_i\), assign candidate values a priority decreasing with distance \(|v-\bar x_i|\). Select a variable by a prescribed score, branch first on a highest-priority value, propagate the constraints, and recompute or update \(\bar x\) after the relaxation changes. Return the first feasible assignment found, or \(\mathrm{UNKNOWN}\) when the search budget expires.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a relaxation solution to prioritize discrete values, then branch, propagate, and refresh the guidance as the relaxation changes.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq P\) and a relaxation point \(\bar x\in P\) is available.
Every discrete domain \(D_i\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any returned assignment lies in \(F\); relaxation proximity orders search but does not certify discrete feasibility.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13
2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

children.title: Rounding Conflict Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers incompatibility between relaxation guidance and discrete feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Conflict Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure mechanism when componentwise relaxation rounding violates coupled constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(F=\{x\in\{0,1\}^2:x_1+x_2=1\}\) and its relaxation \(P=\{x\in[0,1]^2:x_1+x_2=1\}\). The relaxation point \(\bar x=(1/2,1/2)\) is feasible in \(P\), but any deterministic componentwise rule that resolves both ties identically rounds it to either \((0,0)\) or \((1,1)\), neither of which belongs to \(F\). Thus coordinatewise proximity to a relaxation point is insufficient for feasibility when constraints couple rounded variables; repair, coordinated rounding, or perturbation is necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupled constraints can make componentwise rounding infeasible even when the relaxation point is feasible and each coordinate is rounded to a nearest integer.
assumptions_latex: Half-integral ties are resolved identically for both coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{round}(\bar x)\notin F\) although \(\bar x\in P\).

children.title: Relaxation Guidance Quality
children.top_down_role: Covers structural conditions affecting the usefulness of relaxation-derived direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Guidance Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A measurable geometric quality criterion for relaxation-based primal guidance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space, let \(D\subseteq X\) be a discrete assignment set, let \(F\subseteq D\) be a nonempty finite feasible set, and let \(\bar x\in X\) be a relaxation solution. Define the guidance error \(q(\bar x)=\min_{y\in F}d(\bar x,y)\). For \(r\ge0\), define \(N_r(\bar x)=\{x\in D:d(x,\bar x)\le r\}\). Then \(N_r(\bar x)\) contains a feasible assignment if and only if \(r\ge q(\bar x)\). Thus smaller \(q(\bar x)\) means that a smaller relaxation-centered neighborhood suffices to contain a feasible assignment, without implying that a particular search procedure will find one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation guidance is geometrically better under the chosen ambient metric when the relaxation point is closer to a feasible discrete assignment.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a metric space containing \(D\) and \(\bar x\).
\(F\subseteq D\) is nonempty and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_r(\bar x)\cap F\ne\varnothing\iff r\ge q(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Ambient space containing the relaxation point and discrete assignments.
Distance from the relaxation point to the nearest feasible assignment.
Discrete assignments within ambient-metric radius r of the relaxation point.
Ambient metric used to measure guidance proximity.

children.title: Variable Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Covers neighborhoods formed by relaxing or fixing selected variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-neighborhood-search subproblem obtained by relaxing selected incumbent variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a constraint model with variables indexed by \(I\), feasible set \(F\subseteq\prod_{i\in I}D_i\), incumbent \(x^*\in F\), and relaxation set \(R\subseteq I\), the variable neighborhood is \[N_R(x^*)=\{x\in F:x_i=x_i^*\text{ for every }i\in I\setminus R\}.\] Variables in \(R\) are reoptimized over their original domains, while all other variables are fixed to incumbent values. The neighborhood is nonempty because \(x^*\in N_R(x^*)\), and it expands monotonically with \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable neighborhood fixes variables outside a selected set to incumbent values and reoptimizes the selected variables over their original domains.
assumptions_latex: \(R\subseteq I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(R_1\subseteq R_2\), then \(N_{R_1}(x^*)\subseteq N_{R_2}(x^*)\).

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and monotonicity property are mathematically sound, but the cited generic local-search section does not directly support this LNS neighborhood construction. An LNS-specific locator is required.

children.title: Constraint Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Covers neighborhoods organized around selected constraints or constraint groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood induced by relaxing incumbent fixings around selected constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set of constraints \(C\) on variables indexed by \(I\), let \(x^*\in F\), and choose \(S\subseteq C\). Write \(\operatorname{var}(S)\) for the variables occurring in constraints of \(S\). The constraint-induced neighborhood is \[N_S(x^*)=\{x\in F:x_i=x_i^*\text{ for every }i\notin\operatorname{var}(S)\}.\] Thus selecting constraints determines which variables may change; all original constraints remain enforced in the repair subproblem. Enlarging \(S\) can only enlarge the neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select constraints, relax the incumbent values of their incident variables, and retain every original constraint in the repair subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a finite constraint family.
\(x^*\in F\) and \(S\subseteq C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(S_1\subseteq S_2\), then \(N_{S_1}(x^*)\subseteq N_{S_2}(x^*)\).

children.title: Graph Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Covers neighborhoods derived from model-incidence or dependency graphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LNS neighborhoods generated by metric balls in a model-interaction graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(I,E)\) be a variable-interaction graph, where two variable indices are adjacent when they occur together in a constraint. For incumbent \(x^*\in F\), seed set \(S\subseteq I\), and radius \(r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), define \(B_r(S)=\{i\in I:d_G(i,S)\le r\}\) and \[N_{G,S,r}(x^*)=\{x\in F:x_i=x_i^*\text{ for every }i\notin B_r(S)\}.\] The repair subproblem may change exactly the variables in the graph ball while enforcing all original constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph neighborhood reoptimizes variables within a chosen graph distance of seed variables while fixing all remaining variables to the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is the variable-interaction graph of the model.
\(x^*\in F\), \(S\subseteq I\), and \(r\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(r_1\le r_2\), then \(N_{G,S,r_1}(x^*)\subseteq N_{G,S,r_2}(x^*)\).

notation.meaning: Radius-r graph ball around the seeds.
