children.title: Neighborhood Structure Selection
children.top_down_role: Distinguishes structural cues used to choose among neighborhood families.

knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Structure Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive selection among finitely many LNS neighborhood generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H=\{H_1,\ldots,H_m\}\) be neighborhood generators and initialize weights \(w_k^0>0\). At LNS iteration \(t\), sample \(K_t=k\) with probability \(p_k^t=w_k^t/\sum_jw_j^t\), generate and solve the repair neighborhood \(H_k(x^t)\) under a fixed budget, and observe bounded reward \(r_t\in[0,1]\). Update \(w_k^{t+1}=w_k^t\exp(\eta r_t/p_k^t)\) for \(k=K_t\), leaving other weights unchanged. Accept the repaired solution under the portfolio's incumbent rule and repeat until the global limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample a neighborhood generator from adaptive positive weights, solve its repair subproblem, and increase its weight according to observed reward.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is finite and every initial weight is positive.
Rewards satisfy \(0\le r_t\le1\) and \(\eta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generator has positive selection probability at every finite iteration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exponential weight update is a particular adaptive portfolio algorithm and cannot be attributed to CP-SAT neighborhood selection without a direct source. Its content kind is correctly algorithm.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LNS neighborhoods specialized to interval-based scheduling models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let jobs \(J\) have interval variables with start times \(s_j\), optional presence literals \(a_j\), and a feasible incumbent \(x^*\). For a selected job set \(R\subseteq J\), a scheduling neighborhood is \[N_R(x^*)=\{x\in F:(s_j,a_j)=(s_j^*,a_j^*)\text{ for every }j\in J\setminus R\}.\] Durations, resource capacities, precedences, and all other original constraints remain enforced. Jobs in \(R\) may be rescheduled or, when optional, have presence reconsidered; unselected jobs retain their incumbent placements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduling neighborhood reschedules selected jobs while fixing unselected jobs to incumbent placements and retaining all temporal and resource constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the feasible set of the scheduling model.
\(x^*\in F\) and \(R\subseteq J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent belongs to \(N_R(x^*)\), and every member of \(N_R(x^*)\) satisfies the original scheduling constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed scheduling neighborhood is plausible, but no source supports the job-selection construction or the treatment of optional interval presence and start variables in CP-SAT.

children.title: Relaxation-Induced Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Covers neighborhoods derived from relaxation values, discrepancies, or confidence signals.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Induced Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines incumbent-centered neighborhoods whose fixed variables are selected using a relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) be the feasible set, let \(\hat x\in F\) be an incumbent, and let \(\bar x\in R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) solve a relaxation of \(F\). Given agreement predicates \(A_i(\hat x_i,\bar x_i)\), define \(I_0=\{i:A_i(\hat x_i,\bar x_i)\}\). The relaxation-induced neighborhood is \[N(\hat x,\bar x)=\{x\in F:x_i=\hat x_i\text{ for every }i\in I_0\}.\] A neighborhood search optimizes the original objective over \(N(\hat x,\bar x)\), normally subject to a finite subproblem budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation-induced neighborhood fixes incumbent variables selected by agreement with a relaxation solution and reoptimizes all remaining variables under the original constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) is nonempty.
\(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a relaxation containing \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N(\hat x,\bar x)\subseteq F\) and \(\hat x\in N(\hat x,\bar x)\).

children.title: RINS Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Covers neighborhoods based on agreement between incumbent and relaxation assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: RINS Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical relaxation-induced neighborhood search for finite-domain integer optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a feasible incumbent \(\hat x\in F\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\), a relaxation solution \(\bar x\in R\), and a subproblem budget \(B>0\). Form \(I_{\mathrm{RINS}}=\{i:\bar x_i\in\mathbb Z\text{ and }\bar x_i=\hat x_i\}\), impose \(x_i=\hat x_i\) for every \(i\in I_{\mathrm{RINS}}\), and optimize the original objective over the resulting restricted feasible set until budget \(B\) is exhausted or the subproblem is solved. Output the best feasible solution found, retaining \(\hat x\) if no improving solution is obtained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: RINS fixes variables taking the same integral value in the incumbent and relaxation solution, then searches the resulting restricted problem within a budget.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) is the original feasible set.
\(\hat x\in F\) and \(\bar x\in R\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned solution is feasible for \(F\), and its objective is no worse than that of \(\hat x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches a standard RINS description, but no inspectable citation establishes the exact fixing rule, budgeted execution, or incumbent-retention behavior.

children.title: Incumbent–Relaxation Agreement
children.top_down_role: Covers agreement patterns that determine which decisions remain fixed.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent–Relaxation Agreement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the coordinatewise equality test used by the classical RINS fixing rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an incumbent \(\hat x	hickspace\in\mathbb Z^n\) and a relaxation solution \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), coordinate \(i\) has incumbent–relaxation agreement precisely when \[A_i(\hat x_i,\bar x_i)\iff \bar x_i\in\mathbb Z\text{ and }\hat x_i=\bar x_i.\] The agreement set is \(I_A=\{i:A_i(\hat x_i,ar x_i)\}\). Fixing every coordinate in \(I_A\) to its incumbent value preserves the incumbent in the restricted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinate agrees when the incumbent and relaxation solution have exactly the same integral value; agreeing coordinates may be fixed without excluding the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(\hat x\in\mathbb Z^n\).
\(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(i\in I_A\), imposing \(x_i=\hat x_i\) is also equivalent to imposing \(x_i=\bar x_i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-agreement condition requires a RINS source, particularly because implementations may use tolerances. The agreement-set formula also contains the malformed expression `ar x_i` instead of `\bar x_i`.

children.title: Degenerate Relaxation Guidance
children.top_down_role: Covers weak or ambiguous relaxation signals that produce ineffective neighborhoods.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Relaxation Guidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the two extreme agreement sets that make relaxation guidance ineffective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=\{x\in F:x_i=\hat x_i\text{ for all }i\in I_A\}\) be an incumbent-centered relaxation-induced neighborhood. If \(I_A=\varnothing\), then \(N=F\), so the relaxation produces no restriction. If \(I_A=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), then \(N=\{\hat x\}\), so no distinct improving solution can occur in the neighborhood. Thus useful guidance requires a nontrivial fixing set and at least one feasible degree of freedom after propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No agreement leaves the entire problem unchanged, while complete agreement leaves only the incumbent; both extremes make the relaxation-guided neighborhood ineffective.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) and \(\hat x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Effective diversification requires \(0<|I_A|<n\) and a restricted feasible point distinct from \(\hat x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two set identities follow from the neighborhood definition, but the claim that effective diversification requires a nonempty fixing set is too broad: an unrestricted search can diversify even though it receives no relaxation-induced guidance. A source must establish the intended architecture-specific meaning of effectiveness.

children.title: Repair Workers
children.top_down_role: Covers subsolvers dedicated to repairing partial or disrupted solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Repair Workers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a portfolio worker that repeatedly solves incumbent-centered restricted subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an incumbent \(\hat x\in F\), a neighborhood generator \(G\), and a resource budget \(B\), a repair worker constructs \(N=G(\hat x)\subseteq F\) with \(\hat x\in N\), solves or heuristically searches the restricted problem over \(N\) for at most \(B\), and publishes any feasible \(x'\in N\) satisfying \(f(x')<f(\hat x)\) for minimization. After receiving the current shared incumbent, it repeats this procedure until global termination; unsuccessful calls publish no incumbent update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repair worker generates an incumbent-centered neighborhood, searches it under a budget, and publishes any improving feasible solution before repeating.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the original feasible set.
The optimization direction is minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every published repair \(x'\) belongs to \(F\) and satisfies \(f(x')<f(\hat x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the leaf, but no source supports this precise CP-SAT worker lifecycle, strict-improvement publication rule, or repeated interaction with a shared incumbent.

children.title: Adaptive Neighborhood Portfolios
children.top_down_role: Covers dynamic allocation among competing neighborhood generators.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Neighborhood Portfolios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A multiplicative-weight rule for adapting the mixture of neighborhood generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) be neighborhood generators and initialize \(w_{i,1}=1\). At epoch \(t\), select generator \(I_t=i\) with probability \(p_{i,t}=w_{i,t}/\sum_{j=1}^m w_{j,t}\), run its repair subproblem, and observe a bounded reward \(r_t\in[0,1]\). For learning rate \(\eta>0\), update \(w_{I_t,t+1}=w_{I_t,t}\exp(\eta r_t/p_{I_t,t})\) and leave all other weights unchanged. Output the evolving distribution \(p_t\), while retaining positive selection probability for every generator with finite weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive portfolio samples neighborhood generators from learned weights and increases the selected generator's weight according to its normalized repair reward.
assumptions_latex: \(m\geq2\) and all initial weights are positive.
Rewards satisfy \(r_t\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every finite epoch \(t\), \(p_{i,t}>0\) for all \(i\in\{1,ldots,m\}\).

notation.meaning: weight of generator i at epoch t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record introduces a particular importance-weighted exponential update without evidence that it represents the target architecture. The conclusion also contains `ldots` without the required backslash.

children.title: Worker–Neighborhood Assignment
children.top_down_role: Covers assignment of repair capacity to neighborhood families.

knowledge_statements.title: Worker–Neighborhood Assignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized compatibility-constrained assignment of repair workers to neighborhood generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\) be the finite set of idle workers, \(G\) the generator set, and \(C_w\subseteq G\) the nonempty compatibility set of worker \(w\). Given positive generator weights \(q_g\), independently assign each \(w\in W\) a generator \(a(w)\in C_w\) according to \[\Pr(a(w)=g)=\frac{q_g}{\sum_{h\in C_w}q_h}\quad(g\in C_w).\] Worker \(w\) then executes one budgeted repair call using \(a(w)\); reassignment occurs when that call ends or the portfolio controller intervenes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each idle worker samples a compatible neighborhood generator in proportion to adaptive weights and keeps that assignment for one repair call.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) and \(G\) are finite.
Each \(C_w\) is nonempty and every \(q_g>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assignment satisfies \(a(w)\in C_w\) almost surely for every \(w\in W\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The probability distribution is well-defined under the stated assumptions, but the independent compatibility-weighted assignment and reassignment policy are architecture-specific choices with no supporting citation.

children.title: Portfolio Adaptation Failure
children.top_down_role: Covers feedback or allocation behavior that persistently favors ineffective neighborhoods.

knowledge_statements.title: Portfolio Adaptation Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows how adaptation without exploration can permanently reject a delayed-reward neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two generators. Generator \(G_1\) returns reward \(\varepsilon\) on every call, while \(G_2\) returns zero until it receives \(L\) consecutive calls and thereafter returns one per call, where \(0<\varepsilon<1\) and \(L\geq2\). A greedy controller initialized with estimated rewards \(\hat r_1=arepsilon\) and \(\hat r_2=0\) always selects \(G_1\). Consequently it obtains cumulative reward \(T\varepsilon\) over \(T\) epochs and never discovers the eventually superior generator \(G_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A greedy portfolio can lock onto a small immediate reward and never allocate enough consecutive trials to discover a delayed but superior neighborhood generator.
assumptions_latex: The controller always selects a generator with maximal estimated mean reward.
Unselected generators receive no optimistic bonus or forced exploration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(T>L/(1-arepsilon)\), persistent use of \(G_2\) after its warm-up yields greater cumulative reward than the greedy policy.

notation.meaning: warm-up length of the delayed generator
immediate reward of the inferior generator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constructed delayed-reward example is mathematically plausible, but it lacks evidence or an explicit standard-field rationale connecting it to portfolio adaptation failure. The LaTeX contains malformed `arepsilon` expressions in both the statement and conclusion.

children.title: Complete Subsolvers
children.top_down_role: Covers workers responsible for exhaustive search contributions.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Subsolvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines portfolio subsolvers that can certify a finite-domain model when run without limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-domain minimization problem \(P\), a complete subsolver is a sound search procedure that, when run without external resource limits, terminates with exactly one of: an optimal feasible solution \(x^*\) and matching valid lower bound \(L=f(x^*)\), or an infeasibility certificate establishing that \(P\) has no feasible solution. Imported incumbents and valid bounds may prune its search, but cannot remove any solution capable of improving the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete subsolver eventually proves optimality or infeasibility on a finite-domain model, while safely exploiting shared incumbents and bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) has finitely many assignments.
All imported bounds and deductions are valid for \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unlimited execution terminates with a sound optimality or infeasibility certificate for \(P\).

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic definition of completeness is reasonable, but the cited branch-and-bound section does not establish the exact CP-SAT subsolver role or its interaction with imported incumbents and bounds.

children.title: First-Solution Subsolvers
children.top_down_role: Covers workers optimized for rapid discovery of an initial feasible solution.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Solution Subsolvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines subsolvers optimized to supply an initial feasible incumbent rather than a proof.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A first-solution subsolver for feasible set \(F\) is a budgeted procedure whose primary stopping event is discovery of any \(xbin F\). On discovery it immediately publishes \(x\) as an incumbent and may terminate or change role. If its budget expires without a solution, it returns no incumbent; unless the procedure is independently complete, this outcome does not certify \(F=varnothing\) or provide an optimality claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A first-solution subsolver searches quickly for any feasible incumbent and publishes it immediately; failure within its budget does not establish infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The subsolver checks every published assignment against the original constraints.
Its resource budget may be finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every published \(x\) satisfies \(x\in F\), whereas a null return need not imply \(F=varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intended role is clear, but no source supports the CP-SAT classification or stopping behavior. Several formulas are malformed, including `xbin F` and `F=varnothing`.

children.title: Bound Subsolvers
children.top_down_role: Covers workers focused on improving or certifying objective bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Subsolvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines minimization subsolvers devoted to producing globally valid objective lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\) and objective \(f\), a bound subsolver maintains a value \(L\) satisfying \(L\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). It may obtain \(L\) from relaxations, dual reasoning, or exhaustive search and may publish a stronger value \(L'\) only after verifying \(L'\geq L\) and global validity. If a shared incumbent \(\hat x\in F\) satisfies \(L=f(\hat x)\), the pair certifies optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound subsolver computes globally valid lower bounds for minimization and can certify optimality when its bound meets the incumbent value.
assumptions_latex: The optimization direction is minimization.
Published bounds are valid for every point in \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L=f(\hat x)\) for some \(\hat x\in F\), then \(\hat x\) is globally optimal.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Continuous Relaxation and Lagrangian Relaxation p. 24
2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: LNS Subsolvers
children.top_down_role: Covers workers focused on neighborhood-based incumbent improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: LNS Subsolvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines portfolio subsolvers that repeatedly optimize restricted neighborhoods around shared incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a shared incumbent \(\hat xbin F\), choose a relaxation set \(D\subseteq\{1,ldots,n\}\), impose \(x_i=hat x_i\) for every \(i\notin D\), and search the restricted feasible set \[N_D(hat x)=\{xbin F:x_i=hat x_i\text{ for every }i\notin D\}\] under a finite budget. Publish the best improving feasible point found; otherwise retain \(\hat x\). Repeat with a newly selected incumbent or relaxation set until global termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LNS subsolver relaxes selected incumbent variables, searches the restricted model under a budget, and publishes any improving feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) and \(\hat x\in F\).
Each restricted search preserves all original constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every published solution belongs to \(F\) and improves upon the incumbent used to construct its neighborhood.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the leaf, but no source supports the precise CP-SAT LNS-subsolver behavior. The statement repeatedly omits required backslashes in expressions such as `\hat x\in F`, `\ldots`, and `N_D(\hat x)`.

children.title: Subsolver Role Allocation
children.top_down_role: Covers portfolio allocation across complete, primal, bound-focused, and neighborhood roles.

assumptions_latex: The portfolio contains finitely many subsolvers indexed by \(I=I_{\mathrm{comp}}\mathbin{\dot\cup}I_{\mathrm{first}}\mathbin{\dot\cup}I_{\mathrm{{bound}}}\mathbin{\dot\cup}I_{\mathrm{LNS}}\).
The available parallel capacity is \(P\in\mathbb{N}\), and each active subsolver consumes one worker slot.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The allocation is feasible exactly when \(n_r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\) for every role \(r\), \(n_r\le |I_r|\), and \(\sum_r n_r\le P\).

notation.meaning: Index set of available subsolvers having role r
Number of worker slots allocated to role r

auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract allocation rule for complete, first-solution, bound, and LNS roles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given role sets \(I_r\) and capacity \(P\), choose integer counts \(n_r\) satisfying \(0\le n_r\le |I_r|\) and \(\sum_r n_r\le P\). Instantiate any \(n_r\) distinct subsolvers from each \(I_r\). If role-coverage requirements \(m_r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\) are prescribed, additionally require \(n_r\ge m_r\). Start the selected instances on distinct worker slots; unselected instances remain inactive. The output is the active multiset together with its role counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate integer worker counts across complete, first-solution, bound, and LNS roles without exceeding available capacity, while satisfying any prescribed minimum role coverage.
knowledge_statements.title: Subsolver Role Allocation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No inspectable citation supports this CP-SAT role-allocation algorithm. Moreover, the stated exact feasibility characterization omits the optional minimum-coverage constraints n_r>=m_r introduced in the algorithm.

assumptions_latex: All workers solve the same finite optimization model and may differ only in sound search parameters or random seeds.
Each worker preserves feasibility and valid-bound semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Diversification preserves correctness while producing a family \(\{\mathcal A_{\theta_i}\}_{i=1}^P\) of distinct search trajectories.

notation.meaning: Parameter vector controlling a worker's search behavior

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: portfolio diversification uses distinct sound configurations on a common model
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic or randomized diversification of parallel CP-SAT workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For workers \(i\in\{1,\ldots,P\}\), select configurations \(\theta_i\) so that at least two induced search policies \(\mathcal A_{\theta_i}\) differ in branching, restart, propagation, relaxation, neighborhood, or randomization behavior. Every configuration must retain the same feasible set and objective. Consequently, any solution reported by any worker is feasible for the common model, and every reported global bound remains valid, although node sequences and discovery times may differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers use distinct sound search configurations on the same model, yielding different trajectories without changing feasibility or bound validity.
knowledge_statements.title: Worker Diversification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An architecture-specific source is required. Distinct configurations or induced policies do not by themselves guarantee distinct realized search trajectories on a particular model, so the conclusion is stronger than the assumptions.

children.title: Incumbent Sharing
children.top_down_role: Covers dissemination of improved feasible solutions across workers.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\) and objective \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\).
Shared updates are serialized or applied atomically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After accepting \(x\), the shared incumbent value becomes \(U'=\min\{U,f(x)\}\), and \(U'\) remains a valid upper bound on \(\min_{y\in F}f(y)\).

notation.meaning: Candidate solution submitted by a worker

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimization incumbents are shared by atomic feasible-value improvement
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atomic incumbent exchange for a minimization portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the shared incumbent value to \(U=+\infty\). When a worker submits \(x\), first verify \(x\in F\). Admit it exactly when \(f(x)<U\), then atomically set \(U\leftarrow f(x)\) and store \(x\). Each worker periodically imports the latest pair \((x,U)\) and may prune any search region whose valid lower bound is at least \(U\). The final shared incumbent is the admitted feasible point of least reported objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers atomically publish improving feasible solutions; all workers import the best value and may prune regions that cannot improve it.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Sharing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimization update is mathematically standard, and algorithm is an appropriate knowledge kind, but no inspectable source supports the specified validation, atomic publication, import, and pruning interface.

children.title: Bound Sharing
children.top_down_role: Covers dissemination of objective-bound improvements across workers.

assumptions_latex: The problem is \(z^*=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\).
Every submitted lower bound \(L_i\) satisfies \(L_i\le z^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate \(L=\max_i L_i\) satisfies \(L\le z^*\) and dominates every submitted lower bound.

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound supplied by worker i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the maximum of valid minimization lower bounds is valid and strongest among them
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation of global objective bounds for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each worker \(i\) publishes a valid global lower bound \(L_i\le z^*\), define the shared bound by \(L=\max_i L_i\). Then \(L_i\le L\le z^*\) for every \(i\). A worker may replace its local global bound by \(L\). If a feasible incumbent of value \(U\) is also known, equality \(L=U\) certifies optimality, while \(L>U\) signals an invalid update or inconsistent objective convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, share the maximum of valid global lower bounds. It remains valid, strengthens every submitted bound, and certifies optimality when equal to the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Sharing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The maximum-of-valid-lower-bounds property is standard, but the candidate supplies no citation and does not explicitly define a nonempty finite worker index set over which the maximum is taken.

children.title: Domain Sharing
children.top_down_role: Covers dissemination of valid domain reductions across workers.

assumptions_latex: Each variable \(x_j\) has a finite current domain \(D_j\).
Every exported domain \(E_{ij}\) contains every value of \(x_j\) occurring in a globally feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The imported domain \(D'_j=D_j\cap\bigcap_i E_{ij}\) removes no globally feasible value.

notation.meaning: Globally valid domain enclosure exported by worker i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: intersections of globally valid domain enclosures preserve all feasible assignments
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharing only globally valid finite-domain reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each variable \(x_j\), a worker may export an enclosure \(E_{ij}\subseteq D_j\) only after establishing that every globally feasible assignment has \(x_j\in E_{ij}\). An importing worker computes \(D'_j=D_j\cap\bigcap_i E_{ij}\), propagates the resulting reductions, and reports infeasibility if \(D'_j=\varnothing\). Search-local reductions depending on unshared decisions are not admissible as global domain updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers intersect current domains with globally valid shared enclosures; reductions depending on private search decisions cannot be imported globally.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain Sharing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intersection claim is sound under the stated global-validity hypothesis, and algorithm fits the leaf, but no source supports this particular CP-SAT domain-export and import protocol.

children.title: Nogood Sharing
children.top_down_role: Covers dissemination of learned infeasibility information across workers.

assumptions_latex: All workers use a common Boolean encoding with literal set \(\mathcal L\).
A submitted clause is checked against the original model rather than only a worker's current branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A clause \(C=\bigvee_{\ell\in S}\ell\) is globally shareable exactly when every feasible assignment satisfies \(C\).

notation.meaning: Set of Boolean literals in the common encoding
Finite literal set defining the submitted clause
Feasible assignments of the original encoded model

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: globally valid learned clauses may be imported without excluding feasible assignments
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for globally shared Boolean nogoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathcal L\) be finite and let \(C=\bigvee_{\ell\in S}\ell\). The nogood is admissible for global sharing if and only if \(a\models C\) for every \(a\in F\), equivalently no feasible assignment makes every literal in \(S\) false. A clause derived under temporary assumptions may be shared only when those assumptions occur within the clause or have been eliminated by a valid derivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned clause may be shared globally only if every feasible assignment satisfies it; temporary assumptions must be represented or validly eliminated.
knowledge_statements.title: Nogood Sharing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global-validity condition is mathematically coherent, and condition fits the leaf. An inspectable source is still required for the common-encoding and temporary-assumption sharing rules.

children.title: Shared-Information Admission
children.top_down_role: Covers filtering, timing, and relevance controls for imported information.

assumptions_latex: Each message \(m\) has a validity predicate \(V(m)\), utility estimate \(q(m)\), and import cost \(c(m)\ge0\).
The receiver has an import budget \(B\ge0\) for the admission epoch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An admitted set \(A\) must satisfy \(A\subseteq\{m:V(m)\}\) and \(\sum_{m\in A}c(m)\le B\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: admission requires semantic validity and aggregate compliance with an import budget
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-first, budgeted admission of shared portfolio information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate message set \(M\), an admission rule selects \(A\subseteq M\) subject to \(V(m)\) for every \(m\in A\) and \(\sum_{m\in A}c(m)\le B\). Invalid messages are rejected independently of estimated utility. Among valid messages, a deterministic admissible policy may select a maximizer of \(\sum_{m\in A}q(m)\) under the budget constraint, with a fixed tie-breaking order. Deferred messages remain eligible in later epochs unless declared stale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Admit only semantically valid messages whose total import cost fits the epoch budget, optionally maximizing estimated utility with deterministic tie-breaking.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Information Admission

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source establishes this budgeted utility-maximization model as a shared-information admission rule. The validity and budget constraints are coherent, but the utility objective, tie-breaking, and deferred-message policy are unsupported design choices.

children.title: Portfolio Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Covers ordering, activation, and time allocation among subsolvers.

assumptions_latex: There are \(P\) worker slots and finitely many runnable subsolvers \(I\).
Scheduling occurs in discrete epochs \(t=0,1,\ldots\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every epoch satisfies \(\sum_{i\in I}a_i(t)\le P\), so no more than \(P\) subsolvers execute concurrently.

notation.meaning: Indicator that subsolver i is scheduled in epoch t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: epoch scheduling is a capacity-constrained selection of runnable subsolvers
