knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epoch-based scheduling of a parallel search portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At epoch \(t\), form the runnable set \(R(t)\subseteq I\). Assign each \(i\in R(t)\) a priority \(p_i(t)\), select at most \(P\) indices of greatest priority using a fixed tie-breaking rule, and set \(a_i(t)=1\) exactly for selected indices. Run each selected subsolver for its assigned quantum, collect its outputs, update priorities and runnable states, and repeat until infeasibility, optimality, or the external termination limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each epoch, schedule at most the available number of runnable subsolvers by priority, run their quanta, import results, and update priorities.
knowledge_statements.title: Portfolio Scheduling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is appropriate for the scheduling leaf, but no citation supports the proposed epoch, priority, quantum, state-update, and termination mechanics as CP-SAT portfolio architecture.

children.title: Resource Control
children.top_down_role: Covers limits on threads, memory, deterministic effort, and worker capacity.

assumptions_latex: Each scheduled subsolver \(i\) receives nonnegative resource amounts \(r_{ik}\) for resource types \(k\in K\).
Each resource type has capacity \(R_k\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A resource assignment is feasible exactly when \(r_{ik}\ge0\) and \(\sum_i r_{ik}\le R_k\) for every \(k\in K\).

notation.meaning: Amount of resource k assigned to subsolver i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: concurrent resource allocations must satisfy nonnegativity and per-resource capacity constraints
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity constraints for CPU, memory, and communication resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every controlled resource \(k\in K\), choose allocations \(r_{ik}\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_i r_{ik}\le R_k\). A subsolver may execute only when its allocation meets any declared minimum \(d_{ik}\), namely \(r_{ik}\ge d_{ik}\). If a capacity would be exceeded, the controller must reduce allocations, suspend subsolvers, or reject new work before execution. Resource accounting includes portfolio coordination overhead whenever that overhead consumes the same finite capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource control enforces nonnegative per-subsolver allocations, capacity limits, execution minima, and accounting for coordination overhead.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact feasibility conclusion includes only nonnegativity and capacities, while the statement additionally imposes declared execution minima. The subsolver index for the resource sums is also not introduced, and no source supports the control policy.

children.title: Schedule–Resource Coupling
children.top_down_role: Covers how resource constraints shape worker activation and portfolio balance.

assumptions_latex: At epoch \(t\), scheduler indicators are \(a_i(t)\in\{0,1\}\).
An active subsolver \(i\) requires at least \(d_{ik}\ge0\) units of each resource \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Schedule and resources are compatible only if \(a_i(t)d_{ik}\le r_{ik}(t)\) and \(\sum_i r_{ik}(t)\le R_k(t)\) for all \(i,k,t\).

notation.meaning: Activity indicator for subsolver i at epoch t
Resource k assigned to subsolver i at epoch t
Available amount of resource k at epoch t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scheduling decisions and resource feasibility are linked by activation constraints
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activation constraints linking portfolio schedules to finite resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A schedule is resource-realizable only when every active assignment is backed by its required resources: \(a_i(t)d_{ik}\le r_{ik}(t)\) for all \(i,k,t\). Simultaneously, \(\sum_i r_{ik}(t)\le R_k(t)\) must hold for every \(k,t\). Thus changing the active set can change feasible allocations, and a decrease in \(R_k(t)\) requires rescheduling whenever the current inequalities cease to hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduled subsolver must receive its minimum resources, while aggregate allocations remain within capacity; capacity changes can therefore force rescheduling.
knowledge_statements.title: Schedule–Resource Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The activation and capacity inequalities coherently express schedule-resource coupling, but the domain r_ik(t)>=0 and the resource index set are not explicitly introduced. No source supports this architecture-specific formulation.

children.title: Resource Starvation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers portfolio configurations that deprive useful workers of sufficient capacity.

assumptions_latex: A runnable subsolver \(i\) requires \(d_{ik}>0\) units of at least one resource \(k\).
Its allocations over epochs are \(r_{ik}(t)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent starvation occurs when \(\sum_{t=t_0}^{\infty}r_{ik}(t)<\infty\) for a required resource, and complete starvation when \(r_{ik}(t)=0\) for all \(t\ge t_0\).

notation.meaning: Resource k allocated to subsolver i in epoch t
Positive execution requirement for resource k
Epoch after which starvation is assessed

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite cumulative service to a perpetually runnable task formalizes persistent resource starvation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent denial of a resource required for subsolver progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose subsolver \(i\) remains runnable after epoch \(t_0\) and needs resource \(k\) to progress. It is completely starved if \(r_{ik}(t)=0\) for every \(t\ge t_0\). More generally, finite cumulative service \(\sum_{t=t_0}^{\infty}r_{ik}(t)<\infty\) is a persistent-starvation regime whenever unbounded cumulative service is necessary for unbounded search progress. Capacity feasibility alone does not exclude this regime; a fairness or minimum-service condition is additionally required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perpetually runnable subsolver is starved when it receives only finite cumulative service for a resource needed to make continuing progress.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource Starvation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Finite cumulative allocation is not intrinsically starvation without a defined service scale and the additional hypothesis that unbounded cumulative service is necessary for continuing progress. That qualifier appears in the statement but is omitted from the conclusion; no source establishes the proposed boundary.

children.title: Restart Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Covers restart timing or frequency that discards useful search progress.

assumptions_latex: A search run has restart times \(0=\tau_0<\tau_1<\cdots\).
After each restart, the worker retains only information in a state \(S_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A restart pathology occurs when \(\sup_k(\tau_{k+1}-\tau_k)<h\) for a progress threshold \(h\), or when infinitely many restarts reproduce an identical ineffective state-policy pair.

notation.meaning: Search state retained at the k-th restart
Minimum uninterrupted horizon needed for the specified progress event

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: overly short restart intervals or repeated identical post-restart states can prevent search progress
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure mechanisms caused by restart timing and retained search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a progress event that cannot occur within fewer than \(h>0\) units of uninterrupted search. If \(\tau_{k+1}-\tau_k<h\) for every sufficiently large \(k\), restarting prevents that event indefinitely. A second pathology arises when infinitely many restarts return to the same retained state \(S_k=S\) and the same deterministic branching policy, thereby reproducing the same finite search prefix without acquiring information that excludes it. Either mechanism defeats diversification or eventual exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restarts become pathological when intervals are always too short for progress or repeatedly regenerate the same ineffective deterministic search prefix.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Pathologies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conclusion uses sup_k(tau_{k+1}-tau_k)<h, whereas the statement requires only eventually short intervals. Repeating a state-policy pair also implies repetition only with sufficiently deterministic, unchanged search conditions and no newly retained information. A source is required to fix the intended failure boundary.

children.title: Branching Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Covers decision policies that repeatedly explore low-value search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Pathologies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational failure criterion for branching policies within a restarted CP-SAT portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For search episodes \(e=1,\ldots,m\), let \(V_e\) be the set of decision literals selected during episode \(e\), and let \(P_e\) be its propagation or objective progress. Branching is pathological at thresholds \(\rho,\varepsilon>0\) when \[\frac{1}{m}\sum_{e=1}^{m}\mathbf{1}\!\left\{\frac{|V_e\cap V_{e-1}|}{|V_e\cup V_{e-1}|}\ge 1-\rho\right\}\ge 1-\rho \quad\text{and}\quad \frac{1}{m}\sum_{e=1}^{m}P_e\le\varepsilon.\] Thus nearly identical branching decisions recur while producing negligible progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching is pathological when successive search episodes repeatedly choose nearly identical decision literals yet achieve negligible propagation or objective progress.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge 2\) search episodes are observed.
\(P_e\ge 0\) uses one fixed progress measure across episodes.
\(|V_e\cup V_{e-1}|>0\) for every compared pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{High branching overlap together with low mean progress certifies branching pathology at }(\rho,\varepsilon).\)

notation.meaning: decision literals selected in episode e

review_flags: solver-specific branching pathology criterion requires an architecture source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports this solver-specific pathology certificate or its thresholds. The sum starts at e=1 but uses V_{e-1}, so V_0 is undefined; the intended comparison likely runs from e=2 to m with adjusted normalization.

children.title: Restart–Branching Feedback
children.top_down_role: Covers reinforcing interactions between restart behavior and branching choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart–Branching Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-feedback failure between restart timing and post-restart branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_e\) be the search state immediately after restart \(e\), \(B(s_e)\) the resulting branching prefix, and \(T(s_e)\) the conflicts until the next restart. Restart–branching feedback is adverse when, for tolerances \(\delta,\tau>0\), \[d\!\left(B(s_{e+1}),B(s_e)\right)\le\delta,\qquad T(s_{e+1})\le\tau,\] for a sustained sequence of episodes, while no incumbent or bound improves. The restart then recreates conditions selecting the same unproductive prefix and rapidly triggers another restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adverse feedback loop occurs when restarts repeatedly reconstruct the same unproductive branching prefix, quickly cause further restarts, and improve neither solutions nor bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is a fixed distance on finite branching prefixes.
Restart and branching policies remain unchanged over the observed episodes.
Incumbent and bound values are compared using fixed objective conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Persistent prefix similarity, short episodes, and zero primal-dual progress constitute adverse restart--branching feedback.}\)
review_flags: solver-specific feedback criterion requires an architecture source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this CP-SAT restart–branching feedback criterion. “A sustained sequence” is not quantified, and the conditions shown for one adjacent pair do not formally express persistence or zero incumbent/bound improvement.

children.title: Search Diversity Collapse
children.top_down_role: Covers loss of effective search diversity caused by maladaptive restart or branching behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Search Diversity Collapse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Portfolio-level criterion for loss of behavioral diversity among workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For workers \(i=1,\ldots,p\), let \(Q_i(t)\) be the empirical distribution of search features up to time \(t\), such as selected literals, neighborhoods, or visited objective bands. Define \[D(t)=\frac{2}{p(p-1)}\sum_{i<j}d\!\left(Q_i(t),Q_j(t)\right).\] Search diversity collapses at tolerance \(\delta>0\) when \(D(t)\le\delta\) throughout a nontrivial interval and portfolio progress is no better than that of a representative single worker.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search diversity collapses when workers exhibit nearly identical search behavior for a sustained interval without outperforming a representative single worker.
assumptions_latex: \(p\ge 2\) workers use comparable feature distributions.
\(d\) is a bounded divergence or metric.
Single-worker and portfolio progress use the same resource normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(t)\le\delta\) with no portfolio advantage identifies diversity collapse.
review_flags: portfolio diversity metric and comparison baseline require a solver source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed feature distributions, diversity metric, sustained interval, and “representative single worker” baseline are architecture-specific and uncited. Their definitions materially determine whether the claimed failure regime holds.

children.title: Misleading Solution Hints
children.top_down_role: Covers hints that divert search toward poor or infeasible regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Misleading Solution Hints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Performance-based criterion for harmful partial or complete solution hints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a partial assignment supplied as a solution hint, and compare otherwise identical solver runs with and without \(H\). For a fixed resource budget \(R\), write \(G_H(R)\) and \(G_0(R)\) for their final primal-dual gaps. The hint is misleading at margin \(\eta>0\) when \[G_H(R)\ge G_0(R)+\eta,\] or when the hinted run fails to find a feasible solution that the unhinted run finds within \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solution hint is misleading when, under a fixed budget, it worsens the final gap or prevents discovery of feasibility relative to an otherwise identical unhinted run.
assumptions_latex: Hinted and unhinted runs have the same model, budget, parameters, and random seed.
The primal-dual gap convention is fixed and finite whenever compared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_H(R)\ge G_0(R)+\eta\), or comparative failure to find feasibility, identifies a misleading hint.
review_flags: comparative hint-failure definition requires CP-SAT documentation or empirical methodology source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No CP-SAT documentation or experimental-method source supports the proposed definition. A same-seed paired run is not by itself a generally reliable performance criterion for randomized search, and the handling of absent or infinite primal-dual gaps requires specification.

children.title: Primal–Dual Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Covers disproportionate effort between incumbent improvement and bound production.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap-progress imbalance between incumbent discovery and bound improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(U(t)\) be the best feasible objective value and \(L(t)\) a valid lower bound. Over \([t_0,t_1]\), define normalized improvements \[P=\frac{U(t_0)-U(t_1)}{S},\qquad D=\frac{L(t_1)-L(t_0)}{S},\] where \(S>0\) is fixed. Primal–dual progress is imbalanced at factor \(\kappa>1\) when \(P>\kappa D\) or \(D>\kappa P\), provided the remaining gap \(U(t_1)-L(t_1)\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal–dual progress is imbalanced when incumbent and bound improvements differ by more than a chosen factor while a positive optimality gap remains.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(U(t)\) is nonincreasing and \(L(t)\) is nondecreasing.
\(S>0\) is shared by both progress measures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P>\kappa D\) or \(D>\kappa P\), with positive residual gap, certifies primal--dual imbalance.

notation.meaning: incumbent upper bound and valid dual lower bound

review_flags: standard bound notions are clear, but the imbalance threshold is architecture-specific

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Primal and dual bound progress are standard, but the factor-kappa failure boundary is uncited and architecture-specific. The ratio-style disjunction also labels any positive progress on one side as imbalance when the other side has zero progress, which requires explicit justification.

children.title: Hint-Induced Search Bias
children.top_down_role: Covers persistent portfolio bias caused by overvaluing hinted candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Hint-Induced Search Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measurable change in branching distributions caused by a supplied hint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a solution hint, and let \(Q_H^k\) and \(Q_0^k\) be the distributions of the first \(k\) branching decisions in matched hinted and unhinted runs. At tolerance \(\delta>0\), the search exhibits hint-induced bias when \[d\!\left(Q_H^k,Q_0^k\right)\ge\delta.\] The bias is detrimental when the inequality persists over successive restart episodes and the hinted run has neither a better incumbent nor a better valid bound under the same resource budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hint induces search bias when it materially changes early branching distributions; the bias is detrimental if persistent and unsupported by incumbent or bound improvement.
assumptions_latex: Runs differ only by the presence of \(H\).
\(d\) is a fixed bounded distance between decision distributions.
Branching decisions are measured at the same episode positions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d(Q_H^k,Q_0^k)\ge\delta\) establishes hint-induced bias; absent progress makes persistent bias detrimental.

notation.meaning: number of initial branching decisions compared

review_flags: solver-specific mechanism connecting hints to branching requires a CP-SAT source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record combines a threshold definition and a detrimental-failure criterion, so property is not a clean fit for the terminal failure-regime context. No source establishes that CP-SAT hints induce the asserted branching-distribution mechanism or supports the chosen metric and threshold.

children.title: Evidence Imbalance Consequences
children.top_down_role: Covers weak termination evidence or poor solution quality arising from unbalanced progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Evidence Imbalance Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure consequences when portfolio resources disproportionately support primal or dual evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition total search resource \(R>0\) into \(R_P\) devoted to incumbent-producing work and \(R_D\) devoted to bound-producing work, with \(R_P+R_D=R\). Let \(P\\) and \(D\) denote the corresponding normalized improvements. Evidence imbalance is consequential at thresholds \(\alpha,\varepsilon>0\) when \[\min\{R_P,R_D\}\le\alpha R,\qquad \min\{P,D\}\le\varepsilon,\] and the residual optimality gap remains positive. Then termination evidence is bottlenecked by the neglected side despite progress on the favored side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extreme resource concentration on primal or dual work is consequential when the neglected side makes negligible progress and a positive optimality gap persists.
assumptions_latex: \(R_P,R_D\ge 0\) account for all measured search resource.
\(P,D\ge 0\) use fixed normalized progress measures.
The incumbent and dual bound are valid and comparable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Resource skew plus negligible progress on one side and a positive gap identifies consequential evidence imbalance.

notation.meaning: resources assigned to primal and dual evidence

review_flags: resource attribution and consequence criterion require a portfolio-architecture source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement contains malformed notation in “P\\” and provides no source for partitioning CP-SAT work cleanly into primal and dual resources. The displayed conditions do not ensure progress on the favored side, although the conclusion asserts such progress and a causal bottleneck.

knowledge_statements.title: LNS Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational stagnation criterion for large-neighborhood search workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_j\) be the incumbent objective after the \(j\)-th large-neighborhood-search iteration of a minimization run, and let \(C_j>0\) be that iteration's resource cost. For a window of \(w\) iterations, define \[Y_k=\frac{U_{k-w}-U_k}{\sum_{j=k-w+1}^{k}C_j}.\] LNS stagnates at tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) when \(Y_k\le\varepsilon\) for consecutive windows and the neighborhoods continue to yield only infeasible repairs, repeated incumbents, or improvements below the acceptance threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LNS stagnates when several consecutive iteration windows deliver negligible incumbent improvement per resource while repairs remain infeasible, repetitive, or too small to accept.
assumptions_latex: The objective is minimized and every recorded \(U_j\) is a valid incumbent value.
\(w\ge 1\) and each \(C_j>0\).
The neighborhood-generation and acceptance rules remain fixed during measurement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent \(Y_k\le\varepsilon\) together with unsuccessful or repetitive repairs identifies LNS stagnation.

notation.meaning: incumbent value after LNS iteration j

review_flags: LNS stagnation thresholds and CP-SAT integration require a dedicated source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No LNS or CP-SAT source supports this operational stagnation boundary. The number of consecutive windows and acceptance threshold are unspecified, and it is unclear whether the repair outcomes are required jointly with low yield or serve as alternative criteria.

children.title: Synchronization Overhead
children.top_down_role: Covers coordination costs that reduce productive parallel work.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel runtime bound exposing coordination and synchronization costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\ge 1\) workers, let \(W\) be total useful work, \(S\) the unavoidable serial time, and \(H_p\) the aggregate synchronization, communication, and waiting time on the critical path. The parallel runtime satisfies \[T_p\ge S+\frac{W}{p}+H_p.\] Hence the speedup obeys \[\frac{T_1}{T_p}\le\frac{T_1}{S+W/p+H_p}.\] Synchronization dominates useful parallel work when \(H_p\ge W/p\), preventing near-linear speedup even if work is otherwise balanced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel runtime includes an irreducible synchronization term; when that term exceeds useful work per worker, near-linear speedup is impossible.
assumptions_latex: \(H_p\) counts only delay lying on the execution critical path.
Useful work is divisible no better than \(W/p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_p\ge S+W/p+H_p\), and \(H_p\ge W/p\) marks synchronization-dominated execution.

notation.meaning: parallelizable work and unavoidable serial time

review_flags: parallel bound is standard, but CP-SAT synchronization accounting needs a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive lower bound does not follow merely from separate serial-time, divisible-work, and critical-path-overhead quantities; these terms may overlap unless a disjoint execution-time decomposition is assumed. No parallel-computing or CP-SAT source supports the formula or the synchronization-dominance boundary.

children.title: Redundant Worker Effort
children.top_down_role: Covers workers duplicating search without useful diversification.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Worker Effort
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overlap-based criterion for duplicated exploration by portfolio workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_i(t)\) be the set of normalized search tasks completed by worker \(i\) by time \(t\), where tasks may represent subproblems, neighborhoods, or branching prefixes. Define the unique-work ratio \[U(t)=\frac{|\bigcup_{i=1}^{p}E_i(t)|}{\sum_{i=1}^{p}|E_i(t)|}.\] Worker effort is redundant at threshold \(\rho\in(0,1)\) when \(U(t)\le 1-\rho\) and duplicated tasks contribute no distinct incumbent, bound, clause, or infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worker effort is redundant when a large fraction of completed search tasks overlaps and the duplicates contribute no distinct solution, bound, clause, or certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(p\ge 2\) workers use a common task identity.
Each \(E_i(t)\) is finite and the denominator is positive.
Shared outputs are normalized before distinctness is assessed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U(t)\le 1-\rho\) without distinct useful outputs identifies redundant worker effort.

notation.meaning: normalized tasks completed by worker i
ratio of unique tasks to total worker tasks

review_flags: task identity and useful-output criterion require a portfolio implementation source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No portfolio implementation source defines a common task identity across heterogeneous workers or supports this overlap threshold. The additional requirement concerning distinct incumbents, bounds, clauses, or certificates also needs a precise attribution rule.

children.title: Information Pollution
children.top_down_role: Covers low-value shared information that disrupts worker priorities or local reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Information Pollution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Utility-based failure criterion for low-value shared search information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: During interval \(I\), let \(M_I\) be the shared messages imported by workers and \(A_I\subseteq M_I\) those that subsequently cause a measurable propagation, bound improvement, incumbent improvement, or certified pruning event. Define \[q_I=\frac{|A_I|}{|M_I|},\qquad c_I=\sum_{m\in M_I}c(m).\] Information pollution occurs at thresholds \(\varepsilon,C>0\) when \(q_I\le\varepsilon\), \(c_I\ge C\), and importing \(M_I\) yields no net progress advantage over a matched run without those imports.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shared information becomes pollution when few imported messages cause useful events, processing cost is substantial, and imports provide no net progress advantage.
assumptions_latex: \(|M_I|>0\) and every processing cost \(c(m)\ge 0\).
Useful events are attributed using one fixed causal rule.
The comparison run differs only in importing the selected messages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Low actionable fraction, high processing cost, and no comparative benefit identify information pollution.

notation.meaning: imported and actionable messages during interval I

review_flags: message utility and causal attribution require a solver coordination source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The actionable-message fraction and causal attribution rule are solver-specific and uncited. The matched run without imports is a counterfactual experimental condition whose construction and progress statistic materially affect the definition.

children.title: Parallel Efficiency Collapse
children.top_down_role: Covers regimes where additional workers yield negligible or negative benefit.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Efficiency Collapse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-scaling failure criterion for a parallel CP-SAT portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_1\) and \(T_p\) be the resources required by one and \(p\ge 2\) workers to reach the same target event, using a fixed runtime statistic for randomized runs. Define speedup and efficiency by \[S_p=\frac{T_1}{T_p},\qquad E_p=\frac{S_p}{p}.\] Parallel efficiency collapses at threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\) when \(E_p\le\eta\), or equivalently \(T_p\ge T_1/(\eta p)\), and adding workers does not improve the chosen target statistic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel efficiency collapses when normalized speedup falls below a threshold and additional workers fail to improve time to the same target event.
assumptions_latex: All runs solve the same instance and use the same target event.
\(T_1,T_p>0\) use the same resource and randomized-run statistic.
Worker count satisfies \(p\ge 2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_p\le\eta\) with no marginal improvement from added workers identifies parallel efficiency collapse.

notation.meaning: resources to a common target with one and p workers

review_flags: strong-scaling definitions are standard, but the CP-SAT failure threshold needs a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Speedup and efficiency are standard, but the CP-SAT collapse threshold and target statistic are uncited. E_p<=eta is equivalent to T_p>=T_1/(eta p), but neither condition is equivalent to the additional assertion that adding workers gives no improvement; the worker-count comparison needed for that assertion is undefined.

children.title: Solver Correctness Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Separates internal semantic guarantees from externally checkable proof artifacts.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: OR-Tools CP-SAT documentation and source tree
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: CP-SAT return values; cp_model.proto; model validation and response checking
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: OR-Tools CP-SAT documentation and source tree

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Proof Complexity and SAT Solving

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Schrijver, Sizes and Good Characterizations; Cutting Plane Proofs
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

children.title: Expansion Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Covers preservation obligations for expanded model representations.

assumptions_latex: The original model is \(M=(X,F,c)\) with feasible set \(S=\{x\in X:F(x)\}\).
The expanded model is \(M^+=(X\times Y,F^+,c^+)\), with projection \(\pi(x,y)=x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi(S^+)=S\) and corresponding feasible solutions have equal objective values.

notation.meaning: Feasible sets of the original and expanded models.
Projection from expanded assignments to original assignments.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact extension equivalence for auxiliary-variable expansion of a finite CP-SAT model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S^+=\{(x,y)\in X\times Y:F^+(x,y)\}\). The expansion is equivalent to \(M\) when \[\pi(S^+)=S\] and, for every \((x,y)\in S^+\), \[c^+(x,y)=c(\pi(x,y)).\] Thus every original feasible assignment has at least one feasible extension, every expanded feasible assignment projects to an original feasible assignment, and optimization over either model has the same attainable objective values and optimum status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expansion is equivalent when feasible expanded assignments project exactly onto the original feasible set and preserve every corresponding objective value.
knowledge_statements.title: Expansion Equivalence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property matches the Expansion Equivalence leaf and is mathematically coherent for exact auxiliary-variable expansion, but no inspectable citation is supplied for the CP-SAT architecture-specific formulation.

children.title: Presolve Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Covers preservation obligations for presolve transformations.

assumptions_latex: The original and presolved models have feasible sets \(S\) and \(S_p\).
Maps \(P:S\to S_p\) and \(R:S_p\to S\) are supplied for retained and reconstructed assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility, infeasibility, and optimal objective value are preserved, and every reduced solution reconstructs to a valid original solution.

notation.meaning: Presolve projection and postsolve reconstruction maps.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution and objective equivalence for exact presolve reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Presolve equivalence holds when \(S=\varnothing\) if and only if \(S_p=\varnothing\), and when both sets are nonempty, \[R(S_p)\subseteq S,\qquad c(R(z))=c_p(z)\quad(z\in S_p),\] while for every \(x\in S\) there exists \(z\in S_p\) satisfying \(c_p(z)\le c(x)\). Consequently, \[\min_{x\in S}c(x)=\min_{z\in S_p}c_p(z),\] and an optimal presolved assignment reconstructs to an optimal original assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact presolve preserves infeasibility and optimal value, while its reconstruction map converts every reduced feasible solution into an equally valued original solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Equivalence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the stated presolve contract. A source is also needed to determine whether finite feasible sets or attained minima are assumed; otherwise the displayed minima need not exist. The supplied map P is not used in the statement.

children.title: Composed Transformation Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Covers correctness across pipelines combining expansion with presolve.

assumptions_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,k\), transformation \(T_i\) relates feasible sets \(S_{i-1}\) and \(S_i\).
Each stage has a reconstruction map \(R_i:S_i\to S_{i-1}\) preserving feasibility and objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The composed reconstruction \(R_1\circ\cdots\circ R_k\) preserves feasibility and objective value from \(S_k\) to \(S_0\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set after transformation stage i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of exact model equivalence under a finite transformation chain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each stage satisfies \(R_i(S_i)\subseteq S_{i-1}\) and \(c_{i-1}(R_i(z))=c_i(z)\) for every \(z\in S_i\), and each stage preserves infeasibility and optimal value. Define \[R=R_1\circ R_2\circ\cdots\circ R_k.\] Then \(R(S_k)\subseteq S_0\), \(c_0(R(z))=c_k(z)\) for every \(z\in S_k\), and \(S_0\) and \(S_k\) have identical feasibility status and optimal objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite composition of exact transformations remains exact; composing their reconstruction maps preserves feasibility, objective values, infeasibility, and optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Composed Transformation Equivalence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The composition claim fits the leaf and follows from the stated stagewise contracts, but those contracts and their applicability to the intended transformation chain have no inspectable source.

children.title: Equivalence Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Covers transformation cases where solution or objective correspondence can be lost.

assumptions_latex: A claimed transformation uses projection \(P\), reconstruction \(R\), and original and transformed feasible sets \(S,S'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of feasible-set coverage, reconstruction feasibility, objective preservation, or exact arithmetic invalidates full transformation equivalence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary boundaries for claiming exact, rather than merely relaxation-based, equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Full equivalence fails if any one of the following occurs: \[P(S)
e S',\qquad R(S')
subseteq S,\qquad c(R(z))
e c'(z)	ext{ for some }z\in S'.\] It also fails when overflow, truncation, or unchecked division changes a transformed coefficient or bound. For example, replacing \(2x\le1\) over \(x\in\mathbb Z\) by \(x\le1\), rather than the exact \(x\le0\), introduces the spurious feasible assignment \(x=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalence is lost when projection misses solutions, reconstruction creates invalid ones, objectives change, or inexact arithmetic alters a constraint or bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the terminal container, and the integer-rounding example is correct. However, no source fixes the intended notion of full equivalence or establishes that each listed condition is necessary for that architecture-specific notion.

assumptions_latex: A transformed feasible assignment \(z\in S_k\) and recorded inverse transformations \(R_k,\ldots,R_1\) are given.
Each \(R_i:S_i\to S_{i-1}\) is defined on every feasible assignment produced at stage \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Postsolve returns a feasible original assignment with the transformed assignment's objective value.

notation.meaning: Assignment reconstructed after reversing stages k through i+1.
Inverse record for transformation stage i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic reversal of recorded presolve and expansion transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(z_k=z\). For \(i=k,k-1,\ldots,1\), compute \[z_{i-1}=R_i(z_i).\] Stop with failure if an inverse record is absent, its precondition is false, or the reconstructed value violates its declared domain. Otherwise output \(z_0\). Correct reconstruction requires \[z_i\in S_i\Longrightarrow z_{i-1}\in S_{i-1}\quad\text{and}\quad c_{i-1}(z_{i-1})=c_i(z_i).\] Hence successful termination yields \(z_0\in S_0\) with \(c_0(z_0)=c_k(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Postsolve reverses transformations in order, validating each inverse step, and returns an original feasible assignment with the same objective value.
knowledge_statements.title: Postsolve Reconstruction Correctness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record combines a reconstruction algorithm with a correctness claim and is locally relevant, but no source supports the inverse-record preconditions or objective-preservation contract. The source should also clarify whether this correctness leaf is intended to contain an algorithm or a theorem/property about postsolve.

children.title: Objective Mapping Correctness
children.top_down_role: Covers preservation of objective meaning across transformed model representations.

assumptions_latex: Original and transformed feasible assignments correspond through \(R:S'\to S\).
The transformed objective is related to the original by constants \(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective ordering and the set of reconstructed minimizers are preserved.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine objective correspondence for minimization models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Objective mapping is correct when every \(z\in S'\) satisfies \[c'(z)=\alpha c(R(z)) +\beta,\qquad \alpha>0,\] and every \(x\in S\) has a corresponding \(z\in S'\) with the same equality. Then for corresponding assignments \(z_1,z_2\), \[c'(z_1)\le c'(z_2)\Longleftrightarrow c(R(z_1))\le c(R(z_2)).\] Therefore transformed minimizers reconstruct to original minimizers, and \(v'=\alpha v+\beta\) for the respective optimal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive affine objective transformation preserves ordering and minimizers, with transformed optimum equal to the scaled and shifted original optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Mapping Correctness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Positive affine scaling preserves minimization order, but no citation is supplied. The phrase 'corresponding z' should be source-grounded or formalized to require R(z)=x; the displayed equality alone only establishes objective-value coverage, not assignment correspondence.

children.title: Assumption Mapping Correctness
children.top_down_role: Covers preservation of assumption identity and diagnostic correspondence.

assumptions_latex: The original model has assumption literals \(A\), and the transformed model has literals \(A'\).
A literal map \(\mu:A\to A'\) and assignment correspondence \(R:S'\to S\) are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mapped assumptions have exactly the same truth and activation semantics on corresponding assignments.

notation.meaning: Map from original assumptions to transformed literals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truth-preserving correspondence for assumptions used to activate constraints or report cores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assumption mapping is correct when, for every corresponding feasible assignment \(z\in S'\) and every \(a\in A\), \[a(R(z))=\mu(a)(z).\] Moreover, for each subset \(B\subseteq A\), the original model under \(B\) is feasible if and only if the transformed model under \(\mu(B)=\{\mu(a):a\in B\}\) is feasible. If cores are reported, every transformed core \(C'\subseteq\mu(A)\) must map back to an original infeasible assumption set \(\mu^{-1}(C')\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assumption mapping must preserve literal truth, feasibility under every assumption subset, and the validity of any mapped-back infeasible core.
knowledge_statements.title: Assumption Mapping Correctness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf, but the semantics of models 'under' assumption subsets, the domain of corresponding assignments, and core pullback under a potentially noninjective literal map require an architecture-specific source.

children.title: Cross-Representation Mapping
children.top_down_role: Covers traceability between original entities and transformed counterparts.

assumptions_latex: Representations \(U\) and \(V\) encode the same model states.
Encoding \(E:U\to V\) and decoding \(D:V\to U\) are defined on valid states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Encoding and decoding preserve validity, constraints, objective values, and all observables required by certificates.

notation.meaning: Encoding and decoding maps between representations.
Sets of valid states in the two representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lossless correspondence between model, solver, and certificate representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cross-representation mapping is lossless on valid states \(U_0\subseteq U\) and \(V_0\subseteq V\) when \[D(E(u))=u\quad(u\in U_0),\qquad E(D(v))=v\quad(v\in V_0).\] For each atomic constraint or literal \(q\), satisfaction must commute with encoding, \[q(u)=q_E(E(u)),\] and the encoded objective must equal the original objective up to a declared order-preserving affine transformation. Identifiers used in explanations, assumptions, and certificates must also decode to the originating objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lossless representation map is invertible on valid states and preserves constraints, objectives, literals, and certificate identifiers.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Representation Mapping

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the terminal container, but no source supports the proposed certificate-preserving observables. The statement should also establish that E maps U_0 into V_0 and D maps V_0 into U_0, and explicitly quantify the states for the satisfaction equation.

children.title: Mapping Loss Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Covers transformation cases that can obscure objective or assumption provenance.

assumptions_latex: A mapping \(E:U	o V\) is used to transfer models, assignments, objectives, or assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any noninjectivity affecting required observables, arithmetic distortion, or unmapped identifier prevents lossless reconstruction and exact correspondence.

notation.meaning: A required observable such as feasibility, objective, or literal truth.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp conditions under which representation transfer ceases to be certificate-preserving.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Losslessness fails if there exist \(u_1,u_2\in U_0\) with \[E(u_1)=E(u_2)\quad\text{but}\quad q(u_1)\ne q(u_2)\] for any required observable \(q\). It also fails when finite-width overflow, rounding, unsupported coefficients, or identifier deletion changes constraint truth, objective order, or assumption identity. For example, encoding distinct bounds \(x\le2^{63}-1\) and \(x\le2^{63}\) as the same saturated bound destroys injectivity and prevents exact decoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mapping is lossy when distinct relevant states collapse, arithmetic is distorted, or identifiers needed for objectives, assumptions, explanations, or certificates disappear.
knowledge_statements.title: Mapping Loss Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate and the saturation example illustrates information loss, but no inspectable source defines which observables and identifiers must be preserved by the intended solver-to-certificate mapping.

children.title: Boolean Propagation Soundness
children.top_down_role: Covers semantic validity of Boolean propagation outcomes.

assumptions_latex: A Boolean constraint set \(F\) and current consistent partial assignment \(P\) are given.
A propagator emits a literal \(\ell\) with an explanation \(E\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every emitted Boolean literal is entailed by the constraints and its explanation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic soundness of Boolean unit propagation and its recorded explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Boolean propagation is sound if every propagation event satisfies \[F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models\ell.\] Equivalently, \(F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\land\neg\ell\) is unsatisfiable. A reported conflict with explanation \(E\) is sound when \[F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models\bot.\] Because \(E\subseteq P\), adding \(\ell\) removes no completion of the current partial assignment that satisfies \(F\), and the explanation can be checked independently of the propagator's internal state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean propagation is sound when each inferred literal, or conflict, logically follows from the constraints and the recorded explanation literals.
knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Propagation Soundness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The entailment conditions are a precise standard formulation of Boolean propagation and conflict soundness, and the property kind fits the leaf. No authoritative section, theorem, or solver-specific reference is supplied, so it cannot be accepted at candidate review.

children.title: Integer Propagation Soundness
children.top_down_role: Covers semantic validity of integer-domain propagation outcomes.

assumptions_latex: Integer constraints \(F\) and current domains \(D=(D_1,\ldots,D_n)\) are given.
A propagator narrows variable \(x_j\) from \(D_j\) to \(D'_j\subseteq D_j\) using explanation \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The narrowing removes no integer solution satisfying the constraints and explanation.

notation.meaning: Cartesian product of current integer domains.
Explanation predicate for the domain inference.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic soundness of integer-domain reduction and conflict detection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D=\prod_{i=1}^nD_i\). Integer propagation is sound if each narrowing satisfies \[\{x\in\mathcal D:F(x)\land E(x)\}\subseteq\{x\in\mathcal D:x_j\in D'_j\}.\] A domain conflict is sound when \[\{x\in\mathcal D:F(x)\land E(x)\}=\varnothing.\] Thus every integer solution compatible with the current domains and explanation survives the reduction, while a conflict certifies that no such compatible solution exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer propagation is sound when every domain reduction retains all compatible solutions and every reported domain conflict follows from the constraints and explanation.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer Propagation Soundness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-inclusion formulation correctly expresses semantic domain-reduction soundness, but the explanation E is used as a predicate without its solver semantics being sourced or fully introduced. No inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Linear Propagation Soundness
children.top_down_role: Covers semantic validity of linear-constraint propagation outcomes.

assumptions_latex: A valid linear inequality \(a^Tx\le b\) over integer variables has current bounds \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\).
A propagator derives a tighter bound on one variable using exact arithmetic or checked outward rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The derived bound is satisfied by every integer assignment obeying the inequality and current bounds.

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector and right-hand side of the propagated inequality.
Current lower and upper variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-propagation soundness for one integer linear inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a_j>0\), define the minimum contribution of the other variables by \[m_{-j}=\sum_{i\ne j}\min\{a_il_i,a_iu_i\}.\] The inferred upper bound \[x_j\le\left\lfloor\frac{b-m_{-j}}{a_j}\right\rfloor\] is sound because every assignment satisfying \(a^Tx\le b\) and the current bounds satisfies it. The analogous lower bound for \(a_j<0\) is obtained with the inequality direction reversed. A conflict is sound when the minimum possible left-hand side exceeds \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear propagation is sound when exact bound arithmetic derives only bounds satisfied by every feasible integer assignment, and conflicts only when minimum activity exceeds the limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Propagation Soundness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The upper-bound formula for a_j>0 and the minimum-activity conflict condition are mathematically sound for integer variables with finite stated bounds. An authoritative source is still required for the solver-specific exact-arithmetic or outward-rounding contract and for the omitted explicit a_j<0 formula.

children.title: Cross-Propagator Soundness
children.top_down_role: Covers validity preservation when multiple propagation domains exchange deductions.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the conjunction of the original Boolean, integer, linear, and scheduling constraints.
Every propagator emits an explanation over literals whose interpretations are fixed across all participating domains.
All previously recorded trail literals are logical consequences of \(F\) and the current decisions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cross-propagator inference preserves all solutions of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical soundness of explanations exchanged among heterogeneous propagators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be the original constraint conjunction and \(T\) a sound trail. Suppose a propagator derives \(\ell\) from reason literals \(R\subseteq T\), possibly using facts produced by other propagators. Cross-propagator soundness requires
\[
F\models \left(\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\right)\Rightarrow \ell.
\]
Each literal must have one common semantics in every participating domain. Consequently, adding \(\ell\) to \(T\), or learning the clause \(\bigvee_{r\in R}\neg r\vee\ell\), cannot remove any assignment satisfying \(F\) and the current decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagation exchanged between solver components is sound when its shared reason entails the propagated literal under the original model.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Propagator Soundness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the Cross-Propagator Soundness leaf and is internally coherent, but no citation is supplied. An authoritative CP-SAT source is needed to confirm that heterogeneous propagators share the asserted literal semantics and explanation interface.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the original constraint conjunction and \(T\) is a sound trail.
The integer variable \(x\) has an exact finite-domain interpretation.
Each antecedent literal in \(R\) is present on \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reason certifies the new bound and its Boolean encoding.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate route from antecedent literals to an encoded integer-bound inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a propagated lower bound \(x\ge b\) with reason \(R\subseteq T\), correctness is certified by
\[
F\models \left(\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\right)\Rightarrow (x\ge b).
\]
For an upper bound, replace the consequent by \(x\le b\). If the solver represents the bound by a Boolean literal \(p_b\), the encoding must also establish \(p_b\leftrightarrow(x\ge b)\), or the corresponding upper-bound equivalence. The reason clause \(\bigvee_{r\in R}\neg r\vee p_b\) is then valid and may participate in conflict analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer-bound reason is correct when its trail antecedents entail both the mathematical bound and the bound literal used by SAT reasoning.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Bound Reason Correctness Route

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the correctness-route container, but the exact relationship between an integer bound and its Boolean literal is implementation-dependent. With no source, the asserted equivalence and resulting reason-clause route cannot be reliably reviewed.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) includes the complete scheduling semantics for presence, start, duration, end, and resource literals.
\(T\) is a sound trail.
The scheduling propagator returns antecedents \(R\subseteq T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every explained scheduling propagation or conflict yields a clause entailed by \(F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound explanations for scheduling propagation and scheduling conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A scheduling propagation of literal \(\ell\) from reason \(R\) is sound exactly when
\[
F\models \left(\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\right)\Rightarrow\ell.
\]
A reported scheduling conflict is sound exactly when \(F\models\neg\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\). Thus the emitted clause is respectively \(\bigvee_{r\in R}\neg r\vee\ell\) or \(\bigvee_{r\in R}\neg r\), and is entailed by \(F\). Presence conditions and integer bounds used in \(R\) must retain their encoded meanings; otherwise the explanation does not certify the scheduling inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduling explanation is sound when its presence and bound antecedents entail the propagated literal, or jointly entail a conflict.
knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling-Explanation Soundness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle matches scheduling-explanation soundness, including propagation and conflict cases, but no source supports the claimed treatment of presence literals, integer bounds, and scheduling reasons. Those CP-SAT-specific semantics require an authoritative citation.

assumptions_latex: Every initial clause is entailed by the original model \(F\).
Every propagation reason used in conflict analysis is an entailed clause.
Clause transformations preserve logical consequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The learned clause \(C\) satisfies \(F\models C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entailment route for clauses learned from propagation explanations and conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_0\) be an entailed conflict clause. Construct \(C\) by repeatedly resolving the current clause with an entailed reason clause on complementary literals. Since resolution preserves entailment,
\[
F\models C_0,
\qquad
F\models C_i,
	ext{ and }
F\models D_i
\Longrightarrow
F\models \operatorname{resolve}(C_i,D_i)=C_{i+1}.
\]
After the final resolution or another consequence-preserving simplification, \(F\models C\). A checkable validity route records the initial conflict, every reason clause, each pivot, and the resulting learned clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned clause is valid when it is obtained from entailed conflict and reason clauses using consequence-preserving inference steps such as resolution.
knowledge_statements.title: Learned-Clause Validity Route

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the validity-route container, but the record has no source for the solver's actual conflict-analysis and simplification steps. The statement also contains proof-style justification and would need to be restated declaratively after authoritative sourcing.

assumptions_latex: The model has variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) with explicitly represented domains.
Each domain \(D_i\) is finite.
Branching and propagation never introduce values outside the initial domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complete assignment space \(D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite explicit domains as the termination regime for exhaustive CP-SAT search.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The finite-domain search regime holds when each decision variable \(x_i\) has a finite initial domain \(D_i\), so that
\[
\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^{n}D_i,
\qquad
|\Omega|=\prod_{i=1}^{n}|D_i|<\infty.
\]
A search procedure operates within this regime if every branch restricts at least one current domain, propagation only removes values, and a complete branching policy eventually separates every nonterminal subspace. Under these conditions the search tree has finite depth and finitely many distinct subproblems, although implementation fairness is additionally required for actual termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search is finite-domain when every variable has finitely many values and branching progressively partitions the resulting finite assignment space.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Search Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: Search-Space Exhaustion
children.top_down_role: Covers completion evidence from eliminating or resolving every remaining search region.

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) is the finite initial assignment space.
Every processed search node is either closed or partitioned into child nodes.
The search frontier is \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhaustion holds exactly when \(Q=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustion of all open nodes in a finite complete-search tree.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Partial Enumeration p. 14

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Search-space exhaustion is the state \(Q=\varnothing\), where \(Q\) contains every generated but unclosed search node. Completeness additionally requires that the root represents \(\Omega\), every branching step replaces \(S_v\) by children whose union is \(S_v\), and closure is justified by infeasibility, complete assignment evaluation, or an objective bound. Hence every \(a\in\Omega\) belongs to a closed leaf or to a subspace closed by a sound certificate; no unexplored assignment remains represented by an open node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search space is exhausted when no open node remains and sound branching and closure account for every initial assignment.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-Space Exhaustion

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2 Partial Enumeration p. 14

children.title: Enumeration Closure
children.top_down_role: Covers completion evidence that no qualifying unreported solutions remain.

assumptions_latex: The search tree is finite and rooted at a node representing \(\Omega\).
Every internal node is covered by its children.
Every leaf has a checkable closure justification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The root is closed, and therefore every assignment in \(\Omega\) is accounted for.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bottom-up certificate that a finite search enumeration is closed.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An enumeration-closure certificate is a finite rooted tree with root set \(S_r=\Omega\). Each internal node \(v\) records children satisfying
\[
S_v\subseteq\bigcup_{u\in\operatorname{ch}(v)}S_u,
\]
and each leaf records either a checked feasible assignment, a sound infeasibility certificate, or a sound objective-bound closure. Closure is verified bottom-up: certified leaves are closed, and an internal node is closed when all covering children are closed. The certificate is complete when this recursion closes the root.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumeration closure is certified by a finite covering search tree whose leaves all have valid evaluation, infeasibility, or bound certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Enumeration Closure

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: Exhaustion–Closure Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Covers how complete search supports closure claims for enumeration.

assumptions_latex: The recorded search run has a finite rooted tree whose root represents \(\Omega\).
Every recorded branching step replaces a node by children covering its represented set.
A node is removed from the recorded frontier only after sound closure or replacement by all recorded children.
The final frontier \(Q\) contains exactly the generated nodes not closed or replaced in the run record.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The final frontier satisfies \(Q=\varnothing\) if and only if the run record closes the root by a complete enumeration-closure certificate.

notation.meaning: initial assignment space represented by the root

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite recorded-run equivalence between operational exhaustion and certified enumeration closure.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite recorded search run satisfying sound coverage, closure, and frontier-update rules, \[ Q=\varnothing \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \text{the run record closes the root representing }\Omega\text{ by a complete enumeration certificate}. \] The equivalence concerns the final frontier defined by that same run record; it does not claim that the mere existence of a separately constructible certificate makes an unprocessed operational frontier empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite and correctly recorded search run, its final frontier is empty exactly when that same run record provides a complete enumeration certificate closing the root.
knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustion–Closure Correspondence

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: Residual Search Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Covers unresolved search regions that prevent a closure claim.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is the frontier when search stops.
Each node \(v\in Q\) represents an unclosed residual set \(S_v\).
Processed nodes obey sound coverage and closure rules.
The residual region is \(U=\bigcup_{v\in Q}S_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(U\ne\varnothing\) and no independent certificate closes it, no exhaustive infeasibility or optimality claim is justified over \(U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unclosed frontier regions that delimit valid complete-search conclusions.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Partial Enumeration p. 14

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At search termination, define the residual region by \[ U=\bigcup_{v\in Q}S_v. \] If \(U\ne\varnothing\) and no independent certificate closes it, search has established neither infeasibility nor optimality over \(U\). Feasible incumbents and verified regional bounds remain valid within their declared scopes. An enumeration-based global completion claim requires \(U=\varnothing\) or sound certificates closing every residual region represented by \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Open frontier nodes define a residual region over which exhaustive infeasibility or optimality cannot be claimed unless independent certificates close that region.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Search Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2 Partial Enumeration p. 14

children.title: Limit-Interrupted Search
children.top_down_role: Covers termination caused by configured time, effort, memory, or callback limits.

assumptions_latex: The solver halts because a time, node, memory, conflict, or external limit is reached.
The frontier \(Q\) is nonempty at interruption.
All retained local certificates are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Interruption alone establishes neither exhaustive infeasibility nor global optimality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion failure caused by resource or external interruption before frontier exhaustion.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If search stops at a limit with \(Q\ne\varnothing\), the stop event is not a completion certificate. For minimization, a feasible incumbent \(z^{\mathrm{inc}}\) and a valid bound \(B\le z^*\) may be retained, giving
\[
B\le z^*\le z^{\mathrm{inc}}.
\]
However, global optimality requires \(B=z^{\mathrm{inc}}\), while infeasibility requires certified closure of every search region. Without one of these independent certificates, limit interruption permits only an incomplete or unknown search status, even when substantial portions of the tree have been closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reaching a search limit does not certify completion; only independently verified incumbents, bounds, and closed regions remain valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Limit-Interrupted Search

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: Incomplete Search Semantics
children.top_down_role: Covers claims that remain unavailable when the search space is not closed.

assumptions_latex: Search stops with residual frontier \(Q\).
Incumbents, objective bounds, and node closures are individually checked against the original model.
No unrecorded inference is used to strengthen the reported status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The report denotes only its retained partial evidence unless those certificates separately establish the conditions for infeasibility or optimality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical meaning of results returned before a complete-search certificate exists.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Partial Enumeration p. 14

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An incomplete-search result denotes the conjunction of its retained certificates, not a decision of the entire model. If \(Q\ne\varnothing\), certified incumbents \(I\), valid objective bounds, and closures \(K\) remain valid within their declared scopes, while residual regions remain unresolved. The result may assert existence of a feasible solution when \(I\ne\varnothing\). It may assert global infeasibility only if every residual region is certified infeasible, and it may assert global optimality only if a feasible incumbent is accompanied by certificates proving that no residual region contains a strictly better solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incomplete result means exactly what its checked incumbents, bounds, and closures establish; global infeasibility requires all residual regions to be infeasible, while optimality requires proof that none contains a better solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Search Semantics

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2 Partial Enumeration p. 14

children.title: Retained Partial Evidence
children.top_down_role: Covers incumbents, bounds, and diagnostics preserved after interruption.

assumptions_latex: Search produced logged artifacts before interruption.
Each retained artifact is independently verifiable against the original model and, where applicable, its declared search region.
The report distinguishes local evidence from a completion certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every verified retained artifact remains valid after interruption, but completion follows only from certificates resolving every residual region under the claimed status.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial certificates that survive interruption without supporting an unwarranted completion claim.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After interruption, retained partial evidence may comprise feasible assignments \(I\), valid objective bounds \(L\), and sound node-closure certificates \(K\). Each \(a\in I\) is checked against the original constraints, every member of \(L\) is checked for its declared region, and every member of \(K\) is checked from its recorded reasons. These artifacts remain valid independently of normal search termination. Their conjunction certifies global infeasibility only when every residual region is certified infeasible, and certifies global optimality only when a feasible incumbent exists and every residual region is closed or validly bounded against improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checked incumbents, bounds, and node closures survive interruption, but they certify infeasibility only by excluding all residual feasible assignments and certify optimality only by excluding every residual improvement over a feasible incumbent.

children.title: Completion Claim Boundary
children.top_down_role: Covers the boundary between partial progress and justified completion.

knowledge_statements.title: Completion Claim Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for optimality or infeasibility claims after an interrupted finite-domain minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the finite search domain of a fixed minimization model, let \(F\subseteq X\) be its feasible set, and suppose termination leaves a decomposition \(X=E\mathbin{\dot\cup}U\), where \(E\) has been soundly resolved and \(U\neq\varnothing\) remains unresolved. A time, node, memory, or user limit alone certifies neither global optimality of an incumbent nor infeasibility of the model. A completion claim is valid only if \(U=\varnothing\) after exhaustive resolution or independently checkable evidence establishes the claimed conclusion over every point or subregion of \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limit termination alone cannot certify optimality or infeasibility; every unresolved part of the search domain must be exhausted or covered by independently checkable evidence.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the finite search domain of a fixed minimization model with feasible set \(F\subseteq X\).
At termination, \(X=E\mathbin{\dot\cup}U\), with \(E\) soundly resolved and \(U\neq\varnothing\) unresolved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without certified resolution of \(U\), termination alone establishes neither global optimality nor infeasibility.

notation.meaning: resolved portion of the search domain
unresolved portion of the search domain
feasible set of the fixed model

children.title: Incumbent Solutions
children.top_down_role: Covers the best known feasible solution retained by the solver.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbents for a fixed finite-domain CP-SAT minimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem \(z^*=\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\), an incumbent at search time \(t\) is a stored assignment \(x^t\in F\) whose objective value \(U_t=f(x^t)\) is no greater than that of every feasible assignment accepted previously by the solver. Thus \(U_t\) is a primal upper bound on \(z^*\). If no feasible assignment has yet been accepted, the incumbent is undefined and the conventional primal bound is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incumbent is the best currently accepted feasible assignment; its objective value is an upper bound for a minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(f:F\to\mathbb R\) define a fixed minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every incumbent satisfies \(z^*\le U_t=f(x^t)\).

notation.meaning: incumbent objective value and primal upper bound

children.title: Primal Feasibility Evidence
children.top_down_role: Covers evidence supporting satisfaction of the model by an incumbent.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Feasibility Evidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directly checkable feasibility certificate for an incumbent assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the model have variable domains \(D_i\) and constraints \(C_j\). A primal-feasibility certificate is a complete assignment \(\hat x=(\hat x_i)_i\) together with the fixed model instance. Verification checks \(\hat x_i\in D_i\) for every variable and \(C_j(\hat x)=\mathrm{true}\) for every constraint, using the model's exact arithmetic and constraint semantics. Acceptance of all checks certifies \(\hat x\in F\), independently of how the solver found \(\hat x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete assignment certifies primal feasibility when every domain and model constraint evaluates successfully under the model's exact semantics.
assumptions_latex: The recorded model and assignment use the same variable indexing and data.
All constraint checks are performed without unsound numerical relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful verification certifies \(\hat x\in F\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of the recorded model

children.title: Incumbent Objective Evidence
children.top_down_role: Covers evidence associating an incumbent with its reported objective value.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Objective Evidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable objective-value evidence attached to a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a certified feasible assignment \(\hat x\in F\), incumbent objective evidence consists of the recorded objective expression \(f\), its coefficients and offsets, and a claimed value \(U\). A verifier reevaluates the expression on \(\hat x\) under the model's exact integer or rational arithmetic and accepts precisely when \(U=f(\hat x)\). The accepted pair \((\hat x,U)\) certifies the primal bound \(z^*\le U\) for minimization; feasibility without this equality does not certify the reported objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reevaluating the recorded objective at a feasible incumbent certifies its reported value and the resulting primal upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\hat x\in F\) has separately verified primal feasibility.
The objective data belong to the same model instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(U=f(\hat x)\), then \(z^*\le U\).

children.title: Incumbent Validity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Covers conditions that prevent a candidate from serving as reliable primal evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Validity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of the conclusions supported by an incumbent certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed minimization model, a verified pair \((\hat x,U)\) with \(\hat x\in F\) and \(U=f(\hat x)\) certifies only feasibility and the primal inequality \(z^*\le U\). It does not by itself certify that \(U=z^*\), that no better solution exists, or that a separately reported lower bound is valid. Moreover, the certificate does not transfer automatically to a model with changed domains, constraints, objective coefficients, presolve transformations lacking reconstruction, or incompatible arithmetic semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incumbent proves feasibility and a primal bound, but not optimality, dual-bound validity, or validity for a changed model.
assumptions_latex: \((\hat x,U)\) is verified against one fixed minimization model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent alone entails \(z^*\le U\), and no stronger global conclusion.

children.title: Relaxation Bound Evidence
children.top_down_role: Covers objective-bound evidence produced by valid relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Bound Evidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound certificate obtained from a valid minimization relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R\) and let the relaxed objective agree with \(f\) on \(F\). If a verifiable relaxation certificate establishes \(L\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in R\), then it also establishes \(L\le z^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). Evidence must identify the relaxation \(R\), justify the inclusion \(F\subseteq R\), and certify its bound \(L\), for example through an exact relaxation solution or a valid dual certificate. A relaxation value lacking these links is not bound evidence for the original model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified lower bound for a relaxation containing every feasible solution is also a lower bound for the original minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\).
The relaxed objective equals \(f\) on \(F\).
The inequality \(L\le f(x)\) is certified for every \(x\in R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le z^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).

children.title: Search-Tree Bound Evidence
children.top_down_role: Covers objective-bound evidence accumulated through search-region closure.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Tree Bound Evidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global lower-bound evidence assembled from a covering search frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let terminal or open search regions \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\) cover the original feasible set: \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k S_i\). Suppose each region has a certified lower bound \(L_i\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\cap S_i\), with infeasible regions represented by \(L_i=+\infty\). Then \(L=\min_i L_i\) is a certified global lower bound. The certificate comprises the branching decisions proving coverage, the bound certificate for every region, and the record of every validly pruned region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified bounds on search regions can be minimized into a global bound when those regions provably cover the entire feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k S_i\).
For each \(i\), \(L_i\le f(x)\) holds on \(F\cap S_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=\min_{1\le i\le k}L_i\le z^*\).

notation.meaning: i-th terminal or open search region
certified lower bound on region i
