children.title: Bound Evidence Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Covers combination of valid bound contributions from multiple sources.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Evidence Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation rules for global and region-specific minimization bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the same minimization model with optimal value \(z^*\), let \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) be certified global lower bounds, where \(m\ge 1\). They aggregate as \(G=\max_{1\le j\le m}G_j\). By contrast, let \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\) cover the feasible set \(F\), where \(k\ge 1\), and let each \(L_i\) be a certified lower bound on \(F\cap S_i\). These regional bounds aggregate as \(L=\min_{1\le i\le k}L_i\). Valid evidence may first minimize over a covering search frontier and then maximize the resulting global bound with other certified global bounds. Every operand must retain its model identity, scope, and certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take the maximum of certified global lower bounds, but the minimum of certified bounds over regions that collectively cover the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(m,k\in\mathbb{N}\) with \(m\ge 1\) and \(k\ge 1\).
All bounds concern the same objective and model instance.
\(F\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k S_i\).
For every \(i\), \(L_i\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in F\cap S_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{1\le j\le m}G_j\le z^*\) and \(\min_{1\le i\le k}L_i\le z^*\).

notation.meaning: i-th region in a certified cover of the feasible set
certified lower bound on the i-th covered region

children.title: Bound Provenance Gaps
children.top_down_role: Covers missing traceability that weakens interpretation of a reported bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Provenance Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Missing evidence that prevents a reported bound from serving as a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reported scalar \(L\) is not a checkable lower-bound certificate when its provenance omits any link needed to establish \(L\le z^*\). Such gaps include an unidentified model version, an unproved relaxation relation, an uncertified regional bound, incomplete search-region coverage, an unexplained pruning step, incompatible objective scaling, or aggregation of bounds with different scopes. The numerical inequality may happen to be true, but the report supports no certified global-bound claim until every missing link is reconstructed and verified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound without traceable model, scope, derivation, coverage, and aggregation evidence cannot certify a global objective bound.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is presented as a lower bound for a minimization model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If provenance cannot establish \(L\le z^*\), the reported value is not a global-bound certificate.

notation.meaning: optimal value of the claimed model

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Bound Provenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provenance representation for bounds exchanged among parallel solver components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed minimization model \(M\), represent each shared lower-bound contribution as \(b=(M,s,L,\pi)\), where \(s\) identifies its global or regional scope, \(L\) is the value, and \(\pi\) is checkable derivation evidence. A receiver may incorporate \(b\) only after matching \(M\), validating \(\pi\), and respecting \(s\). Certified global contributions combine by maximum; regional contributions combine only through a certified covering aggregation. Thus the shared scalar is sound exactly to the extent that its retained provenance reconstructs a valid inequality for the receiver's model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared bound must carry model identity, scope, value, and derivation evidence so receivers can validate and aggregate it soundly.
assumptions_latex: Every contributing solver component refers to the same immutable model \(M\).
Each accepted derivation object \(\pi\) is independently checkable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted shared evidence reconstructs a valid lower bound for \(M\) under its recorded scope.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is plausible, but no citation supports the proposed provenance tuple, receiver-validation semantics, or parallel CP-SAT bound-sharing interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Incumbent Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal component of an optimality certificate for finite-domain CP-SAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization problem \(z^*=\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\), a feasible-incumbent certificate is a complete assignment \(\hat x\), a verified feasibility record establishing \(\hat x\in F\), and an exact objective evaluation \(U=f(\hat x)\). Verification certifies \(z^*\le U\). This is a primal certificate: it establishes existence of a feasible solution at value \(U\), but it becomes an optimality certificate only when combined with independently verified evidence that \(z^*\ge U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible assignment plus exact objective evaluation certifies a primal bound, becoming optimality evidence only when matched by a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The assignment and objective refer to the same fixed minimization model.
Feasibility and objective evaluation are exactly verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat x\in F\) and \(U=f(\hat x)\) imply \(z^*\le U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Matching Objective-Bound Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-gap optimality certificate under exact minimization bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\hat x\in F\) be a certified feasible incumbent with exact value \(U=f(\hat x)\), and let independent bound evidence certify \(L\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). If \(L=U\), then \(L\le z^*\le U\) implies \(z^*=U\), so \(\hat x\) is globally optimal. If every attainable objective value is integral, the same conclusion follows when the exact rounded lower bound satisfies \(\lceil L\rceil=U\). Any tolerance-based comparison requires separately specified and justified numerical semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent is globally optimal when its exact value equals a certified global lower bound, or, for an integral-valued objective, equals that bound rounded upward exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(\hat x\in F\) and \(U=f(\hat x)\) are certified for a fixed minimization model.
\(L\le f(x)\) is certified for every \(x\in F\).
Either \(L=U\), or all attainable objective values are integral and \(\lceil L\rceil=U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under either matching condition, \(f(\hat x)=z^*=U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Search-Space Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite CP-SAT search under a minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible assignments of a finite-domain model and let \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\) be minimized. A closed search-space certificate consists of a finite collection of disjoint search regions \(R_1,\ldots,R_k\) covering every assignment, together with, for each \(R_i\), either a verified infeasibility deduction or a valid lower bound \(L_i\). Given a feasible incumbent \(x^\star\in F\), if \(L_i\ge f(x^\star)\) for every region not proved infeasible, then no feasible assignment has a smaller objective. Thus \(x^\star\) is globally optimal; if every region is infeasible, then \(F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive certified pruning proves the incumbent optimal when every remaining region has no better objective bound, or proves infeasibility when every region is closed as infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is defined by a finite-domain model.
Every pruning deduction and regional lower bound is valid.
The regions cover the original assignment space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F} f(x)\), or \(F=\varnothing\) when all regions are infeasible.

notation.meaning: A valid lower bound over feasible assignments in region R_i.

children.title: Absolute Gap Semantics
children.top_down_role: Covers interpretation of objective separation in native objective units.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Gap Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization with an incumbent upper bound and global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(U=f(x^{\mathrm{inc}})\) be the objective of a feasible incumbent and let \(L\le f^\star\) be a valid global lower bound on the optimal value. The absolute primal-dual gap is \[g_{\mathrm{abs}}=U-L.\] It is nonnegative whenever both certificates are valid. The inequality \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\) certifies that the incumbent objective exceeds the unknown optimum by at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The absolute gap is incumbent value minus valid lower bound; it directly bounds the incumbent’s additive suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\) is feasible and \(L\) is a valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le U-f^\star\le g_{\mathrm{abs}}=U-L\).

children.title: Relative Gap Semantics
children.top_down_role: Covers scale-normalized interpretation of objective separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Gap Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-normalized minimization gap using the incumbent magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible incumbent value \(U\) and a valid global lower bound \(L\le f^\star\), define the relative gap under the explicit unit-floor convention by \[g_{\mathrm{rel}}=\frac{U-L}{\max\{1,|U|\}}.\] Hence \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\) certifies \(U-f^\star\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|U|\}\). This definition is meaningful only after fixing the denominator convention; solver interfaces may employ a different zero-safe scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relative gap normalizes additive suboptimality by a declared objective scale; its meaning depends on the exact zero-safe denominator convention.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(U\) is feasible and \(L\) is a valid global lower bound.
The unit-floor denominator convention is adopted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le U-f^\star\le g_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|U|\}\).

notation.meaning: Relative gap under the unit-floor convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unit-floor formula is internally correct as a declared convention, but no source establishes that convention or its relevance to CP-SAT semantics. An authoritative solver or optimization reference with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Gap Scaling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers objective scales and sign regimes affecting gap interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap Scaling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive and scale-normalized descriptions of the same bound gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d=U-L\ge0\) and choose a positive scale \(s(U,L)>0\). The absolute and scaled regimes represent the same certified gap as \[g_{\mathrm{abs}}=d,\qquad g_s=\frac{d}{s(U,L)}.\] Common regimes include fixed-unit scaling \(s=1\), incumbent scaling \(s=\max\{1,|U|\}\), and symmetric scaling \(s=\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\). A tolerance is interpretable only together with its scale: \(g_s\le\varepsilon\) is equivalent to \(U-L\le\varepsilon s(U,L)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute and relative gaps differ only through a declared positive scale, so every numerical tolerance must be interpreted with its scaling regime.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is a feasible incumbent value and \(L\) is a valid lower bound.
The scaling function is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_s\le\varepsilon\iff U-L\le\varepsilon s(U,L)\).

notation.meaning: Gap normalized by the selected scale.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic representation is correct and the content kind fits, but the asserted list of common scaling regimes lacks any citation. A source must support the named conventions and their solver-context relevance.

children.title: Gap-Based Termination Boundary
children.top_down_role: Covers the distinction between tolerance-based completion and exact optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Based Termination Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes tolerance termination from exact optimality certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be a feasible incumbent value, \(L\) a valid lower bound, and let \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\). A gap-based stopping rule may terminate when \[U-L\le\max\{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}s(U,L)\}.\] This certifies only the displayed additive error bound. Exact optimality follows from this test alone only when the right-hand side is zero, or when objective discreteness and the bound imply that no strictly better attainable objective lies between \(L\) and \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive gap tolerances certify approximate, not necessarily exact, optimality unless objective discreteness excludes every better attainable value.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is feasible and \(L\) is a valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-f^\star\le\max\{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}s(U,L)\}\), without automatic exact optimality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The approximate-versus-exact optimality boundary is mathematically plausible, but the max-combination stopping rule and its interaction with CP-SAT termination status are implementation-sensitive and unsupported.

children.title: Optimal Status
children.top_down_role: Covers the solver status associated with established optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic meaning of a certifying success status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid minimization model with feasible set \(F\), an Optimal status certifies that the returned assignment \(x^\star\in F\) is feasible and that no \(x\in F\) satisfies \(f(x)<f(x^\star)\). Equivalently, the solver has both a feasible-incumbent certificate and a global lower-bound or closed-search certificate establishing \(f(x^\star)=f^\star\). If positive gap tolerances were permitted to trigger termination, their satisfaction alone does not justify this exact status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal certifies both feasibility of the returned assignment and global absence of any strictly better feasible assignment.
assumptions_latex: The submitted model is valid.
The status uses exact, rather than merely tolerance-based, optimality semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in F\) and \(f(x^\star)=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical meaning stated for exact global optimality is coherent, but the CP-SAT Optimal status contract requires an authoritative solver citation. A status-semantics leaf may also be better represented as a definition rather than a certificate, depending on the taxonomy's role convention.

children.title: Feasible Status
children.top_down_role: Covers the solver status associated with a valid incumbent lacking established optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic meaning of a nonoptimal certifying success status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid model with feasible set \(F\), a Feasible status certifies only that the returned assignment \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\) belongs to \(F\). For optimization, it does not certify \(f(x^{\mathrm{inc}})=f^\star\): search may be incomplete, or the incumbent-bound gap may remain nonzero. Any reported bound \(L\) yields the separate conditional guarantee \(0\le f(x^{\mathrm{inc}})-f^\star\le f(x^{\mathrm{inc}})-L\) when \(L\) is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible certifies the returned assignment satisfies the model, but it does not by itself certify global optimality.
assumptions_latex: The submitted model is valid.
The returned assignment is checked against every enforced constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\in F\), with no implication that \(f(x^{\mathrm{inc}})=f^\star\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between feasibility and optimality is correct, but no authoritative source establishes the precise CP-SAT Feasible status semantics or the availability and meaning of a reported bound. The certificate content kind is also questionable for a status-definition leaf.

children.title: Feasible-to-Optimal Transition
children.top_down_role: Covers the evidence progression required to strengthen a feasible result into an optimal result.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-to-Optimal Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone strengthening of a feasible incumbent into an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a solver has a feasible incumbent \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\in F\) with value \(U\). The semantic transition from Feasible to Optimal is justified when subsequent deductions establish a valid lower bound \(L\ge U\), or close every search region capable of containing a feasible assignment with objective below \(U\). Since feasibility gives \(f^\star\le U\) and the new certificate gives \(f^\star\ge U\), the combined record establishes \(f^\star=U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible becomes Optimal only after a valid global bound or exhaustive search closure excludes every strictly better feasible assignment.
assumptions_latex: The incumbent is feasible.
All bounds and pruning deductions used in the transition are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x^{\mathrm{inc}})=f^\star\), so the status may be strengthened from Feasible to Optimal.

source_refs.locator: 6.1 Continuous-Relaxation-Based Branch-and-Bound Methods p. 150

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1 Continuous-Relaxation-Based Branch-and-Bound Methods p. 150

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic meaning of certified global infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid finite-domain model with feasible set \(F\), an Infeasible status certifies \(F=\varnothing\). Such a status requires a globally valid contradiction or an exhaustive closed-search certificate covering the entire assignment space; failure to find an assignment within a time, conflict, or deterministic-work limit is insufficient. In an optimization model, Infeasible concerns the constraints themselves, not merely the absence of a solution better than the current objective cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infeasible certifies that no assignment satisfies all constraints; resource exhaustion or failure to improve an incumbent does not establish it.
assumptions_latex: The submitted model is valid.
The infeasibility deductions cover the original model, not only an objective-restricted subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the submitted model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global infeasibility semantics are mathematically appropriate, but the precise CP-SAT status contract and required certification scope lack authoritative support. Treating the status itself as a certificate rather than a definition is also questionable.

children.title: Unknown Status
children.top_down_role: Covers unresolved outcomes where available evidence does not justify a stronger status.

knowledge_statements.title: Unknown Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncertifying termination before feasibility or infeasibility is established.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid model with feasible set \(F\), Unknown means that the completed run establishes neither \(F=\varnothing\) nor the existence of a returned verified assignment \(x\in F\) under the status contract. It commonly arises when a resource limit, interruption, or incomplete search occurs before a certifying conclusion. Unknown is epistemic: it implies neither feasibility nor infeasibility of the mathematical model and must not be converted into either conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unknown reports that the run reached no certifying conclusion; it says nothing definitive about whether the model is feasible.
assumptions_latex: The model passed validity checks.
No stronger certifying status was established before termination.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The epistemic warning is reasonable, but CP-SAT's exact Unknown status contract, including whether any incumbent or response values may accompany it, is implementation-specific and unsupported.

children.title: Model-Invalid Status
children.top_down_role: Covers outcomes where model validity prevents normal solve semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Invalid Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation failure prevents solver-result semantics from applying.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Model-Invalid means that the submitted representation violates at least one required well-formedness or supported-domain condition, so the solver does not assign ordinary feasibility, infeasibility, or optimality semantics to the run. Examples may include malformed domains, unsupported numerical ranges, inconsistent structural data, or invalid objective encoding, depending on the implementation contract. The status concerns admissibility of the representation and does not imply that an intended repaired mathematical model is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model-Invalid reports rejection of the submitted representation, not infeasibility or any optimization conclusion about an intended repaired model.
assumptions_latex: Model validity is determined by the solver interface's documented representation rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{ModelInvalid}\not\Rightarrow F=\varnothing\) and no optimality conclusion is certified.

notation.meaning: Feasible set of an intended well-formed interpretation, if one exists.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary between invalid representation and mathematical infeasibility is appropriate, but the stated validity conditions and examples depend on the CP-SAT interface contract and require an authoritative cited locator.

children.title: Unknown-Result Evidence
children.top_down_role: Covers partial solutions, bounds, and interruption context associated with unresolved outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Unknown-Result Evidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: What diagnostic artifacts accompanying Unknown can and cannot establish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An Unknown result may be accompanied by run evidence \(E\), such as termination reason, resource counters, explored-node or conflict counts, incumbent history, and a last valid objective bound. Each verified element of \(E\) certifies only its stated run fact. In particular, a feasible incumbent recorded in \(E\) independently certifies feasibility, and a valid bound yields its stated objective guarantee; however, resource exhaustion or incomplete-search statistics alone certify neither \(F=\varnothing\) nor global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagnostics can verify run facts, incumbents, or bounds, but incomplete-search evidence alone cannot certify infeasibility or optimality.
assumptions_latex: Each diagnostic artifact is interpreted according to its documented interface semantics.
Any reported incumbent or bound has been independently validated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{\mathrm{incomplete}}\not\Rightarrow F=\varnothing\) and \(E_{\mathrm{incomplete}}\not\Rightarrow f(x^{\mathrm{inc}})=f^\star\).

notation.meaning: Evidence and diagnostics retained from the terminated run.
A separately verified incumbent, if recorded.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical limitations of incomplete-search diagnostics are sound, but the listed artifacts and the availability and validity semantics of incumbents or bounds under an Unknown response are CP-SAT-specific claims without a source.

children.title: Model-Validity Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Covers model conditions that preclude meaningful feasibility or optimality claims.

assumptions_latex: The submitted CP-SAT model is represented by finite data \(M\) interpreted under a declared model schema \(\Sigma\).
A deterministic validator \(V_{\Sigma}\) returns either \(\mathrm{valid}\) or a nonempty finite set of validation errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_{\Sigma}(M)\neq\mathrm{valid}\Rightarrow\) no feasibility, infeasibility, or optimality conclusion about the intended optimization problem is certified.

notation.meaning: declared model schema and its semantic rules

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates malformed or unsupported model data from search outcomes for a well-defined CP-SAT instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given submitted data \(M\), schema \(\Sigma\), and validator \(V_{\Sigma}\), define the model-validity boundary by \[\mathcal V_{\Sigma}=\{M:V_{\Sigma}(M)=\mathrm{valid}\}.\] If \(M\notin\mathcal V_{\Sigma}\), the solver may return a model-invalid status together with validation diagnostics, but that status is not a statement that the intended constraint system is infeasible. Feasibility, infeasibility, objective bounds, and optimality are semantically certifying only for \(M\in\mathcal V_{\Sigma}\). Thus rejection before or during validation lies outside the solver's search-correctness claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model-invalid result reports failure to form a valid solver instance; it certifies neither infeasibility nor any objective claim about the intended model.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Validity Failure Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and mathematical statement are coherent, but no authoritative CP-SAT model-validation or status specification is cited. The claimed behavior of model-invalid status and the scope of solver correctness therefore remain unsupported.

children.title: External Proof Verifiability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Distinguishes solver-reported semantic status from independently checkable end-to-end proof artifacts.

assumptions_latex: A finite SAT encoding \(F\) is searched by clause addition, deletion, and conflict analysis.
The checker is given the original clauses and every logged proof step required by the selected proof calculus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Checker acceptance of a terminal contradiction certifies unsatisfiability of \(F\), but not automatically of an unlinked source CP-SAT model.

notation.meaning: finite propositional formula or clause database

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines what an independently checkable SAT-layer contradiction can certify within a hybrid CP-SAT solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A SAT-level proof-logging interface emits an ordered log \(L=(s_1,\ldots,s_k)\) for a clause formula \(F\). Each addition step must be checkable as admissible in the chosen proof calculus from the current clause database; deletion steps affect storage but not logical consequence. The interface is certifying for SAT-level unsatisfiability when an independent checker \(C\), initialized with \(F\), validates every step and accepts a final empty clause: \[C(F,L)=\mathrm{accept}.\] This acceptance certifies \(F\) unsatisfiable. It certifies the source CP-SAT model only if the encoding and all non-SAT transformations are separately linked by checkable semantics-preserving records.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checked SAT proof log can certify contradiction in the emitted clause encoding, but source-model correctness additionally requires verified encoding and transformation links.
knowledge_statements.title: SAT-Level Proof-Logging Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the proof-logging leaf, and the SAT-level versus source-model boundary is appropriately stated. Acceptance conditions depend on a specified proof format, calculus, checker, and CP-SAT interface, none of which is cited.

assumptions_latex: The solver derives Boolean clauses, integer-domain reductions, or linear inequalities from a current mixed Boolean-integer state.
An external checker receives the premises and numerical data used by each recorded inference.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only derivations with independently checkable mixed-integer reasons are externally traceable; opaque propagation or cutting steps cross the traceability boundary.

notation.meaning: recorded reason object for the derivation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes external traceability of clauses, integer bounds, and linear deductions produced by hybrid reasoning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mixed-integer inference producing conclusion \(r\) from current premises \(P\) is traceable when the solver emits a finite reason object \(\rho\) for which an independent checker can verify \[P\models r\] using only declared exact arithmetic and inference rules encoded by \(\rho\). For a bound deduction, \(r\) may be \(x\leq u\) or \(x\geq \ell\); for conflict analysis, it may be a clause; for cutting, it may be a valid inequality. The traceability boundary is crossed whenever correctness depends on an unlogged relaxation, rounding decision, numerical tolerance, propagator state, or cut-validity argument unavailable to the checker.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-integer deduction is traceable only when an independent checker can reconstruct its logical validity from logged premises, exact data, and declared rules.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Reason Traceability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits traceability, but the record ranges over clauses, bounds, and cuts without identifying an authoritative mixed-integer proof calculus or actual solver reason format. Sources are required to determine which deductions are externally reconstructible.

assumptions_latex: Presolve maps a valid source model \(M\) to a reduced model \(M'\) through transformations \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\).
A reduced-model certificate or solution is available for translation back to the source model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A certificate for \(M'\) certifies the corresponding claim for \(M\) only when every relevant presolve transformation has a checkable reconstruction record.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marks the gap between checking a reduced instance and certifying the original submitted model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M'=T_k\circ\cdots\circ T_1(M)\). End-to-source reconstruction is externally checkable only if each \(T_i\) has a record establishing the required relation between its input and output: feasibility correspondence, objective preservation, or a valid implication sufficient for infeasibility. For a feasible reduced solution \(x'\), reconstruction must produce \(x\) feasible for \(M\) with the claimed objective relation. For an infeasibility certificate on \(M'\), the records must imply infeasibility of \(M\). Without this transformation chain, checking a certificate solely against \(M'\) does not certify the corresponding source-model claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced-model certificate reaches the original model only through checkable presolve records that preserve the relevant feasibility and objective claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Proof-Reconstruction Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf and the abstract reconstruction requirement is sound. No presolve specification identifies the transformations, their preservation relations, or the reconstruction records actually available in CP-SAT.

assumptions_latex: The valid minimization model \(M\) has feasible set \(X\) and objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\).
A log records an incumbent \(\hat x\), a lower-bound argument, and every encoding, presolve, and search transformation used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: End-to-end optimality is certified exactly when the log checks \(\hat x\in X\), \(f(\hat x)=U\), and \(f(x)\geq U\) for all \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of the source minimization model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the external-verification boundary for a complete optimality claim on the submitted minimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a source minimization model with feasible set \(X\), an end-to-end optimality log must permit an independent checker to establish both sides of \[\hat x\in X,\qquad f(\hat x)=U,\qquad \forall x\in X:\ f(x)\geq U.\] The log must connect the source model to every reduced or encoded model, validate the incumbent reconstruction, and justify the global lower bound through checkable search or infeasibility certificates. A log that checks only feasibility, only a SAT-layer contradiction, only a reduced model, or only a numerical bound remains below the end-to-end boundary and cannot by itself certify source-model optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality logging is end-to-end only when a checker verifies source feasibility, the incumbent value, the matching global bound, and every transformation link.
knowledge_statements.title: End-to-End Optimality-Logging Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the container, and the minimization optimality conditions are mathematically appropriate. The claim that a log covers every encoding, presolve, and search transformation requires an authoritative end-to-end logging specification that is not supplied.

children.title: Solver Control-Diagnostic Tuning Interface
children.top_down_role: Covers supported solve-control and observational interfaces, including the boundary between callbacks and solver-modifying extension mechanisms.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: OR-Tools CP-SAT documentation and source tree
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Using the CP-SAT solver; troubleshooting.md; sat_parameters.proto; callbacks and response statistics
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: OR-Tools CP-SAT documentation and source tree

children.title: Time Limits
children.top_down_role: Covers wall-clock or runtime-based solve termination controls.

assumptions_latex: A solve starts at wall-clock time \(t_0\) with a finite nonnegative limit \(T\).
The implementation periodically samples a monotone wall-clock source while performing search and solver overhead.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When sampled elapsed time reaches \(T\), termination is requested; the returned status depends on certificates established before termination.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a generic wall-clock stopping condition without asserting implementation-specific precision or status names.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For configured wall-time limit \(T\in[0,\infty)\), the time-limit stopping predicate at a clock sample \(t\) is \[t-t_0\geq T.\] When the predicate first holds, the solver requests termination. Because the clock is sampled at implementation-defined safe points, actual return time may exceed \(t_0+T\) by interruption and cleanup latency. Reaching the limit alone certifies neither infeasibility nor optimality: a feasible incumbent may be returned if one was found, and a conclusive status is valid only when its required certificate was completed before termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A wall-time limit requests termination once sampled elapsed time reaches its threshold; overshoot is possible, and the limit alone proves no optimization claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Time Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the time-limit leaf. Sampling behavior, the meaning of a zero limit, interruption latency, and returned-status semantics are solver-specific and need parameter/API documentation with a precise locator.

children.title: Conflict Limits
children.top_down_role: Covers solve termination controls based on conflict-processing counts.

assumptions_latex: The solver maintains a monotone count \(c\) of conflicts according to a declared counting rule.
A finite nonnegative integer threshold \(C\) is configured for the solve or search component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conflict limit requests termination when \(c\geq C\); this event alone certifies neither infeasibility nor optimality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines conflict-budget exhaustion relative to an implementation-declared conflict counter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a conflict counter \(c\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\) and configured threshold \(C\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\), the conflict-limit stopping predicate is \[c\geq C.\] A conflict is counted only according to the solver's declared rule, which must specify whether the counter is global, per worker, per restart, or per search component. When the predicate holds, the affected search requests termination at an allowed interruption point. Exhausting this budget is a resource event, not a logical certificate; any conclusive returned status must be supported independently by a completed feasibility, infeasibility, or optimality argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conflict limit stops the relevant search after its declared conflict counter reaches a threshold; counter scope must be specified, and exhaustion proves nothing itself.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is locally appropriate, but the record presupposes a configurable CP-SAT conflict limit and an associated counting rule. No solver documentation establishes that interface, its scope, or its stopping semantics.

children.title: Deterministic Limits
children.top_down_role: Covers machine-independent effort budgets used for controlled solve termination.

assumptions_latex: The solver accumulates a monotone deterministic-work measure \(d\) under a fixed implementation and accounting rule.
A finite nonnegative deterministic limit \(D\) is configured.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The deterministic limit requests termination when \(d\geq D\), providing reproducible work budgeting only under the declared execution assumptions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Treats deterministic time as an abstract work counter rather than physical elapsed time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\in[0,\infty)\) be the accumulated deterministic-work measure defined by the solver's accounting rule, and let \(D\in[0,\infty)\) be its limit. The stopping predicate is \[d\geq D.\] Deterministic work is not wall-clock duration. Equal stopping behavior is expected only when the model, solver version, parameters, worker configuration, randomization, and event schedule satisfy the implementation's reproducibility conditions. Reaching \(D\) requests termination at a supported interruption point and supplies no feasibility, infeasibility, or optimality certificate by itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic limit stops at a solver-defined work threshold, not elapsed seconds; reproducibility requires fixed execution conditions, and exhaustion is noncertifying.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the deterministic-limit leaf and correctly distinguishes work from wall time. The accounting rule and reproducibility conditions are implementation-specific and require authoritative solver documentation.

children.title: Limit Interaction Semantics
children.top_down_role: Covers precedence and reporting when multiple solve limits are active.

assumptions_latex: A finite family of enabled limits has stopping predicates \(P_1(s),\ldots,P_m(s)\) on solver state \(s\).
Each predicate is sampled at implementation-defined interruption points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The combined stopping condition is \(\bigvee_{i=1}^{m}P_i(s)\); the earliest observed trigger requests termination without weakening any status-certificate requirement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives generic disjunctive semantics for simultaneously enabled solve limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For enabled stopping predicates \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\), define the aggregate predicate by \[P_{stop}(s)=\bigvee_{i=1}^{m}P_i(s).\] At the first sampling point where \(P_{stop}(s)\) is true, termination is requested. Multiple predicates may become observable at the same point, so a reported primary cause requires a declared precedence rule and need not identify the chronologically first physical event. In parallel search, worker-local and global limits must have explicit aggregation rules. Regardless of which limit triggers, a conclusive solve status remains permissible only if its required certificate was completed independently of limit exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enabled limits combine disjunctively: any observed trigger requests termination, while simultaneous triggers and parallel aggregation require declared precedence and scope rules.
knowledge_statements.title: Limit Interaction Semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits interaction semantics, but disjunctive composition, sampling, precedence, and worker aggregation are interface claims rather than universal mathematical facts. They require a CP-SAT limit-semantics source.

children.title: Solution Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Covers notifications and observations associated with newly reported feasible solutions.

assumptions_latex: The solver produces a finite sequence of accepted feasible incumbents \(x^{(1)},x^{(2)},\ldots\).
A registered callback can inspect a read-only snapshot of each reported incumbent and may request termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every solution-callback event reports an incumbent feasible under the solver's acceptance semantics; callback invocation itself certifies neither completeness nor optimality.

notation.meaning: objective value of the reported incumbent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the event contract for callbacks invoked on accepted feasible incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Register a callback before search. Whenever the solver accepts a reportable feasible incumbent \(x^{(k)}\), it forms an event snapshot containing \(x^{(k)}\), its objective value when present, and declared solve statistics, then invokes the callback. The callback returns or induces \(q_k\in\{\mathrm{continue},\mathrm{stop}\}\). If \(q_k=\mathrm{stop}\), termination is requested at a supported interruption point; otherwise search continues. The output is the ordinary solver result plus the observed event sequence. Invocation does not imply that all feasible solutions are enumerated, that incumbents are unique, or that the reported solution is optimal unless the interface separately guarantees those properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solution callback receives snapshots of reportable feasible incumbents and may request stopping; invocation alone guarantees neither enumeration completeness, uniqueness, nor optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Solution Callbacks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The described callback procedure matches the leaf broadly, although an interface property or representation may fit better than algorithm. Invocation conditions, feasibility semantics, snapshots, stopping behavior, enumeration, and deduplication all require authoritative callback API documentation.

children.title: Bound Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Covers notifications and observations associated with objective-bound changes.

assumptions_latex: For a minimization problem, the solver maintains a valid global lower bound \(L_k\) and incumbent upper bound \(U_k\) when available.
A registered callback is invoked on bound events selected by the implementation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A bound callback observes declared bound snapshots and may request termination, but an observed bound is certifying only under the solver's stated validity contract.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the minimization convention; maximization requires reversing bound roles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Register a bound callback before solving. At each reportable bound event \(k\), the solver supplies a snapshot containing the current valid lower bound \(L_k\), the incumbent upper bound \(U_k\) when defined, and declared statistics. The callback returns or induces \(q_k\in\{\mathrm{continue},\mathrm{stop}\}\); a stop response requests termination at a supported interruption point. For exact minimization semantics, valid snapshots satisfy \[L_k\leq f^star\leq U_k\] whenever both sides are defined. The interface must state whether events are filtered, coalesced, delayed, or aggregated across workers; callback observation alone is not an independently checkable proof of either bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound callback observes reportable global-bound snapshots and may stop search; event filtering, parallel aggregation, and the evidentiary strength of bounds require explicit contracts.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Callbacks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound-callback behavior requires API documentation, and algorithm is a questionable role for an interface contract. In addition, \(f^star\) neither denotes the standard optimum notation \(f^\star\) nor is introduced in the notation list, so the displayed bound relation must be corrected after the supported interface semantics are established.

children.title: Callback Event Ordering
children.top_down_role: Covers ordering and concurrency considerations across callback event streams.

assumptions_latex: A solve emits a finite observed callback sequence \(E=(e_1,\ldots,e_n)\).
Each event carries a dispatch index and an immutable snapshot of the state exposed at invocation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface guarantees only the declared order relation on dispatched events; it must not imply chronological or cross-worker order that is not explicitly specified.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes observable dispatch order from internal discovery order, especially under parallel search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=(e_1,\ldots,e_n)\) be the events observed by a callback consumer. Sequential dispatch guarantees \[i<j\Rightarrow \iota(e_i)<\iota(e_j),\] where \(\iota\) is the interface's dispatch index. This orders callback observations, not necessarily the internal times at which workers discovered the corresponding solutions or bounds. If callbacks can execute concurrently, the contract must instead declare a happens-before relation \(\prec\), synchronization rules, and snapshot consistency; events incomparable under \(\prec\) have no guaranteed order. No monotonicity of solution values, bound values, or event types follows unless separately specified by the solver interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Callback dispatch order need not equal internal discovery order; parallel callbacks require an explicit happens-before and snapshot-consistency contract.
knowledge_statements.title: Callback Event Ordering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the ordering leaf. Sequential dispatch, dispatch indices, concurrency, happens-before guarantees, and snapshot consistency are implementation-specific; no callback-ordering specification supports the proposed alternatives or identifies which one CP-SAT provides.

children.title: Callback Control Boundary
children.top_down_role: Covers the distinction between observing solve progress and modifying internal search.

knowledge_statements.title: Callback Control Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between callback observations, solve termination, and unsupported mutation of an active CP-SAT search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: During an active solve, let an invoked callback observe an event record \(e_k\), such as an incumbent, objective value, or bound. Its supported control action is restricted to setting a termination request \(q_k\in\{0,1\}\). Unless the solver API explicitly provides mutation operations, the callback cannot soundly add constraints, delete constraints, change variable domains, select branches, or replace the objective within that solve. Such modifications require ending the solve and constructing a subsequent model instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A callback may observe documented events and request termination, but it cannot mutate the active model or search unless explicit API operations support that action.
assumptions_latex: The solver exposes observational callbacks and a documented stop operation.
No documented in-search model-mutation operation is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Callback control is limited to observation and termination; model or search mutation lies outside the supported boundary.

notation.meaning: event record supplied at callback invocation k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, and the statement is internally coherent, but callback capabilities and prohibited in-search mutations are API- and version-specific. An official CP-SAT callback reference with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Early Stopping
children.top_down_role: Covers user- or callback-triggered termination before natural completion.

knowledge_statements.title: Early Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven termination with explicit distinction between interrupted and certified-optimal outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a model \(M\), stopping predicate \(P(e_k)\), and event sequence \((e_k)_{k\ge 0}\), initialize \(k=0\) and start the solve. At every supported polling or callback event, evaluate \(P(e_k)\). If it is false, continue and increment \(k\); if true, request termination. Return the solver status, the best incumbent \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\) when one exists, its value, and the valid bound reported at termination. Early termination alone does not certify optimality or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate a stopping predicate at supported events, request termination when it holds, and return the available incumbent, bound, and non-overstated status.
assumptions_latex: The predicate uses only information available through documented solve events.
The solver can process a termination request.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the solver state available at termination, without an optimality claim unless the returned status independently certifies one.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits early stopping, but official lifecycle documentation is needed to establish termination behavior, returned statuses, and when an incumbent or objective bound is available.

children.title: Model Export
children.top_down_role: Covers serialization of model state for inspection or transfer.

knowledge_statements.title: Model Export
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Serialization of a CP-SAT model independently of transient search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An export of a model \(M\) is a serialized representation \(S(M)\) containing every declared variable and domain, constraint, objective term and sense, assumption literal, and model-level annotation required by the chosen interchange format. A faithful import operation \(I\) satisfies \(\operatorname{Feas}(I(S(M)))=\operatorname{Feas}(M)\) and preserves the objective value of every feasible assignment. Solver parameters, incumbent solutions, learned clauses, search queues, callbacks, and random-generator state are separate unless the format explicitly includes them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A faithful model export preserves feasible assignments and objective values, but it does not ordinarily capture transient solver or callback state.
assumptions_latex: Export and import use compatible format versions.
All model constructs used by \(M\) are representable in the format.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The imported model is mathematically equivalent to \(M\), while unrepresented solve state is not preserved.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits, but the asserted serialized contents, import equivalence, and exclusions from transient state depend on the particular CP-SAT format and version. A format specification with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Solve Replay
children.top_down_role: Covers reconstruction of a prior solve context from retained artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Solve Replay
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Re-execution from recorded model, configuration, environment, and external control inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Record a replay package \(R=(S(M),\theta,s,v,h,u)\), where \(S(M)\) is the exported model, \(\theta\) the complete parameter vector, \(s\) the random seed, \(v\) the solver version, \(h\) the execution environment, and \(u\) the ordered external-control inputs. Reconstruct the model, restore the recorded configuration, reproduce \(u\), and execute the solver. Compare the resulting status, incumbent, bound, and event trace with the original run under a declared replay-equivalence criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replay reconstructs a solve from its model, full configuration, environment, and external inputs, then compares outcomes under a stated equivalence criterion.
assumptions_latex: Every component of the replay package can be restored or emulated.
The comparison criterion is fixed before replay.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure yields a comparable rerun, but identical traces require deterministic execution conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm appropriately describes a replay workflow, but CP-SAT does not have a source-cited replay contract here. Authoritative evidence is needed for restorable configuration, environment effects, external-control recording, and the attainable equivalence criteria.

children.title: Replay Fidelity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Covers environmental or nondeterministic factors that limit exact reproduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Replay Fidelity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which reruns need not reproduce an identical CP-SAT search trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equality of the exported model and random seed does not imply an identical replay trace. Trace fidelity can fail when parallel worker scheduling, asynchronous callbacks, wall-clock stopping, nondeterministic iteration order, solver-version changes, platform-dependent arithmetic, or unrecorded external inputs alter the transition sequence. Exact event-by-event replay is justified only when the effective transition function and every input are deterministic and restored. Otherwise replay claims must be limited to a weaker criterion, such as equal feasibility status or objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model and seed alone do not ensure identical replay; concurrency, timing, versions, platforms, callbacks, and omitted inputs can change the search trajectory.
assumptions_latex: Replay is compared with a prior solve of the same intended model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact trace equality is unsupported unless all transition-relevant state and inputs are deterministic and reproduced.

notation.meaning: effective state-transition function of the solve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and mathematical qualification are appropriate, but the listed causes of CP-SAT trace divergence are implementation- and version-dependent. Official determinism and reproducibility documentation is required.

children.title: Repeated-Solve Orchestration
children.top_down_role: Covers coordinated sequences of related solver invocations.

knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-Solve Orchestration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: External loop that constructs and solves a sequence of related CP-SAT models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial model \(M_0\), external state \(s_0\), update rule \(U\), and stopping predicate \(P\), repeat for \(k=0,1,\ldots\): construct \(M_k\) from the current state, solve \(M_k\), and collect the result record \(r_k\). If \(P(s_k,r_k)\) holds, return \((s_k,r_k)\). Otherwise set \(s_{k+1}=U(s_k,r_k)\), construct \(M_{k+1}\), and start a new solve. Only explicitly exported artifacts are transferred between iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An external controller repeatedly builds, solves, evaluates, and updates related models until its stopping predicate holds.
assumptions_latex: Each iteration produces a well-formed finite CP-SAT model.
The update rule defines the next external state from recorded results.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns the first state and solve result satisfying \(P\), if such an iteration occurs.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf and the external loop is coherent. A CP-SAT source is still required for the claim that only explicitly exported artifacts cross independently initialized solves and for the relevant reset semantics.

children.title: Decomposition Orchestration
children.top_down_role: Covers external coordination of submodels or decomposed solve responsibilities.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Orchestration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: External master-subproblem loop for decomposition implemented through repeated solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the decision variables into master variables \(y\) and subproblem variables. Initialize a master model \(M_0\) containing the master constraints and an initial relaxation. At iteration \(k\), solve \(M_k\) to obtain \(y_k\). Solve every induced subproblem at \(y_k\); from each result derive only globally valid feasibility or optimality information \(C_k\). If the declared decomposition termination test holds, return the assembled solution and bounds. Otherwise set \(M_{k+1}=M_k\cup C_k\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An external controller alternates master and subproblem solves, adding globally valid information until the chosen decomposition termination test holds.
assumptions_latex: Each generated member of \(C_k\) is valid for every feasible solution of the original model.
Master and subproblem results provide the bounds required by the termination test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned solution and bounds have the guarantees encoded by the validity conditions and termination test.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
source_refs.locator: 4.4 Benders decomposition p. 52

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
source_witnesses.locator: 4.4 Benders decomposition p. 52

children.title: Cross-Solve State Transfer
children.top_down_role: Covers transfer of solutions, bounds, assumptions, or generated subproblem data between solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Solve State Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity conditions for transferring artifacts between separately initialized CP-SAT solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An artifact \(a_k\) produced while solving \(M_k\) is admissible for transfer to \(M_{k+1}\) only if its receiving interpretation is defined and its validity can be checked independently of discarded internal state. A transferred incumbent must satisfy every constraint of \(M_{k+1}\); a transferred cut or clause must be entailed by \(M_{k+1}\) or the original target model; and a transferred bound must remain valid under the relation between the two feasible regions. Otherwise \(a_k\) may be used only as an untrusted heuristic hint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer an incumbent, constraint, clause, or bound only when its meaning and validity remain checkable for the receiving model.
assumptions_latex: The models \(M_k\) and \(M_{k+1}\) may differ.
Internal learned state is unavailable unless explicitly exported.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only artifacts satisfying the receiving model's validity predicate may support correctness claims in the next solve.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits and the validity principle is plausible, but incumbent, cut, clause, bound, and hint transfer have distinct CP-SAT semantics. Artifact-specific authoritative sources are required before retaining these claims together.

children.title: External Coordination Boundary
children.top_down_role: Covers responsibilities that remain outside the solver's internal architecture.

knowledge_statements.title: External Coordination Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between solver guarantees and correctness obligations of an external multi-solve controller.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sequence of solves \((M_k)_{k\ge0}\), the solver's guarantee for invocation \(k\) concerns only \(M_k\), its supplied parameters, and its returned status. The external coordinator is responsible for constructing \(M_{k+1}\), validating transferred artifacts, synchronizing concurrent solves, combining bounds, and defining global termination. Consequently, global feasibility, optimality, or convergence does not follow from the correctness of individual solves alone; it requires invariants linking all models, transferred information, and the coordinator's stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each solve certifies only its own model; global correctness and convergence depend on invariants maintained by the external coordinator.
assumptions_latex: Multiple solver invocations are coordinated outside the solver.
No documented API assigns global decomposition semantics to those invocations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cross-solve correctness claims require separately justified coordination invariants.

notation.meaning: model supplied to solve invocation k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, and the distinction between per-invocation and global guarantees is mathematically sound. Evidence is nevertheless required for the exact CP-SAT invocation boundary and the absence of built-in global decomposition semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: Assumption-Driven Incremental Workflows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated solves of a fixed base model under changing sets of assumption literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a fixed base constraint model with designated assumption literals \(A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\). For query \(k\), choose \(A_k\subseteq A\) and solve \(F\land\bigwedge_{a\in A_k}a\). If feasible, return a satisfying assignment. If infeasible and the interface supplies an assumption core, return \(C_k\subseteq A_k\) such that \(F\land\bigwedge_{a\in C_k}a\) is infeasible. Repeat with another subset. Reuse of undocumented learned state across separate solves is not part of this workflow's correctness contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve one base model under changing assumption subsets, optionally using returned infeasible cores to guide later queries.
assumptions_latex: Every designated assumption is a Boolean literal accepted by the solver interface.
The base model \(F\) is unchanged across the stated workflow.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each result applies to its selected assumption set; any returned core certifies infeasibility for the conjunction indexed by that core.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits this workflow, but official CP-SAT documentation is needed for accepted assumption literals, replacement or accumulation behavior across queries, core interpretation, and the lack of a minimality guarantee.

children.title: User-Cut Boundary
children.top_down_role: Covers the availability and limitations of injecting user-generated cutting information.

knowledge_statements.title: User-Cut Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unsupported injection of user-generated globally valid cuts during an active CP-SAT search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an external procedure derives an inequality \(c(x)\le0\) that is valid for every solution of the intended model. If the CP-SAT interface exposes no user-cut injection operation, the inequality cannot be inserted into the active search from an observational callback. A supported emulation is to terminate, add \(c(x)\le0\) to a new model, and solve again. This emulation is sound only when global validity is established and does not reproduce the timing or internal effects of native cut injection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a user-cut API, valid cuts require a new model and solve; callbacks cannot inject them into the active search.
assumptions_latex: The callback surface provides observation or termination but no cut-addition operation.
The external inequality is claimed to be globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: In-search user-cut injection is outside the supported boundary; repeated-solve emulation has distinct search semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is exact and the repeated-solve emulation is carefully qualified. The absence of active-search user-cut injection is a version-specific API claim requiring an official source and precise locator.

children.title: Lazy-Constraint Boundary
children.top_down_role: Covers the availability and limitations of deferred constraint generation during search.

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy-Constraint Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unsupported incumbent-triggered addition of omitted constraints during an active CP-SAT search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a constraint family omitted from the submitted model and let an incumbent \(x^k\) violate some \(g_k\in G\). If the solver exposes no lazy-constraint operation, an incumbent callback cannot add \(g_k\) to the active solve. Correct alternatives are to encode \(G\) before solving or to terminate, validate the incumbent externally, add violated constraints to a new model, and re-solve. An incumbent from the relaxed model is not feasible for the intended model until every required constraint is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without lazy-constraint support, omitted constraints must be modeled initially or added between solves after external incumbent validation.
assumptions_latex: The submitted model omits constraints required by the intended feasible set.
No documented lazy-constraint insertion operation is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Callback observation cannot convert a relaxed-model incumbent into a certified solution of the intended model.

notation.meaning: family of constraints required by the intended model
constraint violated by the observed incumbent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, and the distinction between relaxed-model and intended-model feasibility is correct. Official version-scoped evidence is required for the absence of lazy-constraint insertion and the documented callback capabilities.

children.title: Search-Callback Boundary
children.top_down_role: Covers the availability and limitations of user-directed intervention in branching or search.

assumptions_latex: A CP-SAT solve is invoked on a fixed finite-domain model \(M\).
The solver exposes observation callbacks but no documented callback that mutates the active search model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A search callback may observe reported search events but cannot soundly be treated as an in-search model-extension oracle.

notation.meaning: fixed CP-SAT model supplied before solving
information exposed at callback event t

review_flags: CP-SAT-specific callback contract requires authoritative API documentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between observing CP-SAT search and modifying the active model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be the immutable model accepted at solve start, \(S_t\) the solver's internal state at event \(t\), and \(E_t\) the callback-visible event data. An observation callback has the form \(g(E_t)\), possibly requesting termination, but it is not a transformation \(S_{t+1}=T(S_t,C_t)\) that inserts a new constraint \(C_t\) into the active search. Consequently, user cuts, lazy constraints, branching rules, or propagators requiring such a state transformation cannot be implemented merely by executing code when a solution or bound is reported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observation callbacks can inspect reported search information and may stop solving, but they do not constitute an interface for adding constraints, propagators, cuts, or branching rules during search.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-Callback Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the mathematical distinction between observation and active-search mutation is clear. However, the record makes CP-SAT-specific claims about callback capabilities without any cited API or implementation documentation. An authoritative, binding-specific callback reference with a method or section locator is required.

children.title: Supported Callback Surface
children.top_down_role: Covers observational and stopping capabilities exposed through supported callbacks.

assumptions_latex: A documented CP-SAT callback reports a sequence of solver events \((E_t)_{t\ge 0}\).
Each exposed callback method is used only according to its documented event context.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The supported surface consists exactly of documented observations and control requests; mutation of the active model is excluded unless explicitly documented.

notation.meaning: callback event reported at index t
user-side callback state after event t

review_flags: CP-SAT-specific operation set requires authoritative API documentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract contract for documented CP-SAT observation and termination callbacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For event data \(E_t\), define the supported callback surface \(\mathcal A\) as the documented operations that read exposed quantities, update user-owned state by \(u_{t+1}=h(u_t,E_t)\), emit diagnostics, or request that the solve stop. A callback is supported only when every solver interaction belongs to \(\mathcal A\) in the relevant language binding and event context. Operations that alter the accepted model, inject cuts or constraints, replace internal branching, or access unexposed solver state are outside this surface unless the API explicitly specifies otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A supported callback only reads documented event data, updates user state, reports diagnostics, or requests termination within the guarantees of the relevant API binding.
knowledge_statements.title: Supported Callback Surface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is an appropriate role for the supported callback surface, but the claim defines that surface by CP-SAT's documented operations while citing no documentation. The exact observation, diagnostic, and termination operations can vary by language binding and callback context, so authoritative API locators are required.

children.title: External Emulation Workflows
children.top_down_role: Covers repeated-solve patterns used when an internal extension mechanism is unavailable.

assumptions_latex: The desired extension can be expressed by a deterministic separation or validation oracle \(O\).
Each solve is performed on a finite-domain model and terminates with a status that can be inspected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the workflow terminates with no violated oracle constraint, its returned solution satisfies both the base model and every oracle condition checked at termination.

notation.meaning: candidate returned by solving the current model

review_flags: No supplied locator documents CP-SAT external emulation workflows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolve-and-augment emulation for extensions unavailable inside CP-SAT search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(M_0=M\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), solve \(M_k\). If the solve proves infeasibility, return infeasible for the current accumulated model. Otherwise obtain a candidate \(x_k\), evaluate the external oracle \(O(x_k)\), and let \(V_k\) be the finite set of violated valid constraints it returns. If \(V_k=\varnothing\), return \(x_k\). Otherwise set \(M_{k+1}=M_k\cup V_k\) and resolve. This workflow emulates delayed constraint generation between complete solver invocations, not within one active search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve, validate the returned candidate externally, add any violated valid constraints to a new model, and solve again until validation succeeds or infeasibility is established.
knowledge_statements.title: External Emulation Workflows

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the workflow leaf, but no source documents this CP-SAT emulation pattern. Moreover, determinism of the oracle does not imply that an empty returned set certifies satisfaction of all intended external constraints; the oracle must be assumed complete for the relevant candidate. Infeasibility is established for the intended extended model only if every accumulated constraint is valid and the oracle family is represented completely.

children.title: Presolve Parameters
children.top_down_role: Controls governing preprocessing intensity, transformations, elimination, detection, and simplification.

assumptions_latex: A finite-domain constraint model \(M\) and an implementation-defined presolve configuration \(p_{\mathrm{pre}}\) are given.
Every enabled rewrite is required to preserve feasibility and the recoverability of original-variable solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Presolve parameters may change the reduced representation and preprocessing effort but must not change the original model's feasible set after reconstruction.
review_flags: Exact CP-SAT parameter names and levels require authoritative parameter documentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic invariant of parameters controlling preprocessing before or around search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Presolve parameters select or limit transformations forming a reduced model \(P_{p_{\mathrm{pre}}}(M)\), including domain reduction, redundant-constraint removal, substitution, and bounded preprocessing effort. Their correctness invariant is \(x'\in\operatorname{Feas}(P_{p_{\mathrm{pre}}}(M))\Rightarrow R(x')\in\operatorname{Feas}(M)\), together with preservation of infeasibility and the relevant objective value. Changing \(p_{\mathrm{pre}}\) may alter preprocessing time, reduced-model size, and downstream search behavior; it must not license removal of feasible original solutions without a valid reconstruction correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve settings control valid model reductions and their effort. They may change representation and performance, but reconstructed solutions and infeasibility conclusions must remain correct for the original model.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Parameters

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A property is a reasonable role for the semantic invariant of presolve parameters, but no source supports the CP-SAT parameter family. The displayed implication only proves sound reconstruction from reduced solutions; it does not establish the converse correspondence needed for the stronger claim that feasible original solutions are not lost. Objective preservation also needs a precisely stated reconstruction or equivalence condition.

children.title: Probing Parameters
children.top_down_role: Controls governing probing effort, implied-value discovery, and probing limits.

assumptions_latex: Each variable has a finite current domain and probing trials use temporary assumptions.
All deductions retained after a trial are logical consequences of the current model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Probing parameters control the extent and cost of conditional inference without changing the set of feasible assignments.
review_flags: Exact CP-SAT probing controls require authoritative parameter documentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameters governing trial assignments and deductions derived from their propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A probing step temporarily assumes a literal \(\ell\) and computes \(\operatorname{Prop}(M\land\ell)\). If this closure is contradictory, the solver may infer \(\neg\ell\); comparing closures for complementary assumptions may also yield domain reductions or implied relations valid in both branches. Probing parameters govern whether such trials occur and bound their breadth, depth, deterministic effort, or repetition. They therefore trade preprocessing or search effort against additional deductions, while every retained deduction must be entailed by \(M\) and hence preserve \(\operatorname{Feas}(M)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probing settings control temporary assignments and conditional propagation used to derive valid domain reductions or implications, trading inference strength against computational effort.
knowledge_statements.title: Probing Parameters

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property statement gives a coherent generic account of sound probing, but the exact terminal container concerns CP-SAT probing parameters. No authoritative parameter or implementation source is supplied for the asserted breadth, depth, deterministic-effort, or repetition controls.

children.title: Propagation Parameters
children.top_down_role: Controls governing propagation effort, scheduling, and inference limits.

assumptions_latex: The solver maintains finite domains \(D_t(x)\) for all variables.
Each propagator is sound: every removed value is inconsistent with the constraints considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Propagation parameters affect when and how strongly sound domain filtering is performed, but not which feasible assignments are valid.

notation.meaning: domain of variable x at propagation stage t

review_flags: Exact CP-SAT propagation controls require authoritative parameter documentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameters controlling sound domain filtering and propagation effort.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_1,\ldots,F_m\) be contracting, sound domain operators, so \(F_i(D)\subseteq D\) and no assignment satisfying the modeled constraints is removed. Propagation parameters select eligible operators, scheduling rules, and effort or fixpoint limits for iterations \(D_{t+1}=F_{i_t}(D_t)\). Exhaustive fair iteration may reach a common fixpoint \(D^*\); limited propagation may stop earlier with weaker domains.
