In either case, parameter changes may affect runtime and search-tree size, but soundness requires preservation of every feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagation settings govern the scheduling, strength, and effort of sound domain filtering. Stronger propagation may shrink search, while limited propagation may stop before reaching a common fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Parameters

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic soundness property is mathematically plausible and fits the propagation-parameter leaf, but there is no source establishing that CP-SAT exposes parameters selecting propagators, scheduling rules, or fixpoint limits in the stated sense. An authoritative parameter reference with specific field locators is required.

children.title: Search Parameters
children.top_down_role: Controls selecting search modes, search limits, and exploration behavior.

assumptions_latex: A finite-domain optimization model and a parameter configuration \(p_{\mathrm{search}}\) are fixed.
Every complete configuration retains a sound and complete mechanism for proving the reported terminal status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Search parameters govern exploration policy and resource allocation, not the mathematical feasible set or objective function.
review_flags: Exact CP-SAT search policy values require authoritative parameter documentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General semantic role of CP-SAT parameters controlling search policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Search parameters are configuration values determining a policy \(a_t=\pi_{p_{\mathrm{search}}}(S_t)\) for choosing search actions, subsolvers, heuristics, phases, or resource shares from state \(S_t\). They may alter the order and mixture of exploration, the rate at which feasible solutions and bounds appear, and reproducibility under parallel execution. They do not alter the model's feasible set or objective. A terminal claim of optimality or infeasibility remains valid only when the configured search has produced the solver's required proof conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search settings choose how solver states, heuristics, and subsolvers are explored. They affect performance, solution order, bounds, and reproducibility, but not the modeled optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Search Parameters

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the search-parameter container, and the statement appropriately conditions proof claims on the solver's terminal proof requirements. Nevertheless, the enumerated CP-SAT policy effects, subsolver configuration, resource sharing, and parallel reproducibility behavior are unsupported by any cited parameter documentation.

children.title: Branching Parameters
children.top_down_role: Controls selecting branching policies, decision preferences, and variable ordering.

assumptions_latex: At a nonterminal state, at least one unfixed finite-domain variable or decision literal is available.
Each branch partitions or validly covers the current feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Branching parameters change the decision policy and exploration order while preserving completeness whenever the generated branches cover the parent state.
review_flags: Exact CP-SAT branching modes require authoritative parameter documentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy parameters for selecting and ordering CP-SAT branching decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Branching parameters determine a decision \(d=B_p(S)\), such as a variable, literal, value, or prescribed decision-strategy choice, and may determine the order of resulting child states \(S_1,\ldots,S_r\). Correct branching requires \(\operatorname{Feas}(S)=\bigcup_{j=1}^r\operatorname{Feas}(S_j)\), with disjointness when the branching scheme promises a partition. Thus the configuration can substantially change propagation opportunities, incumbent discovery, and tree size, but it preserves completeness provided every feasible parent assignment belongs to an explored child.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching settings select variables, literals, values, and child order. They alter search behavior but preserve completeness when the branches cover every feasible assignment of the parent state.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching Parameters

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role and branch-cover condition are mathematically appropriate, but the candidate provides no authoritative source connecting this abstraction to CP-SAT's actual branching parameters and decision-strategy modes. Specific parameter or API documentation is required.

children.title: Restart Parameters
children.top_down_role: Controls governing restart policies, restart frequency, and restart-trigger behavior.

assumptions_latex: Search accumulates deductions that remain valid independently of the abandoned decision path.
A restart returns to a designated root or earlier state without discarding globally valid information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restart parameters control when search paths are abandoned and resumed; valid retention preserves correctness while changing diversification and repeated-search cost.

notation.meaning: conflict or effort counter since a reference point

review_flags: Exact CP-SAT restart policies require authoritative parameter documentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameters governing restart triggers, schedules, and retained solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under a restart configuration \(p\), a restart is triggered when a policy predicate such as \(c_t\ge\tau_p\) holds. The solver abandons selected path-specific decisions, restores a designated earlier state, retains globally valid learned information \(L_t\), and resumes search under its branching policy. Parameters may select trigger statistics, threshold schedules, blocking rules, or restart frequency. They trade diversification and exploitation against repeated propagation cost; because retained elements of \(L_t\) are consequences of the model, restarting changes exploration order but not feasibility or proof validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart settings determine when the solver abandons a search path, what valid learned information it retains, and how thresholds evolve, affecting diversification and repeated work without changing correctness.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Parameters

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record states a sound generic restart property and its content kind fits the leaf. No source, however, supports the claimed CP-SAT trigger statistics, schedules, blocking rules, frequency controls, or retained state semantics.

children.title: Linearization Parameters
children.top_down_role: Controls governing relaxation construction, linearization levels, and linear encoding choices.

assumptions_latex: The original feasible set is \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) with objective \(c^\top x\).
Every generated linear inequality is valid for all points in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Linearization parameters control the strength and cost of a valid linear relaxation, whose optimization bound remains valid for the integer problem.

notation.meaning: linear relaxation selected at level p

review_flags: CP-SAT-specific linearization levels require authoritative parameter documentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity invariant for parameters selecting CP-SAT linear relaxations.

source_refs.locator: 7.1.1 Linearization cuts p. 84
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Linearization parameters select which valid linear inequalities and auxiliary constructions form a relaxation \(P_p\) satisfying \(X\subseteq P_p\). For minimization, \(z_p=\min\{c^\top x:x\in P_p\}\) is therefore a lower bound on \(z^*=\min\{c^\top x:x\in X\}\); the inequality reverses for maximization bounds. Increasing linearization effort may tighten \(P_p\), strengthen propagation or bounds, and increase relaxation size and solution cost. Disabling linearization may weaken bounds but must not remove feasible integer solutions from the underlying constraint model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearization settings choose valid linear relaxations. Stronger levels may improve bounds and inference at greater computational cost, while correctness requires every integer-feasible solution to remain represented.
knowledge_statements.title: Linearization Parameters

source_witnesses.locator: 7.1.1 Linearization cuts p. 84
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Cut Parameters
children.top_down_role: Controls governing cut families, cut-generation effort, and cut filtering.

assumptions_latex: A relaxation \(P\) contains the integer feasible set \(X\).
Every generated cut is valid for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cut parameters may tighten the relaxation from \(P\) to \(P'\) while maintaining \(X\subseteq P'\subseteq P\).
review_flags: CP-SAT-specific cut families and thresholds require authoritative parameter documentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and monotonic tightening induced by cut-generation parameters.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.3 The Branch-and-Cut Method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a cut configuration \(p\), let \(\mathcal C_p\) be the generated inequalities \(a^\top x\le b\) that are satisfied by every \(x\in X\). The tightened relaxation is \(P'=P\cap\bigcap_{C\in\mathcal C_p}C\), hence \(X\subseteq P'\subseteq P\). Cut parameters may enable cut families and control separation rounds, limits, efficacy thresholds, or filtering. More aggressive separation can improve relaxation bounds but consumes generation and relaxation-solving effort; validity of every accepted cut is required independently of these performance choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut settings select valid cut families and separation effort. Accepted cuts tighten the relaxation without excluding integer-feasible points, trading stronger bounds against generation and relaxation cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Parameters

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.3 The Branch-and-Cut Method p. 15

children.title: Scheduling Parameters
children.top_down_role: Controls governing scheduling-specific propagation, energetic reasoning, and scheduling relaxations.

assumptions_latex: The model contains finite-domain scheduling constraints over activities and resources.
Every enabled scheduling inference or relaxation is valid for the modeled scheduling semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scheduling parameters control specialized inference and relaxation effort without altering the feasible schedules defined by the model.

notation.meaning: set of schedules feasible for the original model

review_flags: Exact CP-SAT scheduling parameters require authoritative parameter documentation
supplied crew-scheduling locator does not document CP-SAT controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameters controlling specialized scheduling propagation, decomposition, or relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Scheduling parameters configure specialized processing of interval, precedence, disjunctive, cumulative, or resource constraints, including optional propagation, decomposition, and valid relaxation generation. If \(Q_{p_{\mathrm{sched}}}\) is a generated relaxation, correctness requires \(\mathcal S\subseteq Q_{p_{\mathrm{sched}}}\); if a propagator removes a domain value, no schedule in \(\mathcal S\) may use that value. Different configurations may trade stronger timetable, overload, energetic, or precedence reasoning against memory and computation. They affect the representation and inference schedule, not the set \(\mathcal S\) specified by the original model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scheduling settings govern specialized propagation, decomposition, and valid relaxations for activities and resources. They trade inference strength against cost while preserving the original set of feasible schedules.
knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Parameters

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits the scheduling-parameter leaf, and the generic validity conditions are coherent. No cited source supports CP-SAT's actual scheduling propagation, decomposition, or relaxation controls; the available crew-scheduling locator concerns an application rather than solver parameters. Authoritative CP-SAT parameter or implementation documentation is required.

children.title: Portfolio Parameters
children.top_down_role: Controls governing subsolver composition, portfolio selection, and search diversification.

knowledge_statements.title: Portfolio Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract configuration of a concurrent CP-SAT search portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{s_1,\ldots,s_m\}\) be a finite family of search strategies. Portfolio parameters are a tuple \(\Pi=(S,w,\tau,\sigma)\), where \(w_i\ge 0\) is the computational share assigned to \(s_i\), \(\sum_{i=1}^m w_i=1\), \(\tau\) specifies information exchanged among strategies, and \(\sigma\) specifies their activation or scheduling rule. Together, these parameters determine which complementary searches run and how their incumbent solutions, bounds, or learned information are shared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Portfolio parameters select search strategies, allocate computational shares, schedule them, and govern the exchange of incumbents, bounds, or learned information.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(m\ge 1\).
\(w\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{m}\) with \(\sum_i w_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi=(S,w,\tau,\sigma)\) defines a portfolio configuration.
review_flags: CP-SAT implementation-specific parameter semantics require an authoritative solver reference

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports this invented tuple or its allocation, scheduling, and information-sharing semantics as CP-SAT portfolio parameters. An authoritative CP-SAT parameter or architecture source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Parallelism Parameters
children.top_down_role: Controls governing worker counts, concurrent execution, and shared-search behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallelism Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource and synchronization controls for concurrent CP-SAT workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Parallelism parameters are a tuple \(P=(p,a,q,\eta)\), where \(p\in\mathbb{N}\) is the worker limit, \(a:\{1,\ldots,p\}\to\mathcal{S}\) assigns a search role to each worker, \(q\) specifies shared-resource limits, and \(\eta\) specifies synchronization events. A run governed by \(P\) may execute at most \(p\) workers concurrently; any sharing of incumbents, bounds, or learned constraints occurs only as prescribed by \(\eta\). Setting \(p=1\) gives sequential execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallelism parameters bound worker concurrency, assign worker roles, constrain shared resources, and determine when search information is synchronized.
assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(p\ge 1\).
\(\mathcal{S}\) is a finite set of admissible worker roles.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=(p,a,q,\eta)\) defines the parallel execution policy.
review_flags: CP-SAT implementation-specific worker and synchronization semantics require a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract worker-role tuple, synchronization policy, and sequential-execution interpretation are uncited and may not match CP-SAT's actual exposed parameters or worker architecture.

children.title: LNS Parameters
children.top_down_role: Controls governing large-neighborhood-search activation, neighborhood families, and effort allocation.

knowledge_statements.title: LNS Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controls for large-neighborhood search embedded in CP-SAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a feasible incumbent \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^n\), LNS parameters are a tuple \(L=(
u,ho,T,eta)\). The neighborhood generator \(

children.title: Model Statistics
children.top_down_role: Reported evidence about model size, variable domains, constraint composition, and structural features.

knowledge_statements.title: Model Statistics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite summary of the submitted CP-SAT model before search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite model \(M=(V,D,C,f)\), its model-statistics vector is \(s_M=(|V|,|C|,n_B,n_I,n_L,n_N,d_{vg},d_{max})\). Here \(n_B\) and \(n_I\) count Boolean and general integer variables, \(n_L\) and \(n_N\) count linear and non-linearized constraint classes, and \(d_{vg}\), \(d_{max}\) summarize constraint arity. The vector is descriptive: it records structural size and composition without asserting feasibility, boundedness, or expected solution time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model statistics summarize variable and constraint counts, types, and arities, but do not by themselves certify feasibility or difficulty.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(C\) are finite.
Each variable and constraint has a designated modeling class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_M\) is a structural diagnostic summary of \(M\).

notation.meaning: variables, domains, constraints, and optional objective

review_flags: Exact CP-SAT model-statistics fields and constraint classes require a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed statistics vector and categories, including average and maximum constraint arity, are generic and uncited; they are not established as CP-SAT model diagnostics.

children.title: Presolve Statistics
children.top_down_role: Reported evidence about presolve reductions, eliminations, transformations, and detected structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Statistics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting identities for transformations performed before or during search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_0\) be the submitted model and \(M_p\) the presolved model obtained by sound transformations. Presolve statistics may be represented by \(s_p=(r_V,r_C,t_D,n_F,n_S,n_R)\), where \(r_V=|V_0|-|V_p|\), \(r_C=|C_0|-|C_p|\), \(t_D=\sum_{v\in V_p}(|D_v^0|-|D_v^p|)\), and \(n_F,n_S,n_R\) count fixings, substitutions, and detected redundancies. Negative \(r_V\) or \(r_C\) is permitted when reformulation introduces auxiliary objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve statistics count changes in variables, constraints, domains, fixings, substitutions, and redundancies between the submitted and reduced models.
assumptions_latex: Presolve maps \(M_0\) to an equisatisfiable model \(M_p\).
All recorded domains are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_p\) quantifies the structural effect of presolve.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: transformation-accounting interpretation of presolve diagnostics
Exact CP-SAT presolve counters and their counting conventions require a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed counters and their formulas are not sourced to CP-SAT, and the assumption that presolve produces an equisatisfiable model may be too narrow for optimization-model transformations and reconstruction semantics.

children.title: Propagation Statistics
children.top_down_role: Reported evidence about propagation activity, deductions, domain reductions, and inference workload.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Statistics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event counts measuring domain inference during a CP-SAT run.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a run producing domains \(D^0,D^1,\ldots,D^T\), a propagation event at time \(t\) replaces some \(D_v^{t-1}\) by a strict subset \(D_v^t\). Propagation statistics are summarized by \(s_{prop}=(N_{calls},N_{red},N_{fix},N_{fail})\), counting propagator invocations, strict domain reductions, singleton fixings, and detected empty domains. If every event is counted once, then \(0\le N_{fix}\le N_{red}\); \(N_{fail}>0\) records detection of inconsistency in at least one explored state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagation statistics count inference calls, strict domain reductions, variable fixings, and detected inconsistencies during model processing and search.
assumptions_latex: Each variable domain \(D_v^t\) is finite.
A strict domain change is counted once under a fixed accounting convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_{prop}\) summarizes propagation activity and detected failures.

notation.meaning: domain of variable v after event t

review_flags: Exact CP-SAT propagation counters and aggregation conventions require a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The event model and four counters are plausible generic propagation accounting, but no source establishes that CP-SAT reports these fields or uses the asserted counting convention.

children.title: Conflict Statistics
children.top_down_role: Reported evidence about conflict volume, conflict processing, and search difficulty.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Statistics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts and summaries of contradictions encountered by SAT-style search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: During a SAT-style search, let \(K\) be the sequence of conflicts, where each conflict is a state in which propagation derives the empty clause. Conflict statistics may be represented by \(s_K=(|K|,L_{avg},L_{max},b_{avg})\), where \(L(k)\) is the decision level of conflict \(k\), \(L_{avg}=|K|^{-1}\sum_{k\in K}L(k)\), and \(b_{avg}\) is the average backjump distance. For \(|K|=0\), averages are reported as undefined or by an explicitly declared sentinel.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict statistics count propagation contradictions and summarize their decision levels and the resulting nonchronological backjumps.
assumptions_latex: The run uses decision levels and conflict-driven backtracking.
Every recorded conflict corresponds to a derived contradiction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_K\) summarizes the frequency and search-level geometry of conflicts.
review_flags: Exact CP-SAT conflict counters and reported aggregates require a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The average conflict level, maximum conflict level, and average backjump distance are uncited generic CDCL aggregates and are not shown to be CP-SAT diagnostic fields.

children.title: Clause Statistics
children.top_down_role: Reported evidence about learned clauses, clause retention, clause deletion, and clause-database growth.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause Statistics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inventory and lifecycle summary for SAT clauses used by CP-SAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At search time \(t\), partition the clause multiset as \(C_t=C_{orig}\uplus C_{learn}^t\), with learned clauses further partitioned into active and deleted clauses. Clause statistics may be represented by \(s_C(t)=(|C_{orig}|,|C_{learn}^t|,N_{add}(t),N_{del}(t),bar\ell_t,\ell_t^{max})\), where \(N_{add}\) and \(N_{del}\) are cumulative lifecycle counts and \(bar\ell_t\), \(\ell_t^{max}\) are the average and maximum lengths of currently retained clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clause statistics track original and learned clauses, additions and deletions, and the size distribution of retained clauses.
assumptions_latex: \(C_t\) is finite at every reporting time \(t\).
Clause additions and deletions follow one fixed counting convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_C(t)\) summarizes the current clause database and its cumulative lifecycle.

notation.meaning: learned clauses retained at time t

review_flags: Exact CP-SAT clause categories and deletion counters require a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intended average-length symbol is written as bar followed by ell rather than as a barred ell, and no authoritative source supports the proposed CP-SAT clause categories, lifecycle counters, or length aggregates.

children.title: Restart Statistics
children.top_down_role: Reported evidence about restart counts, restart timing, and restart-policy activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Statistics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summary of search restarts and work completed between them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_R\le T\) be the search indices at which the current decision trail is restarted to the root level. Restart statistics are \(s_R=(R,\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_R,c_1,\ldots,c_R)\), where \(\Delta_i=t_i-t_{i-1}\) is the work interval before restart \(i\), and \(c_i\) identifies its triggering policy. A restart retains globally valid learned information while discarding non-root decisions; thus \(R\) counts trail resets, not independent solver executions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart statistics count root-level trail resets, measure work between them, and classify their triggering policies.
assumptions_latex: Search progress is indexed by a nondecreasing work counter.
Restarts preserve globally valid learned constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_R\) records restart frequency, spacing, and causes.
review_flags: Exact CP-SAT restart categories and work-counter conventions require a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restart semantics are standard for CDCL, but the full vector of restart intervals and trigger classes is not established as a CP-SAT diagnostic representation.

children.title: Relaxation Statistics
children.top_down_role: Reported evidence about relaxation size, relaxation activity, and relaxation-solving effort.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Statistics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostics for linear or other tractable relaxations used during search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization model with feasible set \(X\) and relaxation \(R_t\supseteq X\) at reporting time \(t\), let \(z_R^t=\inf\{f(x):x\in R_t\}\). Relaxation statistics may be represented by \(s_R^t=(n_{row}^t,n_{col}^t,n_{nz}^t,N_{solve}^t,z_R^t)\), recording the relaxation dimensions, nonzero coefficient count, cumulative relaxation solves, and current lower bound. Whenever the relaxation is solved validly, \(z_R^t\le z^*\), where \(z^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation statistics report relaxation size, sparsity, solve count, and the valid bound obtained from the relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem.
\(X\subseteq R_t\) and both use the same objective \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_R^t\) summarizes relaxation effort and \(z_R^t\le z^*\).
review_flags: Exact CP-SAT relaxation diagnostics and reporting conventions require a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relaxation bound relation is mathematically standard under the stated assumptions, but the proposed dimensions, sparsity, solve count, and current-bound vector is not sourced as CP-SAT diagnostic output.

children.title: Cut Statistics
children.top_down_role: Reported evidence about generated cuts, accepted cuts, cut families, and filtering outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Statistics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting for valid inequalities generated and retained during search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with feasible set \(X\), a generated cut \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) is valid when it holds for every \(x\in X\). At time \(t\), cut statistics may be represented by \(s_{cut}^t=(N_{gen}^t,N_{valid}^t,N_{add}^t,N_{active}^t,N_{del}^t)\), counting generated, validated, added, active, and deleted cuts. Under single-count accounting, \(N_{active}^t\le N_{add}^t\le N_{valid}^t\le N_{gen}^t\). Cuts may additionally be grouped by generator family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut statistics count generated, valid, added, active, and deleted inequalities, optionally separated by cut family.
assumptions_latex: Every validated cut is satisfied by all \(x\in X\).
Each cut is counted once in each lifecycle category.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_{cut}^t\) summarizes the cut-generation lifecycle and satisfies the stated count inequalities.

notation.meaning: validated cuts added by time t

review_flags: Exact CP-SAT cut families, validation stages, and counters require a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity definition is standard, but the proposed generated, validated, added, active, and deleted lifecycle stages and inequalities are not sourced to CP-SAT's actual cut accounting.

children.title: Primal–Dual Statistics
children.top_down_role: Reported evidence about incumbent quality, bound quality, optimality gaps, and progress balance.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Statistics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent-bound diagnostics for a minimization CP-SAT run.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At reporting time \(t\) for a minimization problem, let \(p_t\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the best feasible objective value and \(d_t\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\) a valid lower bound. Primal–dual statistics are \(s_{pd}(t)=(p_t,d_t,g_t,r_t)\), where \(g_t=p_t-d_t\ge0\) and, when both bounds are finite, \(r_t=g_t/\max\{1,|p_t|,|d_t|\}\). If \(g_t=0\), the incumbent is optimal; otherwise the statistics quantify the remaining certified objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal–dual statistics report the best feasible value, valid bound, absolute gap, and normalized gap; zero gap certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(p_t\) is feasible and \(d_t\le z^*\le p_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_t\ge0\), and \(g_t=0\) certifies \(p_t=z^*=d_t\).

notation.meaning: best feasible objective value at time t
valid objective lower bound at time t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard primal-bound gap relation for minimization
Exact CP-SAT gap normalization and infinite-bound reporting require a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimization bound and zero-gap claims are standard, but the normalized-gap formula and treatment of infinite bounds are not cited as CP-SAT's reporting convention. The listed local sources were not attached to this record and do not establish CP-SAT-specific diagnostics.

children.title: Worker Statistics
children.top_down_role: Reported evidence attributed to individual parallel workers, including workload, progress, and resource use.

knowledge_statements.title: Worker Statistics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-worker diagnostic counters for one parallel CP-SAT run.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For workers indexed by \(w\in W\), represent the diagnostic record at termination time \(T\) by \[S_w(T)=(t_w,n_w^{\mathrm{branch}},n_w^{\mathrm{conflict}},n_w^{\mathrm{prop}},n_w^{\mathrm{sol}},n_w^{\mathrm{bound}}).\] Here \(t_w\) is active worker time, and the remaining coordinates count branches, conflicts, propagations, accepted incumbent improvements, and accepted bound improvements attributable to worker \(w\). Every counter is nonnegative and nondecreasing in time. The aggregate count for any additive event coordinate \(e\) is \(n^{e}(T)=\sum_{w\in W}n_w^{e}(T)\), provided each event has exactly one recorded origin worker.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worker record collects its time and event counts; uniquely attributed additive events may be summed across workers.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is a finite set of workers.
Each counted event has a unique origin worker when aggregation is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(n^{e}(T)=\sum_{w\in W}n_w^{e}(T)\) for every additive event coordinate \(e\).

notation.meaning: terminal diagnostic record of worker w
count of event type e attributed to worker w

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: formalization of additive per-worker event accounting
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the Worker Statistics container and is internally coherent, but no inspectable source supports the asserted CP-SAT worker fields, monotonicity, or unique-origin aggregation semantics. A CP-SAT-specific log or implementation reference with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Subsolver Statistics
children.top_down_role: Reported evidence attributed to named subsolvers, including contributions, effort, and solution discoveries.

knowledge_statements.title: Subsolver Statistics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Statistics grouped by subsolver strategy rather than physical worker.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be the finite set of subsolver types and let \(A_k\) contain all invocations of type \(k\). For additive event coordinate \(e\), define \[N_k^e=\sum_{a\in A_k}N_a^e,\qquad T_k=\sum_{a\in A_k}T_a.\] The subsolver record is \(S_k=(T_k,(N_k^e)_{e\in E})\). If invocations can overlap in wall-clock time, \(T_k\) is consumed invocation time and need not equal elapsed run time. Counts may be compared across subsolvers only after normalizing for opportunity, for example by \(N_k^e/T_k\) when \(T_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subsolver statistics aggregate invocation-level time and event counts by strategy; overlapping invocation time is not wall-clock time.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) and every \(A_k\) are finite.
Event coordinates in \(E\) are additive across invocations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_k=(\sum_{a\in A_k}T_a,(\sum_{a\in A_k}N_a^e)_{e\in E})\).

notation.meaning: total invocation time assigned to type k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: grouped additive accounting with exposure normalization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Subsolver Statistics, but the invocation grouping, additivity of time and counters, overlap interpretation, and asserted need for exposure normalization are not supported by an inspectable CP-SAT source. The available inventory does not address these diagnostics.

children.title: Cross-Worker Contribution Attribution
children.top_down_role: Comparative evidence linking worker activity to bound improvements, incumbent discoveries, and shared progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Worker Contribution Attribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique-origin accounting for shared incumbents and bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=(u_1,\ldots,u_m)\) be the chronologically accepted global improvements during a parallel run. Assign each \(u_j\) an origin \(o(u_j)\in W\) and contribution value \(v(u_j)\ge 0\). The attributed contribution of worker \(w\) is \[C_w=\sum_{j:o(u_j)=w}v(u_j),\qquad \sum_{w\in W}C_w=\sum_{j=1}^{m}v(u_j).\] For event-count attribution take \(v(u_j)=1\); for objective or bound movement, use a declared nonnegative increment. Improvements discovered independently but accepted once are credited according to the declared tie-breaking origin rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each accepted global improvement receives one origin worker, making worker contributions additive under a declared value and tie-breaking rule.
assumptions_latex: Every accepted improvement has exactly one recorded origin in \(W\).
The contribution valuation satisfies \(v(u_j)\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{w\in W}C_w=\sum_{j=1}^{m}v(u_j)\).

notation.meaning: origin worker of accepted improvement j
declared contribution value of improvement j
total contribution attributed to worker w

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conservation-based attribution under unique event origins
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unique-origin formula is mathematically valid under its assumptions and fits the attribution container, but it is unclear whether CP-SAT records accepted improvements, origins, tie breaking, and contribution values in this manner. A precise implementation or diagnostic-schema source is required.

children.title: Single-Worker Variability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sources and manifestations of run variability under single-worker execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Worker Variability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions distinguishing deterministic and seed-sensitive single-worker execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an instance \(I\), solver build \(b\), parameter vector \(\theta\), worker count one, resource rule \(L\), and execution environment \(E\). Let \(Y(I,b,\theta,L,E,s)\) be the observable run outcome under seed \(s\). The configuration is seed-invariant on \(S\) when \[Y(I,b,\theta,L,E,s)=Y(I,b,\theta,L,E,s')\quad\text{for all }s,s'\in S.\] It is seed-variable when this equality fails. Even with fixed \(s\), reproducibility requires deterministic resource accounting and an environment that does not alter the solver's operation sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-worker regime is seed-invariant exactly when all allowed seeds produce the same declared observable under fixed execution conditions.
assumptions_latex: The compared runs use one worker and identical \(I,b,\theta,L,E\).
The observable \(Y\) is fixed before comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Seed variability occurs exactly when \(\exists s,s'\in S\) such that \(Y(\cdot,s)\ne Y(\cdot,s')\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: controlled-experiment definition of seed variability
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The seed-invariance definition fits the container, but the stronger claim about deterministic resource accounting and preservation of the operation sequence depends on the chosen observable and actual CP-SAT execution semantics. No solver-reproducibility source is cited, so the reliable mathematical boundary cannot be confirmed.

children.title: Parallel Variability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sources and manifestations of run variability under concurrent worker execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Variability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondeterminism induced by asynchronous multiworker search and sharing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For worker count \(p>1\), let \(\sigma\) denote the realized schedule of worker steps and shared-information deliveries, and write the observable outcome as \(Y(I,b,\theta,L,E,s,p,\sigma)\). A parallel configuration is schedule-invariant only if \[Y(I,b,\theta,L,E,s,p,\sigma)=Y(I,b,\theta,L,E,s,p,\sigma')\quad\text{for all admissible }\sigma,\sigma'.\] If a received incumbent, bound, or clause changes a later branching, pruning, or propagation decision, two admissible delivery orders may yield unequal outcomes. Fixing the seed alone therefore does not establish parallel reproducibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel reproducibility fails when admissible scheduling or message order changes search decisions and hence the declared outcome.
assumptions_latex: Workers exchange search information asynchronously.
At least one later search decision can depend on received information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A fixed seed does not imply \(Y(\cdot,\sigma)=Y(\cdot,\sigma')\) for all admissible schedules.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: asynchronous schedule dependence in parallel search
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits Parallel Variability Regimes. However, decision dependence on shared information does not by itself ensure that two admissible schedules produce unequal declared outcomes, and the CP-SAT-specific asynchronous-sharing premise is uncited. An architecture or reproducibility source is needed to determine the warranted formulation.

children.title: Cross-Regime Comparability
children.top_down_role: Limits on comparing outcomes collected under different worker-count or execution regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Regime Comparability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity conditions for comparing single-worker and parallel measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let regimes \(r\) and \(r'\) produce samples of a performance functional \(M\). A direct comparison is valid only when both experiments use the same instance distribution, solver build, objective convention, termination criterion, resource unit, hardware normalization, and aggregation functional. Formally, with common instance distribution \(P\), define \[\mu_r=\mathbb{E}_{I\sim P,\,\omega\sim Q_r}[M(I,r,\omega)].\] The contrast \(\mu_r-\mu_{r'}\) isolates execution regime only when all controlled factors except the regime agree. Otherwise it is a composite contrast and cannot be attributed solely to worker count or parallelism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-regime contrasts isolate execution mode only when instances, limits, hardware normalization, termination, and aggregation are aligned.
assumptions_latex: Both regimes are evaluated on the same instance distribution \(P\).
The performance functional and resource convention are identical.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only controlled comparisons identify \(\mu_r-\mu_{r'}\) as an execution-regime effect.

notation.meaning: distribution of run-level variability in regime r

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the comparability container, but the claim that the listed controls are jointly necessary and sufficient to isolate an execution-regime effect requires a defined estimand and identification assumptions. No experimental-methodology source is supplied.

children.title: Parameter Overfitting
children.top_down_role: Tuning failures caused by excessive adaptation to selected instances, seeds, budgets, or hardware.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter Overfitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical tuning failure caused by reuse of the tuning sample.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_{\mathrm{train}}\) and \(D_{\mathrm{test}}\) be disjoint instance samples, let \(R(\theta;D)\) be empirical loss, and choose \(\widehat\theta\in\arg\min_{\theta\in\Theta}R(\theta;D_{\mathrm{train}})\). For a fixed reference \(\theta_0\), define \[G_{\mathrm{train}}=R(\theta_0;D_{\mathrm{train}})-R(\widehat\theta;D_{\mathrm{train}}),\qquad G_{\mathrm{test}}=R(\theta_0;D_{\mathrm{test}})-R(\widehat\theta;D_{\mathrm{test}}).\] Parameter overfitting is evidenced when the apparent training gain materially exceeds the held-out gain, especially when \(G_{\mathrm{train}}>0\) but \(G_{\mathrm{test}}\le 0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tuning is overfit when its apparent training improvement substantially shrinks or reverses on disjoint held-out instances.
assumptions_latex: \(D_{\mathrm{train}}\cap D_{\mathrm{test}}=\varnothing\).
Lower values of \(R\) are better.
The reference configuration \(\theta_0\) is fixed independently of both evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_{\mathrm{train}}>0\) and \(G_{\mathrm{test}}\le 0\) constitute a clear overfitting failure pattern.

notation.meaning: empirical loss of parameters theta on sample D
training and held-out gains against the reference

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure pattern fits Parameter Overfitting, but disjoint samples alone do not distinguish overfitting from sampling variability or distribution shift. The record needs an authoritative generalization source and assumptions governing how the training and held-out samples are drawn before its diagnostic conclusion can be accepted.

children.title: Ablation Design
children.top_down_role: Structural choices for isolating the contribution of parameter groups or individual settings.

knowledge_statements.title: Ablation Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled removal or replacement of one solver component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a baseline configuration and \(C^{(-j)}\) the configuration obtained by disabling component \(j\) or replacing it by a declared neutral setting. A valid paired ablation holds fixed the solver build, all nonablated parameters, instance set, per-instance seeds, execution regime, resource limits, hardware assignment, and performance functional. For paired instances \(i=1,\ldots,n\), record \[d_i=M(C^{(-j)},i)-M(C,i).\] Component \(j\)'s effect is assessed from the prespecified aggregation and uncertainty analysis of \((d_i)_{i=1}^n\), not from unmatched aggregate runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid ablation changes one component while pairing all other experimental factors and analyzing per-instance performance differences.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(C^{(-j)}\) differ only in the declared ablation.
Every instance is evaluated under matched run conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The paired contrast is represented by \((d_i)_{i=1}^n\), where \(d_i=M(C^{(-j)},i)-M(C,i)\).

notation.meaning: performance of configuration C on instance i
paired ablation difference on instance i

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The paired-ablation condition fits the exact container and the notation is coherent, but no inspectable methodology source supports the stated validity requirements or the exclusion of unmatched aggregate runs. The local source inventory is not relevant to experimental design.

children.title: Ablation-Based Attribution
children.top_down_role: Scope limits for attributing performance changes to settings examined through ablation.

knowledge_statements.title: Ablation-Based Attribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal component attribution from a controlled paired ablation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under a valid paired ablation, define the marginal loss attributable to removing component \(j\) by \[\Delta_j=\mathcal{A}_{i=1}^{n}\bigl(M(C^{(-j)},i)-M(C,i)\bigr),\] where larger \(M\) is worse and \(\mathcal{A}\) is a prespecified aggregation functional, such as the arithmetic mean. Then \(\Delta_j>0\) attributes beneficial marginal performance to retaining \(j\) in baseline \(C\). This attribution is local to \(C\): interactions imply that generally \(\Delta_j\) need not equal the effect of adding \(j\) to another configuration, and separate ablation effects need not sum to the total improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A paired ablation estimates a component's marginal effect in one baseline, but interactions prevent universal or additive attribution.
assumptions_latex: The ablation satisfies the paired-control conditions.
Larger values of \(M\) denote worse performance.
The aggregation functional \(\mathcal{A}\) is chosen before observing results.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_j>0\) supports a beneficial local contribution of component \(j\) within baseline \(C\).

notation.meaning: aggregated marginal ablation loss for component j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: marginal attribution by controlled intervention
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local marginal-effect representation fits the container and appropriately warns about interactions. Nevertheless, interpreting a positive aggregated difference as support for beneficial contribution requires uncertainty and sampling conditions that are not explicit in the conclusion, and no methodology source is cited.

children.title: Held-Out Evaluation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Evaluation settings used to test whether tuning gains persist beyond the tuning workload.

knowledge_statements.title: Held-Out Evaluation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation protocol separating tuning decisions from final assessment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite instance collection \(D\), parameter family \(\Theta\), loss \(R\), and split rule independent of observed solver outcomes. Partition \(D\) into disjoint sets \(D_{\mathrm{train}},D_{\mathrm{val}},D_{\mathrm{test}}\). Initialize candidate parameters using only \(D_{\mathrm{train}}\); update and select \(\widehat\theta\) using only training and validation results. Freeze \(\widehat\theta\), the execution protocol, and the analysis rule. Run the test set once under the frozen protocol and output \[R_{\mathrm{test}}=R(\widehat\theta;D_{\mathrm{test}})\] together with run-level uncertainty summaries. No test outcome may trigger further tuning reported under the same held-out evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tune on training and validation instances, freeze all choices, then evaluate once on an untouched test set.
assumptions_latex: The three data subsets are pairwise disjoint.
The split rule is independent of observed solver outcomes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the frozen-configuration assessment \(R(\widehat\theta;D_{\mathrm{test}})\).

notation.meaning: training, validation, and test instance sets
parameter vector frozen before test evaluation

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind correctly matches a held-out evaluation protocol, but its exact train-validation-test rules, one-time test evaluation requirement, and uncertainty obligations have no inspectable supporting citation. A statistical learning or algorithm-configuration source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Solve-Status Overinterpretation
children.top_down_role: Interpretation failures caused by treating solver status as richer evidence than it supplies.

knowledge_statements.title: Solve-Status Overinterpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical limits of conclusions licensed by solver termination statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set and let \(f^*\) denote the optimal objective value when it exists. A status reporting a feasible incumbent certifies only that the returned \(x\) satisfies \(x\in F\); it does not certify \(f(x)=f^*\). An optimal status licenses optimality only under the solver's stated exactness, tolerance, and model-validity conventions. An unknown or limit status licenses neither feasibility nor infeasibility unless accompanied by a separately verifiable witness. Consequently, inferring optimality from feasibility, or infeasibility from absence of a found solution, is solve-status overinterpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible does not mean optimal, and failure to find a solution does not mean infeasible without an appropriate certificate.
assumptions_latex: The reported status is interpreted under its documented solver semantics.
Model construction and numerical conventions are part of the claimed result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in F\) alone does not imply \(f(x)=f^*\), and absence of an incumbent does not imply \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of the submitted model

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard logical semantics of optimization statuses
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and core logical cautions fit the container, but status meanings are solver-specific. No CP-SAT status documentation is cited to support the treatment of feasible, optimal, unknown, and limit statuses or the referenced exactness and tolerance conventions.

children.title: Aggregate-Statistic Overinterpretation
children.top_down_role: Interpretation failures caused by relying on totals or averages that conceal run-level variation.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate-Statistic Overinterpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of causal or instance-level inference from pooled diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_{ir}\) be a diagnostic measurement for instance \(i\) and replicate \(r\), and let \(A((z_{ir}))\) be a reported aggregate. In general, equality or ordering of aggregates does not imply the corresponding instancewise relation: \[A((x_{ir}))\le A((y_{ir}))\ \not\Rightarrow\ x_{ir}\le y_{ir}\quad\text{for every }i,r.\] Moreover, a correlation between an aggregate counter and performance does not identify a causal contribution when instance difficulty, runtime exposure, or worker count affects both. Aggregate statistics support descriptive comparison only under declared weighting, normalization, sampling, and uncertainty conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pooled diagnostic neither determines every instance-level outcome nor establishes causality without normalization, controls, and uncertainty analysis.
assumptions_latex: The aggregate \(A\) is many-to-one.
Measurements may vary across instances or replicates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Aggregate ordering alone implies neither pointwise ordering nor causal attribution.

notation.meaning: measurement for instance i and replicate r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: non-identifiability from many-to-one aggregation and observational correlation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon fits Aggregate-Statistic Overinterpretation, and the general warning is plausible. However, the pointwise nonimplication depends on properties of the aggregation functional, while the causal claim requires a specified data-generating and identification framework. No statistical-methodology source is supplied.

children.title: Cross-Signal Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Consistency relationships among status, bounds, timing, workload, and run-level diagnostic evidence.

assumptions_latex: The model is a finite CP-SAT minimization problem with an exact integer-valued objective.
All diagnostic signals are taken from the same solver run and the same reporting snapshot.
Solver statuses have their documented semantic meanings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any violated implication makes the diagnostic snapshot internally inconsistent and prevents sound interpretation until signal provenance, timing, or status semantics are resolved.

notation.meaning: incumbent objective, with positive infinity when no incumbent exists
valid lower bound on the optimum

review_flags: No authoritative source locator was supplied for the precise cross-signal predicate.
CP-SAT status and bound semantics require source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency predicate for minimization status, incumbent, bound, and solution-count signals from one CP-SAT snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A diagnostic snapshot is cross-signal consistent only if all applicable implications hold: \(S=\mathrm{OPTIMAL}\Rightarrow U<+\infty\) and \(L=U\); \(S=\mathrm{FEASIBLE}\Rightarrow U<+\infty\) and \(L\le U\); \(S=\mathrm{INFEASIBLE}\Rightarrow U=+\infty\); and \(S=\mathrm{MODEL\_INVALID}\Rightarrow\) neither \(U\) nor \(L\) is interpreted as optimization evidence. Moreover, if \(n\) is the reported number of feasible solutions, then \(n>0\Rightarrow U<+\infty\), while any reported incumbent requires \(n>0\). Comparisons of \(U\), \(L\), elapsed time, conflicts, or branches are admissible only when their run identifier and snapshot time agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver snapshot is interpretable only when status, incumbent, bound, solution count, run identity, and reporting time satisfy their joint semantic implications.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Signal Consistency Checks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the exact Cross-Signal Consistency Checks leaf, but the record supplies no inspectable citation for the asserted CP-SAT status, incumbent, best-bound, and solution-count implications. In particular, the meaning and availability of a reported feasible-solution count, the equality expected between an integer objective and a reported bound at OPTIMAL status, and which signals remain meaningful under MODEL_INVALID are interface- and version-sensitive. The plain statement also omits the detailed run-identity and snapshot-time comparison condition expressed in the LaTeX statement. Source uncertainty therefore affects the precise predicate and prevents acceptance.

assumptions_latex: At least two asynchronous workers can communicate incumbents or bounds during a run.
The stopping rule uses a wall-clock limit or another schedule-sensitive interruption criterion.
Worker completion and communication order are not fixed by the recorded experimental configuration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A one-run comparison cannot attribute an observed outcome difference solely to the tuned configuration; reproducibility requires deterministic execution or a repeated-trial distributional comparison over execution schedules.

notation.meaning: reported outcome under configuration and schedule

review_flags: No authoritative source locator was supplied for CP-SAT parallel nondeterminism.
The exact deterministic-mode guarantees are solver-version dependent and require documentation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for tuning comparisons under asynchronous, schedule-sensitive parallel CP-SAT execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a model, configuration \(\theta\), nominal random seed, worker count, machine, and wall-clock limit. If two admissible execution schedules \(\sigma_1\) and \(\sigma_2\) can change which worker result is communicated before termination, then the reported outcome may satisfy \(Y(\theta,\sigma_1)\ne Y(\theta,\sigma_2)\), even though every recorded tuning parameter agrees. Consequently, comparing single parallel runs of configurations \(\theta_a\) and \(\theta_b\) confounds configuration effects with schedule effects. A reproducible comparison must either enforce an execution mode for which \(Y(\theta,\sigma)\) is schedule invariant, or estimate a declared statistic of the distribution of \(Y(\theta,\Sigma)\) from replicated runs under a specified schedule-generating regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single parallel runs confound parameter effects with execution-schedule effects unless execution is deterministic or replicated outcomes are compared distributionally.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonreproducible Parallel Comparisons

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role correctly fits the Nonreproducible Parallel Comparisons leaf, and the configuration-versus-schedule confounding claim is plausible. However, no inspectable source establishes the assumed CP-SAT worker communication behavior or any solver-version-specific execution mode under which the full reported outcome is schedule invariant. The record also does not define the components or measurable domain of Y, so the claimed invariant mode and distributional statistic cannot be assessed precisely. Authoritative solver documentation or a specific experimental-method source is required before the mathematical scope and conclusion can be relied upon.
